# Roadmap: foundations of adic spaces, Part II — analytic and formal geometry

*Proposed roadmap `AdicSpacesPartII`. It extends the Tau Ceti roadmap
**Foundations of adic spaces** (`tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/AdicSpaces`), called **the anchor** below, and
starts where the anchor's reusable Layers 0–5 stop; "anchor Layer n" is the anchor's Layer n. Layer 6 of the
anchor (the adic Fargues–Fontaine curve) is an application and is not used here.*

## Purpose

The anchor builds Huber rings and Huber pairs, the valuation and adic spectra, rational
localisation, the structure presheaf, sheafiness for strongly noetherian and stably uniform Tate
rings, and the category of adic spaces with open and closed immersions, morphisms locally of finite
type and gluing. It deliberately stops before fibre products: separatedness, properness and the
diagonal formalism are to be treated "together with completed tensor products and fibre products in
a separate roadmap". This is that roadmap. It develops the geometry that p-adic Hodge theory, the
étale cohomology of rigid spaces, overconvergent automorphic forms and p-adic Shimura varieties use:

- **completed tensor products** of Huber pairs, with their topology and plus ring, their universal
  property and their uniformisation, and **fibre products** of adic spaces under Huber's noetherian
  hypotheses;
- the **morphism theory**: adic morphisms, Huber's finite-type classes, separated, proper and
  partially proper morphisms with the valuative criteria, finite and quasi-finite morphisms,
  continuous differentials, unramified, smooth and étale morphisms, the Jacobian criterion and the
  standard étale presentation;
- the **classical affinoid algebras** (Noether normalisation, residue fields, the supremum seminorm,
  integrality of A°, reductions) and **analytification** of schemes locally of finite type (Huber's
  fibre product of a scheme with an adic space), Tate's rigid-analytic spaces with affinoid subdomains
  and Huber's rigid–adic comparison, and the analytification of group schemes, abelian schemes and
  isogenies;
- **noetherian formal geometry**: Spf, formal schemes, formal completion, coherent formal modules,
  the theorem on formal functions, and Grothendieck's existence and algebraisation theorems;
- **formal models**: admissible formal schemes over O_K for an arbitrary complete rank-one
  valuation ring, admissible blow-ups, Raynaud's theorem, Huber's generic fibre of formal schemes
  of type (S), Conrad's functor on FS_C, the good-reduction locus, residue discs, and Hasse domains
  defined through fractional valuation bounds;
- **coherent sheaves**: the associated sheaf of a finite module, Tate acyclicity for finite modules
  and for sheafy Tate pairs, Kiehl's theorems on affinoid and quasi-Stein spaces, vector bundles
  on sheafy affinoids, the proper mapping theorem, base change, proper GAGA, and the **trace**
  along finite locally free morphisms with pull–identify–trace on correspondences;
- the **étale and pro-étale sites** of AdicEtaleGeometry A1, transported to these carriers, with
  smooth pairs and the restriction to boundary complements;
- **sousperfectoid** rings and spaces, products of perfectoid spaces with smooth rigid spaces, and
  the completed coefficient algebras and sheaves of p-adic families;
- **dagger geometry**: overconvergent Tate algebras, dagger algebras, Monsky–Washnitzer weak
  completions, dagger spaces, strict neighbourhoods, Grosse-Klönne's comparison with rigid spaces,
  and the overconvergent, logarithmic and compactly supported de Rham complexes.

The morphism theory is built once, here, for the whole area: AdicEtaleGeometry, PerfectoidSpaces,
ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology, DiamondsAndVStacks, PadicDifferentialEquationsAndRigidCohomology and
the Shimura-variety roadmaps import it.

## Layers and their order

```text
anchor Layers 0–5  → R0 → R1 → R2 → R3 → R5
F0                 → R0,  F0 → R2,  F0 → R3
R0, R1             → R4 ← AdicEtaleGeometry A1
R0, R1, R2, R3, R4 → F1
AdicEtaleGeometry A1, PerfectoidSpaces P1–P3 → R5
```

| Layer | Title | What it builds |
|---|---|---|
| R0 | Morphisms and admissible affinoid products | classical affinoid algebras, completed tensor products, fibre products, the morphism classes, differentials, smooth and étale morphisms |
| R1 | Analytification and algebraic correspondences | X ↦ X^ad, rigid spaces and affinoid subdomains, rigid–adic comparison, analytic groups |
| F0 | Formal geometry | Spf and formal schemes, completion, coherent formal modules, formal functions, existence and algebraisation |
| R2 | Formal schemes, generic fibres and Hasse domains | admissible formal schemes, blow-ups, Raynaud, generic fibres, good reduction, Hasse domains |
| R3 | Coherent sheaves and finite traces | M̃, Tate and Kiehl, vector bundles, proper mapping theorem, GAGA, traces |
| R4 | Étale and pro-étale sites | A1's sites on these carriers, functoriality, smooth pairs, boundary complements |
| R5 | Families and sousperfectoid spaces | sousperfectoid rings and spaces, perfectoid × smooth, coefficient algebras and sheaves |
| F1 | Dagger geometry and overconvergent de Rham complexes | dagger algebras and spaces, strict neighbourhoods, de Rham complexes |

F0 depends on nothing in this roadmap and precedes R0 (Huber's sheafiness for rings with a noetherian
ring of definition uses the Artin–Rees lemma for cohomology of F0) and R2. R4 needs R0, R1 and AdicEtaleGeometry A1.
R5 needs R0, R3, AdicEtaleGeometry A1 and PerfectoidSpaces P1–P3. F1 needs R0–R4.

## Prerequisites

- **Foundations of adic spaces** (Tau Ceti), Layers 0–5, as a whole: Huber rings, completion,
  weighted restricted power series, strong noetherianness and the open mapping theorem (Layer 0);
  valuation spectra and continuous valuations (Layer 1); `Spa(A, A⁺)`, rational subsets, quotient
  pairs and polydiscs (Layer 2); rational localisation, the structure presheaf and pre-adic spaces
  (Layer 3); sheafiness and Tate acyclicity of strongly noetherian Tate rings and the
  Buzzard–Verberkmoes theorem (Layer 4); adic spaces, open and closed immersions, morphisms locally
  of finite type and gluing (Layer 5). Every node that uses one of these records the layer in
  `importsFromTauCetiRoadmaps`, and the packet's requests say exactly what is used.
- **AdicEtaleGeometry A1**: the étale and pro-étale sites of analytic adic spaces with the corrected
  pro-étale covering convention, geometric points, and the local description of étale and finite
  étale morphisms (R4 and R5).
- **PerfectoidSpaces P1–P3**: perfectoid Tate rings, their rational localisations and fibre products,
  and almost purity (R5).
- **ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology H0**: tilde-limits of affinoids (R5).
- **Coherent cohomology of schemes**: higher direct images along proper morphisms and their
  coherence (Tau Ceti StableReduction, Layer 2), flat base change and acyclicity of affines (Tau Ceti
  JacobianChallenge, Layers B and C), Godement resolutions (SchemeAndStackFoundations SF.2),
  projective bundles, Serre vanishing, Chow's lemma and Grothendieck's dévissage
  (AlgebraicModuliForArithmeticGeometry R09.1–R09.3). F0 and R3 use them.
- **DiamondsAndVStacks D0** (Cartan's criterion and Čech-to-derived comparison on a basis),
  **TropicalAndBerkovichArithmetic TB.0** (the Gel'fand spectrum of a Banach ring),
  **ModularCurvesPartII R13.1** (generalised elliptic curves and their moduli, for the Hasse loci)
  and **Tau Ceti ModularCurves 0e** (effective faithfully flat descent of modules).

## Boundaries

- **The anchor owns** Huber rings and pairs, completion, restricted power series, strong
  noetherianness, `Spa`, rational localisation, the structure presheaf, strongly noetherian and
  stably uniform sheafiness with Tate acyclicity of the structure sheaf in that generality, adic
  spaces, open immersions, closed immersions defined affinoid-locally by closed ideals, morphisms
  locally of finite type and gluing. This roadmap cites all of it and plans only what lies beyond:
  completed tensor products, fibre products and the morphism theory that needs them; sheafiness
  for rings with a noetherian ring of definition that are not Tate (Huber's Case I); Tate acyclicity
  for every sheafy Tate pair; coherent and finite-projective module theory.
- **AdicEtaleGeometry A1 owns** the étale and pro-étale sites. R4 builds no second site: it proves
  that A1's sites on the carriers of R0–R1 behave as needed (functoriality, the rigid comparison,
  smooth pairs, boundary complements). Derived cohomology of these sites is
  **ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology H0**'s.
- **PerfectoidSpaces owns** perfectoid rings and spaces, tilting and almost purity (P0–P3), and the
  continuous torsor descent of modules with coefficients (P9). R5 builds only the sousperfectoid
  ambient class, perfectoid × smooth products and the coefficient algebras and sheaves on them.
- **PadicDifferentialEquationsAndRigidCohomology owns** frames, tubes of frames, `j†`, Robba rings,
  Frobenius structures and rigid cohomology (RD.0–RD.6); **AutomorphicGaloisRepresentationsPartII
  AG2.4** owns the ordinary-locus rigid cohomology used by HLTT. F1 supplies the dagger carrier:
  dagger algebras, weak completions, dagger spaces, affinoid strict neighbourhoods and the de Rham
  complexes; it does not infer a rigid/de Rham comparison from an equality of point sets.
- **ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology H1** owns the specialisation morphism of étale sites and the
  nearby-cycle comparisons; R2 supplies the generic fibre and the formal completion comparison.
- **LocalGaloisDeformationRings L7** owns bounded-height Grassmannians, proper maps to deformation
  rings and their component images; F0 supplies the formal algebraisation it uses.
- **Consumers.** PerfectoidSpaces P2–P9, AdicEtaleGeometry A0–A4, ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology H0–H5,
  DiamondsAndVStacks D2–D6, HodgeTateAndCanonicalSubgroups T0–T6, OverconvergentAutomorphicForms O0–O8,
  PadicHodgeTheory P8, RelativeFarguesFontaine RF0, CohomologyComparisons CP.0,
  AlgebraicModuliForArithmeticGeometry R09.6, NeronModelsAndSemistableAbelianVarieties R11.1,
  ModularCurvesPartII R13.1, LocalGaloisDeformationRings L7 and R08.3,
  TorsionCohomologyInfrastructure TC.0, PadicFamilies L2a, BunGAndNewtonStrata BG0,
  HilbertModularVarietiesAndShimuraCurves R18.2, TropicalAndBerkovichArithmetic TB.0,
  PadicDifferentialEquationsAndRigidCohomology RD.0–RD.6 and ColemanIntegration L1 import the layers

## Pinned conventions

These hold throughout; each layer adds its own.

1. **Huber pairs.** A Huber pair is Tau Ceti's `TauCeti.Huber.Pair A`: the plus ring `A⁺` is explicit
   data, never selected by a typeclass. A morphism of Huber pairs is `TauCeti.Huber.Pair.Hom`, a
   continuous ring homomorphism carrying `A⁺` into `B⁺`.
2. **Complete includes Hausdorff**, as in the anchor. Every statement about complete rings,
   modules or pairs carries both hypotheses.
3. **Adic spaces** are the objects of the anchor's category (Layer 5): locally `Spa(A, A⁺)` for
   sheafy complete Huber pairs. A point is **analytic** if it has an open neighbourhood whose ring of
   sections contains a topologically nilpotent unit. An adic space is **locally noetherian** if every
   point has an open affinoid neighbourhood `Spa(A, A⁺)` with `A` of noetherian type: a noetherian ring
   of definition, or a strongly noetherian Tate ring (R0). Every discrete ring is of noetherian type.
4. **The base field.** When a base field is needed, `K` is complete for a nontrivial nonarchimedean
   absolute value of rank one, `O_K = K°`, `ϖ` is a pseudouniformiser (`0 < |ϖ| < 1`) and
   `Spa K := Spa(K, K°)`. `O_K` is noetherian exactly when `K` is discretely valued; no statement assumes
   it unless it says so. Characteristic, discreteness and spherical completeness are stated per result
   where the sources need them (F1, R3).
5. **Completed tensor products** `B ⊗̂_A C` are those of R0: defined when both structure maps are adic,
   with topology from rings and ideals of definition, plus ring the integral closure of the image of
   `B⁺ ⊗_{A⁺} C⁺`, then completion. They are not uniform or sheafy in general; every fibre product
   carries its existence and sheafiness theorem.
6. **Fibre products** of adic spaces are taken in the anchor's category and exist under Huber's
   hypotheses (R0): the map from `|X ×_Z Y|` to the fibre product of the underlying sets is surjective
   and not injective in general.
7. **Formal schemes** are F0's: locally `Spf A` for `A` complete and separated for an adic topology with
   a finitely generated ideal of definition; the noetherian theorems of F0 say so. Admissible formal
   `O_K`-schemes (topologically finitely presented and `ϖ`-torsion-free) carry the `ϖ`-adic topology and
   are not noetherian unless `K` is discretely valued (R2).
8. **Rigid spaces** are Tate's rigid-analytic spaces over `K` (R1). The rigid analytification is written
   `X^an` and the adic one `X^ad`; they are identified only through Huber's functor, `r_K(X^an) ≅ X^ad`.
9. **Valuation bounds.** A fractional bound `|f| ≤ |g|^{a/b}` means `v(f^b) ≤ v(g^a)`; no element
   `g^{a/b}` of the base field is assumed. Tubes and strict Hasse loci in adic spaces are interiors of
   preimages under the specialisation map, not the preimages themselves (R2).
10. **Coherent and locally free.** Coherent sheaves are defined on locally noetherian adic spaces only.
    Vector bundles (finite locally free modules) are defined on every adic space; on a sheafy Tate
    affinoid they correspond to finite projective modules. Finite projective, finite locally free and
    finitely generated locally free modules are the same.
11. **Traces.** The trace of an endomorphism of a finite projective module is `LinearMap.projectiveTrace`
    (R3), defined through `dualTensorHomEquiv`; Mathlib's `LinearMap.trace` and `Algebra.trace` are used
    only for free modules, because they are defined to be `0` when no finite basis exists. A trace is
    never defined as a sum over geometric points; that formula is a theorem for finite étale maps.
12. **Names.** Ring-level declarations live in `TauCeti.Huber`, geometry of adic spaces in
    `TauCeti.AdicSpace`, formal schemes in `TauCeti.FormalScheme`, dagger algebras in `TauCeti.Dagger`
    and dagger spaces in `TauCeti.DaggerSpace`; the names below omit `TauCeti.`.

## What the libraries supply, and what this roadmap adds

At the pinned commits (Mathlib `082e2d3`, Tau Ceti `f790474`) Tau Ceti contains the affine part of the
anchor: Huber pairs and their morphisms, completion of Huber rings, weighted restricted power
series with their universal property, strong noetherianness, topologically-finite-type maps, rational
localisation with its universal property, `Spa` and rational subsets, the homeomorphism
`Spa(A⟨T/s⟩) ≅ R(T/s)`, flatness of rational restriction maps, faithful flatness over finite rational
covers and a sheaf criterion on rational covers. It has no category of adic spaces, no structure sheaf
as a sheaf, no completed tensor product and no fibre product. Mathlib contains schemes with their
morphism classes, quasi-coherent modules on affine schemes, Kähler differentials, formally étale,
smooth and unramified algebras, adic completion and the trace of free algebras. Neither library has
formal schemes, rigid or dagger spaces, coherent sheaves on analytic spaces, traces of finite
projective algebras, or sousperfectoid rings. The declarations below build them; each node's
`prerequisites` lists the library declarations it rests on, read at the pinned commits.
