## R0. Morphisms and admissible affinoid products


Throughout, `K` is complete of rank one and a `K`-affinoid algebra is a complete Hausdorff topological `K`-algebra `A` with
`K → A` strictly topologically of finite type (Tau Ceti `IsStrictlyTopologicallyFiniteType`: a continuous open surjection
`K⟨X₁,…,X_n⟩ → A`; Wedhorn Definition 5.57; the anchor's Layer 2.4 names these affinoid algebras). `Max A` is the set of
maximal ideals. The anchor supplies Weierstrass theory and strong noetherianness (Layer 0.5), the open mapping theorem
(Layer 0.6) and Tate acyclicity for rational coverings (Layer 4.1); Tau Ceti supplies the canonical topology of finite
modules and closedness of submodules (`IsTateRing.isModuleTopology`, `isClosed_of_isNoetherian`,
`LinearMap.isStrictMap_of_module_finite`), which is Kedlaya–Liu Lemma 2.5.2 and needs no node here. This section plans the
algebraic part of the classical theory the roadmap uses (R0, R1, R2, R3 and the dagger proofs of F1); the
affinoid subdomains, the Gerritzen–Grauert theorem and the rigid local rings are R1's. BGR is not public: where its proof
was not read, the node records a gap named after the BGR result.

- **Noether normalisation** (`R0/affinoid-noether-normalisation`, `Huber.Affinoid.exists_finite_injective_tateAlgebra`).
  For `A ≠ 0` there is a finite injection `K⟨T₁,…,T_d⟩ → A`; every such map is continuous and strict (Kedlaya–Liu 2.5.4;
  Conrad, *Several approaches*, 1.2.6(4)). Proof: induction with Weierstrass division after the automorphisms
  `X_i ↦ X_i + X_n^{c_i}`; strictness from `LinearMap.isStrictMap_of_module_finite`. Acceptance: `T ↦ X + Y` makes the annulus
  `K⟨X, Y⟩/(XY − 1)` finite over `K⟨T⟩`, while `K⟨X⟩ → K⟨X, X⁻¹⟩` is injective and not finite.
- **Residue fields** (`R0/affinoid-residue-fields-finite`, `Huber.Affinoid.finiteDimensional_residueField`). `A/m` is finite
  over `K` for every maximal ideal (Wedhorn 5.61, Kedlaya–Liu 2.5.5(a)); `|·|` extends uniquely (`spectralNorm_unique`);
  `Max` is functorial along `K`-algebra maps. Acceptance: `(T² − c)` in `K⟨T⟩` has residue field `K(√c)`.
- **Jacobson property** (`R0/affinoid-jacobson`, `Huber.Affinoid.isJacobsonRing`). Every prime is an intersection of maximal
  ideals; nilpotent ⇔ vanishing on `Max A`; unit ⇔ no zero on `Max A` (Conrad 1.1.5(2)). Gap: BGR 5.2.6/3.
- **Maximal ideals of Tate algebras** (`R0/tate-algebra-maximal-ideals-polynomial`). Every maximal ideal of `K⟨X₁,…,X_n⟩` is
  generated by polynomials `p_i ∈ K[X₁,…,X_i]` monic in `X_i`, and `K[X]/m₀ ≅ K⟨X⟩/m` (BGR 7.1.1/3 as cited by Conrad,
  *irreducible components*, A.1.2, and Grosse-Klönne 1.5). Gap: BGR 7.1.1/3.
- **Supremum seminorm** (`R0/affinoid-supremum-seminorm`, definition, `Huber.Affinoid.supNorm`).

  ```text
  |f|_sup = sup_{x ∈ Max A} |f(x)|,   |f|_sup ≤ |f|_π for every residue norm |·|_π.
  ```

  A power-multiplicative `K`-algebra seminorm, contracted by homomorphisms, a norm iff `A` is reduced, the Gauss norm on
  `K⟨X⟩`, equal to the spectral seminorm `lim |fⁿ|_π^{1/n}` (Kedlaya, *Finiteness*, Definition 2.1.7). API:
  `supNorm`, `supNorm_le_residueNorm`, `supNorm_add_le`, `supNorm_mul_le`, `supNorm_pow`, `supNorm_algebraMap`,
  `supNorm_map_le`, `supNorm_eq_zero_iff`, `supNorm_tateAlgebra`, `supNorm_eq_spectralSeminorm`, `exists_supNorm_eq`,
  `mem_powerBoundedSubring_iff_supNorm_le_one`. Unit tests: `supNorm_test_dualNumbers` (`|T|_sup = 0` in `K⟨T⟩/(T²)`: not
  a residue norm), `supNorm_test_gauss`, `supNorm_test_zero`, `supNorm_test_sqrt` (`|T|_sup = |p|^{1/2}` in
  `ℚ_p⟨T⟩/(T² − p)`).
- **Maximum modulus** (`R0/affinoid-maximum-modulus`). The supremum is attained at a point of `Max A`, so
  `|f|_sup ∈ √|K^×| ∪ {0}`; minimum modulus for units (Conrad 1.2.6(5), Remark 1.2.7). Gap: BGR 6.2.1/4.
- **Power-boundedness** (`R0/affinoid-power-bounded-iff-sup`). `A° = {|f|_sup ≤ 1}` and `A°° = {|f|_sup < 1}`. Gap: BGR
  6.2.3/1 for `|f|_sup ≤ 1 ⇒ f ∈ A°`; the other implications are proved on the node.
- **Reduced affinoids** (`R0/reduced-affinoid-supremum-norm`). For reduced `A`, `|·|_sup` is a norm equivalent to every
  residue norm, so `A°` is bounded; conversely a bounded `A°` forces `A` reduced (Kedlaya–Liu 2.5.6; Conrad, *adic notes*,
  Examples 2.3–2.4; Morel II.1.4). Gap: BGR 6.2.4/1.
- **Automatic continuity** (`R0/affinoid-homomorphism-continuous`). Every `K`-algebra homomorphism of `K`-affinoid algebras
  is continuous (Wedhorn 5.60, Conrad 1.2.6(2)); the proof compares with the continuous map given by the universal property
  of `K⟨X⟩` modulo all `nᵏ` and uses Krull's intersection theorem, as in Grosse-Klönne 1.6(2).
- **Integrality of `A°`** (`R0/affinoid-power-bounded-integral`). For a surjection `π : K⟨X⟩ → A`, `A°` is the integral
  closure of `π(K°⟨X⟩)` (BGR 6.3.4/1 and 6.4.3 as cited by Huber 1994 Lemma 4.4 and Bosch–Lütkebohmert I 4.5); this is the
  input of `R1/tft-plus-ring-power-bounded`. Gap: BGR 6.3.4/1.
- **Reductions** (`R0/affinoid-reduction-finite`). `Ã = A°/A°°`; a finite `A → B` gives a finite `Ã → B̃`
  (Kedlaya–Liu 2.5.7), so `Ã` is a finitely generated `K̃`-algebra. Gap: BGR 6.3.4/2.
- **Reduced reduction** (`R0/reduced-reduction-ring-of-definition`). In a Tate ring, a ring of definition `A₀ ∋ ϖ` with
  `A₀/ϖA₀` reduced equals `A°`; the proof is elementary (Tau Ceti `PairOfDefinition.adjoin`,
  `IsPseudoUniformizer.hasBasis_nhds_zero`). Non-example: `ℤ_p⟨T⟩[S]/(S² − p²T)` has non-reduced reduction and
  `S/p ∈ A° \ A₀`.

These nodes are ring-level: they use only the base roadmap and the pinned libraries. R0 uses Noether
normalisation and the integrality of `A°` in `R0/quasi-finite-fibre-criteria`; R1 uses them for the Tate topology,
`R1/tft-plus-ring-power-bounded` and the affinoid subdomains; R2, R3 and F1 use them as listed in the declaration index.


This part of stage R0 builds the completed tensor product of Huber pairs, the classes of morphisms needed to state
when fibre products of adic spaces exist, the fibre products themselves, and the closed-subspace and diagonal
formalism that separatedness and properness (R0b) and differentials, smoothness and étaleness (R0c) are built on.
It starts where the anchor roadmap `tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/AdicSpaces` stops: Huber rings, pairs of definition,
completion, weighted restricted power series, strong noetherianness and topologically-finite-type maps (Layer 0),
continuous valuations (Layer 1), `Spa`, rational subsets, quotient pairs and analytic points (Layer 2), rational
localisation and sheafiness predicates (Layer 3), sheafiness of strongly noetherian Tate pairs (Layer 4), and the
category of adic spaces with open and closed immersions, morphisms locally of finite type and gluing (Layer 5) are
imported, never rebuilt. The anchor explicitly excludes completed tensor products, fibre products and the diagonal;
they are planned here.

Three boundaries are pinned. First, no sheafiness is claimed for a completed tensor product without a hypothesis
that proves it: the affinoid fibre product theorem takes sheafiness of `B ⊗̂_A C` as a hypothesis, and this part
supplies it only in the noetherian case; perfectoid products are PerfectoidSpaces P2 and sousperfectoid products
are R5. Second, no unrestricted existence of fibre products is claimed; fibre products do not exist in general.
Third, the completed tensor product performs no uniformization (a completed tensor product need not be uniform); the uniformization of a Tate Huber pair and the uniform completed tensor product are separate constructions (R0a.2b), built on the spectral seminorm.

### Conventions

- A *Huber pair* is Tau Ceti's `TauCeti.Huber.Pair A`: the plus ring is explicit data, never a typeclass. A
  morphism of Huber pairs is `TauCeti.Huber.Pair.Hom`: a continuous ring homomorphism carrying `A⁺` into `B⁺`.
- *Complete* always includes *Hausdorff*. Every statement about complete rings carries both hypotheses.
- *Topologically of finite type* for a ring homomorphism means Tau Ceti's `IsTopologicallyFiniteType` (Wedhorn
  6.29(i), weighted presentation, finite weights forming an `IsWeightFamily`). For a morphism of pairs it means the
  anchor's Layer 5.2 notion: a quotient mapping out of the weighted restricted power-series pair `A⟨X⟩_M`, whose plus
  ring is the integral closure of `{∑ a_ν X^ν : a_ν ∈ M^ν·Â⁺}`. A *quotient mapping* `(C, C⁺) → (B, B⁺)` is a
  surjective, continuous and open ring homomorphism with `B⁺` the integral closure of the image of `C⁺`.
- Weights: `M = (M₁, …, M_n)` finite subsets of `A` with every `M_i·A` open. By Huber 1994 Lemma 1.1 (= Wedhorn
  Lemma 6.20, stated as an equivalence by the anchor's Layer 0.4) this is Tau Ceti's `IsWeightFamily`.
- `B ⊗̂_A C` always denotes the completed pair of `R0/completed-tensor-product`: topology `{Iⁿ·F}` from rings and
  ideals of definition, plus ring the integral closure of the image of `B⁺ ⊗_{A⁺} C⁺`, then completion. It is
  defined only when both structure maps are adic.
- A point of an adic space is *analytic* if some open neighbourhood has a ring of sections containing a topologically
  nilpotent unit; on `Spa(A, A⁺)` this is Tau Ceti's `ValuationSpectrum.IsAnalyticPoint` (support not open).
- *Of noetherian type* means Huber's hypothesis: a noetherian ring of definition, or a strongly noetherian Tate
  ring. It is weaker than being a noetherian ring (every discrete ring is of noetherian type).

```text
    A ──f──▶ B                 Spa(B ⊗̂_A C) ──▶ Spa C
    │        │ inl                   │              │
    g        ▼                       ▼              ▼
    ▼   B ⊗̂_A C                   Spa B ────────▶ Spa A
    C ──inr──▶
```

### Organisation

- R0a.1 ring-level inputs: noetherian type, adic homomorphisms, topological finite type (6 nodes).
- R0a.1a sheafiness of rings of noetherian type: Huber 1994 Theorem 2.2, Case I, and the discrete case (14 nodes).
- R0a.2 the completed tensor product and its computations (5 nodes; planet “Completed tensor product”).
- R0a.2b the norm and spectral seminorm of a Tate ring, the spectral topology, uniformization and the uniform completed tensor product (6 nodes).
- R0a.3 adic morphisms, the finite-type hierarchy and locally noetherian spaces (6 nodes).
- R0a.4 fibre products (6 nodes; planet “Fibre product of adic spaces”).
- R0a.5 closed subspaces and the diagonal (2 nodes).

### R0a.1 Ring-level inputs

Huber's hypotheses are stated for the topological ring alone. The first group of declarations makes them usable: the predicate `Huber.IsNoetherianType`, adic homomorphisms, the fact that topologically-finite-type maps are adic and preserve noetherian type, closedness of ideals, and stable sheafiness. The last of these combines the anchor's Tate case (Layer 4) with Huber's Case I and the discrete case, planned in R0a.1a.

#### `Huber.IsNoetherianType` — Huber rings of noetherian type (Huber's noetherian hypothesis)

*Node* `AdicSpacesPartII:R0/noetherian-type-huber-ring` (definition); module `TauCeti/RingTheory/Huber/NoetherianType`.

Let A be a commutative topological ring which is a Huber ring (Tau Ceti `IsHuberRing A`). A is *of noetherian type* if (i) A admits a pair of definition (A₀, I) (Tau Ceti `PairOfDefinition A`) whose ring of definition A₀ is a noetherian ring, or (ii) A is a Tate ring (`IsTateRing A`) and strongly noetherian in Tau Ceti's sense (`IsStronglyNoetherian A`: every completed restricted power-series ring A⟨X₁,…,X_k⟩, k ≥ 0, is a noetherian ring). This is the hypothesis Huber places on affinoid rings in Theorem 2.2 and Propositions 3.6–3.8 of the 1994 paper ('has a noetherian ring of definition or is a strongly noetherian Tate ring'). Conventions: the predicate concerns the topological ring only (no plus ring); completeness is not part of it, and every result that needs a complete ring assumes completeness and the Hausdorff property separately. Clause (i) does not say that A is a noetherian ring: every discrete ring is of noetherian type because its prime subring (the image of ℤ) is an open noetherian subring with ideal of definition 0. For a Tate ring clause (i) implies clause (ii) (a Tate ring with a noetherian ring of definition is strongly noetherian), so for Tate rings the predicate is exactly strong noetherianness; the converse implication fails: ℂ_p is strongly noetherian but has no noetherian ring of definition (a ring of definition A₀ ⊆ O_{ℂ_p} contains some p^N·O_{ℂ_p}, and the A₀-ideal p^N·𝔪_{ℂ_p} is not finitely generated). Lean name: `Huber.IsNoetherianType A` (a Prop-valued class).

*Hypotheses.* A is a commutative ring with a topology making it a topological ring and a Huber ring (`IsHuberRing A`).

*Proof outline.*

1. The definition is the disjunction of (i) and (ii); no choice of pair of definition is part of the data.
2. The discrete case: for discrete A the image R of ℤ → A is a subring, open because A is discrete, and (R, 0) is a pair of definition since the subspace topology on R is discrete, which is the 0-adic topology; R is a quotient of ℤ, hence noetherian.
3. Clause (i) implies clause (ii) for Tate rings: if A is Tate with noetherian ring of definition A₀, the completed rings A⟨X₁,…,X_k⟩ have the ring of definition Â₀⟨X₁,…,X_k⟩, the completion of the finitely generated A₀-algebra A₀[X], which is noetherian by R0/noetherian-adic-completion; inverting a pseudouniformiser gives A⟨X⟩ noetherian (Wedhorn Remark 6.37(3)).

*API.*

- `Huber.IsNoetherianType` (structure): The Prop-valued class: (∃ P : PairOfDefinition A, IsNoetherianRing P.ringOfDefinition) ∨ (IsTateRing A ∧ IsStronglyNoetherian A).
- `Huber.IsNoetherianType.of_pairOfDefinition` (constructor): If P : PairOfDefinition A and P.ringOfDefinition is a noetherian ring, then A is of noetherian type.
- `Huber.IsNoetherianType.of_isStronglyNoetherian` (constructor): If A is a Tate ring and IsStronglyNoetherian A, then A is of noetherian type.
- `Huber.IsNoetherianType.of_discreteTopology` (instance): Every discrete ring is of noetherian type (prime subring, ideal of definition 0).
- `Huber.IsNoetherianType.isStronglyNoetherian` (characterisation): For a Tate ring A: IsNoetherianType A ↔ IsStronglyNoetherian A (Wedhorn Remark 6.37(3) for →).
- `Huber.IsNoetherianType.isNoetherianRing_of_isTateRing` (projection): If A is a complete Hausdorff Tate ring of noetherian type, then A is a noetherian ring (Tau Ceti `isNoetherianRing_of_isStronglyNoetherian`).
- `Huber.IsNoetherianType.completion` (instance): The Hausdorff completion Â (Tau Ceti `IsHuberRing.completion`) of a ring of noetherian type is of noetherian type (clause (i) by R0/noetherian-adic-completion; clause (ii) by the anchor's Layer 4.1 statement that completion preserves strong noetherianness).
- `Huber.IsNoetherianType.of_isTopologicallyFiniteType` (functoriality): Promoted to R0/topologically-finite-type-noetherian-type: if A → B is topologically of finite type (Tau Ceti `IsTopologicallyFiniteType`), B complete Hausdorff, and A complete of noetherian type, then B is of noetherian type.
- `Huber.IsNoetherianType.isClosed_ideal` (other): Promoted to R0/noetherian-type-ideals-closed: every ideal of a complete Hausdorff ring of noetherian type is closed.
- `Huber.IsNoetherianType.isStablySheafyRing` (relation): Promoted to R0/noetherian-type-stably-sheafy: a complete Hausdorff ring of noetherian type is stably sheafy in the anchor's sense.
- `Huber.IsNoetherianType.of_ringEquiv` (other): Invariance under a ring isomorphism that is a homeomorphism.

*Unit tests.*

- `isNoetherianType_discrete_polynomial` (non-example): The discrete ring ℤ[T₁, T₂, …] (countably many variables) is of noetherian type (via its prime subring ℤ) but is not a noetherian ring; a definition 'A is a noetherian ring' fails this test.
- `isNoetherianType_padicPowerSeries` (computation): ℤ_p⟦T⟧ with the (p, T)-adic topology is of noetherian type through the pair of definition (ℤ_p⟦T⟧, (p, T)), and has no topologically nilpotent unit, so clause (ii) does not apply.
- `not_isNoetherianType_perfectoidDisc` (non-example): For a perfectoid field K, the Tate ring K⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩ is not of noetherian type: it is not a noetherian ring (the ideal generated by all T^{1/p^n} is not finitely generated), so it is not strongly noetherian, and a noetherian ring of definition A₀ would make A = A₀[1/ϖ] noetherian.
- `isNoetherianType_iff_isStronglyNoetherian_of_isTateRing` (compatibility): For a Tate ring A, `IsNoetherianType A ↔ IsStronglyNoetherian A` (Tau Ceti's predicate).
- `isNoetherianType_of_subsingleton` (degenerate): The zero ring is of noetherian type.

*Acceptance.*

- ℤ_p⟦T⟧ with the (p, T)-adic topology is of noetherian type by (i) and is not a Tate ring.
- ℚ_p⟨T⟩ is of noetherian type by (i) (ring of definition ℤ_p⟨T⟩) and by (ii).
- K⟨T^{1/p^∞}⟩ for a perfectoid field K is not of noetherian type.

*Depends on* within R0a: `Huber.isNoetherianRing_completion_of_isAdic`; anchor stages: `layer-4-sheafiness-and-tate-acyclicity`; library: `TauCeti.Huber.IsHuberRing`, `TauCeti.Huber.PairOfDefinition`, `TauCeti.Huber.IsTateRing`, `TauCeti.Huber.IsStronglyNoetherian`, `TauCeti.Huber.isNoetherianRing_of_isStronglyNoetherian`, `TauCeti.Huber.IsHuberRing.completion`.

*Sources.* Huber-GeneralizationFormalRigid-1994, §3, Proposition 3.7 (hypotheses), printed p. 535; Huber-GeneralizationFormalRigid-1994, §2, Theorem 2.2, printed p. 524; Wedhorn-AdicSpaces-2019, §6.7, Remark 6.37(3), p. 54.

#### `Huber.isNoetherianRing_completion_of_isAdic` — A noetherian ring of definition stays noetherian under completion

*Node* `AdicSpacesPartII:R0/noetherian-adic-completion` (lemma); module `TauCeti/RingTheory/Huber/NoetherianType`.

Let A be a Huber ring with a pair of definition (A₀, I) whose ring of definition A₀ is noetherian. Then the ring of
definition Â₀ of the completion Â (Tau Ceti `PairOfDefinition.completion`) is noetherian, Â₀ is I·Â₀-adically complete,
and Â₀/Iⁿ·Â₀ ≅ A₀/Iⁿ for every n. This is the Huber-ring form of EGA 0_I (7.3.1), whose ring-level statement (the adic
completion of a noetherian ring is noetherian) is F0's `AdicSpacesPartII:F0/adic-completion-noetherian`.

*Hypotheses.* A is a Huber ring with a pair of definition (A₀, I); A₀ is a noetherian ring (so I is finitely generated).

*Proof outline.*

1. The completion of A₀ for its I-adic topology is the ring of definition of Â (Tau Ceti `PairOfDefinition.completion`)
   and, as a ring, Mathlib's `AdicCompletion I A₀` (both are the inverse limit of the A₀/Iⁿ).
2. `AdicSpacesPartII:F0/adic-completion-noetherian`: the adic completion of a noetherian ring is noetherian, adically
   complete for the extended ideal, with the same quotients by powers of the ideal.

*Acceptance.*

- ℤ_p = completion of ℤ at (p) and ℤ_p⟦T⟧ = completion of ℤ_p[T] at (p, T) are noetherian.

*Depends on* `AdicSpacesPartII:F0/adic-completion-noetherian`; library: `TauCeti.Huber.PairOfDefinition.completion`,
`UniformSpace.Completion`.

*Sources.* EGA-I-1960, Chapitre 0, §7.3, (7.3.1), p. 66; Wedhorn-AdicSpaces-2019, §6.6, proof of Proposition 6.35, p. 54.

#### `Huber.IsAdicHom` — Adic homomorphisms of Huber rings

*Node* `AdicSpacesPartII:R0/adic-ring-homomorphism` (definition); module `TauCeti/RingTheory/Huber/AdicHom`.

Let A and B be Huber rings. A ring homomorphism φ : A → B is *adic* if there exist a pair of definition (A₀, I) of A and a ring of definition B₀ of B such that φ(A₀) ⊆ B₀ and the ideal φ(I)·B₀ of B₀ is an ideal of definition of B₀ (it is finitely generated, and the subspace topology of B₀ is the φ(I)B₀-adic topology); equivalently, there is a Tau Ceti pair of definition Q of B with φ(P.ringOfDefinition) ⊆ Q.ringOfDefinition and Q.idealOfDefinition equal to the ideal of Q.ringOfDefinition generated by φ(P.idealOfDefinition). Every adic homomorphism is continuous. Lean name: `Huber.IsAdicHom φ` (a Prop). Huber 1994 recalls this definition from his 1993 paper; Wedhorn records it as Definition 6.23.

*Hypotheses.* A, B are Huber rings (Tau Ceti `IsHuberRing`). φ : A →+* B is a ring homomorphism.

*Proof outline.*

1. Definition by existence of the pairs of definition; continuity: φ(Iⁿ A₀) ⊆ (φ(I)B₀)ⁿ, and the latter form a basis of neighbourhoods of 0 in B.

*API.*

- `Huber.IsAdicHom` (structure): The predicate: ∃ (P : PairOfDefinition A) (Q : PairOfDefinition B), φ(P.A₀) ⊆ Q.A₀ ∧ Q.I = Ideal.span (φ(P.I)).
- `Huber.IsAdicHom.continuous` (projection): An adic homomorphism is continuous.
- `Huber.IsAdicHom.comp` (functoriality): If φ : A → B and ψ : B → C are adic then ψ ∘ φ is adic (Wedhorn 6.26(1)).
- `Huber.IsAdicHom.of_comp` (relation): If φ is continuous, ψ is continuous and ψ ∘ φ is adic, then ψ is adic (Wedhorn 6.26(2)).
- `Huber.IsAdicHom.id` (functoriality): The identity is adic.
- `Huber.IsAdicHom.of_isTateRing` (instance): Every continuous ring homomorphism from a Tate ring to a Huber ring is adic, and its target is Tate (Wedhorn Proposition 6.25).
- `Huber.IsAdicHom.of_radical_eq` (characterisation): If (A₀, I), (B₀, J) are pairs of definition with φ(A₀) ⊆ B₀, φ(I) ⊆ J and √(φ(I)B₀) = √J, then φ is adic (J finitely generated gives Jⁿ ⊆ φ(I)B₀ ⊆ J).
- `Huber.IsAdicHom.of_discrete_iff` (characterisation): From a discrete ring: adic iff the target is discrete.
- `Huber.isAdicHom_completion_coe` (compatibility): The completion map A → Â is adic (Tau Ceti `PairOfDefinition.completion`).
- `Huber.isAdicHom_algebraMap_weightedRestrictedSubring` (example): The structure map A → A⟨X⟩_T is adic for every weight family T (Tau Ceti `PairOfDefinition.weighted`: the ideal of definition of A₀⟨X⟩_T is generated by I).
- `Huber.IsAdicHom.comp_isOpenQuotientMap` (relation): If φ is adic and π : B → C is a surjective continuous open ring homomorphism, then π ∘ φ is adic (π maps rings and ideals of definition to rings and ideals of definition).
- `Huber.IsTopologicallyFiniteType.isAdicHom` (relation): Promoted to R0/topologically-finite-type-is-adic.

*Unit tests.*

- `isAdicHom_padicInt_padic` (computation): The inclusion ℤ_p → ℚ_p is adic: A₀ = B₀ = ℤ_p, I = pℤ_p, and pℤ_p is an ideal of definition of ℤ_p.
- `not_isAdicHom_padicInt_powerSeries` (non-example): The inclusion ℤ_p → ℤ_p⟦T⟧ with the p-adic topology on ℤ_p and the (p, T)-adic topology on ℤ_p⟦T⟧ is continuous but not adic: p·ℤ_p⟦T⟧ contains no power of (p, T). A definition 'adic = continuous' fails this test.
- `isAdicHom_of_discrete_iff` (characterisation): For a discrete ring A and a Huber ring B, a ring homomorphism A → B is adic iff B is discrete (Wedhorn Example 6.24); in particular ℤ → ℤ_p is continuous and not adic.
- `isAdicHom_completion_coe` (compatibility): For a Huber ring A the completion map A → Â is adic, with the pair of definition of Â given by Tau Ceti `PairOfDefinition.completion` (Â₀ the closure of the image of A₀, Î generated by the image of I).
- `isAdicHom_id` (degenerate): The identity of a Huber ring is adic.

*Acceptance.*

- ℤ_p → ℚ_p is adic; ℤ_p → ℤ_p⟦T⟧ ((p, T)-adic) is continuous and not adic.

*Depends on* library: `TauCeti.Huber.IsHuberRing`, `TauCeti.Huber.PairOfDefinition`, `TauCeti.Huber.IsTateRing`, `TauCeti.Huber.PairOfDefinition.completion`, `TauCeti.Huber.PairOfDefinition.weighted`.

*Sources.* Huber-GeneralizationFormalRigid-1994, §3, paragraph before the Definition of adic morphisms, printed p. 532; Wedhorn-AdicSpaces-2019, §6.5, Definition 6.23, p. 51; Morel-AdicSpacesNotes, §II.3.2, Example II.3.2.2.

#### `Huber.IsTopologicallyFiniteType.isAdicHom` — Topologically-finite-type homomorphisms are adic

*Node* `AdicSpacesPartII:R0/topologically-finite-type-is-adic` (lemma); module `TauCeti/RingTheory/Huber/TopologicallyFiniteType/Adic`.

Let A be a Huber ring, B a complete Hausdorff Huber ring and φ : A → B a ring homomorphism which is topologically of finite type in Tau Ceti's sense (`IsTopologicallyFiniteType φ`: there are k, finite weights T₁,…,T_k ⊆ A forming a weight family, and an open quotient map π from the completion of A⟨X₁,…,X_k⟩_T onto B with π ∘ (structure map) = φ). Then φ is adic (R0/adic-ring-homomorphism). More precisely, for every pair of definition (A₀, I) of A, B₀ := π(closure of A₀⟨X⟩_T) is a ring of definition of B and φ(I)·B₀ is an ideal of definition of B₀.

*Hypotheses.* A is a Huber ring; B is a complete Hausdorff Huber ring. φ : A → B satisfies Tau Ceti `IsTopologicallyFiniteType φ`.

*Proof outline.*

1. The structure map A → A⟨X⟩_T is adic: Tau Ceti `PairOfDefinition.weighted` gives the pair of definition (A₀⟨X⟩_T, I⟨X⟩_T) with I⟨X⟩_T generated by I (Wedhorn Proposition 6.21(2)); passing to completions preserves adicness (Tau Ceti `PairOfDefinition.completion`, the completed ideal of definition is generated by the image of the old one).
2. An open quotient map π of Huber rings sends a ring of definition S with ideal of definition K to a ring of definition π(S) with ideal of definition π(K)π(S): π(S) is open because π is open, and the sets π(Kⁿ S) = π(K)ⁿ π(S) form a basis of neighbourhoods of 0 because π is open and continuous.
3. Compose: `Huber.IsAdicHom.comp` from R0/adic-ring-homomorphism.

*Acceptance.*

- The rational localisation A → A⟨T/s⟩ (Tau Ceti `completionLocalization`) is adic.
- A → A⟨X₁,…,X_n⟩/𝔞 is adic for every closed ideal 𝔞.

*Depends on* within R0a: `Huber.IsAdicHom`; library: `TauCeti.Huber.IsTopologicallyFiniteType`, `TauCeti.Huber.PairOfDefinition.weighted`, `TauCeti.Huber.PairOfDefinition.completion`, `IsOpenQuotientMap`.

*Sources.* Huber-GeneralizationFormalRigid-1994, §3, Lemma 3.3(ii), condition (b), printed p. 533; Wedhorn-AdicSpaces-2019, §8.5, Remark 8.49(2), p. 88.

#### `Huber.IsNoetherianType.of_isTopologicallyFiniteType` — Rings topologically of finite type over a ring of noetherian type are of noetherian type

*Node* `AdicSpacesPartII:R0/topologically-finite-type-noetherian-type` (lemma); module `TauCeti/RingTheory/Huber/TopologicallyFiniteType/NoetherianType`.

Let A be a complete Hausdorff Huber ring of noetherian type (R0/noetherian-type-huber-ring) and φ : A → B a ring homomorphism to a complete Hausdorff Huber ring B with `IsTopologicallyFiniteType φ` (Tau Ceti). Then B is of noetherian type. More precisely: (i) if A has a noetherian ring of definition A₀, then B has the noetherian ring of definition π(Â₀⟨X⟩_T) (Huber 1994 Corollary 3.4(iii), Wedhorn Proposition 6.35); (ii) if A is a strongly noetherian Tate ring, then B is a strongly noetherian Tate ring (Huber 1994 Corollary 3.4(ii), Wedhorn Remark 6.37(1)).

*Hypotheses.* A complete Hausdorff Huber ring of noetherian type. B complete Hausdorff Huber ring. φ : A → B with Tau Ceti `IsTopologicallyFiniteType φ`.

*Proof outline.*

1. (i) The presenting ring Â⟨X⟩_T has the ring of definition Â₀⟨X⟩_T, the completion of A₀[t·X_i : t ∈ T_i] (Tau Ceti `PairOfDefinition.weighted` and `PairOfDefinition.completion`). A₀[t·X_i] is a finitely generated A₀-algebra (the T_i are finite), hence noetherian (Hilbert basis theorem), and its completion is noetherian by R0/noetherian-adic-completion.
2. (i) cont.: π is an open quotient map, so π(Â₀⟨X⟩_T) is a ring of definition of B (proof of R0/topologically-finite-type-is-adic), and a quotient of a noetherian ring is noetherian.
3. (ii) B is Tate: a continuous homomorphism from a Tate ring has Tate target (Wedhorn Proposition 6.25, `Huber.IsAdicHom.of_isTateRing` in R0/adic-ring-homomorphism). Over a Tate base, topologically finite type equals strictly topologically finite type (Wedhorn Proposition 6.34), and a ring strictly topologically of finite type over a strongly noetherian ring is strongly noetherian (Tau Ceti `IsStrictlyTopologicallyFiniteType.isStronglyNoetherian`). The weighted-to-strict step is the step of the anchor's Corollary 8.35 (every Tate ring topologically of finite type over a strongly noetherian Tate ring is strongly noetherian), imported from anchor Layer 4.

*Acceptance.*

- Every rational localisation of a strongly noetherian Tate ring is strongly noetherian; every rational localisation of ℤ_p⟨T⟩ has a noetherian ring of definition.
- Huber 1994 Corollary 3.4(ii),(iii) in full.

*Depends on* within R0a: `Huber.IsNoetherianType`, `Huber.isNoetherianRing_completion_of_isAdic`, `Huber.IsAdicHom`, `Huber.IsTopologicallyFiniteType.isAdicHom`; anchor stages: `layer-4-sheafiness-and-tate-acyclicity`; library: `TauCeti.Huber.IsTopologicallyFiniteType`, `TauCeti.Huber.IsStrictlyTopologicallyFiniteType.isStronglyNoetherian`, `TauCeti.Huber.PairOfDefinition.weighted`, `TauCeti.Huber.PairOfDefinition.completion`.

*Sources.* Huber-GeneralizationFormalRigid-1994, §3, Corollary 3.4(iii), printed p. 534; Wedhorn-AdicSpaces-2019, §6.7, Remark 6.37(1), p. 54; Wedhorn-AdicSpaces-2019, §6.6, Proposition 6.34, p. 54.

#### `Huber.IsNoetherianType.isClosed_ideal` — Ideals of complete rings of noetherian type are closed

*Node* `AdicSpacesPartII:R0/noetherian-type-ideals-closed` (lemma); module `TauCeti/RingTheory/Huber/NoetherianType`.

Let A be a complete Hausdorff Huber ring of noetherian type. Then every ideal J ⊆ A is closed, and A/J with the quotient topology is a complete Hausdorff Huber ring of noetherian type; the quotient pair (A/J, integral closure of the image of A⁺) (Tau Ceti `Pair.quotient`) is a complete Huber pair and the quotient map is a quotient mapping in Huber's sense.

*Hypotheses.* A complete Hausdorff Huber ring of noetherian type. J an ideal of A; A⁺ a ring of integral elements for the quotient-pair statement.

*Proof outline.*

1. Tate case: A is a noetherian ring (R0/noetherian-type-huber-ring), complete and first countable; Tau Ceti `isClosed_of_isNoetherian` (every submodule of a noetherian complete metrisable module over a complete Tate ring is closed) applied to A as a module over itself.
2. Noetherian ring of definition case: let (A₀, I) be a pair of definition with A₀ noetherian; A₀ is I-adically complete because A is complete and A₀ is open (closed); J ∩ A₀ is an ideal of A₀ and A₀/(J ∩ A₀) is I-adically Hausdorff by Krull's intersection theorem (Mathlib `IsHausdorff.of_le_jacobson`, with I ⊆ Jac(A₀) by `IsAdicComplete.le_jacobson_bot`), so J ∩ A₀ = ⋂ₙ (J ∩ A₀ + Iⁿ) is closed in A₀; since A₀ is open, J is closed in A (an additive subgroup whose intersection with an open subgroup is closed is closed).
3. A/J is Hausdorff because J is closed, complete because a quotient of a complete metrisable group by a closed subgroup is complete, and Huber with pair of definition the image of (A₀, I); A → A/J is an open quotient map, hence topologically of finite type, so A/J is of noetherian type (R0/topologically-finite-type-noetherian-type).
4. The plus ring of the quotient pair is Tau Ceti's `Pair.quotient` construction.

*Acceptance.*

- In ℚ_p⟨T⟩ every ideal, e.g. (T), is closed; in ℤ_p⟦T⟧ every ideal is closed.
- Non-example outside the hypothesis: in the Tate ring C(ℤ_p, ℚ_p) of continuous functions with the supremum norm, the ideal of functions vanishing on a neighbourhood of 0 is not closed (its closure is the ideal of functions vanishing at 0, which contains x ↦ x).

*Depends on* within R0a: `Huber.IsNoetherianType`, `Huber.IsNoetherianType.of_isTopologicallyFiniteType`; library: `TauCeti.Huber.isClosed_of_isNoetherian`, `IsHausdorff.of_le_jacobson`, `IsAdicComplete.le_jacobson_bot`, `TauCeti.Huber.Pair.quotient`.

*Sources.* Huber-GeneralizationFormalRigid-1994, §2, Lemma 2.3(ii), printed p. 525; EGA-I-1960, Chapitre 0, §7.3, Corollaire (7.3.6), p. 67.

### R0a.1a Sheafiness of rings of noetherian type (Huber 1994 Theorem 2.2)

The anchor's Layer 4 proves sheafiness for strongly noetherian Tate rings only. Huber's hypothesis also allows a noetherian ring of definition without a topologically nilpotent unit (ℤ_p⟨T⟩, ℤ_p⟦T⟧, discrete rings); these rings are the affinoid pieces of the adic spaces t(Spf A) attached to noetherian formal schemes and of the non-analytic parts of fibre products. Huber's proof (1994, §2, Case I) is planned here: finite modules over such rings carry natural topologies in which linear maps are strict (Lemma 2.3); the algebraic Čech complex of a standard rational covering is compared, through the blow-up scheme Y = Proj(⊕ Jⁿ) of the C-submodule J generated by the covering functions ((1.1)–(1.2)), with the Čech complexes of the coherent sheaves Iⁱ𝒢 on the proper C-scheme Y, whose cohomology satisfies Artin–Rees (EGA III 3.3.2); this makes the Čech differentials strict ((1.3.1), (1.3)), and completion then gives exact strict Čech complexes of M ⊗ 𝒪 on standard rational coverings, which refine every covering ((1.5), Lemma 2.6). The discrete case has a separate elementary proof (Wedhorn 8.28(c)). The module-level Čech statement is planned here once; R3 imports it for M̃ and adds sheaf-cohomology vanishing.

#### `TauCeti.cechComplexLocalization_exact` — Exactness of the extended Čech complex of localisations

*Node* `AdicSpacesPartII:R0/localization-cech-complex-exact` (lemma); module `TauCeti/Algebra/Module/CechLocalization`.

Let R be a commutative ring, f₁, …, fₙ ∈ R elements generating the unit ideal and M an R-module. The extended alternating Čech complex 0 → M → ∏_{i₀} M_{f_{i₀}} → ∏_{i₀<i₁} M_{f_{i₀}f_{i₁}} → ⋯ is exact.

*Hypotheses.* f₁, …, fₙ generate the unit ideal of R

*Proof outline.*

1. Exactness can be checked after localising at every prime 𝔭 (localisation is exact and a module vanishing at all primes is zero).
2. Choose i_fix with f_{i_fix} ∉ 𝔭; the operator h(s)_{i₀…i_p} = s_{i_fix i₀…i_p} is a contracting homotopy of the localised complex (Stacks Tag 01X9).

*Acceptance.*

- For R = K[T], f₁ = T, f₂ = 1 − T and M = R the complex 0 → R → R_T × R_{1−T} → R_{T(1−T)} → 0 is exact.

*Depends on* `mathlib:Module.Flat`.

*Sources.* Stacks-Project, Tag 01X9, Lemma 30.2.1; Huber-GeneralizationFormalRigid-1994, §2, proof of (1.3), printed p. 527.

#### `TauCeti.StrictComplex.completion_exact` — Completion of a strict exact complex is strict exact

*Node* `AdicSpacesPartII:R0/strict-complex-completion-exact` (lemma); module `TauCeti/Topology/Algebra/Group/StrictComplex`.

Let C⁰ → C¹ → ⋯ be a complex of Hausdorff abelian topological groups whose topologies are defined by a countable fundamental system of open subgroups, with continuous differentials. If the complex is exact and every differential is strict (continuous and open onto its image with the subspace topology), then the completed complex Ĉ⁰ → Ĉ¹ → ⋯ is exact and its differentials are strict.

*Hypotheses.* each Cⁱ is linearly topologised with a countable basis of open subgroups exactness and strictness of every differential

*Proof outline.*

1. Uniform structures: each Cⁱ is a Hausdorff abelian group with a countable basis (Uⁱ_k) of open subgroups, so it is metrisable and its completion Ĉⁱ (Mathlib UniformSpace.Completion) has the closures of the Uⁱ_k as a basis of open subgroups; every continuous homomorphism extends uniquely to a continuous homomorphism of completions.
2. Strict maps complete to strict maps: for a strict d : C → D with image E ⊆ D, openness gives for every k an l with d(U_l) ⊇ E ∩ V_k. The closure Ē of E in D̂ is the completion of E; given y ∈ Ē ∩ V̄_k choose a sequence e_j ∈ E converging to y with e_{j+1} − e_j ∈ V_{k_j} for a rapidly increasing sequence k_j, lift each difference to U_{l_j} and sum the lifts: the series converges in Ĉ (the U_{l_j} shrink) to x ∈ Ū_l with d̂(x) = y. Hence d̂(Ĉ) = Ē and d̂ : Ĉ → Ē is open.
3. Exactness at Ĉⁱ: im(d̂ⁱ⁻¹) is the closure of im(dⁱ⁻¹) by the previous step; ker(d̂ⁱ) is the closure of ker(dⁱ), because for x ∈ ker(d̂ⁱ) approximated by x_j ∈ Cⁱ the elements dⁱ(x_j) → 0 lift, by strictness of dⁱ, to elements z_j → 0 with dⁱ(z_j) = dⁱ(x_j), and x_j − z_j ∈ ker(dⁱ) converges to x. Since ker(dⁱ) = im(dⁱ⁻¹), the two closures agree.

*Acceptance.*

- The strict exact complex 0 → B → B_f × B_g → B_{fg} → 0 of localisations with adic topologies completes to the exact complex of completed localisations used in Huber (1.3).

*Depends on* `mathlib:UniformSpace.Completion`.

*Sources.* Huber-GeneralizationFormalRigid-1994, §2, proof of (1.3), printed p. 527.

#### `Huber.PairOfDefinition.isStrictMap_of_isNoetherianRing` — Linear maps of finite modules over a Huber ring with a noetherian ring of definition are strict (Huber Lemma 2.3(i))

*Node* `AdicSpacesPartII:R0/noetherian-rod-module-topology-strict` (lemma); module `TauCeti/RingTheory/Huber/NoetherianModuleTopology`.

Let A be a Huber ring with a pair of definition (A₀, I) (Tau Ceti `PairOfDefinition A`) such that A₀ is a noetherian ring. For a finitely generated A-module M, the natural topology of M is the module topology (Mathlib `IsModuleTopology A M`: the finest topology making M a topological A-module); for every finitely generated A₀-submodule M₀ ⊆ M generating M over A, the subgroups IⁿM₀ (n ≥ 0) form a fundamental system of open neighbourhoods of 0. Then for finitely generated A-modules M and N with their natural topologies, every A-linear map u : M → N is strict: it is continuous, and u : M → u(M) is open for the subspace topology on u(M) ⊆ N.

*Hypotheses.* A Huber ring with a pair of definition (A₀, I), A₀ noetherian (completeness is not assumed). M, N finitely generated A-modules with their natural (module) topologies.

*Proof outline.*

1. Natural topology: if m₁, …, m_s generate M₀ over A₀ and M over A, then (x₁, …, x_s) ↦ ∑ x_j m_j is a continuous open surjection Aˢ → M for the module topology, and it maps (IⁿA₀)ˢ onto IⁿM₀; hence the IⁿM₀ form a basis of open neighbourhoods of 0 (Huber 1994, before Lemma 2.3). A-linear maps between modules with module topologies are continuous (Mathlib IsModuleTopology.continuous_of_linearMap).
2. Choose a finitely generated A₀-submodule N₀ ⊆ N generating N with u(M₀) ⊆ N₀ (add the finitely many u(m_j) to generators of N). Q := u(M) ∩ N₀ is an A₀-submodule of the finite A₀-module N₀, hence finitely generated (A₀ noetherian).
3. Artin–Rees (Mathlib Ideal.exists_pow_inf_eq_pow_smul; EGA 0_I 7.3.2): there is c with Q ∩ IⁿN₀ = Iⁿ⁻ᶜ(Q ∩ IᶜN₀) ⊆ Iⁿ⁻ᶜQ for n ≥ c, so the subspace topology on Q ⊆ N₀ is its I-adic topology.
4. Each of the finitely many generators q of Q lies in u(M) = A·u(M₀); for a ∈ A there is k with Iᵏa ⊆ A₀ (a·x → 0 as x → 0 and A₀ is open), so IᵏQ ⊆ A₀·u(M₀) = u(M₀) for some k.
5. Hence u(IⁿM₀) = Iⁿu(M₀) ⊇ Iⁿ⁺ᵏQ ⊇ u(M) ∩ Iⁿ⁺ᵏ⁺ᶜN₀, which is a neighbourhood of 0 in u(M) for the subspace topology: u is open onto its image.

*Acceptance.*

- For A = ℤ_p⟨T⟩ (ring of definition itself, ideal (p)) the inclusion of the ideal (T) into A is strict: the subspace topology on (T) is the p-adic topology of (T) ≅ A.
- Outside the hypothesis the statement fails: for the Tate ring A = C(ℤ_p, ℚ_p) (supremum norm, ring of definition the functions with values in ℤ_p, not noetherian), multiplication by the function x ↦ x is an A-linear map A → A with non-closed image, hence not strict (a strict map of complete metrisable groups has complete, hence closed, image).

*Depends on* `tauceti:TauCeti.Huber.PairOfDefinition`, `mathlib:IsModuleTopology`, `mathlib:IsModuleTopology.continuous_of_linearMap`, `mathlib:Ideal.exists_pow_inf_eq_pow_smul`.

*Sources.* Huber-GeneralizationFormalRigid-1994, §2, Lemma 2.3, printed p. 525; Huber-GeneralizationFormalRigid-1994, §2, proof of Lemma 2.3, printed p. 525; Huber-GeneralizationFormalRigid-1994, §2, before Lemma 2.3, printed p. 524; EGA-I-1960, Chapitre 0, §7.3, Théorème (7.3.2), p. 66.

#### `Huber.PairOfDefinition.completeSpace_isClosed_of_isNoetherianRing` — Finite modules over a complete Huber ring with a noetherian ring of definition are complete, with closed submodules (Huber Lemma 2.3(ii))

*Node* `AdicSpacesPartII:R0/noetherian-rod-module-complete` (lemma); module `TauCeti/RingTheory/Huber/NoetherianModuleTopology`.

Let A be a complete Hausdorff Huber ring with a pair of definition (A₀, I) such that A₀ is noetherian, and let M be a finitely generated A-module with its natural topology (R0/noetherian-rod-module-topology-strict). Then M is complete and Hausdorff, and every A-submodule of M is closed in M. For every finitely generated A₀-submodule M₀ ⊆ M generating M, M₀ is open in M and I-adically complete and separated.

*Hypotheses.* A complete Hausdorff Huber ring with a pair of definition (A₀, I), A₀ noetherian. M a finitely generated A-module with its natural topology.

*Proof outline.*

1. A₀ is open, hence closed, in the complete ring A, so A₀ is complete for its I-adic topology; being noetherian with I ⊆ Jac(A₀) (Mathlib IsAdicComplete.le_jacobson_bot), every finite A₀-module M₀ is I-adically Hausdorff (Mathlib IsHausdorff.of_le_jacobson) and the canonical map Â₀ ⊗ M₀ → M̂₀ is bijective (Mathlib AdicCompletion.ofTensorProduct_bijective_of_finite_of_isNoetherian), so M₀ = M̂₀ is I-adically complete (EGA 0_I 7.3.6).
2. M₀ is open in M with the I-adic topology as subspace topology (R0/noetherian-rod-module-topology-strict); an abelian topological group with a complete Hausdorff open subgroup is complete and Hausdorff, so M is.
3. For a submodule M' ⊆ M, M' ∩ M₀ is an A₀-submodule of M₀, finite (A₀ noetherian), hence I-adically complete by the first step; by Artin–Rees (Mathlib Ideal.exists_pow_inf_eq_pow_smul) its I-adic topology is the subspace topology, so M' ∩ M₀ is a complete subgroup of the Hausdorff group M₀, hence closed in M₀. A subgroup whose intersection with an open subgroup is closed is closed, so M' is closed in M.

*Acceptance.*

- For A = ℤ_p⟦T⟧ ((p, T)-adic) every ideal is closed and A/(pT) is complete.
- M = ℤ_p⟨T⟩/(T − p) ≅ ℤ_p over A = ℤ_p⟨T⟩ is complete, and its submodule pM is closed.

*Depends on* `AdicSpacesPartII:R0/noetherian-rod-module-topology-strict`, `mathlib:IsAdicComplete.le_jacobson_bot`, `mathlib:IsHausdorff.of_le_jacobson`, `mathlib:AdicCompletion.ofTensorProduct_bijective_of_finite_of_isNoetherian`, `mathlib:Ideal.exists_pow_inf_eq_pow_smul`.

*Sources.* Huber-GeneralizationFormalRigid-1994, §2, Lemma 2.3, printed p. 525; Huber-GeneralizationFormalRigid-1994, §2, proof of Lemma 2.3, printed p. 525; EGA-I-1960, Chapitre 0, §7.3, Corollaire (7.3.6), p. 67.

#### `Huber.PairOfDefinition.completionTensorEquiv` — Completion of a finite module over a Huber ring with a noetherian ring of definition is base change to Â (Huber Lemma 2.3(iii))

*Node* `AdicSpacesPartII:R0/noetherian-rod-module-completion-tensor` (lemma); module `TauCeti/RingTheory/Huber/NoetherianModuleTopology`.

Let A be a Huber ring with a pair of definition (A₀, I) such that A₀ is noetherian, Â its completion (Tau Ceti `IsHuberRing.completion`), and M a finitely generated A-module with its natural topology. Then the canonical map M ⊗_A Â → M̂ to the Hausdorff completion of M is an isomorphism of topological Â-modules, where M ⊗_A Â carries its natural Â-module topology. In particular M ⊗_A Â is complete and Hausdorff.

*Hypotheses.* A Huber ring with a pair of definition (A₀, I), A₀ noetherian. M a finitely generated A-module.

*Proof outline.*

1. Â has the pair of definition (Â₀, I·Â₀) with Â₀ noetherian (R0/noetherian-adic-completion), so R0/noetherian-rod-module-topology-strict and R0/noetherian-rod-module-complete apply over Â.
2. Choose a surjection π : Aⁿ → M with kernel K (an A-submodule, not necessarily finitely generated). The natural topology of M is the quotient topology of Aⁿ (module topology), so π is open, and K ⊆ Aⁿ carries the subspace topology: 0 → K → Aⁿ → M → 0 is exact with strict maps, and its completion 0 → K̂ → Âⁿ → M̂ → 0 is exact, with K̂ the closure of K in Âⁿ (R0/strict-complex-completion-exact).
3. By right exactness of ⊗_A Â, M ⊗_A Â = Âⁿ / Â·K. The Â-submodule Â·K ⊆ Âⁿ is closed (R0/noetherian-rod-module-complete over the complete ring Â) and contains K, so Â·K ⊇ K̂; conversely K̂ is an Â-submodule (closure of an A-submodule, by continuity of the Â-action) containing K, so Â·K ⊆ K̂. Hence M ⊗_A Â = Âⁿ/K̂ ≅ M̂ as Â-modules, compatibly with the canonical maps.
4. Topologies: both sides are finite Â-modules; M̂ is complete Hausdorff with the natural Â-topology (R0/noetherian-rod-module-complete) and the bijection is Â-linear, hence a homeomorphism for the natural topologies (R0/noetherian-rod-module-topology-strict over Â).

*Acceptance.*

- For A = ℤ_p[T] with the p-adic topology and M = A/(T), M ⊗_A Â = ℤ_p⟨T⟩/(T) = ℤ_p = M̂.
- For the uncompleted rational localisation B(F/f) (ring B_f with ring of definition C[F/f]) and a finite B-module P, (P ⊗_B B_f) ⊗ B⟨F/f⟩ is the completion of P_f; this identifies Huber's completed complex (**)^ with (*).

*Depends on* `AdicSpacesPartII:R0/noetherian-rod-module-topology-strict`, `AdicSpacesPartII:R0/noetherian-rod-module-complete`, `AdicSpacesPartII:R0/strict-complex-completion-exact`, `AdicSpacesPartII:R0/noetherian-adic-completion`, `tauceti:TauCeti.Huber.IsHuberRing.completion`, `mathlib:IsModuleTopology`.

*Sources.* Huber-GeneralizationFormalRigid-1994, §2, Lemma 2.3, printed p. 525; Huber-GeneralizationFormalRigid-1994, §2, proof of Lemma 2.3, printed p. 525.

#### `Huber.bijective_localizationAway_of_isOpen` — Spec of a Huber ring and of an open subring agree away from the open primes (Huber 1993 Lemma 3.7)

*Node* `AdicSpacesPartII:R0/open-subring-spec-isomorphism` (lemma); module `TauCeti/RingTheory/Huber/OpenSubringSpec`.

Let A be a Huber ring and B ⊆ A an open subring. Let T ⊆ Spec B be the set of open prime ideals of B (a closed subset) and f : Spec A → Spec B the morphism induced by the inclusion. Then f⁻¹(T) is the set of open prime ideals of A, and f restricts to an isomorphism of schemes Spec A ∖ f⁻¹(T) → Spec B ∖ T. Concretely, for every topologically nilpotent s ∈ B the map of localisations B_s → A_s is bijective, and the open sets D(s) ⊆ Spec B for such s cover Spec B ∖ T. For B = A₀ a ring of definition with ideal of definition I this reads Spec A ∖ V(I·A) ≅ Spec A₀ ∖ V(I).

*Hypotheses.* A Huber ring; B ⊆ A an open subring.

*Proof outline.*

1. For s ∈ B topologically nilpotent and a ∈ A, sⁿa → 0, so sⁿa ∈ B for n large because B is open; hence every a/sᵐ ∈ A_s equals sⁿa/sⁿ⁺ᵐ with sⁿa ∈ B, and B_s → A_s is surjective. It is injective because localisation is exact and B → A is injective (Mathlib IsLocalization.Away).
2. A prime 𝔭 of B is open iff it contains every topologically nilpotent element of B: if 𝔭 is open, sⁿ ∈ 𝔭 for topologically nilpotent s; conversely B ∩ A°° is open (A°° is open in the Huber ring A), so 𝔭 ⊇ B ∩ A°° is open (for B = A₀ this reads I ⊆ 𝔭). So every 𝔭 ∉ T misses some topologically nilpotent s ∈ B, i.e. the D(s) cover Spec B ∖ T, and their preimages D(s) ⊆ Spec A cover Spec A ∖ f⁻¹(T).
3. A prime 𝔮 of A is open iff 𝔮 ∩ B is open in B (B is open in A), so f⁻¹(T) is the set of open primes of A.
4. The isomorphisms Spec A_s ≅ Spec B_s are compatible on overlaps D(ss'), so they glue to the isomorphism Spec A ∖ f⁻¹(T) ≅ Spec B ∖ T.

*Acceptance.*

- For A = ℚ_p⟨T⟩ and B = A₀ = ℤ_p⟨T⟩: T = V(p), f⁻¹(T) = ∅ and Spec ℚ_p⟨T⟩ ≅ Spec ℤ_p⟨T⟩ ∖ V(p), i.e. A = A₀[1/p].
- For a discrete ring A and B its prime subring every prime is open and both complements are empty.

*Depends on* `tauceti:TauCeti.Huber.IsHuberRing`, `tauceti:TauCeti.Huber.PairOfDefinition`, `mathlib:IsLocalization.Away`, `mathlib:AlgebraicGeometry.Spec`.

*Sources.* Huber-ContinuousValuations-1993, §3, Lemma 3.7, printed p. 469; Huber-ContinuousValuations-1993, §3, proof of Lemma 3.7, printed p. 469; Huber-GeneralizationFormalRigid-1994, §2, proof of (1.3.1)(i), printed p. 528.

#### `AlgebraicGeometry.submoduleBlowup` — The blow-up scheme Proj(⊕ Jⁿ) of a finitely generated submodule (Huber 1994 (1.1)–(1.2))

*Node* `AdicSpacesPartII:R0/submodule-blow-up` (construction); module `TauCeti/AlgebraicGeometry/ProjectiveSpectrum/SubmoduleBlowup`.

Let φ : C → B be a ring homomorphism, F = {f₀, …, fₙ} ⊆ B a finite subset generating the unit ideal of B, and J ⊆ B the C-submodule generated by F. Let R(J) := ⊕_{n≥0} Jⁿ·Tⁿ ⊆ B[T] (J⁰ := φ(C); for n ≥ 1, Jⁿ is the additive subgroup generated by the products j₁⋯jₙ, j_i ∈ J), an ℕ-graded ring (Mathlib `GradedAlgebra`) generated over R(J)₀ = φ(C) by the degree-one elements f·T, f ∈ F. Put Y := Proj R(J) with g : Y → Spec C the composite of Mathlib's `Proj.toSpecZero` and Spec(C → φ(C)). The evaluation R(J) → B, T ↦ 1, maps the irrelevant ideal onto an ideal containing F, hence onto B, and so defines s : X := Spec B → Y (Mathlib `Proj.fromOfGlobalSections`) with g ∘ s = Spec φ; this is Huber's diagram (1.1) in the case I := J·B = B, where X = Proj(⊕ Iⁿ) = Spec B. Properties (Huber (1.2)(i),(ii)): (a) the opens D₊(f·T), f ∈ F, cover Y and s⁻¹(D₊(f·T)) = D(f), so s is affine; (b) for a nonempty S ⊆ F with product t = ∏_{f∈S} f, the open U = D₊(t·T^{|S|}) is affine with O_Y(U) = C[f/f' : f ∈ F, f' ∈ S] ⊆ B_t (the φ(C)-subalgebra of the localisation B_t generated by these fractions) and O_X(s⁻¹U) = B_t; (c) g is projective, hence proper and separated, and Y is noetherian when C is. Lean name: `AlgebraicGeometry.submoduleBlowup φ F`.

*Hypotheses.* C, B commutative rings, φ : C → B a ring homomorphism. F ⊆ B finite with F·B = B; J the C-submodule generated by F.

*Proof outline.*

1. R(J) is a graded subring of B[T]; since J is generated by F as a C-module, Jⁿ is generated by the monomials of degree n in F, so R(J) is generated in degree one by F·T and is of finite type over φ(C) (Mathlib GradedAlgebra, Submodule powers).
2. The irrelevant ideal is generated by F·T, so the D₊(f·T) cover Y (Mathlib Proj.iSup_basicOpen_eq_top). Its image under T ↦ 1 contains F, which generates B, so Mathlib Proj.fromOfGlobalSections gives s, with s⁻¹(D₊(r)) = D(r(1)) for homogeneous r of positive degree (Proj.fromOfGlobalSections_preimage_basicOpen) and g ∘ s = Spec φ (Proj.fromOfGlobalSections_toSpecZero).
3. (b): D₊(t·T^{|S|}) ≅ Spec of the degree-zero part of R(J)_{tT^{|S|}} (Mathlib Proj.basicOpenIsoSpec, HomogeneousLocalization.Away). Its elements are a·T^{k|S|}/(t·T^{|S|})ᵏ with a ∈ J^{k|S|}; writing a as a sum of products of k|S| elements of F and tᵏ as a product of k|S| elements of S shows that the map to B_t, a·T^{k|S|}/(tT^{|S|})ᵏ ↦ a/tᵏ, has image C[f/f']. It is injective: if a/tᵏ = 0 in B_t then tᴺa = 0 in B, so (tT^{|S|})ᴺ·aT^{k|S|} = 0 in R(J) ⊆ B[T].
4. (c): R(J) is of finite type over φ(C), so Proj.toSpecZero is proper (Mathlib: separated by Proj.isSeparated, universally closed by Proj.valuativeCriterion_existence, the IsProper instance for finite type graded algebras); Spec φ(C) → Spec C is a closed immersion, hence proper.

*Acceptance.*

- For C = ℤ_p⟨T⟩ ⊆ B = ℚ_p⟨T⟩ and F = {p, T} (p is a unit of B), J = (p, T) is an ideal of C, R(J) is the Rees algebra of (p, T) and Y is the blow-up of Spec ℤ_p⟨T⟩ in (p, T), with the two charts Spec ℤ_p⟨T⟩[T/p] and Spec ℤ_p⟨T⟩[p/T]; s maps Spec ℚ_p⟨T⟩ into the complement of the exceptional divisor.
- Huber's construction is recovered: the charts C[F/f] are the rings of definition of the rational localisations B(F/f) used in (1.3.1)(ii).

*API.*

- `AlgebraicGeometry.submoduleBlowup` (constructor): The scheme Y = Proj R(J) for φ : C → B and a finite F ⊆ B with F·B = B.
- `AlgebraicGeometry.submoduleBlowup.gradedRing` (data): The graded ring R(J) = ⊕ Jⁿ·Tⁿ ⊆ B[T] with its `GradedAlgebra` structure, generated in degree one by F·T.
- `AlgebraicGeometry.submoduleBlowup.toSpec` (projection): g : Y → Spec C (Proj.toSpecZero followed by Spec(C → φ(C))).
- `AlgebraicGeometry.submoduleBlowup.fromSpec` (projection): s : Spec B → Y, from Proj.fromOfGlobalSections for the evaluation T ↦ 1.
- `AlgebraicGeometry.submoduleBlowup.fromSpec_toSpec` (compatibility): s ≫ g = Spec φ.
- `AlgebraicGeometry.submoduleBlowup.fromSpec_preimage_basicOpen` (characterisation): s⁻¹(D₊(f·T)) = D(f) for f ∈ F.
- `AlgebraicGeometry.submoduleBlowup.iSup_basicOpen_eq_top` (relation): The D₊(f·T), f ∈ F, cover Y.
- `AlgebraicGeometry.submoduleBlowup.isAffineHom_fromSpec` (instance): s is an affine morphism (Huber (1.2)(i)).
- `AlgebraicGeometry.submoduleBlowup.basicOpenIsoSpec` (characterisation): For nonempty S ⊆ F with product t, D₊(t·T^{|S|}) ≅ Spec C[f/f' : f ∈ F, f' ∈ S], the subring of B_t (Huber (1.2)(ii)).
- `AlgebraicGeometry.submoduleBlowup.isProper_toSpec` (instance): g is proper (indeed projective); Y is noetherian when C is.
- `AlgebraicGeometry.submoduleBlowup.gradedRing_eq_reesAlgebra` (compatibility): For B = C, φ = id and an ideal 𝔞 = span F, R(J) is Mathlib's `reesAlgebra 𝔞`.
- `AlgebraicGeometry.submoduleBlowup.isIso_toSpec_restrict` (other): Promoted to R0/submodule-blow-up-isomorphism-away: g is an isomorphism over Spec C ∖ V(H) under Huber's hypothesis (1.2)(iii).

*Unit tests.*

- `submoduleBlowup_test_unit` (degenerate): For F = {1} (so J = φ(C)), R(J) = φ(C)[T], Y ≅ Spec φ(C) and s = Spec(φ : C → B) corestricted; g is the closed immersion Spec φ(C) → Spec C.
- `submoduleBlowup_test_padicLaurent` (computation): For C = ℤ_p⟨T⟩ ⊆ B = ℚ_p⟨T⟩ and F = {p, T}, O_Y(D₊(pT')) = ℤ_p⟨T⟩[T/p] and O_Y(D₊(TT')) = ℤ_p⟨T⟩[p/T] inside ℚ_p⟨T⟩ and ℚ_p⟨T⟩_T respectively (T' the grading variable).
- `submoduleBlowup_reesAlgebra_compat` (compatibility): If B = C, φ = id and F generates an ideal 𝔞 of C (not necessarily the unit ideal), R(J) is Mathlib's `reesAlgebra 𝔞` as a graded subalgebra of C[T].
- `submoduleBlowup_fromSpec_preimage` (characterisation): For every f ∈ F, s⁻¹(D₊(f·T)) = D(f) ⊆ Spec B; in particular s⁻¹ of the covering {D₊(f_i·T)} is the covering {D(f_i)} of Spec B.
- `submoduleBlowup_test_not_unit_ideal` (non-example): For C = B = ℤ_p⟨T⟩ and F = {p, T}, F·B ≠ B and there is no morphism s : Spec B → Y with s⁻¹(D₊(f·T)) = D(f) for f ∈ F: the prime (p, T) of B lies in no D(f), f ∈ F.

*Depends on* `mathlib:GradedAlgebra`, `mathlib:AlgebraicGeometry.Proj.toSpecZero`, `mathlib:AlgebraicGeometry.Proj.fromOfGlobalSections`, `mathlib:AlgebraicGeometry.Proj.fromOfGlobalSections_preimage_basicOpen`, `mathlib:AlgebraicGeometry.Proj.fromOfGlobalSections_toSpecZero`, `mathlib:AlgebraicGeometry.Proj.iSup_basicOpen_eq_top`, `mathlib:AlgebraicGeometry.Proj.basicOpenIsoSpec`, `mathlib:HomogeneousLocalization.Away`, `mathlib:AlgebraicGeometry.Proj.isSeparated`, `mathlib:AlgebraicGeometry.Proj.valuativeCriterion_existence`, `mathlib:AlgebraicGeometry.IsAffineHom`, `mathlib:AlgebraicGeometry.IsProper`, `mathlib:reesAlgebra`.

*Sources.* Huber-GeneralizationFormalRigid-1994, §2, proof of Theorem 2.5, Case I, (1.1), printed p. 526; Huber-GeneralizationFormalRigid-1994, §2, (1.2)(i), printed p. 526; Huber-GeneralizationFormalRigid-1994, §2, (1.2)(ii), printed p. 526.

#### `AlgebraicGeometry.submoduleBlowup.isIso_toSpec_restrict` — The submodule blow-up is an isomorphism away from the centre (Huber 1994 (1.2)(iii))

*Node* `AdicSpacesPartII:R0/submodule-blow-up-isomorphism-away` (lemma); module `TauCeti/AlgebraicGeometry/ProjectiveSpectrum/SubmoduleBlowup`.

In the situation of R0/submodule-blow-up (φ : C → B, F ⊆ B finite with F·B = B, J = ∑_{f∈F} C·f, Y = Proj R(J), g : Y → Spec C), let H ⊆ C be an ideal such that Spec φ restricts to an isomorphism Spec B ∖ V(H·B) → Spec C ∖ V(H). Then g restricts to an isomorphism g⁻¹(Spec C ∖ V(H)) → Spec C ∖ V(H). In particular, if B is a Huber ring, C ⊆ B a ring of definition with ideal of definition I and φ the inclusion, then g is an isomorphism over Spec C ∖ V(I).

*Hypotheses.* φ, F, J, Y, g as in R0/submodule-blow-up (F·B = B). H ⊆ C an ideal with Spec B ∖ V(H·B) ≅ Spec C ∖ V(H) via Spec φ.

*Proof outline.*

1. Let h ∈ H. Localisation is exact, so R(J) ⊗_C C_h = ⊕ (J_h)ⁿTⁿ ⊆ B_h[T] with J_h the C_h-submodule of B_h generated by F, and g⁻¹(D(h)) = Proj R(J_h) (Mathlib Proj.basicOpenIsoSpec on the charts D₊(f·T), whose rings C[F/f] localise to C_h[F/f]).
2. By hypothesis C_h → B_h is an isomorphism, so J_h is an ideal of C_h ≅ B_h containing F, hence J_h = C_h (F generates the unit ideal), and R(J_h) = C_h[T]; each chart C_h[F/f] equals (C_h)_f because 1/f = ∑ c_i f_i/f for a relation 1 = ∑ c_i f_i.
3. The charts D₊(f·T) ∩ g⁻¹(D(h)) ≅ D(f) ⊆ Spec C_h cover g⁻¹(D(h)) and map isomorphically onto the cover {D(f)} of D(h) (F generates the unit ideal), compatibly on overlaps; so g⁻¹(D(h)) → D(h) is an isomorphism, and these glue over h ∈ H.
4. For a ring of definition C ⊆ B with ideal of definition I, Spec B ∖ V(I·B) ≅ Spec C ∖ V(I) by R0/open-subring-spec-isomorphism, so H = I satisfies the hypothesis.

*Acceptance.*

- For C = ℤ_p⟨T⟩ ⊆ B = ℚ_p⟨T⟩, F = {p, T} and H = I = (p): over Spec ℤ_p⟨T⟩[1/p] = Spec ℚ_p⟨T⟩ the blow-up of (p, T) is an isomorphism, since (p, T) becomes the unit ideal after inverting p.

*Depends on* `AdicSpacesPartII:R0/submodule-blow-up`, `AdicSpacesPartII:R0/open-subring-spec-isomorphism`, `mathlib:AlgebraicGeometry.Proj.basicOpenIsoSpec`, `mathlib:IsLocalization.Away`.

*Sources.* Huber-GeneralizationFormalRigid-1994, §2, (1.2)(iii), printed p. 526; Huber-GeneralizationFormalRigid-1994, §2, proof of (1.3.1)(i), printed p. 528.

#### `Huber.NoetherianCech.ker_le_range` — Deep Čech cocycles are coboundaries from a fixed level (Huber 1994 (1.3.1)(i))

*Node* `AdicSpacesPartII:R0/blow-up-cech-artin-rees` (lemma); module `TauCeti/AlgebraicGeometry/AdicSpace/Sheafy/NoetherianCech`.

Let B be a Huber ring with a pair of definition (C, I) such that C is noetherian, let F = {f₀, …, fₙ} ⊆ B generate the unit ideal, J = ∑ C·f_i, and let g : Y = Proj R(J) → Spec C and s : Spec B → Y be as in R0/submodule-blow-up. Let P be a finitely generated B-module and N ⊆ P a finitely generated C-submodule generating P over B; let 𝒢 ⊆ s_*(P̃) be the image of the morphism σ : g*(Ñ) → s_*(P̃) adjoint to Ñ → g_*s_*(P̃) = (P as a C-module)~ induced by N ⊆ P, a coherent O_Y-module. For i ≥ 1 let K_i^• be the augmented Čech complex of Iⁱ𝒢 for the affine open covering 𝔘 = {D₊(f₀T), …, D₊(fₙT)} of Y (degree −1: global sections), and let K_0^• be that of s_*(P̃); since s_*(P̃) ⊇ 𝒢 ⊇ I𝒢 ⊇ I²𝒢 ⊇ ⋯ these are subcomplexes K_0 ⊇ K_1 ⊇ K_2 ⊇ ⋯, and K_0^• is the augmented Čech complex (**) 0 → P → ∏ P_{f_{i₀}} → ∏ P_{f_{i₀}f_{i₁}} → ⋯ of P̃ for the covering D(f₀), …, D(fₙ) of Spec B (s⁻¹D₊(f_iT) = D(f_i)). Write d_i^p : K_i^p → K_i^{p+1} for the differentials. Then for every p ∈ ℤ and every u ≥ 1 there is v ≥ u with ker(d_v^{p+1}) ⊆ im(d_u^p) = d^p(K_u^p).

*Hypotheses.* B Huber with noetherian ring of definition C, ideal of definition I (finitely generated). F ⊆ B finite generating the unit ideal; P a finite B-module; N ⊆ P a finite C-submodule generating P.

*Proof outline.*

1. Y is noetherian and proper over Spec C (R0/submodule-blow-up (c)); 𝒢 is coherent as the image of the coherent g*(Ñ) in the quasi-coherent s_*(P̃) (s affine), and so is every Iⁱ𝒢 (coherent sheaves on noetherian schemes: supplier JacobianChallenge Layer B).
2. For p ≤ −2 the claim is empty; for p = −1, ker(d_v^0) = d^{−1}(K_v^{−1}) ⊆ d^{−1}(K_u^{−1}) for v ≥ u. Fix p ≥ 0.
3. Čech cohomology computes sheaf cohomology: 𝔘 is a finite affine open covering of the separated scheme Y and Iⁱ𝒢 is quasi-coherent, so Hⁿ(K_i^•) = Hⁿ(Y, Iⁱ𝒢) (TauCeti.AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Modules.Cohomology) for n ≥ 1 (supplier JacobianChallenge Layer B: Čech ≃ derived on a separated scheme).
4. Artin–Rees in cohomology (EGA III 3.3.2; AdicSpacesPartII:F0/graded-cohomology-finiteness (i) applied to the proper C-scheme Y, the ideal I and 𝒢): ⊕_u H^{p+1}(Y, I^u𝒢) is a finite module over the Rees algebra ⊕ I^u, so there is k with H^{p+1}(Y, I^{u+r}𝒢) = I^r ⊙ H^{p+1}(Y, I^u𝒢) for all u ≥ k, r ≥ 0, where x ⊙ y is the image of y under multiplication by x : I^u𝒢 → I^{u+r}𝒢 (Huber (1)). In particular each H^{p+1}(Y, I^u𝒢) is a finite C-module.
5. Torsion: for c ∈ I, localisation at c is exact and commutes with the Čech complex of a quasi-coherent sheaf on an affine covering (Mathlib IsAffineOpen.isLocalization_basicOpen), so H^{p+1}(Y, I^u𝒢)_c = H^{p+1}(g⁻¹D(c), I^u𝒢); g⁻¹(D(c)) ≅ D(c) is affine (R0/submodule-blow-up-isomorphism-away with H = I), so this vanishes (acyclicity of affines, supplier JacobianChallenge Layer B). Hence Supp H^{p+1}(Y, I^u𝒢) ⊆ V(I), I ⊆ √Ann (Mathlib Module.support_eq_zeroLocus), and since I is finitely generated there is t with I^t·H^{p+1}(Y, I^u𝒢) = 0 (Mathlib Ideal.exists_pow_le_of_le_radical_of_fg) — Huber (2), replacing his reference to EGA I (1971) 1.6.8.4.
6. Conclusion (Huber): it suffices to treat u ≥ k, since im(d_u^p) ⊇ im(d_k^p) for u ≤ k. Put v = u + t. For a ∈ ker(d_v^{p+1}) with class ā ∈ H^{p+1}(Y, I^{u+t}𝒢) write ā = ∑ x_j ⊙ ȳ_j with x_j ∈ I^t and y_j ∈ ker(d_u^{p+1}); then a − ∑ x_j y_j ∈ im(d_v^p) ⊆ im(d_u^p), and each x_j y_j ∈ im(d_u^p) because x_j ȳ_j = 0 in H^{p+1}(Y, I^u𝒢). Hence a ∈ im(d_u^p).

*Acceptance.*

- For B = ℤ_p⟨T⟩ (C = B, I = (p)), F = {1, T} and P = B: J = C, Y = Spec C, g = id, 𝒢 = O_Y and the complexes K_i are the Čech complexes of pⁱO_Y for the covering {D(1), D(T)} = {Spec C, D(T)}, which are exact in positive degrees; the claim holds with v = u.

*Depends on* `AdicSpacesPartII:R0/submodule-blow-up`, `AdicSpacesPartII:R0/submodule-blow-up-isomorphism-away`, `AdicSpacesPartII:R0/open-subring-spec-isomorphism`, `AdicSpacesPartII:F0/graded-cohomology-finiteness`, `tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/JacobianChallenge#layer-b-coherent-cohomology-over-k-genus-riemannroch-serre-duality`, `tauceti:TauCeti.AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Modules.Cohomology`, `mathlib:AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Modules`, `mathlib:AlgebraicGeometry.tilde`, `mathlib:AlgebraicGeometry.IsAffineOpen.isLocalization_basicOpen`, `mathlib:Module.support_eq_zeroLocus`, `mathlib:Ideal.exists_pow_le_of_le_radical_of_fg`.

*Sources.* Huber-GeneralizationFormalRigid-1994, §2, (1.3.1)(i), printed p. 527; Huber-GeneralizationFormalRigid-1994, §2, proof of (1.3.1)(i), printed p. 528; Huber-GeneralizationFormalRigid-1994, §2, proof of (1.3.1)(i), printed p. 528; Huber-GeneralizationFormalRigid-1994, §2, proof of (1.3), printed p. 527; EGA-III-1-1961, Ch. III, (3.3.2) Corollaire, printed p. 118.

#### `Huber.NoetherianCech.hasBasis_nhds_zero` — The Čech complexes of Iⁱ𝒢 form a neighbourhood basis in the natural topology (Huber 1994 (1.3.1)(ii))

*Node* `AdicSpacesPartII:R0/blow-up-cech-filtration-neighbourhoods` (lemma); module `TauCeti/AlgebraicGeometry/AdicSpace/Sheafy/NoetherianCech`.

Let B be a Huber ring with a pair of definition (C, I) such that C is noetherian, let F = {f₀, …, fₙ} ⊆ B generate the unit ideal, J = ∑ C·f_i, and let g : Y = Proj R(J) → Spec C and s : Spec B → Y be as in R0/submodule-blow-up. Let P be a finitely generated B-module and N ⊆ P a finitely generated C-submodule generating P over B; let 𝒢 ⊆ s_*(P̃) be the image of the morphism σ : g*(Ñ) → s_*(P̃) adjoint to Ñ → g_*s_*(P̃) = (P as a C-module)~ induced by N ⊆ P, a coherent O_Y-module. For i ≥ 1 let K_i^• be the augmented Čech complex of Iⁱ𝒢 for the affine open covering 𝔘 = {D₊(f₀T), …, D₊(fₙT)} of Y (degree −1: global sections), and let K_0^• be that of s_*(P̃); since s_*(P̃) ⊇ 𝒢 ⊇ I𝒢 ⊇ I²𝒢 ⊇ ⋯ these are subcomplexes K_0 ⊇ K_1 ⊇ K_2 ⊇ ⋯, and K_0^• is the augmented Čech complex (**) 0 → P → ∏ P_{f_{i₀}} → ∏ P_{f_{i₀}f_{i₁}} → ⋯ of P̃ for the covering D(f₀), …, D(fₙ) of Spec B (s⁻¹D₊(f_iT) = D(f_i)). Write d_i^p : K_i^p → K_i^{p+1} for the differentials. Give P its natural topology as a B-module and, for S = {f_{i₀}, …, f_{i_p}} ⊆ F with product t, give P_t = P ⊗_B B_t its natural topology over the Huber ring B(F/S) (the uncompleted rational localisation: the ring B_t with ring of definition C[f/f' : f ∈ F, f' ∈ S] and ideal of definition I·C[f/f'], Tau Ceti `PairOfDefinition.locSubring`, `PairOfDefinition.locIdeal`), and K_0^p the product topology. Then for every p ∈ ℤ the subgroups K_i^p (i ≥ 1) form a fundamental system of neighbourhoods of 0 in K_0^p.

*Hypotheses.* As in R0/blow-up-cech-artin-rees.

*Proof outline.*

1. p ≤ −2: K^p = 0.
2. p ≥ 0: by R0/submodule-blow-up (b), D₊(t·T^{|S|}) is affine with ring C[F/S] ⊆ B_t and s⁻¹ of it is D(t), so Γ(D₊(tT^{|S|}), s_*P̃) = P_t and Γ(D₊(tT^{|S|}), Iⁱ𝒢) = Lⁱ·G_S, where G_S is the image of N ⊗_C C[F/S] in P_t and L = I·C[F/S]. G_S is a finitely generated C[F/S]-submodule generating P_t over B_t, and C[F/S] is noetherian (Mathlib Algebra.FiniteType.isNoetherianRing), so {Lⁱ·G_S} is a basis of neighbourhoods of 0 for the natural topology (R0/noetherian-rod-module-topology-strict applied to the Huber ring B(F/S)); K_i^p is the finite product of these.
3. p = −1: K_i^{−1} = Γ(Y, Iⁱ𝒢) and K_0^{−1} = P. By construction IⁱN ⊆ Γ(Y, Iⁱ𝒢), and IⁱN is open in P (R0/noetherian-rod-module-topology-strict), so every K_i^{−1} is a neighbourhood of 0.
4. Conversely fix k. By EGA III 3.3.2 (AdicSpacesPartII:F0/graded-cohomology-finiteness (i) with p = 0) there is r with Γ(Y, I^{r+j}𝒢) = I^j·Γ(Y, I^r𝒢) for all j ≥ 0. Γ(Y, I^r𝒢) ⊆ P is a finitely generated C-submodule and IᵏN is an open C-submodule, so I^j·Γ(Y, I^r𝒢) ⊆ IᵏN for some j (finitely many generators, I^j·x → 0); hence K_{r+j}^{−1} ⊆ IᵏN.

*Acceptance.*

- For B = ℤ_p⟨T⟩, F = {1, T}, P = N = B: K_i^{−1} = pⁱB and K_i^0 = pⁱB × pⁱ·B[1/T], the p-adic neighbourhood bases of B and of B_T = B[1/T] (ring of definition C[F/T] = B[1/T]).

*Depends on* `AdicSpacesPartII:R0/submodule-blow-up`, `AdicSpacesPartII:R0/noetherian-rod-module-topology-strict`, `AdicSpacesPartII:F0/graded-cohomology-finiteness`, `tauceti:TauCeti.Huber.PairOfDefinition.locSubring`, `tauceti:TauCeti.Huber.PairOfDefinition.locIdeal`, `mathlib:Algebra.FiniteType.isNoetherianRing`, `mathlib:AlgebraicGeometry.Proj.basicOpenIsoSpec`.

*Sources.* Huber-GeneralizationFormalRigid-1994, §2, (1.3.1)(ii), printed p. 527; Huber-GeneralizationFormalRigid-1994, §2, proof of (1.3.1)(ii), printed p. 528; Huber-GeneralizationFormalRigid-1994, §2, proof of (1.3.1)(ii), printed p. 528.

#### `Huber.laurentCech_exact_isStrict` — Strict Čech exactness for standard rational coverings when B has a noetherian ring of definition (Huber 1994 (1.3))

*Node* `AdicSpacesPartII:R0/noetherian-rod-laurent-cech-strict` (lemma); module `TauCeti/AlgebraicGeometry/AdicSpace/Sheafy/NoetherianDefinition`.

Let B be a complete Hausdorff Huber ring with a noetherian ring of definition C (ideal of definition I), B⁺ a ring of integral elements, f₀, …, fₙ ∈ B elements generating the unit ideal, and P a finitely generated B-module. Put U_i = R(f₀, …, fₙ / f_i) ⊆ Spa(B, B⁺) and, for i₀ < ⋯ < i_p, U_{i₀…i_p} = U_{i₀} ∩ ⋯ ∩ U_{i_p} (rational, with 𝒪(U_{i₀…i_p}) the completion B⟨F/f_{i₀}, …, F/f_{i_p}⟩ of the uncompleted rational localisation B(F/f_{i₀}, …, F/f_{i_p}), whose ring is B_{f_{i₀}⋯f_{i_p}}). Give each P ⊗_B 𝒪(U_{i₀…i_p}) its natural topology. Then the augmented Čech complex (*) 0 → P → ∏_{i₀} P ⊗_B 𝒪(U_{i₀}) → ∏_{i₀<i₁} P ⊗_B 𝒪(U_{i₀i₁}) → ⋯ is exact and all its differentials are strict. This is Huber's (1.3) for 𝓕 = P ⊗ 𝒪_B, stated with the terms written out; the case P = B is the structure sheaf.

*Hypotheses.* B complete Hausdorff with a noetherian ring of definition C and ideal of definition I ⊆ C. f₀, …, fₙ ∈ B generate the unit ideal. P a finitely generated B-module.

*Proof outline.*

1. The algebraic Čech complex (**) 0 → P → ∏ P_{f_{i₀}} → ∏ P_{f_{i₀}f_{i₁}} → ⋯ of P̃ for the covering D(f₀), …, D(fₙ) of Spec B is exact (R0/localization-cech-complex-exact).
2. Give P_{f_{i₀}⋯f_{i_p}} = P ⊗_B B(F/f_{i₀}, …) its natural topology over the uncompleted rational localisation (ring of definition C[F/f_{i₀}, …], noetherian, Tau Ceti `PairOfDefinition.locSubring`); the differentials are linear, hence continuous (Mathlib IsModuleTopology.continuous_of_linearMap). Each term has a countable basis of neighbourhoods of 0, and its completion is P ⊗_B 𝒪(U_{i₀…i_p}) (R0/noetherian-rod-module-completion-tensor, with 𝒪(U) the completion of B(F/f), Tau Ceti `PairOfDefinition.completionLocObj`), so the completion (**)^ of (**) is (*).
3. Strictness of (**): with Y, g, s, 𝒢 and the subcomplexes K_0 = (**) ⊇ K_1 ⊇ ⋯ of R0/submodule-blow-up and R0/blow-up-cech-artin-rees, fix p and u ≥ 1 and take v as in R0/blow-up-cech-artin-rees; then im(d_0^p) ∩ K_v^{p+1} ⊆ ker(d_v^{p+1}) ⊆ im(d_u^p) = d_0^p(K_u^p).
4. By R0/blow-up-cech-filtration-neighbourhoods for K^{p+1}, im(d_0^p) ∩ K_v^{p+1} is a neighbourhood of 0 in im(d_0^p); so d_0^p(K_u^p) is a neighbourhood of 0 in the image for every u, and since the K_u^p form a neighbourhood basis of K_0^p (R0/blow-up-cech-filtration-neighbourhoods), d_0^p : K_0^p → im(d_0^p) is open.
5. (**) is exact with strict differentials between Hausdorff groups with countable neighbourhood bases, so its completion (*) is exact with strict differentials (R0/strict-complex-completion-exact).

*Acceptance.*

- For B = ℤ_p⟨T⟩ with ring of definition ℤ_p⟨T⟩ (p-adic) and f₀ = 1, f₁ = T the covering {|T| ≤ 1}, {|T| ≥ 1} of Spa(B, B) gives an exact strict complex 0 → B → B × ℤ_p⟨T, T⁻¹⟩ → ℤ_p⟨T, T⁻¹⟩ → 0.

*Depends on* `AdicSpacesPartII:R0/localization-cech-complex-exact`, `AdicSpacesPartII:R0/strict-complex-completion-exact`, `AdicSpacesPartII:R0/noetherian-rod-module-completion-tensor`, `AdicSpacesPartII:R0/submodule-blow-up`, `AdicSpacesPartII:R0/blow-up-cech-artin-rees`, `AdicSpacesPartII:R0/blow-up-cech-filtration-neighbourhoods`, `tauceti:TauCeti.Huber.PairOfDefinition.locSubring`, `tauceti:TauCeti.Huber.PairOfDefinition.completionLocObj`, `mathlib:IsModuleTopology.continuous_of_linearMap`, `tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/AdicSpaces#layer-3-rational-localisation-and-the-structure-presheaf`.

*Sources.* Huber-GeneralizationFormalRigid-1994, §2, proof of Theorem 2.5, Case I, printed p. 526; Huber-GeneralizationFormalRigid-1994, §2, (1.3), printed p. 526; Huber-GeneralizationFormalRigid-1994, §2, (1.3), printed p. 526; Huber-GeneralizationFormalRigid-1994, §2, proof of (1.3), printed p. 527; Huber-GeneralizationFormalRigid-1994, §2, end of the proof of (1.3), printed p. 528.

#### `Huber.isSheafyPair_of_noetherianRingOfDefinition` — Huber pairs with a noetherian ring of definition are sheafy (Huber 1994 Theorem 2.2, Case I)

*Node* `AdicSpacesPartII:R0/noetherian-rod-sheafy` (theorem); module `TauCeti/AlgebraicGeometry/AdicSpace/Sheafy/NoetherianDefinition`.

Let (A, A⁺) be a Huber pair with A complete and Hausdorff and having a noetherian ring of definition, and X = Spa(A, A⁺). Then: (a) for every rational subset U ⊆ X the complete ring 𝒪_X(U) has a noetherian ring of definition; (b) for every finitely generated A-module M, every rational subset U and every g₀, …, g_m ∈ 𝒪_X(U) generating the unit ideal, the augmented Čech complex of the standard rational covering {V_j = U ∩ R(g/g_j)} of U with terms M ⊗_A 𝒪_X(V_{j₀} ∩ ⋯ ∩ V_{j_p}) (natural topologies) is exact with strict differentials; (c) every open covering of a rational subset U has a refinement by such a standard rational covering; (d) the structure presheaf 𝒪_X is a sheaf of complete topological rings, i.e. (A, A⁺) is sheafy (the anchor's `Huber.IsSheafyPair`). Sheaf-cohomology vanishing is AdicSpacesPartII:R3/noetherian-rod-acyclicity-finite-modules.

*Hypotheses.* A complete Hausdorff Huber ring with a noetherian ring of definition (A is not assumed Tate). A⁺ a ring of integral elements; M a finitely generated A-module (for (b)).

*Proof outline.*

1. (a) For U = R(T/s), 𝒪_X(U) is the completion of A(T/s), whose ring of definition A₀[T/s] (Tau Ceti `PairOfDefinition.locSubring`) is a finitely generated A₀-algebra, hence noetherian (Mathlib Algebra.FiniteType.isNoetherianRing); its completion is noetherian (R0/noetherian-adic-completion) and is a ring of definition of 𝒪_X(U) (Tau Ceti `PairOfDefinition.completionLocObj`). Huber: 'for every rational subset U, F_A(U)^ is complete and has a noetherian ring of definition'.
2. (b) Spa(𝒪_X(U), 𝒪_X⁺(U)) ≅ U matching rational subsets and their rings (Huber 1994 Lemma 1.5, (1.4); anchor Layer 3), so the covering {V_j} is the standard covering {R(g/g_j)} of Spa 𝒪_X(U); apply R0/noetherian-rod-laurent-cech-strict to B = 𝒪_X(U) (noetherian ring of definition by (a)) and P = M ⊗_A 𝒪_X(U), using M ⊗_A 𝒪_X(V) = P ⊗_B 𝒪_X(V).
3. (c) Huber Lemma 2.6 = Wedhorn Lemma 7.54 for the complete affinoid ring 𝒪_X(U) (anchor Layer 2), transported to U by (b)'s identification.
4. (d) Rational subsets form a basis closed under finite intersections (anchor Layer 2), so by Tau Ceti `ValuationSpectrum.isSheaf_iff_isSheafFor_rationalCover` and EGA 0_I 3.2.2 it suffices to treat coverings 𝔙 of rational U by rational subsets. Choose a standard refinement 𝔘 (c). Exactness of 0 → 𝒪(U) → ∏_𝔘 𝒪 → ∏ 𝒪 ((b), M = A) gives injectivity and gluing for 𝔘; 𝔘 restricted to each V ∈ 𝔙 is a standard covering of V (images of the g_j), so injectivity on V gives the sheaf condition for 𝔙 (Huber: a refinement suffices).
5. Topology: 𝒪(U) → ∏_𝔙 𝒪(V) → ∏_𝔘 𝒪(W) is injective and strict by (b), so the first map is a topological embedding; each 𝒪(U) is complete (R0/noetherian-rod-module-complete with M = A). Hence 𝒪_X is a sheaf of complete topological rings on the basis and on X (EGA 0_I 3.2.2).

*Acceptance.*

- Spa(ℤ_p⟨T⟩, ℤ_p⟨T⟩) and Spa(ℤ_p⟦T⟧, ℤ_p⟦T⟧) are sheafy although neither ring is Tate; the only non-analytic point of the latter is the trivial valuation with support (p, T).
- For M = A and the covering {|T| ≤ 1}, {|T| ≥ 1} of Spa(ℤ_p⟨T⟩, ℤ_p⟨T⟩) the complex 0 → ℤ_p⟨T⟩ → ℤ_p⟨T⟩ × ℤ_p⟨T, T⁻¹⟩ → ℤ_p⟨T, T⁻¹⟩ → 0 is exact and strict.
- Huber 1994 Theorem 2.2 in the case of a noetherian ring of definition (the Tate case is the anchor's Layer 4.1).
