#### `Huber.isSheafyPair_of_discreteTopology` — Discrete Huber pairs are sheafy with Čech-acyclic rational coverings (Wedhorn Theorem 8.28(c))

*Node* `AdicSpacesPartII:R0/discrete-huber-pair-sheafy` (lemma); module `TauCeti/AlgebraicGeometry/AdicSpace/Sheafy/Discrete`.

Let A be a ring with the discrete topology and A⁺ ⊆ A an integrally closed subring, so that (A, A⁺) is a complete Huber pair (pair of definition (A, 0)) and Spa(A, A⁺) = {v ∈ Spv A : v(a) ≤ 1 for all a ∈ A⁺}. Then: (a) for every rational subset U = R(T/s), 𝒪(U) = A_s with the discrete topology; (b) for every finite covering (U_j = R(T_j/s_j)) of a rational subset U = R(T/s) by rational subsets and every A-module M, the augmented Čech complex 0 → M_s → ∏ M_{s_{j₀}} → ∏ M_{s_{j₀}s_{j₁}} → ⋯ of the covering with coefficients M ⊗_A 𝒪 is exact in all degrees; (c) 𝒪 is a sheaf of complete (discrete) topological rings on Spa(A, A⁺), i.e. (A, A⁺) is sheafy. No noetherian hypothesis is made.

*Hypotheses.* A a discrete ring (any commutative ring); A⁺ ⊆ A integrally closed. M an arbitrary A-module (for (b)).

*Proof outline.*

1. (a) With the pair of definition (A, 0), the uncompleted rational localisation A(T/s) is A_s with ring of definition A[T/s] and ideal of definition 0 (Tau Ceti `PairOfDefinition.locSubring`, `PairOfDefinition.locIdeal`), so its topology is discrete and it is complete: 𝒪(R(T/s)) = A_s (anchor Layer 3).
2. Covering: U_j ⊆ U gives a restriction A_s → A_{s_j}, so D(s_j) ⊆ D(s) in Spec A. For 𝔭 ∈ D(s) the trivial valuation v_𝔭 (value 0 on 𝔭, 1 elsewhere) lies in Spa(A, A⁺) (every valuation is continuous on a discrete ring) and in U, hence in some U_j, so s_j ∉ 𝔭: the D(s_j) cover D(s) = Spec A_s (anchor Layer 2).
3. Intersections: U_{j₀} ∩ ⋯ ∩ U_{j_p} is rational with ring A_{s_{j₀}⋯s_{j_p}} (anchor Layer 2, Wedhorn Remark 7.30(5)), and M ⊗_A A_{s_{j₀}⋯} = (M_s)_{s_{j₀}⋯} because s is a unit there.
4. (b) The complex is the extended Čech complex of the A_s-module M_s for the elements s_j of A_s, which generate the unit ideal; it is exact by R0/localization-cech-complex-exact.
5. (c) Every open covering of a rational subset is refined by a finite rational covering (rational subsets are a quasi-compact basis, anchor Layer 2); (b) with M = A in degrees −1, 0 gives the sheaf condition on rational coverings, which suffices by Tau Ceti `ValuationSpectrum.isSheaf_iff_isSheafFor_rationalCover`; all rings are discrete, so the topological condition is automatic.

*Acceptance.*

- The discrete ring ℤ[T₁, T₂, …] (not noetherian) with A⁺ = A gives a sheafy Spa(A, A).
- For A = k[T] discrete and A⁺ = k, the covering R(1, T / T) ∪ R(T, 1 / 1) of Spa(A, A⁺) gives the exact complex 0 → k[T] → k[T, T⁻¹] × k[T] → k[T, T⁻¹] → 0.

*Depends on* `AdicSpacesPartII:R0/localization-cech-complex-exact`, `tauceti:TauCeti.Huber.PairOfDefinition.locSubring`, `tauceti:TauCeti.Huber.PairOfDefinition.locIdeal`, `tauceti:TauCeti.ValuationSpectrum.rationalSubset`, `tauceti:TauCeti.ValuationSpectrum.isSheaf_iff_isSheafFor_rationalCover`, `tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/AdicSpaces#layer-2-affinoid-spectra-and-rational-subsets`, `tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/AdicSpaces#layer-3-rational-localisation-and-the-structure-presheaf`.

*Sources.* Wedhorn-AdicSpaces-2019, §8.2, Theorem 8.28, p. 81; Wedhorn-AdicSpaces-2019, §8.2, proof of Theorem 8.28 in the discrete case, p. 81; Wedhorn-AdicSpaces-2019, §8.2, proof of Theorem 8.28 in the discrete case, p. 81; Wedhorn-AdicSpaces-2019, §8.2, proof of Theorem 8.28 in the discrete case, p. 81.

#### `Huber.IsNoetherianType.isStablySheafyRing` — Complete rings of noetherian type are stably sheafy

*Node* `AdicSpacesPartII:R0/noetherian-type-stably-sheafy` (lemma); module `TauCeti/AlgebraicGeometry/AdicSpace/Sheafy/NoetherianType`.

Let A be a complete Hausdorff Huber ring of noetherian type. Then A is stably sheafy in the anchor's sense (`Huber.IsStablySheafyRing A`, Wedhorn Definition 8.26): for every complete Hausdorff Huber ring B topologically of finite type over A (Tau Ceti `IsTopologicallyFiniteType`) and every ring of integral elements B⁺ of B, the structure presheaf of Spa(B, B⁺) is a sheaf of complete topological rings. Three cases occur: (T) B Tate — B is strongly noetherian and the anchor's Layer 4.1 theorem applies, with all-degree exactness of augmented Čech complexes on finite rational covers of rational subsets; (N) B has a noetherian ring of definition (for instance ℤ_p⟨T⟩, ℤ_p⟦T⟧) — Huber 1994 Theorem 2.2, Case I (R0/noetherian-rod-sheafy), with exact strict Čech complexes on standard rational covers of rational subsets, which refine every open cover; (D) B discrete — R0/discrete-huber-pair-sheafy, with all-degree Čech exactness on finite rational covers (a special case of (N), since the prime subring of a discrete ring is a noetherian ring of definition, with an elementary proof).

*Hypotheses.* A complete Hausdorff Huber ring of noetherian type.

*Proof outline.*

1. Every complete B topologically of finite type over A is of noetherian type (R0/topologically-finite-type-noetherian-type): it has a noetherian ring of definition or is a strongly noetherian Tate ring (R0/noetherian-type-huber-ring).
2. Case (T): the anchor's Layer 4.1 proves `Huber.IsSheafyPair B B⁺` and all-degree Čech exactness for complete strongly noetherian Tate B (Wedhorn Theorem 8.28(b), Corollary 8.35).
3. Case (N): R0/noetherian-rod-sheafy (d) applied to (B, B⁺) (Huber 1994 Theorem 2.2, Case I: the blow-up construction (1.1)–(1.2), strictness (1.3.1), (1.3), refinement (1.5) with Lemma 2.6).
4. Case (D): R0/discrete-huber-pair-sheafy (c) applied to (B, B⁺).

*Acceptance.*

- Spa(ℚ_p⟨T⟩, ℤ_p⟨T⟩) and all its rational localisations are sheafy (case T).
- Spa(ℤ_p⟨T⟩, ℤ_p⟨T⟩) and Spa(ℤ_p⟦T⟧⟨X⟩, ℤ_p⟦T⟧⟨X⟩) are sheafy (case N).
- Spa(𝔽_p[T], 𝔽_p) is sheafy (case D).

*Depends on* `AdicSpacesPartII:R0/noetherian-type-huber-ring`, `AdicSpacesPartII:R0/topologically-finite-type-noetherian-type`, `AdicSpacesPartII:R0/noetherian-rod-sheafy`, `AdicSpacesPartII:R0/discrete-huber-pair-sheafy`, `tauceti:TauCeti.Huber.IsTopologicallyFiniteType`, `tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/AdicSpaces#layer-3-rational-localisation-and-the-structure-presheaf`, `tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/AdicSpaces#layer-4-sheafiness-and-tate-acyclicity`.

*Sources.* Huber-GeneralizationFormalRigid-1994, §2, Theorem 2.2, printed p. 524; Wedhorn-AdicSpaces-2019, §8.2, Definition 8.26, p. 81; Wedhorn-AdicSpaces-2019, §8.2, Theorem 8.28, p. 81.

### R0a.2 The completed tensor product

The construction follows the proof of Huber 1994 Lemma 3.9(i). Both structure maps must be adic: otherwise the topology `{Iⁿ·F}` does not make the structure maps continuous (Morel's example `ℤ_ℓ⟦X⟧ ⊗_{ℤ_ℓ} ℚ_ℓ`). The universal property is proved against complete Hausdorff nonarchimedean rings with a closed integrally closed subring, which includes the global sections `(O_X(X), O_X⁺(X))` of any adic space; this is what turns it into the fibre-product property. Base change of weighted restricted series and rational localisation are identified by comparing universal properties.

#### `Huber.Pair.completedTensor` — The completed tensor product of Huber pairs along adic homomorphisms

*Node* `AdicSpacesPartII:R0/completed-tensor-product` (construction); module `TauCeti/RingTheory/Huber/CompletedTensor/Basic`; planet “Completed tensor product”.

Let (A, A⁺), (B, B⁺), (C, C⁺) be Huber pairs (Tau Ceti `Pair`) and f : (A, A⁺) → (B, B⁺), g : (A, A⁺) → (C, C⁺) morphisms of Huber pairs (Tau Ceti `Pair.Hom`) whose underlying ring homomorphisms are adic (R0/adic-ring-homomorphism). Choose a pair of definition (A₀, I) of A and rings of definition B₀ ⊆ B⁺, C₀ ⊆ C⁺ with f(A₀) ⊆ B₀, g(A₀) ⊆ C₀ such that f(I)B₀ and g(I)C₀ are ideals of definition. Let E := B ⊗_A C (Mathlib `Algebra.TensorProduct`, B and C being A-algebras through f and g), let F ⊆ E be the image of B₀ ⊗_{A₀} C₀ (a subring), and give E the group topology for which {Iⁿ·F : n ≥ 0} is a fundamental system of neighbourhoods of 0, where Iⁿ·F is the additive subgroup generated by the products of images of elements of Iⁿ with elements of F. Then E is a Huber ring with pair of definition (F, I·F), the maps inl : b ↦ b ⊗ 1 and inr : c ↦ 1 ⊗ c are adic, the topology does not depend on the choice of (A₀, I, B₀, C₀), and E⁺ := the integral closure in E of the image of B⁺ ⊗_{A⁺} C⁺ is a ring of integral elements of E. The *completed tensor product* is the complete Hausdorff Huber pair B ⊗̂_A C := (Ê, Ê⁺), where Ê is the Hausdorff completion of E (Tau Ceti `IsHuberRing.completion`) and Ê⁺ is the closure of the image of E⁺; it carries the morphisms of Huber pairs inl : (B, B⁺) → B ⊗̂_A C, inr : (C, C⁺) → B ⊗̂_A C with inl ∘ f = inr ∘ g. It is a Tate ring whenever B or C is. Pinned conventions: B ⊗̂_A C always means this completed pair; the plus ring is the integral closure of the image of B⁺ ⊗_{A⁺} C⁺ (not the image itself), then closed up in the completion; no uniformisation is performed; the construction is not defined unless both f and g are adic. Lean name: `Huber.Pair.completedTensor f g hf hg`.

*Hypotheses.* (A, A⁺), (B, B⁺), (C, C⁺) Huber pairs; B and C need not be complete. f : (A, A⁺) → (B, B⁺) and g : (A, A⁺) → (C, C⁺) morphisms of Huber pairs. The ring homomorphisms underlying f and g are adic.

*Proof outline.*

1. Common choice of rings of definition: adicness of f gives (A₀¹, I¹, B₀) and of g gives (A₀², I², C₀). Let A₀ ⊆ A₀¹ ∩ A₀² ∩ A⁺ be a ring of definition with ideal of definition I (intersections of rings of definition and of a ring of definition with the open subring A⁺ are rings of definition, anchor Layer 0.2, Wedhorn Corollary 6.4). Since I is open in A, (I¹)ᴺ ⊆ I for large N, so f(I)B₀ ⊇ (f(I¹)B₀)ᴺ is open in B₀; it is finitely generated by topologically nilpotent elements, so a power of it lies in f(I¹)B₀; hence f(I)B₀ is an ideal of definition; likewise for g. Replace B₀, C₀ by B₀ ∩ B⁺, C₀ ∩ C⁺ (still rings of definition containing the images of A₀ ⊆ A⁺).
2. Ring topology (Morel Proposition II.3.2.1): multiplication is continuous at 0 because F is a subring and Iᵃ F · Iᵇ F ⊆ I^{a+b} F; for a pure tensor b ⊗ c choose k with b·f(I)ᵏB₀ ⊆ B₀ and c·g(I)ᵏC₀ ⊆ C₀ (B₀, C₀ open and multiplication by b, c continuous), then (b ⊗ c)·I^{2k}F ⊆ F, so every x ↦ ax is continuous; Bourbaki's criterion (Topologie générale III §6 no. 3) gives a ring topology.
3. Pair of definition: F is open, I·F is generated by the finitely many images of generators of I, and Iⁿ·F = (I·F)ⁿ, so (F, I·F) is a pair of definition (Tau Ceti `PairOfDefinition`); inl(B₀) ⊆ F and inl(f(I))·F = I·F, so inl (and likewise inr) is adic.
4. Independence of choices: for two admissible choices take a third inside both (intersections as in step 1); the neighbourhood bases are mutually cofinal because each ideal of definition is open in A and each ring of definition of B (resp. C) contains a power of the other's ideal of definition times it.
5. Plus ring: E⁺ contains F (B₀ ⊆ B⁺, C₀ ⊆ C⁺), so it is open; images of b ⊗ 1 with b ∈ B⁺ ⊆ B° are power-bounded because f(I)ᵏ·{bⁿ} ⊆ B₀ gives Iᵏ·{(b ⊗ 1)ⁿ}·F ⊆ F; E° is an integrally closed subring (anchor Layer 0.2), so the integral closure of the image of B⁺ ⊗ C⁺ lies in E°; Tau Ceti `Pair.isRingOfIntegralElements_integralClosure` concludes.
6. Completion: Ê is a Huber ring (Tau Ceti `IsHuberRing.completion`, `PairOfDefinition.completion`), and the closure of the image of E⁺ is a ring of integral elements of Ê with Spa(Ê, Ê⁺) ≅ Spa(E, E⁺) (completion of Huber pairs, anchor Layer 0.3; Wedhorn Lemma 7.47(4), Proposition 7.48).
7. Tate: the image of a pseudouniformiser of B under inl is a topologically nilpotent unit of Ê (Tau Ceti `IsTateRing.completion`).

*API.*

- `Huber.Pair.completedTensor` (constructor): The complete Hausdorff Huber pair B ⊗̂_A C built from adic morphisms f, g (data: the ring, its topology, its plus ring).
- `Huber.Pair.completedTensor.inl` (projection): The morphism of Huber pairs (B, B⁺) → B ⊗̂_A C, b ↦ b ⊗ 1.
- `Huber.Pair.completedTensor.inr` (projection): The morphism of Huber pairs (C, C⁺) → B ⊗̂_A C, c ↦ 1 ⊗ c.
- `Huber.Pair.completedTensor.inl_comp` (relation): inl ∘ f = inr ∘ g as morphisms of Huber pairs.
- `Huber.Pair.completedTensor.tmul` (data): The ring homomorphism B ⊗[A] C → B ⊗̂_A C from Mathlib's algebraic tensor product; tmul (b ⊗ₜ c) = inl b * inr c (simp).
- `Huber.Pair.completedTensor.denseRange_tmul` (characterisation): tmul has dense range; its kernel is the closure of 0 in B ⊗_A C.
- `Huber.Pair.completedTensor.pairOfDefinition` (structure): The pair of definition (closure of the image of B₀ ⊗ C₀, ideal generated by the image of I); the topology does not depend on the choices.
- `Huber.Pair.completedTensor.isAdicHom_inl` (other): inl and inr are adic.
- `Huber.Pair.completedTensor.plus_eq` (characterisation): The plus ring is the closure of the integral closure of the image of B⁺ ⊗_{A⁺} C⁺; it contains the image of every b ⊗ c with b ∈ B⁺, c ∈ C⁺.
- `Huber.Pair.completedTensor.lift` (universal-property): For a complete Hausdorff nonarchimedean ring R with closed integrally closed subring R⁺ and morphisms φ : (B, B⁺) → (R, R⁺), ψ : (C, C⁺) → (R, R⁺) with φ ∘ f = ψ ∘ g, the morphism B ⊗̂_A C → (R, R⁺) (theorem R0/completed-tensor-product-universal-property).
- `Huber.Pair.completedTensor.lift_comp_inl` (universal-property): (lift φ ψ h) ∘ inl = φ; similarly lift_comp_inr.
- `Huber.Pair.completedTensor.hom_ext` (extensionality): Two continuous morphisms out of B ⊗̂_A C agreeing after inl and after inr are equal.
- `Huber.Pair.completedTensor.map` (functoriality): Morphisms (B, B⁺) → (B', B'⁺), (C, C⁺) → (C', C'⁺) over (A, A⁺) → (A', A'⁺) with all structure maps adic induce B ⊗̂_A C → B' ⊗̂_{A'} C'; map_id, map_comp.
- `Huber.Pair.completedTensor.comm` (equivalence): B ⊗̂_A C ≅ C ⊗̂_A B exchanging inl and inr.
- `Huber.Pair.completedTensor.cancelBaseChange` (equivalence): For adic A → C → C': (B ⊗̂_A C) ⊗̂_C C' ≅ B ⊗̂_A C' (transitivity of base change, from the universal property).
- `Huber.Pair.completedTensor.isTateRing` (instance): B ⊗̂_A C is Tate if B or C is Tate.

*Unit tests.*

- `completedTensor_test_polydisc` (computation): For a complete nonarchimedean field K: (K⟨T⟩, K°⟨T⟩) ⊗̂_{(K,K°)} (K⟨S⟩, K°⟨S⟩) is isomorphic, compatibly with inl and inr, to (K⟨T, S⟩, K°⟨T, S⟩) with T ↦ T ⊗ 1 and S ↦ 1 ⊗ S.
- `completedTensor_test_plus_not_image` (non-example): For K = ℚ_p and L = ℚ_p(√p): (L, O_L) ⊗̂_K (L, O_L) ≅ (L × L, O_L × O_L), and the idempotent (1, 0) lies in the plus ring but not in the image of O_L ⊗_{ℤ_p} O_L (that image is O_L[Y]/(Y² − p) embedded by Y ↦ (√p, −√p)). A definition taking the plus ring to be the image of B⁺ ⊗ C⁺ fails.
- `completedTensor_test_not_adic` (non-example): For A = ℤ_p (p-adic), B = ℤ_p⟦X⟧ ((p, X)-adic), C = ℚ_p: A → B is not adic, and there is no Huber-ring topology on B ⊗_A C = ℤ_p⟦X⟧[1/p] making B → B ⊗_A C and C → B ⊗_A C continuous with ℤ_p⟦X⟧ open (Morel Example II.3.2.2); the construction requires adicness of both maps.
- `completedTensor_test_unit` (degenerate): For g = id: (B, B⁺) ⊗̂_A (A, A⁺) ≅ (B̂, closure of B⁺) via inl, and for complete B this is (B, B⁺).
- `completedTensor_test_banach` (compatibility): If A, B, C are Banach rings with a topologically nilpotent unit and f, g bounded, the topology of B ⊗̂_A C equals the topology of the completion of B ⊗_A C for the product seminorm (Kedlaya–Liu Definition 2.1.10), and the plus ring equals Kedlaya–Liu's coproduct plus ring (completion of the integral closure of the image of B⁺ ⊗_{A⁺} C⁺).
- `completedTensor_test_algebraic` (compatibility): The map B ⊗[A] C → B ⊗̂_A C from Mathlib's algebraic tensor product has dense image and kernel the closure of 0 for the {Iⁿ·F} topology.

*Acceptance.*

- (K⟨T⟩, K°⟨T⟩) ⊗̂_{(K, K°)} (K⟨S⟩, K°⟨S⟩) ≅ (K⟨T, S⟩, K°⟨T, S⟩) (Hübner Example 9.3).
- For L = ℚ_p(√p) over K = ℚ_p: (L, O_L) ⊗̂_K (L, O_L) ≅ (L × L, O_L × O_L), and the image of O_L ⊗_{ℤ_p} O_L is not integrally closed in L × L.
- (ℤ_p⟨T⟩, ℤ_p⟨T⟩) ⊗̂_{ℤ_p} (ℚ_p, ℤ_p) ≅ (ℚ_p⟨T⟩, ℤ_p⟨T⟩) and (ℤ_p⟨T⟩, ℤ_p⟨T⟩) ⊗̂_{ℤ_p} (𝔽_p, 𝔽_p) ≅ (𝔽_p[T], 𝔽_p[T]) discrete (Hübner Examples 9.4, 9.5).

#### `Huber.Pair.completedTensor.existsUnique_lift` — Universal property of the completed tensor product

*Node* `AdicSpacesPartII:R0/completed-tensor-product-universal-property` (theorem); module `TauCeti/RingTheory/Huber/CompletedTensor/UniversalProperty`.

Let f : (A, A⁺) → (B, B⁺) and g : (A, A⁺) → (C, C⁺) be morphisms of Huber pairs with adic underlying ring homomorphisms, and let D = B ⊗̂_A C with inl, inr (R0/completed-tensor-product). Let R be a complete Hausdorff nonarchimedean topological commutative ring and R⁺ ⊆ R a closed subring integrally closed in R (for instance a complete Huber pair, or (O_X(X), O_X⁺(X)) for an adic space X). For all continuous ring homomorphisms φ : B → R, ψ : C → R with φ(B⁺) ⊆ R⁺, ψ(C⁺) ⊆ R⁺ and φ ∘ f = ψ ∘ g, there is exactly one continuous ring homomorphism χ : D → R with χ(D⁺) ⊆ R⁺, χ ∘ inl = φ and χ ∘ inr = ψ. In particular the square of f, g, inl, inr is cocartesian in the category of complete Hausdorff Huber pairs. If moreover R is Huber and φ is adic, then χ is adic. No adicness of φ or ψ is needed.

*Hypotheses.* f, g morphisms of Huber pairs whose underlying ring homomorphisms are adic. R complete Hausdorff, nonarchimedean (open additive subgroups form a basis of neighbourhoods of 0). R⁺ ⊆ R a closed subring, integrally closed in R. φ, ψ continuous, φ(B⁺) ⊆ R⁺, ψ(C⁺) ⊆ R⁺, φ ∘ f = ψ ∘ g.

*Proof outline.*

1. Algebraic factorisation: Mathlib `Algebra.TensorProduct.lift` gives the unique ring homomorphism χ₀ : B ⊗_A C → R with χ₀(b ⊗ c) = φ(b)ψ(c) (R is commutative, so the commutation hypothesis is automatic).
2. Continuity of χ₀ for the topology {Iⁿ·F}: given an open subgroup U of R choose an open subgroup V with V·V ⊆ U (continuity of multiplication at (0, 0)), then k with φ(f(I)ᵏB₀) ⊆ V and ψ(g(I)ᵏC₀) ⊆ V (continuity of φ, ψ and f(I)B₀, g(I)C₀ ideals of definition — this is where adicness of f and g is used); I^{2k}·F is generated by images of (f(I)ᵏB₀) ⊗ (g(I)ᵏC₀), so χ₀(I^{2k}·F) ⊆ V·V ⊆ U.
3. Extension: Mathlib `UniformSpace.Completion.extensionHom` extends χ₀ to the completion D, with `UniformSpace.Completion.extensionHom_coe` giving χ ∘ inl = φ, χ ∘ inr = ψ.
4. Plus rings: χ maps the image of B⁺ ⊗ C⁺ into R⁺, hence its integral closure into the integral closure of R⁺ in R, which is R⁺; by continuity and closedness of R⁺ the closure D⁺ maps into R⁺.
5. Uniqueness: two such χ agree on the image of B ⊗_A C (Mathlib `Algebra.TensorProduct.ext`), which is dense (`Huber.Pair.completedTensor.denseRange_tmul`), and R is Hausdorff.
6. Adicness of χ when φ is adic: χ(F) lies in a ring of definition R₀ ⊇ φ(B₀)ψ(C₀) and χ(I·F) = φ(f(I))·χ(F) generates an ideal of definition of R₀ because φ(f(I)B₀)R₀ does.

*Acceptance.*

- For K⟨T⟩ and K⟨S⟩ over K, the unique map K⟨T⟩ ⊗̂_K K⟨S⟩ → K⟨T, S⟩ given by the two inclusions is an isomorphism (both represent pairs of power-bounded elements).
- Hom(B ⊗̂_A C, R) ≅ Hom(B, R) ×_{Hom(A, R)} Hom(C, R) for R = O_X(X) of any adic space X (the form used in R0/affinoid-fibre-product).
- Without adicness of f the statement fails: for ℤ_p → ℤ_p⟦X⟧ and ℤ_p → ℚ_p no Huber topology on the tensor product makes the structure maps continuous (Morel Example II.3.2.2).

*Depends on* within R0a: `Huber.Pair.completedTensor`, `Huber.IsAdicHom`; library: `Algebra.TensorProduct.lift`, `Algebra.TensorProduct.ext`, `UniformSpace.Completion.extensionHom`, `UniformSpace.Completion.extensionHom_coe`.

*Sources.* Huber-GeneralizationFormalRigid-1994, §3, proof of Proposition 3.7, printed p. 536; Morel-AdicSpacesNotes, §II.3.2, Proposition II.3.2.1; Wedhorn-AdicSpaces-2019, §8.6, proof of Theorem 8.56, p. 90.

#### `Huber.Pair.completedTensorRestrictedEquiv` — Base change of weighted restricted power series and of their quotients

*Node* `AdicSpacesPartII:R0/completed-tensor-restricted-power-series` (lemma); module `TauCeti/RingTheory/Huber/CompletedTensor/RestrictedSeries`.

Let λ : (A, A⁺) → (B, B⁺) be a morphism of Huber pairs whose ring homomorphism is adic, and let M = (M₁,…,M_n) be finite subsets of A with every M_i·A open in A. Then (a) every λ(M_i)·B is open in B, so the weighted restricted power-series pair B⟨X⟩_{λ(M)} = B⟨X₁,…,X_n⟩_{λ(M₁),…,λ(M_n)} is defined (Huber's plus ring: the integral closure of {∑ b_ν X^ν : b_ν ∈ λ(M)^ν·(B⁺)^ for all ν}); (b) the morphism A⟨X⟩_M ⊗̂_A B → B⟨X⟩_{λ(M)} induced by the natural extension λ' : A⟨X⟩_M → B⟨X⟩_{λ(M)} of λ (X_i ↦ X_i) and by the structure map B → B⟨X⟩_{λ(M)} is an isomorphism of complete Huber pairs; (c) if σ : A⟨X⟩_M → (C, C⁺) is a quotient mapping of complete Huber pairs (surjective, continuous and open, C⁺ the integral closure of σ(A⟨X⟩_M⁺)) with kernel 𝔞, then C ⊗̂_A B ≅ B⟨X⟩_{λ(M)}/𝔟 with 𝔟 the closure of λ'(𝔞)·B⟨X⟩_{λ(M)}, quotient topology and plus ring the integral closure of the image of B⟨X⟩⁺_{λ(M)}; if B is complete of noetherian type then 𝔟 = λ'(𝔞)·B⟨X⟩_{λ(M)}. Consequently B → C ⊗̂_A B is topologically of finite type as a morphism of Huber pairs (a quotient mapping out of B⟨X⟩_{λ(M)}) and as a ring homomorphism (Tau Ceti `IsTopologicallyFiniteType`).

*Hypotheses.* λ : (A, A⁺) → (B, B⁺) a morphism of Huber pairs with adic ring homomorphism. M₁,…,M_n finite subsets of A with each M_i·A open. For (c): σ a quotient mapping of complete Huber pairs out of A⟨X⟩_M.

*Proof outline.*

1. (a) An open ideal of A contains Iᵏ·A for a pair of definition (A₀, I) (Wedhorn Lemma 6.6, anchor Layer 0.2), so λ(M_i)·B ⊇ λ(I)ᵏ·B ⊇ (λ(I)B₀)ᵏ, which is open because λ is adic. The weight-family hypothesis of Tau Ceti's `weightedRestrictedSubring` (λ(M_i)ᵐ·U a neighbourhood of 0 for all m and all neighbourhoods U) follows from openness of λ(M_i)·B by Wedhorn Lemma 6.20 = Huber Lemma 1.1, which the anchor's Layer 0.4 states as the equivalent form of its standing hypothesis (imported).
2. (b) The pair-level universal property of A⟨X⟩_M (Huber 1994 Lemma 3.5(i): morphisms A⟨X⟩_M → (R, R⁺) to complete pairs correspond to morphisms φ : A → R together with r_i ∈ R such that φ(m)·r_i ∈ R⁺ for m ∈ M_i), imported with the plus ring of A⟨X⟩_M from the anchor's Layer 5.2; its ring-level part is Tau Ceti `existsUnique_continuous_ringHom_completion_weightedRestrictedSubring_of_isWeightedVarPowerBounded` (elements of R⁺ are power-bounded), and λ' is Tau Ceti `weightedMapCompletion` (λ(M_i) ⊆ λ(M_i)).
3. (b) cont.: by R0/completed-tensor-product-universal-property, morphisms A⟨X⟩_M ⊗̂_A B → (R, R⁺) correspond to pairs (A⟨X⟩_M → R, B → R) agreeing on A, hence to (ψ : B → R, r_i with ψ(λ(m))·r_i ∈ R⁺), which by Lemma 3.5(i) for B are the morphisms B⟨X⟩_{λ(M)} → (R, R⁺). Both objects represent the same functor on complete Hausdorff Huber pairs, and the comparison morphism is the one of the statement; so it is an isomorphism (Yoneda).
4. (c) C ⊗̂_A B represents pairs (C → R, B → R) agreeing on A; C → R is a morphism A⟨X⟩_M → R killing 𝔞 (universal property of the quotient pair, Tau Ceti `Pair.quotient` and `Pair.Hom.quotientLift`, plus continuity: a continuous map to a Hausdorff R killing 𝔞 kills its closure); so C ⊗̂_A B represents morphisms B⟨X⟩_{λ(M)} → R killing λ'(𝔞), which B⟨X⟩_{λ(M)}/𝔟 represents. The noetherian case: 𝔟 is closed by R0/noetherian-type-ideals-closed applied to B⟨X⟩_{λ(M)}, which is of noetherian type by R0/topologically-finite-type-noetherian-type.
5. Topologically finite type: B → B⟨X⟩_{λ(M)}/𝔟 is the composite of the presenting map with an open quotient map (Tau Ceti `IsTopologicallyFiniteType.comp_isOpenQuotientMap`).

*Acceptance.*

- K⟨X⟩ ⊗̂_K L ≅ L⟨X⟩ for a complete extension L/K of nonarchimedean fields.
- ℤ_p⟨X⟩_{p}/(pX − 1) = ℚ_p, and ℚ_p ⊗̂_{ℤ_p} ℤ_p⟨T⟩ ≅ ℤ_p⟨T⟩⟨X⟩_{p}/(pX − 1) ≅ ℚ_p⟨T⟩ (Hübner Example 9.4).
- Failure without adicness: for λ : ℤ_p → ℤ_p⟦T⟧ and M = {p}, λ(M)·B = p·ℤ_p⟦T⟧ is not open, so B⟨X⟩_{λ(M)} is not defined; this is why R0/fibre-product-along-finite-type enlarges the weights by powers of an ideal of definition.

*Depends on* within R0a: `Huber.Pair.completedTensor`, `Huber.Pair.completedTensor.existsUnique_lift`, `Huber.IsAdicHom`, `Huber.IsNoetherianType.isClosed_ideal`, `Huber.IsNoetherianType.of_isTopologicallyFiniteType`; anchor stages: `layer-0-topological-algebra-huber-rings-and-tate-algebras`, `layer-5-adic-spaces-and-elementary-geometry`; library: `TauCeti.Huber.weightedRestrictedSubring`, `TauCeti.Huber.IsWeightFamily`, `TauCeti.Huber.weightedMapCompletion`, `TauCeti.Huber.existsUnique_continuous_ringHom_completion_weightedRestrictedSubring_of_isWeightedVarPowerBounded`, `TauCeti.Huber.Pair.quotient`, `TauCeti.Huber.Pair.Hom.quotientLift`, `TauCeti.Huber.IsTopologicallyFiniteType.comp_isOpenQuotientMap`.

*Sources.* Huber-GeneralizationFormalRigid-1994, §3, proof of Proposition 3.7, printed pp. 535–536; Huber-GeneralizationFormalRigid-1994, §3, proof of Proposition 3.7, printed p. 536; Huber-GeneralizationFormalRigid-1994, §3, Lemma 3.5(i), printed p. 534; Hubner-AdicSpaces-2024, §9, proof of Theorem 9.2(iii), p. 42.

#### `Huber.Pair.completedTensor.isNoetherianType` — Completed base change along a topologically-finite-type map preserves noetherian type and sheafiness

*Node* `AdicSpacesPartII:R0/completed-tensor-noetherian-stability` (lemma); module `TauCeti/RingTheory/Huber/CompletedTensor/NoetherianType`.

Let λ : (A, A⁺) → (B, B⁺) and μ : (A, A⁺) → (C, C⁺) be morphisms of complete Hausdorff Huber pairs with λ adic and μ topologically of finite type as a ring homomorphism (Tau Ceti `IsTopologicallyFiniteType`; then μ is adic by R0/topologically-finite-type-is-adic). If B is of noetherian type, then inl : B → B ⊗̂_A C is topologically of finite type, B ⊗̂_A C is a complete Hausdorff Huber ring of noetherian type, and B ⊗̂_A C (with its plus ring, or with any other ring of integral elements) is sheafy — indeed stably sheafy (R0/noetherian-type-stably-sheafy). If μ is topologically of finite type as a morphism of pairs, inl is so as a morphism of pairs.

*Hypotheses.* λ adic; μ topologically of finite type (ring level); A, B, C complete Hausdorff. B of noetherian type (R0/noetherian-type-huber-ring).

*Proof outline.*

1. Present C = A⟨X⟩_M/𝔞 by a quotient mapping (the ring-level presentation of `IsTopologicallyFiniteType`; for the pair-level statement, a quotient mapping of pairs).
2. R0/completed-tensor-restricted-power-series: B ⊗̂_A C ≅ B⟨X⟩_{λ(M)}/𝔟, so inl is topologically of finite type.
3. R0/topologically-finite-type-noetherian-type: B ⊗̂_A C is of noetherian type.
4. R0/noetherian-type-stably-sheafy: it is stably sheafy, hence sheafy for every ring of integral elements.

*Acceptance.*

- Huber 1994: in the proof of 3.7, D^▷ has a noetherian ring of definition or is a strongly noetherian Tate ring, so Spa D is an adic space.
- Spa(ℚ_p⟨T⟩) ×_{Spa ℚ_p} Spa(ℚ_p⟨S⟩) = Spa(ℚ_p⟨T, S⟩) is sheafy.
- No sheafiness is asserted for completed tensor products of rings not of noetherian type (for instance of two perfectoid rings over a non-perfectoid base); those cases are PerfectoidSpaces:P2 and R5.

*Depends on* within R0a: `Huber.Pair.completedTensorRestrictedEquiv`, `Huber.IsNoetherianType.of_isTopologicallyFiniteType`, `Huber.IsNoetherianType.isStablySheafyRing`, `Huber.IsTopologicallyFiniteType.isAdicHom`, `Huber.IsNoetherianType`; library: `TauCeti.Huber.IsTopologicallyFiniteType`.

*Sources.* Huber-GeneralizationFormalRigid-1994, §3, proof of Proposition 3.7, printed p. 536; Wedhorn-AdicSpaces-2019, §8.6, proof of Theorem 8.56(ii), p. 90; HansenKedlaya-SheafinessCriteria, Remark 7.2.

#### `Huber.Pair.completedTensorRationalEquiv` — Rational localisation commutes with completed tensor products

*Node* `AdicSpacesPartII:R0/completed-tensor-rational-localisation` (lemma); module `TauCeti/AlgebraicGeometry/AdicSpace/Spa/CompletedTensor`.

Let f : (A, A⁺) → (B, B⁺), g : (A, A⁺) → (C, C⁺) be morphisms of complete Hausdorff Huber pairs with adic ring homomorphisms, D = B ⊗̂_A C, and p_B = Spa(inl) : Spa D → Spa B, p_C = Spa(inr) (Tau Ceti `Pair.Hom.spaComap`). Let U = R(T/s) ⊆ Spa B, V = R(T'/s') ⊆ Spa C, W = R(T''/s'') ⊆ Spa A be rational subsets with Spa(f)(U) ⊆ W and Spa(g)(V) ⊆ W, and let O(U) = B⟨T/s⟩ etc. denote the rational localisations as complete Huber pairs (anchor Layer 3.1; Tau Ceti `completionLocalization`). Then: (1) p_B⁻¹(U) = R(inl(T)/inl(s)) and p_C⁻¹(V) = R(inr(T')/inr(s')) are rational, and p_B⁻¹(U) ∩ p_C⁻¹(V) is the rational subset R(inl(T ∪ {s})·inr(T' ∪ {s'}) / inl(s)inr(s')); (2) the maps O(W) → O(U), O(W) → O(V) are adic and the canonical morphism O(U) ⊗̂_{O(W)} O(V) → O_D(p_B⁻¹(U) ∩ p_C⁻¹(V)) is an isomorphism of complete Huber pairs; (3) consequently Spa(O(U) ⊗̂_{O(W)} O(V)) → Spa D is a homeomorphism onto p_B⁻¹(U) ∩ p_C⁻¹(V) matching rational subsets.

*Hypotheses.* f, g morphisms of complete Hausdorff Huber pairs with adic ring homomorphisms. U, V, W rational subsets (T·B open, etc.) with Spa(f)(U) ⊆ W, Spa(g)(V) ⊆ W.

*Proof outline.*

1. (1) Preimages: Tau Ceti `Pair.Hom.spaComap_preimage_rationalSubset` computes p_B⁻¹(R(T/s)) = R(inl(T)/inl(s)) as sets; since inl is adic, inl(T)·D is open (T·B ⊇ power of an ideal of definition, Wedhorn Lemma 6.6), so this is a rational subset in Huber's sense (Wedhorn Lemma 7.46(3)). Finite intersections of rational subsets are rational with the product presentation (anchor Layer 2.2, Wedhorn Remark 7.30(5)).
2. (2) Adicness: B → O(U) is topologically of finite type (Wedhorn Example 6.38, Huber 1994 Corollary 3.4(i)) hence adic (R0/topologically-finite-type-is-adic); O(W) → O(U) is adic by cancellation (`Huber.IsAdicHom.of_comp`, R0/adic-ring-homomorphism) since A → O(W) → O(U) equals A → B → O(U).
3. (2) cont.: morphisms O(U) ⊗̂_{O(W)} O(V) → (R, R⁺) (complete Huber pairs) correspond (R0/completed-tensor-product-universal-property) to pairs (O(U) → R, O(V) → R) agreeing on O(W); by the universal property of rational localisation (Tau Ceti `existsUnique_continuous_ringHom_of_forall_comap_mem_rationalSubset`, Huber 1994 Proposition 1.3) these are pairs (B → R with Spa R → U, C → R with Spa R → V) agreeing on A (agreement on O(W) follows from agreement on A by uniqueness in O(W)'s universal property), i.e. morphisms D → R whose Spa-image lies in p_B⁻¹(U) ∩ p_C⁻¹(V), i.e. morphisms O_D(p_B⁻¹(U) ∩ p_C⁻¹(V)) → R. Yoneda gives the isomorphism.
4. (3) The adic spectrum of a rational localisation is homeomorphic to the rational subset with rational subsets matched (Tau Ceti `spaLocalizationHomeomorph`, anchor Layer 3.1; Huber 1994 Lemma 1.5(ii)).

*Acceptance.*

- For X = Spa(ℚ_p⟨T⟩), Y = Spa(ℚ_p⟨S⟩) over Spa ℚ_p, U = R(T/p) = {|T| ≤ |p|} ⊆ X and V = R(1/S) = {|S| = 1} ⊆ Y: p_X⁻¹(U) ∩ p_Y⁻¹(V) = {|T| ≤ |p|, |S| = 1} in the bidisc Spa(ℚ_p⟨T, S⟩), and ℚ_p⟨T/p⟩ ⊗̂_{ℚ_p} ℚ_p⟨S, S⁻¹⟩ ≅ ℚ_p⟨T, S⟩⟨T/p, 1/S⟩.
- Kedlaya–Liu: the completed tensor product of two rational localisations is the rational localisation of the intersection.

*Depends on* within R0a: `Huber.Pair.completedTensor`, `Huber.Pair.completedTensor.existsUnique_lift`, `Huber.IsTopologicallyFiniteType.isAdicHom`, `Huber.IsAdicHom`; anchor stages: `layer-0-topological-algebra-huber-rings-and-tate-algebras`, `layer-2-affinoid-spectra-and-rational-subsets`, `layer-3-rational-localisation-and-the-structure-presheaf`, `layer-5-adic-spaces-and-elementary-geometry`; library: `TauCeti.Huber.Pair.Hom.spaComap`, `TauCeti.Huber.Pair.Hom.spaComap_preimage_rationalSubset`, `TauCeti.ValuationSpectrum.rationalSubset`, `TauCeti.Huber.PairOfDefinition.completionLocalization`, `TauCeti.ValuationSpectrum.existsUnique_continuous_ringHom_of_forall_comap_mem_rationalSubset`, `TauCeti.ValuationSpectrum.spaLocalizationHomeomorph`.

*Sources.* KedlayaLiu-RelativeFoundations-2015, §2.4, after Definition 2.4.12, p. 41; Wedhorn-AdicSpaces-2019, §7.5, Lemma 7.46(3), p. 68; Huber-GeneralizationFormalRigid-1994, §1, Lemma 1.5(ii), printed p. 518.

### R0a.2b The spectral seminorm, uniformization and the uniform completed tensor product

A completed tensor product of uniform rings need not be uniform (Kedlaya–Liu Remark 2.8.5: `ℂ_p ⊗̂_{ℚ_p} ℂ_p`), so
the uniform theory is planned separately from R0a.2. A Tate ring carries a norm attached to a ring of definition, a
pseudouniformiser and a radius (Kedlaya–Liu Remark 2.4.4); its smoothing is the spectral seminorm (Kedlaya–Liu
Definition 2.1.9, Mathlib's `smoothingSeminorm`). The spectral seminorm defines the *spectral topology*, which does
not depend on the choices, is coarser than the given topology, has the same continuous valuations, and is uniform.
The uniformization (Kedlaya–Liu Definition 2.8.13) is the Hausdorff completion of the spectral topology with the
closure of the image of the plus ring; it is left adjoint to the inclusion of complete uniform Tate Huber pairs and
does not change `Spa`. The uniform completed tensor product is the uniformization of the completed tensor product and
is the pushout among complete uniform Tate Huber pairs. The proofs use no Gel'fand-spectrum input: the supremum
formula for the spectral seminorm (Berkovich) stays with `AdicSpacesPartII:R3/uniform-spectral-seminorm`.

```text
   (A, A⁺) ──id──▶ (A_sp, A⁺) ──completion──▶ (A^u, A^{u+})        B ⊗̂ᵘ_A C := (B ⊗̂_A C)^u
```

#### `Huber.tateNorm` — The norm of a Tate ring attached to a ring of definition, a pseudouniformiser and a radius

*Node* `AdicSpacesPartII:R0/tate-ring-norm` (definition); module `TauCeti/RingTheory/Huber/Uniform/TateNorm`.

Let A be a Tate ring (Tau Ceti `IsTateRing A`). A *norm datum* d = (A₀, ϖ, r) on A consists of a ring of definition A₀ (the `ringOfDefinition` of a Tau Ceti `PairOfDefinition A`), a pseudouniformiser ϖ of A lying in A₀ (Tau Ceti `IsPseudoUniformizer ϖ`: a topologically nilpotent unit; A₀ contains one by Wedhorn Proposition 6.14) and a real number r with 0 < r < 1. The *norm of A attached to d* is α_d : A → ℝ≥0, α_d(x) := inf{ rⁿ : n ∈ ℤ, ϖ⁻ⁿx ∈ A₀ } (Kedlaya–Liu Remark 2.4.4). The exponent set is nonempty and downward closed, so α_d(x) = r^{N(x)} with N(x) = sup{ n ∈ ℤ : x ∈ ϖⁿA₀ } ∈ ℤ ∪ {+∞} (r^{+∞} := 0). Then α_d is a nonarchimedean ring seminorm (Mathlib `RingSeminorm A` with `IsNonarchimedean`), α_d(1) ≤ 1 and α_d(ϖx) = r·α_d(x); its closed balls are {α_d ≤ rⁿ} = ϖⁿA₀ (n ∈ ℤ), so it defines the topology of A; it vanishes exactly on the closure of {0} = ⋂ₙ ϖⁿA₀, so it is a norm iff A is Hausdorff, and (A, α_d) is a Banach ring in Kedlaya–Liu's sense iff A is moreover complete. Pinned conventions: ϖ must lie in A₀; the function depends on d, and only its equivalence class (for fixed ϖ and r) and the topology it defines are canonical. Lean names: `Huber.TateNormDatum A` for d and `Huber.tateNorm d` for α_d.

*Hypotheses.* A is a Tate ring (Tau Ceti `IsTateRing`). A₀ is the ring of definition of a Tau Ceti `PairOfDefinition A`, and ϖ ∈ A₀ is a pseudouniformiser of A. r is a real number with 0 < r < 1.

*Construction and proof outline.*

1. Nonempty exponent set: A₀ is an open neighbourhood of 0 and ϖ is topologically nilpotent, so ϖᵏx → 0 and ϖᵏx ∈ A₀ for k ≫ 0; downward closed: ϖ⁻ⁿx ∈ A₀ implies ϖ⁻⁽ⁿ⁻¹⁾x = ϖ·(ϖ⁻ⁿx) ∈ A₀ because ϖ ∈ A₀.
2. Seminorm axioms: A₀ is a subring, so ϖ⁻ⁿx, ϖ⁻ᵐy ∈ A₀ give ϖ⁻ⁿ⁻ᵐxy ∈ A₀ and, for m = n, ϖ⁻ⁿ(x ± y) ∈ A₀; hence α_d(xy) ≤ α_d(x)α_d(y), α_d(x + y) ≤ max(α_d(x), α_d(y)), α_d(−x) = α_d(x); 1 ∈ A₀ gives α_d(1) ≤ 1 and every n is allowed for x = 0. These are the fields of Mathlib `RingSeminorm` and the inequality `IsNonarchimedean`.
3. Balls and topology: α_d(x) ≤ rⁿ iff ϖ⁻ⁿx ∈ A₀ iff x ∈ ϖⁿA₀, and the sets ϖⁿA₀ (n ≥ 0) form a basis of neighbourhoods of 0 in A (Tau Ceti `IsPseudoUniformizer.hasBasis_nhds_zero`).
4. Kernel: α_d(x) = 0 iff x ∈ ⋂ₙ ϖⁿA₀, the closure of {0} because the ϖⁿA₀ are a basis of open subgroups.
5. Change of datum: rings of definition A₀, A₀' both containing ϖ satisfy ϖᵏA₀ ⊆ A₀' and ϖᵏA₀' ⊆ A₀ for some k ≥ 0 (each is bounded, the other open), so α' ≤ r⁻ᵏα and α ≤ r⁻ᵏα'; replacing r by r' replaces α_d by α_d^{log r'/log r} because α_d takes values in r^ℤ ∪ {0}.

*API.*

- `Huber.TateNormDatum` (structure): A norm datum on a Tate ring A: a pair of definition P, a pseudouniformiser ϖ ∈ P.ringOfDefinition, and r ∈ (0, 1).
- `Huber.tateNorm` (constructor): The nonarchimedean ring seminorm α_d : RingSeminorm A of a norm datum d.
- `Huber.tateNorm_apply` (characterisation): α_d(x) = sInf { rⁿ : n ∈ ℤ, ϖ⁻ⁿx ∈ A₀ }.
- `Huber.isNonarchimedean_tateNorm` (structure): IsNonarchimedean α_d: α_d(x + y) ≤ max(α_d(x), α_d(y)).
- `Huber.tateNorm_one_le` (simp): α_d(1) ≤ 1.
- `Huber.tateNorm_pseudoUniformizer_mul` (simp): α_d(ϖ·x) = r·α_d(x) and α_d(ϖ⁻¹·x) = r⁻¹·α_d(x).
- `Huber.tateNorm_le_zpow_iff` (characterisation): For n ∈ ℤ: α_d(x) ≤ rⁿ ↔ x ∈ ϖⁿ·A₀.
- `Huber.tateNorm_hasBasis_nhds_zero` (compatibility): The balls {x : α_d(x) < ε}, ε > 0, form a basis of neighbourhoods of 0 for the topology of A: α_d defines the topology of A.
- `Huber.tateNorm_eq_zero_iff` (characterisation): α_d(x) = 0 ↔ x ∈ closure {0}; α_d is a norm iff A is T2.
- `Huber.tateNorm_equiv_of_ringOfDefinition` (equivalence): For two data differing only in the ring of definition there is k with α' ≤ r⁻ᵏ·α and α ≤ r⁻ᵏ·α'.
- `Huber.tateNorm_rpow` (relation): Changing r to r' (same A₀, ϖ): α_{d'} = α_d ^ (log r' / log r).
- `Huber.tateNorm_map_le` (functoriality): For a continuous ring homomorphism φ : A → B of Tate rings and data d on A, d' = (B₀, φ(ϖ), r) on B with φ(A₀) ⊆ B₀: α_{d'}(φ x) ≤ α_d(x).

*Unit tests.*

- `tateNorm_padic` (computation): For A = ℚ_p with A₀ = ℤ_p, ϖ = p and r = 1/p, α_d(x) = |x|_p for every x.
- `tateNorm_not_multiplicative` (non-example): For A = ℚ_p with A₀ = ℤ_p, ϖ = p² and r = 1/p: α_d(p) = 1 and α_d(p²) = 1/p ≠ α_d(p)², so α_d is neither multiplicative nor power-multiplicative although A is a field; a definition expecting α_d to be the absolute value of the field fails this test.
- `tateNorm_zero_ring` (degenerate): On the zero ring (a Tate ring with A₀ = 0 and ϖ = 0 = 1) α_d is 0.
- `tateNorm_banachAlgebra` (compatibility): For a Banach algebra (A, ‖·‖) over a complete nonarchimedean field K with ‖cy‖ = |c|‖y‖, A₀ the unit ball, ϖ ∈ K and r = |ϖ|: ‖x‖ ≤ α_d(x) < r⁻¹‖x‖.
- `tateNorm_le_pow_iff_tateAlgebra` (characterisation): For A = K⟨T⟩, A₀ = K°⟨T⟩, ϖ ∈ K° with 0 < |ϖ| < 1 and n ≥ 0: α_d(f) ≤ rⁿ iff every coefficient of f lies in ϖⁿK°.

*Acceptance.*

- For A = ℚ_p, A₀ = ℤ_p, ϖ = p and r = 1/p the norm is the p-adic absolute value.
- For a Banach algebra (A, ‖·‖) over a complete nonarchimedean field K with ‖cy‖ = |c|·‖y‖ (c ∈ K), A₀ the unit ball, ϖ ∈ K with 0 < |ϖ| < 1 and r = |ϖ|: ‖x‖ ≤ α_d(x) < r⁻¹‖x‖ for all x, so α_d is equivalent to ‖·‖.

*Uses.* Kedlaya–Liu, Remark 2.4.4 — a Tate f-adic ring is given the structure of a Banach ring by this norm, so the Banach-ring statements of Kedlaya–Liu §§2.3–2.8 apply to complete Tate Huber rings; Hansen–Kedlaya, Remark 2.11 — every Tate Huber ring can be promoted to a Banach ring; bounded Banach morphisms correspond to continuous Huber morphisms; AdicSpacesPartII:R0/spectral-seminorm — the spectral seminorm is the smoothing lim α_d(xⁿ)^{1/n} of α_d; AdicSpacesPartII:R3/uniform-iff-power-bound, R3/glueing-square — the Banach norm of a complete Tate ring used in Kedlaya–Liu's uniformity criteria and strictness estimates.

*Depends on* library: `TauCeti.Huber.IsTateRing`, `TauCeti.Huber.PairOfDefinition`, `TauCeti.Huber.IsPseudoUniformizer`, `TauCeti.Huber.IsPseudoUniformizer.hasBasis_nhds_zero`, `RingSeminorm`, `IsNonarchimedean`.

*Sources.* KedlayaLiu-RelativeFoundations-2015, §2.4, Remark 2.4.4, p. 38; HansenKedlaya-SheafinessCriteria, §2, Remark 2.11, p. 4; Wedhorn-AdicSpaces-2019, §6.2, Proposition 6.14, p. 48.

#### `Huber.spectralSeminorm` — The spectral seminorm of a Tate ring

*Node* `AdicSpacesPartII:R0/spectral-seminorm` (definition); module `TauCeti/RingTheory/Huber/Uniform/SpectralSeminorm`.

Let A be a Tate ring with a norm datum d = (A₀, ϖ, r) and norm α_d (AdicSpacesPartII:R0/tate-ring-norm). The *spectral seminorm* of (A, d) is |x|_sp := lim_{n→∞} α_d(xⁿ)^{1/n} = inf_{n≥1} α_d(xⁿ)^{1/n} (Kedlaya–Liu Definition 2.1.9; the limit exists by Fekete's lemma), which is Mathlib's `smoothingSeminorm α_d` (defined because α_d(1) ≤ 1 and α_d is nonarchimedean). It is a power-multiplicative nonarchimedean ring seminorm (Mathlib `IsPowMul`: |xⁿ|_sp = |x|_spⁿ for n ≥ 1) with |x|_sp ≤ α_d(x). It does not change when A₀ is replaced by another ring of definition containing ϖ (equivalent norms have the same spectral seminorm), and replacing r by r' raises it to the power log r'/log r. Intrinsic properties: |x|_sp < 1 iff x is topologically nilpotent; |x|_sp ≤ 1 for every power-bounded x; the kernel {x : |x|_sp = 0} is the ideal ⋂ₙ ϖⁿ·A°° (A°° the topologically nilpotent elements), it contains the nilradical and the closure of {0}; |1|_sp = 1 if A is Hausdorff and nonzero. Functoriality: if φ : A → B is a continuous ring homomorphism of Tate rings and B carries a datum (B₀, φ(ϖ), r) with φ(A₀) ⊆ B₀ (such B₀ exists because φ is adic), then |φ(x)|_sp ≤ |x|_sp. Pinned convention: the Gel'fand-spectrum formula |x|_sp = max_{β ∈ M(A)} β(x) (Berkovich) is not part of this node; it is the input of AdicSpacesPartII:R3/uniform-spectral-seminorm. Lean name: `Huber.spectralSeminorm d`.

*Hypotheses.* A is a Tate ring with a norm datum d = (A₀, ϖ, r) (AdicSpacesPartII:R0/tate-ring-norm).

*Construction and proof outline.*

1. Definition: `smoothingSeminorm α_d` with the hypotheses α_d(1) ≤ 1 and `IsNonarchimedean α_d` (AdicSpacesPartII:R0/tate-ring-norm, API tateNorm_one_le, isNonarchimedean_tateNorm); the limit formula is Mathlib `tendsto_smoothingFun_of_map_one_le_one`, power-multiplicativity is `isPowMul_smoothingFun`, and |x|_sp ≤ α_d(x) is `smoothingFun_le_self`.
2. Independence of A₀: if α' ≤ Cα then α'(xⁿ)^{1/n} ≤ C^{1/n}α(xⁿ)^{1/n}, and C^{1/n} → 1 (tate-ring-norm, API tateNorm_equiv_of_ringOfDefinition); the r-dependence follows from tateNorm_rpow.
3. |x|_sp < 1 iff x ∈ A°°: if |x|_sp < 1 then α_d(x^N) < 1 for some N, so α_d(x^{Nk+j}) ≤ α_d(x^N)^k α_d(x^j) → 0 and xⁿ → 0 (α_d defines the topology); conversely xⁿ → 0 gives α_d(x^N) ≤ r for some N and |x|_sp ≤ α_d(x^N)^{1/N} < 1 (Mathlib `smoothingFun_le`). Power-bounded x have bounded α_d(xⁿ), so |x|_sp ≤ 1.
4. Kernel: |x|_sp = 0 implies |ϖ⁻ⁿx|_sp ≤ |ϖ⁻¹|_spⁿ·|x|_sp = 0 < 1, so ϖ⁻ⁿx ∈ A°° for all n; conversely x ∈ ϖⁿA°° gives |x|_sp ≤ |ϖ|_spⁿ < rⁿ. Nilpotents and the closure of {0} (where α_d = 0) lie in the kernel. If A is Hausdorff and nonzero, α_d(1) > 0 and α_d(1ⁿ) = α_d(1), so |1|_sp = 1.
5. Functoriality: φ is adic because A is Tate (AdicSpacesPartII:R0/adic-ring-homomorphism, API IsAdicHom.of_isTateRing), giving a ring of definition B₀ ⊇ φ(A₀); φ(ϖ) is a pseudouniformiser of B; α_{d'}(φ x) ≤ α_d(x) (tate-ring-norm, API tateNorm_map_le), and smoothing is monotone.

*API.*

- `Huber.spectralSeminorm` (constructor): The power-multiplicative ring seminorm |·|_sp : RingSeminorm A of a norm datum d, defined as smoothingSeminorm (tateNorm d).
- `Huber.spectralSeminorm_apply` (characterisation): |x|_sp = lim_{n→∞} α_d(xⁿ)^{1/n} = ⨅ n ≥ 1, α_d(xⁿ)^{1/n}.
- `Huber.spectralSeminorm_eq_smoothingSeminorm` (compatibility): spectralSeminorm d = smoothingSeminorm (tateNorm d) _ _ (Mathlib).
- `Huber.isPowMul_spectralSeminorm` (structure): IsPowMul |·|_sp.
- `Huber.spectralSeminorm_le_tateNorm` (relation): |x|_sp ≤ α_d(x).
- `Huber.spectralSeminorm_eq_of_ringOfDefinition` (equivalence): Two data differing only in the ring of definition have the same spectral seminorm.
- `Huber.spectralSeminorm_rpow` (relation): Changing r to r': |x|_sp' = |x|_sp ^ (log r' / log r).
- `Huber.spectralSeminorm_lt_one_iff` (characterisation): |x|_sp < 1 ↔ IsTopologicallyNilpotent x.
- `Huber.spectralSeminorm_le_one_of_isPowerBounded` (relation): IsPowerBounded x → |x|_sp ≤ 1.
- `Huber.spectralSeminorm_eq_zero_iff` (characterisation): |x|_sp = 0 ↔ ∀ n, ϖ⁻ⁿx is topologically nilpotent; the kernel is an ideal containing the nilradical and the closure of {0}.
- `Huber.spectralSeminorm_one` (simp): |1|_sp = 1 if A is Hausdorff and nontrivial.
- `Huber.spectralSeminorm_map_le` (functoriality): For continuous φ : A → B of Tate rings with a datum (B₀, φ(ϖ), r), φ(A₀) ⊆ B₀: |φ x|_sp ≤ |x|_sp.
- `Huber.spectralSeminorm_eq_spectralNorm` (compatibility): For a finite extension L/K of a complete nonarchimedean field with the unit-ball datum: |·|_sp = spectralNorm K L.

*Unit tests.*

- `spectralSeminorm_tateAlgebra` (computation): For A = K⟨T⟩ with A₀ = K°⟨T⟩, ϖ ∈ K° (0 < |ϖ| < 1) and r = |ϖ|: |Σ aₙTⁿ|_sp = sup |aₙ| (the Gauss norm).
- `spectralSeminorm_dualNumbers` (non-example): For A = K[ε]/(ε²) with A₀ = K° ⊕ K°ε: |ε|_sp = 0 while α_d(ε) = 1; a definition taking |·|_sp to be the norm α_d, or claiming it is always a norm, fails.
- `spectralSeminorm_eq_spectralNorm` (compatibility): For a finite extension L of a complete nontrivially normed nonarchimedean field K, with A₀ the unit ball of L, ϖ ∈ K and r = |ϖ|: |·|_sp equals Mathlib's `spectralNorm K L` (both are power-multiplicative K-algebra norms on L; Mathlib `spectralNorm_unique`).
- `spectralSeminorm_lt_one_iff_test` (characterisation): In ℚ_p⟨T⟩: |pT|_sp < 1 and pT is topologically nilpotent, while |T|_sp = 1 and T is power-bounded but not topologically nilpotent.
- `spectralSeminorm_zero_ring` (degenerate): On the zero ring |·|_sp = 0; on a Hausdorff nonzero A, |1|_sp = 1.

*Acceptance.*

- For A = K⟨T⟩, A₀ = K°⟨T⟩, ϖ ∈ K° with 0 < |ϖ| < 1 and r = |ϖ|, |f|_sp is the Gauss norm sup |aₙ|.
- For A = K[ε]/(ε²) (finite free over K, A₀ = K° ⊕ K°ε) |ε|_sp = 0 while α_d(ε) = 1.

*Uses.* Kedlaya–Liu, Definition 2.1.9 and Definition 2.8.1(b) — the spectral seminorm and the definition of uniform Banach rings as those whose norm is equivalent to it; Hansen–Kedlaya, Definition 2.10 — uniformity as 'the spectral seminorm defines the same topology'; Kedlaya–Liu, Definition 2.8.13 — the uniformization is the separated completion for the spectral seminorm (AdicSpacesPartII:R0/spectral-topology, R0/uniformization); AdicSpacesPartII:R3/uniform-spectral-seminorm — spectral norms of uniform rings, submetric maps and the isometry criterion (Kedlaya–Liu Remark 2.8.3); AdicSpacesPartII:R3/uniform-iff-power-bound — criterion (b) of Kedlaya–Liu Definition 2.8.1; PerfectoidSpaces:P8 request to AdicSpacesPartII:R3 — 'for uniform Banach rings the spectral seminorm is the supremum over the spectrum, so a map of uniform rings surjective on spectra is isometric'.

*Depends on* within R0a: `Huber.tateNorm`, `Huber.IsAdicHom`; library: `smoothingSeminorm`, `isPowMul_smoothingFun`, `smoothingFun_le_self`, `smoothingFun_le`, `tendsto_smoothingFun_of_map_one_le_one`, `IsPowMul`, `IsTopologicallyNilpotent`, `TauCeti.Huber.IsPowerBounded`, `spectralNorm`, `spectralNorm_unique`.

*Sources.* KedlayaLiu-RelativeFoundations-2015, §2.1, Definition 2.1.9, p. 26; KedlayaLiu-RelativeFoundations-2015, §2.1, Definition 2.1.9, p. 26; HansenKedlaya-SheafinessCriteria, §2, Definition 2.10, p. 4.

#### `Huber.SpectralTop` — The spectral topology of a Tate ring

*Node* `AdicSpacesPartII:R0/spectral-topology` (definition); module `TauCeti/RingTheory/Huber/Uniform/SpectralTopology`.

Let A be a Tate ring. The *spectral topology* on A is the topology defined by a spectral seminorm |·|_sp (AdicSpacesPartII:R0/spectral-seminorm): the ring topology whose neighbourhoods of 0 are generated by the balls {x : |x|_sp < ε}, ε > 0. For every pseudouniformiser ϖ of A the sets ϖⁿ·A°° (n ≥ 0; A°° the ideal of topologically nilpotent elements) form a basis of neighbourhoods of 0 for it; in particular it does not depend on the norm datum. Write A_sp for A with this topology (Lean: the type synonym `Huber.SpectralTop A`, with the ring equivalence `toSpectralTop : A ≃+* SpectralTop A`). Then: (i) the identity A → A_sp is continuous; (ii) A_sp is a Tate ring with pseudouniformiser ϖ and pair of definition (A_sp,≤1, ϖ·A_sp,≤1), where A_sp,≤1 = {x : |x|_sp ≤ 1}; (iii) the topologically nilpotent elements of A_sp are those of A, and A_sp° = {x : |x|_sp ≤ 1} is bounded, so A_sp is uniform (Hansen–Kedlaya Definition 2.3, the anchor's Layer 4.2 predicate); (iv) every ring of integral elements A⁺ of A is a ring of integral elements of A_sp, giving a Tau Ceti `Pair` on A_sp and a morphism of Huber pairs (A, A⁺) → (A_sp, A⁺); (v) every continuous ring homomorphism φ : A → B of Tate rings is continuous as a map A_sp → B_sp; (vi) the identity A → A_sp is a homeomorphism iff A° is bounded, i.e. iff A is uniform. Lean name: `Huber.SpectralTop A`.

*Hypotheses.* A is a Tate ring (Tau Ceti `IsTateRing`).

*Construction and proof outline.*

1. Basis: ϖⁿ·A°° ⊆ {|x|_sp < rⁿ} because |ϖⁿy|_sp ≤ |ϖ|_spⁿ|y|_sp ≤ rⁿ|y|_sp and |y|_sp < 1 for y ∈ A°°; and {|x|_sp < rⁿ·|ϖ⁻¹|_sp⁻ⁿ} ⊆ ϖⁿ·A°° because |ϖ⁻ⁿx|_sp ≤ |ϖ⁻¹|_spⁿ|x|_sp < 1 (AdicSpacesPartII:R0/spectral-seminorm, API spectralSeminorm_lt_one_iff). A°° is an additive subgroup (Tau Ceti `topologicallyNilpotentIdeal`, an ideal of A°). Changing ϖ to ϖ' gives the same filter since ϖ'^m ∈ ϖ·A° and ϖ^m ∈ ϖ'·A° for m ≫ 0.
2. (i): A°° ⊇ ϖ·A₀ is open in A, so each ϖⁿA°° is an open subgroup of A.
3. (ii),(iii): A_sp,≤1 is a subring (|·|_sp is a nonarchimedean submultiplicative seminorm with |1|_sp ≤ 1), open (it contains A°°) and bounded (ϖⁿ⁺¹·A_sp,≤1 ⊆ ϖⁿA°°); ϖ is a unit with ϖⁿ ∈ ϖⁿ⁻¹A°°; so (A_sp,≤1, ϖ) is a pair of definition. If x is power-bounded in A_sp then |x|_spⁿ = |xⁿ|_sp is bounded, so |x|_sp ≤ 1; conversely |x|_sp ≤ 1 puts all powers in the bounded set A_sp,≤1.
4. (iv): A⁺ ⊆ A° ⊆ A_sp,≤1 = A_sp°; A⁺ contains A°° (Tau Ceti `IsRingOfIntegralElements.mem_of_isTopologicallyNilpotent`), which is open in A_sp; integral closedness does not involve the topology.
5. (v): φ maps A°° into B°° and ϖ to a pseudouniformiser φ(ϖ) of B (φ is adic, AdicSpacesPartII:R0/adic-ring-homomorphism), so φ(ϖⁿA°°) ⊆ φ(ϖ)ⁿB°°, a basic neighbourhood of B_sp.
6. (vi): if A° is bounded it is a ring of definition, the sets ϖⁿA° are a basis of A (Tau Ceti `IsPseudoUniformizer.hasBasis_nhds_zero`) and ϖⁿ⁺¹A° ⊆ ϖⁿA°° ⊆ ϖⁿA°; conversely equal topologies give A° = A_sp°, which is bounded by (iii).

*API.*

- `Huber.SpectralTop` (constructor): The type synonym SpectralTop A := A with the ring structure of A and the topology of |·|_sp; toSpectralTop : A ≃+* SpectralTop A.
- `Huber.SpectralTop.hasBasis_nhds_zero` (characterisation): For a pseudouniformiser ϖ, the sets toSpectralTop '' (ϖⁿ • A°°) form a basis of 𝓝 0 in SpectralTop A.
- `Huber.SpectralTop.nhds_zero_eq_seminorm` (compatibility): For every norm datum d, the topology of SpectralTop A is the topology of spectralSeminorm d (independent of d).
- `Huber.SpectralTop.continuous_toSpectralTop` (projection): toSpectralTop : A → SpectralTop A is continuous.
- `Huber.SpectralTop.isTateRing` (instance): SpectralTop A is a Tate ring, with pseudouniformiser ϖ.
- `Huber.SpectralTop.pairOfDefinition` (structure): The pair of definition ({|x|_sp ≤ 1}, ϖ·{|x|_sp ≤ 1}).
- `Huber.SpectralTop.isTopologicallyNilpotent_iff` (simp): toSpectralTop x is topologically nilpotent ↔ x is.
- `Huber.SpectralTop.powerBoundedSubring_eq` (characterisation): (SpectralTop A)° = {x : |x|_sp ≤ 1}.
- `Huber.SpectralTop.isBounded_powerBoundedSubring` (instance): (SpectralTop A)° is bounded: SpectralTop A is uniform (the anchor's Layer 4.2 predicate).
- `Huber.SpectralTop.pair` (constructor): A Huber pair (A, A⁺) gives the Huber pair (SpectralTop A, A⁺) and the morphism Pair.Hom (A, A⁺) (SpectralTop A, A⁺) with underlying map toSpectralTop.
- `Huber.SpectralTop.map` (functoriality): A continuous φ : A →+* B of Tate rings induces a continuous SpectralTop A →+* SpectralTop B; map_id, map_comp.
- `Huber.SpectralTop.homeomorph_of_isBounded` (equivalence): If A° is bounded, toSpectralTop is a homeomorphism; conversely a homeomorphism forces A° bounded.

*Unit tests.*

- `spectralTop_uniform_tateAlgebra` (degenerate): For A = K⟨T⟩ the identity K⟨T⟩ → SpectralTop K⟨T⟩ is a homeomorphism (K°⟨T⟩ = A° is bounded).
- `spectralTop_dualNumbers` (computation): For A = K[ε]/(ε²) with the topology of a finite free K-module, the closure of {0} in SpectralTop A is K·ε, so SpectralTop A is not Hausdorff while A is.
- `spectralTop_weightedSeries` (non-example): Let A = {Σ aₙTⁿ ∈ K⟦T⟧ : |aₙ|(n+1) → 0} with the complete submultiplicative norm ‖f‖ = sup |aₙ|(n+1). Its spectral seminorm is the Gauss norm sup |aₙ| (a norm), T ∈ (SpectralTop A)° while T ∉ A° (‖Tⁿ‖ = n + 1), and SpectralTop A is not complete; so the identity A → SpectralTop A is not a homeomorphism although both are Hausdorff, and A is not uniform.
- `spectralTop_isUniform` (characterisation): For every Tate ring A, (SpectralTop A)° is bounded, i.e. SpectralTop A is uniform in the sense of Hansen–Kedlaya Definition 2.3.

*Acceptance.*

- For K⟨T⟩ (uniform) the identity K⟨T⟩ → K⟨T⟩_sp is a homeomorphism.
- For K[ε]/(ε²) the closure of {0} in the spectral topology is Kε.

*Uses.* Kedlaya–Liu, Definition 2.8.13 — 'the separated completion of A for the spectral seminorm': A_sp is the space being completed; Kedlaya–Liu, Remark 2.3.11(c) — A need not be complete for its spectral seminorm even when it is a norm, so the uniformization must complete A_sp; Hansen–Kedlaya, Definition 2.3 and Remark 2.11 — uniformity of a Huber ring (A° bounded) agrees with uniformity of a Banach ring (spectral seminorm defines the topology): API homeomorph_of_isBounded; AdicSpacesPartII:R0/spectral-topology-cont-eq — A_sp has the same continuous valuations and adic spectrum; AdicSpacesPartII:R0/uniformization — the uniformization is the Hausdorff completion of A_sp.

*Depends on* within R0a: `Huber.spectralSeminorm`, `Huber.tateNorm`, `Huber.IsAdicHom`; anchor stages: `layer-4-sheafiness-and-tate-acyclicity`; library: `TauCeti.Huber.IsTateRing`, `TauCeti.Huber.PairOfDefinition`, `TauCeti.Huber.powerBoundedSubring`, `TauCeti.Huber.IsBounded`, `TauCeti.Huber.IsPseudoUniformizer.hasBasis_nhds_zero`, `TauCeti.Huber.IsRingOfIntegralElements.mem_of_isTopologicallyNilpotent`, `TauCeti.Huber.topologicallyNilpotentIdeal`, `TauCeti.Huber.Pair`, `TauCeti.Huber.Pair.Hom`, `IsTopologicallyNilpotent`.

*Sources.* KedlayaLiu-RelativeFoundations-2015, §2.3, Remark 2.3.11(c), p. 36; HansenKedlaya-SheafinessCriteria, §2, Definition 2.3, p. 3; HansenKedlaya-SheafinessCriteria, §2, Remark 2.11, p. 4; KedlayaLiu-RelativeFoundations-2015, §2.8, Definition 2.8.1(b),(d), p. 59.

#### `Huber.SpectralTop.cont_eq` — The spectral topology has the same continuous valuations, adic spectrum and rational subsets

*Node* `AdicSpacesPartII:R0/spectral-topology-cont-eq` (lemma); module `TauCeti/RingTheory/Huber/Uniform/SpectralTopology`.

Let A be a Tate ring and A_sp = `Huber.SpectralTop A` (AdicSpacesPartII:R0/spectral-topology). A valuation on A is continuous for the topology of A iff it is continuous for the spectral topology: Cont(A_sp) = Cont(A) as subsets of Spv(A) (Tau Ceti `ValuationSpectrum.cont`). Consequently, for every ring of integral elements A⁺ of A, Spa(A_sp, A⁺) = Spa(A, A⁺) as subspaces of Spv(A) (Tau Ceti `ValuationSpectrum.spa A⁺` for the two topologies), and for every finite T ⊆ A and s ∈ A the rational subsets R(T/s) (Tau Ceti `ValuationSpectrum.rationalSubset A⁺ T s`) of the two spectra are equal; a finite subset generates an open ideal of A iff it generates an open ideal of A_sp (in both Tate rings: iff it generates the unit ideal).

*Hypotheses.* A is a Tate ring; A⁺ is a ring of integral elements of A.

*Proof outline.*

1. Cont(A_sp) ⊆ Cont(A): the identity A → A_sp is continuous (AdicSpacesPartII:R0/spectral-topology (i)), and a valuation all of whose sets {x : v(x) < γ} are open for the coarser topology has them open for the finer one.
2. Cont(A) ⊆ Cont(A_sp): let v ∈ Cont(A) and γ ≠ 0 in its value group; for a pseudouniformiser ϖ some power satisfies v(ϖ)ⁿ < γ (Tau Ceti `Valuation.exists_pow_lt_of_isTopologicallyNilpotent`, {v < γ} being a neighbourhood of 0), and v(y) < 1 for every topologically nilpotent y (Tau Ceti `Valuation.IsContinuous.lt_one_of_isTopologicallyNilpotent`); so the subgroup {x : v(x) < γ} contains ϖⁿ·A°°, a neighbourhood of 0 in A_sp (AdicSpacesPartII:R0/spectral-topology, basis), and is open in A_sp.
3. Spa and rational subsets are defined inside Spv(A) from Cont, the plus ring and the elements T, s only (Tau Ceti `ValuationSpectrum.spa_def`, `ValuationSpectrum.rationalSubset`), and the subspace topology comes from Spv(A), which does not depend on the topology of A; so they coincide. In a Tate ring an ideal is open iff it is the unit ideal (Tau Ceti `IsTateRing.isOpen_iff_eq_top`), for both topologies.

*Acceptance.*

- For A = K[ε]/(ε²) with A⁺ = K° + Kε and K = ℚ_p, Spa(A_sp, A⁺) = Spa(A, A⁺) is a single point, the valuation a + bε ↦ |a|_p.
- For uniform A the statement is the identity (A_sp = A by AdicSpacesPartII:R0/spectral-topology (vi)).

*Uses.* AdicSpacesPartII:R0/uniformization — Spa(A^u, A^{u+}) → Spa(A, A⁺) is a homeomorphism identifying rational subsets (Kedlaya–Liu Definition 2.8.13).

*Depends on* within R0a: `Huber.SpectralTop`; library: `TauCeti.ValuationSpectrum.cont`, `TauCeti.ValuationSpectrum.spa`, `TauCeti.ValuationSpectrum.spa_def`, `TauCeti.ValuationSpectrum.rationalSubset`, `Valuation.IsContinuous.lt_one_of_isTopologicallyNilpotent`, `Valuation.exists_pow_lt_of_isTopologicallyNilpotent`, `TauCeti.Huber.IsTateRing.isOpen_iff_eq_top`.

*Sources.* KedlayaLiu-RelativeFoundations-2015, §2.8, Definition 2.8.13, p. 63; KedlayaLiu-RelativeFoundations-2015, §2.4, Definition 2.4.3, p. 38.

#### `Huber.Pair.uniformization` — The uniformization of a Tate Huber pair

*Node* `AdicSpacesPartII:R0/uniformization` (construction); module `TauCeti/RingTheory/Huber/Uniform/Uniformization`.

Let (A, A⁺) be a Huber pair (Tau Ceti `Pair`) with A a Tate ring. Its *uniformization* is the Huber pair (A^u, A^{u+}) where A^u is the Hausdorff completion of A_sp = `Huber.SpectralTop A` (AdicSpacesPartII:R0/spectral-topology; Tau Ceti `IsHuberRing.completion`, `IsTateRing.completion`), i.e. the separated completion of A for its spectral seminorm (Kedlaya–Liu Definition 2.8.13), and A^{u+} is the closure of the image of A⁺ in A^u. It comes with the morphism of Huber pairs ι : (A, A⁺) → (A^u, A^{u+}), the composite of the continuous identity A → A_sp and the completion map. Properties: (a) (A^u, A^{u+}) is a complete Hausdorff Huber pair, A^u is a Tate ring, and A^u is uniform (A^{u°} is bounded; the continuous extension of |·|_sp to A^u is a power-multiplicative norm defining its topology); (b) ι has dense image and kernel {x : |x|_sp = 0}; (c) for every complete Hausdorff Huber pair (B, B⁺) with B° bounded and every morphism of Huber pairs φ : (A, A⁺) → (B, B⁺) there is exactly one morphism φ^u : (A^u, A^{u+}) → (B, B⁺) with φ^u ∘ ι = φ, so uniformization is left adjoint to the inclusion of complete Hausdorff uniform Tate Huber pairs into Tate Huber pairs; (d) Spa(ι) : Spa(A^u, A^{u+}) → Spa(A, A⁺) is a homeomorphism under which rational subsets correspond to rational subsets; (e) if A is complete, Hausdorff and uniform, ι is an isomorphism. Pinned conventions: morphisms are Tau Ceti `Pair.Hom` (continuous, plus rings respected), which for Banach rings are the bounded morphisms (Hansen–Kedlaya Remark 2.11); the plus ring is the closure of the image of A⁺, not the image. Lean name: `Huber.Pair.uniformization`.

*Hypotheses.* (A, A⁺) is a Huber pair and A is a Tate ring. For the universal property: (B, B⁺) is a complete Hausdorff Huber pair with B° bounded.

*Construction and proof outline.*

1. A_sp is a uniform Tate ring, A⁺ is a ring of integral elements of A_sp and the identity is a morphism of Huber pairs (A, A⁺) → (A_sp, A⁺) (AdicSpacesPartII:R0/spectral-topology).
2. Completion: Completion(A_sp) is a complete Hausdorff Tate ring with the completed pair of definition (Tau Ceti `IsHuberRing.completion`, `IsTateRing.completion`, `PairOfDefinition.completion`); the closure of the image of A⁺ is a ring of integral elements (anchor Layer 0: completion of Huber pairs, Wedhorn Lemma 7.47).
3. Uniformity: |·|_sp is uniformly continuous on A_sp and extends to a seminorm β on A^u; β is power-multiplicative (β(xⁿ) = β(x)ⁿ passes to limits), a norm (A^u is separated for it) and defines the topology of A^u; a power-bounded x has β(x)ⁿ = β(xⁿ) bounded, so A^{u°} ⊆ {β ≤ 1}, which is bounded.
4. Dense image and kernel: Mathlib `UniformSpace.Completion.denseRange_coe`; the kernel of A_sp → Completion(A_sp) is the closure of {0} in A_sp, which is {x : |x|_sp = 0} (AdicSpacesPartII:R0/spectral-seminorm, API spectralSeminorm_eq_zero_iff).
5. Universal property: φ is continuous as a map A_sp → B_sp (AdicSpacesPartII:R0/spectral-topology (v)) and B_sp = B because B° is bounded (spectral-topology (vi)); B being complete and Hausdorff, φ extends uniquely to a continuous ring homomorphism A^u → B (Mathlib `UniformSpace.Completion.extensionHom`, `extensionHom_coe`); it maps A^{u+} into B⁺ since B⁺ is an open, hence closed, subgroup containing φ(A⁺). Uniqueness: two continuous extensions agree on the dense image of ι. B is Tate because it receives a continuous map from a Tate ring (AdicSpacesPartII:R0/adic-ring-homomorphism, API IsAdicHom.of_isTateRing).
6. Spa: the completion morphism induces a homeomorphism Spa(A^u, A^{u+}) → Spa(A_sp, A⁺) identifying rational subsets (anchor Layer 0: Spa of the completion, Wedhorn Proposition 7.48), and Spa(A_sp, A⁺) = Spa(A, A⁺) with the same rational subsets (AdicSpacesPartII:R0/spectral-topology-cont-eq); preimages of rational subsets are Tau Ceti `ValuationSpectrum.spaComap_preimage_rationalSubset`.
7. (e): for complete Hausdorff uniform A, A_sp = A (spectral-topology (vi)) and the completion map of a complete Hausdorff ring is an isomorphism.

*API.*

- `Huber.Pair.uniformization` (constructor): The complete Hausdorff Huber pair (A^u, A^{u+}) on Completion (SpectralTop A) with plus ring the closure of the image of A⁺.
- `Huber.Pair.toUniformization` (projection): The morphism of Huber pairs ι : (A, A⁺) → (A^u, A^{u+}).
- `Huber.Pair.uniformization.isTateRing` (instance): A^u is a complete Hausdorff Tate ring.
- `Huber.Pair.uniformization.isBounded_powerBoundedSubring` (instance): A^{u°} is bounded: A^u is uniform (the anchor's Layer 4.2 predicate).
- `Huber.Pair.uniformization.lift` (universal-property): For a complete Hausdorff pair (B, B⁺) with B° bounded and φ : Pair.Hom (A, A⁺) (B, B⁺), the morphism φ^u : Pair.Hom (A^u, A^{u+}) (B, B⁺).
- `Huber.Pair.uniformization.lift_comp_toUniformization` (universal-property): (lift φ).comp ι = φ.
- `Huber.Pair.uniformization.hom_ext` (extensionality): Two morphisms out of (A^u, A^{u+}) that agree after composing with ι are equal.
- `Huber.Pair.uniformization.map` (functoriality): A morphism of Tate Huber pairs induces a morphism of uniformizations commuting with ι; map_id, map_comp.
- `Huber.Pair.uniformization.denseRange_toUniformization` (characterisation): ι has dense range, and ι x = 0 ↔ |x|_sp = 0.
- `Huber.Pair.uniformization.plus_eq_closure` (characterisation): A^{u+} is the closure of ι(A⁺).
- `Huber.Pair.uniformization.extendSpectralSeminorm` (relation): |·|_sp extends continuously to a power-multiplicative norm on A^u defining its topology.
- `Huber.Pair.uniformization.spaComap_homeomorph` (equivalence): Spa(ι) : Spa(A^u, A^{u+}) → Spa(A, A⁺) is a homeomorphism.
- `Huber.Pair.uniformization.spaComap_preimage_rationalSubset` (compatibility): Spa(ι)⁻¹(R(T/s)) = R(ι(T)/ι(s)), and every rational subset of Spa(A^u, A^{u+}) is of this form.
- `Huber.Pair.uniformization.isIso_of_isUniform` (compatibility): If A is complete, Hausdorff and A° is bounded, ι is an isomorphism of Huber pairs.

*Unit tests.*

- `uniformization_dualNumbers` (computation): For K complete nonarchimedean and (A, A⁺) = (K[ε]/(ε²), K° + Kε): (A, A⁺)^u ≅ (K, K°) with ι(a + bε) = a.
- `uniformization_weightedSeries` (non-example): For A = {Σ aₙTⁿ ∈ K⟦T⟧ : |aₙ|(n+1) → 0} with ‖f‖ = sup |aₙ|(n+1) and any ring of integral elements A⁺: the spectral seminorm is the Gauss norm, a norm, yet A^u ≅ K⟨T⟩ ≠ A; a definition taking only the Hausdorff quotient of A for |·|_sp (no completion) gives a ring that is not complete.
- `uniformization_tateAlgebra` (degenerate): (K⟨T⟩, K°⟨T⟩)^u = (K⟨T⟩, K°⟨T⟩) and ι is the identity; the uniformization of the zero pair is the zero pair.
- `uniformization_lift_dualNumbers` (characterisation): For (A, A⁺) = (K[ε]/(ε²), K° + Kε) and the uniform pair (K, K°), the morphism a + bε ↦ a factors uniquely through ι, and every morphism from (A, A⁺) to a complete Hausdorff pair with bounded power-bounded subring kills ε.
- `uniformization_banach` (compatibility): For a Banach ring A containing a topologically nilpotent unit, the ring A^u is Kedlaya–Liu's uniformization (separated completion for the spectral seminorm) and A^{u+} is their 'completion of the image of A⁺'.

*Acceptance.*

- (K[ε]/(ε²), K° + Kε)^u = (K, K°) with ι the reduction map ε ↦ 0.
- For A = {Σ aₙTⁿ ∈ K⟦T⟧ : |aₙ|(n+1) → 0} with ‖f‖ = sup |aₙ|(n+1), A^u = K⟨T⟩ and ι is the inclusion.
- For a complete Hausdorff uniform (A, A⁺), for instance (K⟨T⟩, K°⟨T⟩), ι is an isomorphism.

*Uses.* Kedlaya–Liu, Definition 2.8.13 — uniformization is left adjoint to the forgetful functor from uniform (adic) Banach rings, and Spa is unchanged; AdicEtaleGeometry:A0 (stage description, supplier contract) — 'In the cases in which uniformization is necessary, construct it and prove its universal property separately; a separated completion need not be uniform.'; Hansen–Kedlaya, proof of Proposition 6.7 — the uniform completion of A ⊕ A modulo {(az, −ay)} adjoins x with x² = y, x³ = z to a uniform sheafy ring; Hansen–Kedlaya, Example 10.5 — the uniform completion of B ⊗ A receives a dense-image map from a perfectoid B and is therefore perfectoid; AdicSpacesPartII:R0/uniform-completed-tensor-product — the uniform completed tensor product is the uniformization of the completed tensor product; PerfectoidSpaces:P2 — fibre products of perfectoid spaces: the completed tensor product is already uniform, so the uniformization morphism is an isomorphism (API isIso_of_isUniform); AdicSpacesPartII:R3/uniform-spectral-seminorm — spectral norms of uniform rings; ι is isometric for the spectral seminorms.

*Depends on* within R0a: `Huber.SpectralTop`, `Huber.SpectralTop.cont_eq`, `Huber.spectralSeminorm`, `Huber.IsAdicHom`; anchor stages: `layer-0-topological-algebra-huber-rings-and-tate-algebras`, `layer-4-sheafiness-and-tate-acyclicity`; library: `TauCeti.Huber.Pair`, `TauCeti.Huber.Pair.Hom`, `TauCeti.Huber.Pair.Hom.spaComap`, `TauCeti.Huber.IsHuberRing.completion`, `TauCeti.Huber.IsTateRing.completion`, `TauCeti.Huber.PairOfDefinition.completion`, `TauCeti.ValuationSpectrum.spaComap_preimage_rationalSubset`, `UniformSpace.Completion`, `UniformSpace.Completion.denseRange_coe`, `UniformSpace.Completion.extensionHom`, `UniformSpace.Completion.extensionHom_coe`.

#### `Huber.Pair.uniformCompletedTensor` — The uniform completed tensor product of Tate Huber pairs

*Node* `AdicSpacesPartII:R0/uniform-completed-tensor-product` (construction); module `TauCeti/RingTheory/Huber/CompletedTensor/Uniform`.

Let (A, A⁺), (B, B⁺), (C, C⁺) be complete Hausdorff Huber pairs with A a Tate ring, and f : (A, A⁺) → (B, B⁺), g : (A, A⁺) → (C, C⁺) morphisms of Huber pairs (Tau Ceti `Pair.Hom`; f and g are adic and B, C are Tate by Wedhorn Proposition 6.25). The *uniform completed tensor product* is B ⊗̂ᵘ_A C := (B ⊗̂_A C)^u, the uniformization (AdicSpacesPartII:R0/uniformization) of the completed tensor product (AdicSpacesPartII:R0/completed-tensor-product), with inlᵘ := ι ∘ inl and inrᵘ := ι ∘ inr. Properties: (a) it is a complete Hausdorff uniform Tate Huber pair and inlᵘ ∘ f = inrᵘ ∘ g; (b) it is a pushout of (f, g) in the category of complete Hausdorff uniform Tate Huber pairs: for every such (R, R⁺) and morphisms φ : (B, B⁺) → (R, R⁺), ψ : (C, C⁺) → (R, R⁺) with φ ∘ f = ψ ∘ g there is exactly one morphism χ : B ⊗̂ᵘ_A C → (R, R⁺) with χ ∘ inlᵘ = φ and χ ∘ inrᵘ = ψ; (c) the canonical morphism ι : B ⊗̂_A C → B ⊗̂ᵘ_A C induces a homeomorphism of adic spectra identifying rational subsets; (d) ι is an isomorphism iff B ⊗̂_A C is uniform (for instance K⟨T⟩ ⊗̂_K K⟨S⟩ = K⟨T, S⟩), and it is not an isomorphism in general: ℂ_p ⊗̂_{ℚ_p} ℂ_p is not uniform (Kedlaya–Liu Remark 2.8.5). No sheafiness of B ⊗̂ᵘ_A C and no fibre-product property of its Spa is claimed. Lean name: `Huber.Pair.uniformCompletedTensor f g`.

*Hypotheses.* (A, A⁺), (B, B⁺), (C, C⁺) complete Hausdorff Huber pairs, A a Tate ring. f : (A, A⁺) → (B, B⁺), g : (A, A⁺) → (C, C⁺) morphisms of Huber pairs.

*Construction and proof outline.*

1. f and g are adic and B, C are Tate (AdicSpacesPartII:R0/adic-ring-homomorphism, API IsAdicHom.of_isTateRing), so B ⊗̂_A C is defined and is a complete Hausdorff Tate Huber pair (AdicSpacesPartII:R0/completed-tensor-product, API completedTensor.isTateRing).
2. (a), (c): uniformize (AdicSpacesPartII:R0/uniformization: uniformity, completeness, Spa homeomorphism).
3. (b): given φ, ψ into a complete Hausdorff uniform (R, R⁺) — R⁺ is closed and integrally closed — the universal property of the completed tensor product (AdicSpacesPartII:R0/completed-tensor-product-universal-property) gives a unique χ₀ : B ⊗̂_A C → (R, R⁺), and the universal property of the uniformization (R0/uniformization, lift) factors χ₀ uniquely through ι; uniqueness of χ follows from hom_ext of both constructions.
4. (d): R0/uniformization (isIso_of_isUniform) for ⇐; for ⇒ an isomorphic copy of a uniform pair is uniform. The non-example is Kedlaya–Liu Remark 2.8.5.

*API.*

- `Huber.Pair.uniformCompletedTensor` (constructor): The complete Hausdorff uniform Tate Huber pair (B ⊗̂_A C)^u.
- `Huber.Pair.uniformCompletedTensor.inl` (projection): inlᵘ : Pair.Hom (B, B⁺) (B ⊗̂ᵘ_A C).
- `Huber.Pair.uniformCompletedTensor.inr` (projection): inrᵘ : Pair.Hom (C, C⁺) (B ⊗̂ᵘ_A C).
- `Huber.Pair.uniformCompletedTensor.inl_comp` (relation): inlᵘ ∘ f = inrᵘ ∘ g.
- `Huber.Pair.uniformCompletedTensor.lift` (universal-property): For a complete Hausdorff (R, R⁺) with R° bounded and φ, ψ with φ ∘ f = ψ ∘ g: the morphism χ : B ⊗̂ᵘ_A C → (R, R⁺).
- `Huber.Pair.uniformCompletedTensor.lift_comp_inl` (universal-property): lift ∘ inlᵘ = φ and lift ∘ inrᵘ = ψ.
- `Huber.Pair.uniformCompletedTensor.hom_ext` (extensionality): Morphisms out of B ⊗̂ᵘ_A C agreeing after inlᵘ and inrᵘ are equal.
- `Huber.Pair.uniformCompletedTensor.isBounded_powerBoundedSubring` (instance): B ⊗̂ᵘ_A C is uniform.
- `Huber.Pair.uniformCompletedTensor.fromCompletedTensor` (compatibility): The morphism ι from Pair.completedTensor f g; fromCompletedTensor_isIso_iff: it is an isomorphism iff B ⊗̂_A C is uniform.
- `Huber.Pair.uniformCompletedTensor.spaHomeomorph` (equivalence): Spa(B ⊗̂ᵘ_A C) ≅ Spa(B ⊗̂_A C), identifying rational subsets.
- `Huber.Pair.uniformCompletedTensor.map` (functoriality): Morphisms of the diagrams induce morphisms of uniform completed tensor products; map_id, map_comp.
- `Huber.Pair.uniformCompletedTensor.comm` (equivalence): B ⊗̂ᵘ_A C ≅ C ⊗̂ᵘ_A B exchanging inlᵘ and inrᵘ.
- `Huber.Pair.uniformCompletedTensor.unitIso` (other): B ⊗̂ᵘ_A A ≅ B^u.

*Unit tests.*

- `uniformCompletedTensor_polydisc` (computation): For a complete nonarchimedean field K: (K⟨T⟩, K°⟨T⟩) ⊗̂ᵘ_{(K,K°)} (K⟨S⟩, K°⟨S⟩) ≅ (K⟨T, S⟩, K°⟨T, S⟩), and ι from the completed tensor product is an isomorphism.
- `uniformCompletedTensor_Cp` (non-example): For A = ℚ_p and B = C = ℂ_p the canonical morphism ℂ_p ⊗̂_{ℚ_p} ℂ_p → ℂ_p ⊗̂ᵘ_{ℚ_p} ℂ_p is not an isomorphism, because ℂ_p ⊗̂_{ℚ_p} ℂ_p is not uniform; a definition that omits the uniformization is not a pushout among uniform pairs.
- `uniformCompletedTensor_unit` (degenerate): For g = id: B ⊗̂ᵘ_A A ≅ B^u, which is (B, B⁺) when B is uniform.
- `uniformCompletedTensor_galois` (characterisation): For a finite Galois extension L/K of complete nonarchimedean fields: L ⊗̂ᵘ_K L ≅ ∏_{σ ∈ Gal(L/K)} L via x ⊗ y ↦ (x·σ(y))_σ, the σ-component being lift (id_L, σ).
- `uniformCompletedTensor_of_isUniform` (compatibility): If B ⊗̂_A C is uniform (e.g. B, C perfectoid over a perfectoid A), the canonical morphism B ⊗̂_A C → B ⊗̂ᵘ_A C is an isomorphism of Huber pairs compatible with inl, inr.

*Acceptance.*

- K⟨T⟩ ⊗̂ᵘ_K K⟨S⟩ ≅ K⟨T, S⟩ for a complete nonarchimedean field K.
- ℂ_p ⊗̂_{ℚ_p} ℂ_p → ℂ_p ⊗̂ᵘ_{ℚ_p} ℂ_p is not an isomorphism (Kedlaya–Liu Remark 2.8.5).

*Uses.* AdicEtaleGeometry:A0/supplier-contract-fibre-products — the contract lists uniformization among what Huber's Proposition 1.2.2 does not supply: 'uniformization, and any sheafiness statement for the resulting affinoid rings'; PerfectoidSpaces:P2 — fibre products of perfectoid spaces: for perfectoid B, C over perfectoid A the completed tensor product is perfectoid, in particular uniform, so B ⊗̂ᵘ_A C = B ⊗̂_A C (API fromCompletedTensor_isIso_iff); Hansen–Kedlaya, Remark 7.2 and Example 10.5 — completed tensor products do not preserve uniformity; the uniform completion of a base extension of a perfectoid frame is perfectoid, and passing to it can destroy a splitting; AdicSpacesPartII:R5/split-injection-completed-base-change — records that the sousperfectoid base change uses B ⊗̂_A C itself, not B ⊗̂ᵘ_A C (a uniform completion can destroy the splitting); Kedlaya–Liu, Definition 2.4.1 and Remark 2.8.5 — the coproduct of adic Banach rings is not uniform in general, which is why uniformization is introduced.

*Depends on* within R0a: `Huber.Pair.completedTensor`, `Huber.Pair.completedTensor.existsUnique_lift`, `Huber.Pair.uniformization`, `Huber.IsAdicHom`; anchor stages: `layer-4-sheafiness-and-tate-acyclicity`; library: `TauCeti.Huber.Pair`, `TauCeti.Huber.Pair.Hom`.

### R0a.3 Adic morphisms, finiteness classes, locally noetherian spaces

Huber's hierarchy `lfp ⊆ lft ⊆ l+wft ⊆ lwft ⊆ adic` is completed around the anchor's morphisms locally of finite type, which are Huber's and are not redefined. Morphisms locally of weakly finite type impose topological finite type on rings only; +weakly finite type controls plus rings up to a finite set and topologically nilpotent elements (the finiteness in Huber's proper morphisms); finite presentation adds a condition only over discrete affinoids.

#### `AdicSpace.IsAdic` — Adic morphisms of adic spaces

*Node* `AdicSpacesPartII:R0/adic-morphism` (definition); module `TauCeti/AlgebraicGeometry/AdicSpace/Morphisms/Adic`.

A morphism f : X → Y of adic spaces (the anchor's category, Layer 5) is *adic* if every x ∈ X has an open affinoid neighbourhood U and there is an open affinoid V ⊆ Y with f(U) ⊆ V such that the ring homomorphism O_Y(V) → O_X(U) induced by f is adic (R0/adic-ring-homomorphism). Equivalently (R0/adic-iff-analytic-locus) f maps analytic points to analytic points, and then the ring maps O_Y(V) → O_X(U) are adic for all open affinoids with f(U) ⊆ V. Here a point is analytic if it has an open neighbourhood U whose ring O_X(U) contains a topologically nilpotent unit; on Spa(A, A⁺) this means that its support is not open (Tau Ceti `ValuationSpectrum.IsAnalyticPoint`). Every morphism into an analytic adic space is adic. Lean name: `AdicSpace.IsAdic f` (a `MorphismProperty` of the anchor's category).

*Hypotheses.* f : X → Y a morphism of adic spaces.

*Proof outline.*

1. Definition by an affinoid-local condition; independence of the chosen affinoids and the analytic-locus characterisation are R0/adic-iff-analytic-locus.

*API.*

- `AdicSpace.IsAdic` (structure): The morphism property; affinoid-local definition.
- `AdicSpace.isAdic_iff_image_analytic` (characterisation): IsAdic f ↔ f(X_a) ⊆ Y_a (promoted to R0/adic-iff-analytic-locus).
- `AdicSpace.IsAdic.isAdicHom_app` (characterisation): If f is adic then O_Y(V) → O_X(U) is adic for all open affinoids U, V with f(U) ⊆ V (R0/adic-iff-analytic-locus (i)).
- `AdicSpace.image_nonanalytic_subset` (relation): For every morphism f, f(X_na) ⊆ Y_na (R0/adic-iff-analytic-locus (iii)).
- `AdicSpace.IsAdic.of_isAnalytic` (instance): If Y is analytic, every f : X → Y is adic.
- `AdicSpace.IsAdic.comp` (functoriality): Composites of adic morphisms are adic; identities are adic (the property is multiplicative).
- `AdicSpace.IsAdic.of_comp` (relation): If g ∘ f is adic then f is adic (a non-analytic image f(x) would give a non-analytic g(f(x))).
- `AdicSpace.IsAdic.of_isOpenImmersion` (instance): Open immersions are adic.
- `AdicSpace.IsAdic.spa_iff` (compatibility): For affinoids, adicness of Spa(φ) is adicness of φ.
- `AdicSpace.LocallyOfWeaklyFiniteType.isAdic` (relation): Locally weakly-finite-type morphisms are adic (R0/finite-type-morphism-classes).
- `AdicSpace.IsAdic.isStableUnderBaseChange` (other): Base change of an adic morphism is adic when the fibre product exists (R0/base-change-stability (v)).

*Unit tests.*

- `isAdic_test_disc` (computation): The structure morphism of the closed unit disc Spa(ℚ_p⟨T⟩, ℤ_p⟨T⟩) → Spa(ℚ_p, ℤ_p) is adic (ℚ_p is Tate).
- `not_isAdic_test_powerSeries` (non-example): Spa(ℤ_p⟦T⟧, ℤ_p⟦T⟧) → Spa(ℤ_p, ℤ_p) ((p, T)-adic over p-adic) is not adic: the point given by the T-adic valuation of 𝔽_p((T)) is analytic (support (p) not open) and maps to the non-analytic point of Spa ℤ_p with support (p). A definition 'adic = continuous on rings' fails.
- `isAdic_of_isAnalytic_test` (characterisation): Every morphism X → Spa(ℚ_p, ℤ_p) is adic, because Spa(ℚ_p, ℤ_p) is analytic.
- `isAdic_spa_iff` (compatibility): For a morphism of complete Huber pairs φ : (A, A⁺) → (B, B⁺) (Tau Ceti `Pair.Hom`) with sheafy pairs, Spa(φ) is adic iff the ring homomorphism of φ is adic (`Huber.IsAdicHom`).
- `isAdic_id_test` (degenerate): Identities and open immersions are adic.

*Acceptance.*

- Spa(ℚ_p⟨T⟩) → Spa(ℚ_p) is adic; Spa(ℤ_p⟦T⟧) → Spa(ℤ_p) is not.
