*Acceptance.*

- X_n = Spec(ℤ/p^{n+1}) gives Spf ℤ_p; X_n = Spec(k[x][t]/(t^{n+1})) gives Spf k[x]⟦t⟧.
- The system A_n = k[x_1, x_2, …]/((x_1,…,x_n)^n + (x_{n+1}, x_{n+2}, …)) satisfies (a) but not (b); its limit is an admissible, non-adic ring and is not covered.

*Uses.* EGA I, 10.6.8 and 10.12.3.1: adic inductive systems of S_n-schemes have formal limits; morphisms of systems have limits. EGA III, 5.1.7 and 5.4.2: formal deformation data (compatible systems of schemes over A/I^{n+1}) are turned into formal schemes before algebraisation. AlgebraicModuliForArithmeticGeometry R09.6: effective formal deformations: a compatible system of deformations over R/𝔪^{n+1} is a formal scheme over Spf R.

*Depends on.* The formal spectrum Spf A of an adic ring (`AdicSpacesPartII:F0/formal-spectrum`); Noetherianity of adically complete rings and of adic completions (`AdicSpacesPartII:F0/adic-completion-noetherian`); Formal schemes and locally noetherian formal schemes (`AdicSpacesPartII:F0/locally-noetherian-formal-scheme`); Ideals of definition of a formal scheme and the thickenings X_n (`AdicSpacesPartII:F0/ideal-of-definition`); Adic rings of finite ideal type and their ideals of definition (`AdicSpacesPartII:F0/adic-ring`); `mathlib:AlgebraicGeometry.IsClosedImmersion`; `mathlib:AlgebraicGeometry.IsAffine`; `mathlib:TopCat.Sheaf`.

*Sources.* EGA-I-1960, Ch. I, (10.6.3) Proposition b), c), printed p. 189; EGA-I-1960, Ch. I, (10.6.3) Proposition, printed pp. 189-190; EGA-I-1960, Ch. I, (10.6.4) Corollaire, printed p. 191.


##### A locally noetherian formal scheme is the colimit of its thickenings

`AdicSpacesPartII:F0/formal-scheme-as-colimit` (theorem; Lean module `TauCeti/AlgebraicGeometry/FormalScheme/Colimit`, namespace `TauCeti.FormalScheme`)

Let X be a locally noetherian formal scheme and 𝒥 an ideal of definition; let X_n = (X, O_X/𝒥^{n+1}) with the canonical closed immersions X_m → X_n and morphisms ι_n : X_n → X (AdicSpacesPartII:F0/ideal-of-definition). Then (X_n) is an adic thickening system with X_0 locally noetherian, and (X, (ι_n)) is a colimit of the diagram (X_n) in the category of formal schemes (EGA I, 10.6.2): for every formal scheme Y and compatible morphisms g_n : X_n → Y there is a unique g : X → Y with g ∘ ι_n = g_n. Consequently the canonical morphism ofThickenings(X_n) → X is an isomorphism, and ofThickenings is an equivalence from adic thickening systems with locally noetherian X_0 to pairs (X, 𝒥) of a locally noetherian formal scheme with an ideal of definition (EGA I, 10.6.4 and the remark after it).

*Hypotheses.* X locally noetherian; 𝒥 an ideal of definition (exists: take the largest one 𝒯).

*Construction / proof route.*

1. The system (X_n) satisfies the adic conditions: ker(O/𝒥^{n+1} → O/𝒥^{m+1}) = 𝒥^{m+1}/𝒥^{n+1} and 𝒥/𝒥² is of finite type because 𝒥 is coherent on locally noetherian X (affine-locally J/J² is a finite A/J-module, A noetherian) (AdicSpacesPartII:F0/ideal-of-definition).
2. Universal property: compatible g_n have one underlying continuous map (the X_n share their space) and a projective system of sheaf maps O_Y → g_*(O_X/𝒥^{n+1}); pass to the limit using O_X = lim O_X/𝒥^{n+1} (AdicSpacesPartII:F0/ideal-of-definition, structureSheafIsoLimit). The limit map has local stalk maps: this is local, and on affine pieces X = Spf A, Y = Spf B it is Spf of the continuous map B → lim A/J^{n+1} = A given by the compatible maps, by AdicSpacesPartII:F0/spf-morphism-correspondence and Mathlib IsAdicComplete.liftRingHom.
3. Equivalence: AdicSpacesPartII:F0/colimit-of-thickenings constructs the inverse; the comparison ofThickenings(X_n) → X is the identity on spaces and the identity O_X = lim O_X/𝒥^{n+1} on sheaves.

*Acceptance.*

- X = Spf ℤ_p with 𝒥 = (p): X = colim Spec(ℤ/p^{n+1}) in formal schemes; a compatible system of morphisms Spec(ℤ/p^{n+1}) → Y is a morphism Spf ℤ_p → Y.
- The canonical morphism Spf ℤ_p → FormalScheme.ofScheme(Spec ℤ_p) induced by the compatible maps Spec(ℤ/p^{n+1}) → Spec ℤ_p is not an isomorphism of formal schemes (one point against two): the colimit is taken in formal schemes, not in schemes.

*Depends on.* Ideals of definition of a formal scheme and the thickenings X_n (`AdicSpacesPartII:F0/ideal-of-definition`); The formal scheme attached to an adic system of thickenings (`AdicSpacesPartII:F0/colimit-of-thickenings`); Morphisms into Spf A and automatic continuity (`AdicSpacesPartII:F0/spf-morphism-correspondence`); Formal schemes and locally noetherian formal schemes (`AdicSpacesPartII:F0/locally-noetherian-formal-scheme`); `mathlib:IsAdicComplete.liftRingHom`.

*Sources.* EGA-I-1960, Ch. I, (10.6.2) Proposition, printed p. 189; EGA-I-1960, Ch. I, after (10.6.4), printed p. 191.


##### Morphisms of locally noetherian formal schemes as compatible systems

`AdicSpacesPartII:F0/morphisms-as-compatible-systems` (theorem; Lean module `TauCeti/AlgebraicGeometry/FormalScheme/Colimit`, namespace `TauCeti.FormalScheme`)

Let X, Y be locally noetherian formal schemes with ideals of definition 𝒥 ⊆ O_X and 𝒦 ⊆ O_Y, and X_n = (X, O_X/𝒥^{n+1}), Y_n = (Y, O_Y/𝒦^{n+1}). (i) For every morphism f : X → Y, f*(𝒦)·O_X ⊆ 𝒯_X, the largest ideal of definition of X (EGA I, 10.6.10(i)). (ii) If f*(𝒦)·O_X ⊆ 𝒥 then f*(𝒦^{n+1})·O_X ⊆ 𝒥^{n+1} and f induces morphisms of schemes f_n : X_n → Y_n with commuting squares (EGA I, 10.6.7); the map f ↦ (f_n) is a bijection from {f : f*(𝒦)O_X ⊆ 𝒥} onto compatible sequences (f_n) (EGA I, 10.6.9). In particular, with 𝒥 = 𝒯_X, Hom(X, Y) ≃ lim_n Hom(X_n, Y_n) (EGA I, 10.6.10(ii)). (iii) Over a locally noetherian base S with ideal of definition ℒ, f*(ℒ)O_X ⊆ 𝒥, g*(ℒ)O_Y = 𝒦 and S_n = (S, O_S/ℒ^{n+1}): Hom_S(X, Y) ≃ lim_n Hom_{S_n}(X_n, Y_n) (EGA I, 10.6.11).

*Hypotheses.* X, Y (and S) locally noetherian formal schemes with chosen ideals of definition.

*Construction / proof route.*

1. (i) Local on X and Y; for Spf A → Spf B given by continuous φ : B → A (AdicSpacesPartII:F0/spf-morphism-correspondence), elements of an ideal of definition of B are topologically nilpotent, so their images are topologically nilpotent in A, hence lie in √I_A = 𝒯(Spf A) (AdicSpacesPartII:F0/adic-ring, isTopologicallyNilpotent_iff and radical_isAdic).
2. (ii) Given f with the ideal condition, the reduction f_n is the unique morphism X_n → Y_n compatible with the canonical morphisms (EGA I, 10.5.6, affine case: φ(K^{n+1}) ⊆ J^{n+1} induces B/K^{n+1} → A/J^{n+1}). Conversely a compatible (f_n) induces f = colim f_n by AdicSpacesPartII:F0/formal-scheme-as-colimit; the ideal condition holds because, affine-locally, the limit map φ = lim φ_n satisfies φ(K) ⊆ J from the commutativity at n = 0 (EGA I, 10.6.9).
3. (iii) An S-morphism satisfies the ideal condition for 𝒥, 𝒦 as above; apply (ii) and note that compatibility with the structure maps is checked levelwise.

*Acceptance.*

- Hom(Spf ℤ_p⟦T⟧, Spf ℤ_p⟦S⟧) ≃ lim_n Hom(Spec ℤ_p⟦T⟧/(p,T)^{n+1}, Spec ℤ_p⟦S⟧/(p,S)^{n+1}) ≃ (p, T)ℤ_p⟦T⟧ (the image of S).
- For 𝒥 strictly smaller than 𝒯_X, not every morphism satisfies f*(𝒦)O_X ⊆ 𝒥: the identity of Spf k⟦t⟧ with 𝒥 = (t²) and 𝒦 = (t) does not.

*Depends on.* A locally noetherian formal scheme is the colimit of its thickenings (`AdicSpacesPartII:F0/formal-scheme-as-colimit`); Ideals of definition of a formal scheme and the thickenings X_n (`AdicSpacesPartII:F0/ideal-of-definition`); Morphisms into Spf A and automatic continuity (`AdicSpacesPartII:F0/spf-morphism-correspondence`); Adic rings of finite ideal type and their ideals of definition (`AdicSpacesPartII:F0/adic-ring`); `mathlib:IsAdicComplete.liftRingHom`.

*Sources.* EGA-I-1960, Ch. I, (10.6.10) Corollaire (i), printed p. 192; EGA-I-1960, Ch. I, (10.6.10) Corollaire (ii), printed p. 192; EGA-I-1960, Ch. I, after (10.6.11), printed p. 193.

##### A formal scheme of finite ideal type is the colimit of its thickenings

`AdicSpacesPartII:F0/thickening-colimit-finite-ideal-type` (lemma; Lean module `TauCeti/AlgebraicGeometry/FormalScheme/Colimit`, namespace `TauCeti.FormalScheme`)

Let X be a formal scheme of finite ideal type (no noetherian hypothesis) and 𝒥 an ideal of definition of finite type (on every affine formal open U ≅ Spf A, 𝒥|_U = J^Δ for a finitely generated ideal of definition J ⊆ A), X_n = (X, O_X/𝒥^{n+1}). Then (i) J^Δ = J·O_U and (𝒥|_U)^{n+1} = (J^{n+1})^Δ, so the 𝒥^{n+1} form a fundamental system of ideals of definition of finite type and X_n|_U = Spec(A/J^{n+1}); (ii) (X_n) is an adic thickening system; (iii) (X, (ι_n)) is the colimit of (X_n) in formal schemes. For locally noetherian X this is `F0/formal-scheme-as-colimit`.

*Hypotheses.* X a formal scheme of finite ideal type; 𝒥 an ideal of definition of finite type.

*Construction / proof route.*

1. (i) Fujiwara–Kato I, Proposition 1.1.22 (𝒥|_U = J^Δ with J finitely generated), Proposition 1.1.20 and Corollary 1.1.21 ((J^Δ)^n = (J^n)^Δ, replacing the noetherian EGA I (10.3.6)), Corollary 1.1.24.
2. (ii) The kernels 𝒥^{m+1}/𝒥^{n+1} = 𝒥_n^{m+1} are nilpotent, the transition maps surjective, and 𝒥/𝒥² is of finite type: conditions (a)–(c) of `F0/colimit-of-thickenings`.
3. (iii) EGA I (10.6.2) holds for any formal prescheme with a fundamental system of ideals of definition: compatible g_n share one continuous map, their sheaf maps pass to the limit O_X = lim O_X/𝒥^{n+1} (EGA I (10.5.3)), and locally the limit map is Spf of lim_n (B → A/J^{n+1}) (`F0/spf-morphism-correspondence`); Fujiwara–Kato I, Proposition 1.4.1.

*Acceptance.*

- Over a non-discretely valued K, X = Spf O_K⟨T⟩ with 𝒥 = ϖO_X has X_n = Spec (O_K/ϖ^{n+1})[T], and morphisms X → Y are compatible families Spec (O_K/ϖ^{n+1})[T] → Y.
- 𝒥 = ϖ²O_X gives the cofinal subsystem Spec (O_K/ϖ^{2n+2})[T] with the same colimit.

*Depends on.* Formal schemes (`AdicSpacesPartII:F0/locally-noetherian-formal-scheme`); Ideals of definition (`AdicSpacesPartII:F0/ideal-of-definition`); Adic rings (`AdicSpacesPartII:F0/adic-ring`); Completed localisation (`AdicSpacesPartII:F0/completed-localization`); The formal scheme attached to an adic system of thickenings (`AdicSpacesPartII:F0/colimit-of-thickenings`); Morphisms into Spf A (`AdicSpacesPartII:F0/spf-morphism-correspondence`).

*Sources.* EGA-I-1960, Ch. I, (10.6.2), printed p. 189; FujiwaraKato-RigidGeometryI, Chapter I, Corollaries 1.1.21 and 1.1.24, pp. 260–261, Proposition 1.4.1, p. 266.

##### Morphisms of formal schemes of finite ideal type as compatible systems

`AdicSpacesPartII:F0/morphisms-as-compatible-systems-finite-ideal-type` (theorem; Lean module `TauCeti/AlgebraicGeometry/FormalScheme/Colimit`, namespace `TauCeti.FormalScheme`)

Let X, Y be formal schemes of finite ideal type with ideals of definition of finite type 𝒥, 𝒦 and thickenings X_n, Y_n. (i) If f*(𝒦)O_X ⊆ 𝒥, f has unique reductions f_n : X_n → Y_n, compatible with the transition maps (EGA I (10.5.6), (10.6.7)). (ii) f ↦ (f_n) is a bijection from {f : f*(𝒦)O_X ⊆ 𝒥} onto compatible sequences (f_n). (iii) Over S of finite ideal type with ℒ of finite type, p*(ℒ)O_X ⊆ 𝒥 and q*(ℒ)O_Y = 𝒦: Hom_S(X, Y) ≃ lim_n Hom_{S_n}(X_n, Y_n) (EGA I (10.6.11); Fujiwara–Kato I, Exercise I.1.7). There is in general no largest ideal of definition, so the ideal condition is part of (ii); for locally noetherian X, Y, S this is `F0/morphisms-as-compatible-systems` (ii)–(iii).

*Hypotheses.* X, Y (and S) formal schemes of finite ideal type; 𝒥, 𝒦 (and ℒ) of finite type; in (iii) p*(ℒ)O_X ⊆ 𝒥 and q*(ℒ)O_Y = 𝒦.

*Construction / proof route.*

1. (i) EGA I (10.5.6), (10.6.7), valid for arbitrary formal preschemes; affine-locally the ideal condition is φ(K) ⊆ J and f_n = Spec(B/K^{n+1} → A/J^{n+1}).
2. (ii) Surjectivity and injectivity from the colimit property (`F0/thickening-colimit-finite-ideal-type` (iii); EGA I (10.6.8)).
3. (ii) The limit satisfies the ideal condition: φ_n(K/K^{n+1}) ⊆ J/J^{n+1} for all n gives φ(K) ⊆ lim J/J^{n+1} = J (J is open, hence closed) — EGA I, proof of (10.6.9), with (10.3.6) replaced by `F0/thickening-colimit-finite-ideal-type` (i).
4. (iii) u*(𝒦)O_X = u*(q*(ℒ)O_Y)O_X = p*(ℒ)O_X ⊆ 𝒥 for S-morphisms; S-compatibility is checked levelwise.

*Acceptance.*

- Over a possibly non-discretely valued K: Hom_{O_K}(Spf O_K⟨T⟩, Spf O_K⟨U⟩) ≃ lim_n (O_K/ϖ^{n+1})[T] = O_K⟨T⟩.
- Without the ideal condition (ii) fails: the identity of Spf O_K⟨T⟩ with 𝒥 = ϖ²O, 𝒦 = ϖO has no reduction X_0 → Y_0.

*Uses.* AdicSpacesPartII:R2/admissible-blow-up: morphisms into an admissible blow-up are compatible systems of morphisms into its levels. AdicSpacesPartII:F0/adic-systems-equivalence-finite-ideal-type: full faithfulness.

*Depends on.* A formal scheme of finite ideal type is the colimit of its thickenings (`AdicSpacesPartII:F0/thickening-colimit-finite-ideal-type`); Ideals of definition (`AdicSpacesPartII:F0/ideal-of-definition`); Morphisms into Spf A (`AdicSpacesPartII:F0/spf-morphism-correspondence`); Adic rings (`AdicSpacesPartII:F0/adic-ring`); Formal schemes (`AdicSpacesPartII:F0/locally-noetherian-formal-scheme`).

*Sources.* EGA-I-1960, Ch. I, (10.6.7), (10.6.8) and the proof of (10.6.9), printed pp. 191–192; FujiwaraKato-RigidGeometryI, Chapter I, Exercise I.1.7, p. 280.

##### Fibre products of formal schemes

`AdicSpacesPartII:F0/formal-fibre-product` (theorem; Lean module `TauCeti/AlgebraicGeometry/FormalScheme/Pullback`, namespace `TauCeti.FormalScheme`)

Let f : X → S and g : Y → S be morphisms of formal schemes (finite ideal type). The fibre product X ×_S Y exists in formal schemes; for affine formal schemes, Spf B ×_{Spf A} Spf C ≅ Spf(B ⊗̂_A C) with the projections induced by the canonical maps into the completed tensor product (EGA I, 10.7.2–10.7.3); every open cover of X, Y, S by affine formal opens gives an affine formal cover of X ×_S Y. If S, X, Y have ideals of definition ℒ, 𝒥, 𝒦 with f*(ℒ)O_X ⊆ 𝒥 and g*(ℒ)O_Y ⊆ 𝒦, then X ×_S Y is the colimit in formal schemes of the schemes X_n ×_{S_n} Y_n, and the ideal generated by 𝒥 and 𝒦 is an ideal of definition of X ×_S Y whose powers are cofinal with the kernels of the X_n ×_{S_n} Y_n (EGA I, 10.7.4). If S, X, Y are locally noetherian and f is of finite type, then X ×_S Y is locally noetherian and X ×_S Y → Y is of finite type (EGA I, 10.13.5 (ii)); in general X ×_S Y need not be locally noetherian (EGA I, 10.7.4).

*Hypotheses.* formal schemes of finite ideal type; local noetherianity of the product only when f is of finite type.

*Construction / proof route.*

1. Affine case: by AdicSpacesPartII:F0/spf-morphism-correspondence, morphisms Spf D → Spf(B ⊗̂_A C) are continuous maps B ⊗̂_A C → D, which by the universal property of AdicSpacesPartII:F0/completed-tensor-product-adic are pairs of continuous A-maps B → D, C → D; extend from affine D to arbitrary formal schemes D with AdicSpacesPartII:F0/spf-morphism-correspondence (general X).
2. General case: glue the affine products over affine formal covers as in the scheme case (AdicSpacesPartII:F0/formal-scheme-gluing; EGA I, 10.7.3 via 3.2.6).
3. System description: affine-locally B ⊗̂_A C = lim_n (B/J^{n+1} ⊗_{A/L^{n+1}} C/K^{n+1}), since the ideals J^{n+1}⊗1 + 1⊗K^{n+1} and (J⊗1 + 1⊗K)^{n+1} of B ⊗_A C have cofinal powers (AdicSpacesPartII:F0/completed-tensor-product-adic); a compatible family X_n ×_{S_n} Y_n → T glues to X ×_S Y → T as in AdicSpacesPartII:F0/colimit-of-thickenings.
4. Noetherian case: if B is topologically of finite type over A, B ⊗̂_A C is noetherian and topologically of finite type over C (AdicSpacesPartII:F0/completed-tensor-product-adic, isNoetherianRing; AdicSpacesPartII:F0/topologically-finite-type-criterion); finite type of X ×_S Y → Y is checked on X_0 ×_{S_0} Y_0 → Y_0 (AdicSpacesPartII:F0/formal-morphism-finite-type).

*Acceptance.*

- Spf ℤ_p⟦S⟧ ×_{Spf ℤ_p} Spf ℤ_p⟦T⟧ ≅ Spf ℤ_p⟦S, T⟧.
- For X = Spf ℤ_p⟨x⟩ over S = Spf ℤ_p and any locally noetherian Y over Spf ℤ_p, X ×_S Y = Y⟨x⟩ is locally noetherian.

*Depends on.* Completed tensor product of adic rings of finite ideal type (`AdicSpacesPartII:F0/completed-tensor-product-adic`); Morphisms into Spf A and automatic continuity (`AdicSpacesPartII:F0/spf-morphism-correspondence`); Gluing formal schemes along open subschemes (`AdicSpacesPartII:F0/formal-scheme-gluing`); The formal scheme attached to an adic system of thickenings (`AdicSpacesPartII:F0/colimit-of-thickenings`); Adic algebras topologically of finite type over an adic noetherian ring (`AdicSpacesPartII:F0/topologically-finite-type-criterion`); Morphisms of finite type of locally noetherian formal schemes (`AdicSpacesPartII:F0/formal-morphism-finite-type`); `mathlib:CategoryTheory.Limits.pullback`.

*Sources.* EGA-I-1960, Ch. I, proof of (10.7.2), printed p. 193; EGA-I-1960, Ch. I, (10.7.3) Proposition, printed p. 193; EGA-I-1960, Ch. I, (10.7.4), printed p. 194; EGA-I-1960, Ch. I, (10.13.5) Proposition (i), printed p. 208.


#### F0.4 Adic, finite-type and proper morphisms; closed formal subschemes

##### Adic morphisms of locally noetherian formal schemes

`AdicSpacesPartII:F0/adic-morphism-of-formal-schemes` (definition; Lean module `TauCeti/AlgebraicGeometry/FormalScheme/Morphisms`, namespace `TauCeti.FormalScheme`)

A morphism f : X → Y of locally noetherian formal schemes is adic if there is an ideal of definition 𝒦 of Y such that f*(𝒦)·O_X is an ideal of definition of X; then f*(𝒦′)·O_X is an ideal of definition of X for every ideal of definition 𝒦′ of Y (EGA I, 10.12.1). An adic formal scheme over S is a locally noetherian formal S-scheme with adic structure morphism; every S-morphism between adic S-formal schemes is adic. For affine X = Spf A, Y = Spf B, f = Spf φ is adic iff I_B·A is an ideal of definition of A (IsAdic (I_B.map φ)). Notation: for fixed 𝒦 and 𝒥 := f*(𝒦)O_X, f_n : X_n → Y_n denotes the reduction modulo 𝒥^{n+1}, 𝒦^{n+1} (AdicSpacesPartII:F0/morphisms-as-compatible-systems); f is adic iff every square X_m → X_n over Y_m → Y_n is cartesian, i.e. X_m = X_n ×_{Y_n} Y_m (EGA I, 10.12.3).

*Hypotheses.* X, Y locally noetherian formal schemes.

*Construction / proof route.*

1. Independence of 𝒦: locally, K′^n ⊆ K and K^m ⊆ K′, so KA and K′A have cofinal powers and one is an ideal of definition iff the other is (EGA I, 10.12.1; AdicSpacesPartII:F0/adic-ring).
2. S-morphisms between adic S-formal schemes: if f = g ∘ u then u*(g*(ℒ)O_Y)O_X = f*(ℒ)O_X is an ideal of definition (EGA I, 10.12.1).
3. Cartesian squares: affine-locally, KA ideal of definition gives A/K^{m+1}A = (A/K^{n+1}A) ⊗_{B/K^{n+1}} B/K^{m+1}.

*API.*

- `FormalScheme.Hom.IsAdic` (structure): class: ∃ ideal of definition 𝒦 of Y with f*(𝒦)O_X an ideal of definition of X.
- `FormalScheme.Hom.IsAdic.forall` (characterisation): f.IsAdic → for every ideal of definition 𝒦 of Y, f*(𝒦)O_X is an ideal of definition.
- `FormalScheme.Hom.IsAdic.comp` (instance): Adic morphisms are stable under composition.
- `FormalScheme.Hom.IsAdic.of_comp` (other): If g ∘ f and g are adic then f is adic (EGA I, 10.12.1 for S-morphisms).
- `FormalScheme.Hom.isAdic_iff_isPullback` (characterisation): f.IsAdic ↔ for all m ≤ n the square X_m → X_n, Y_m → Y_n is a pullback of schemes.
- `FormalScheme.Hom.reduction` (projection): f.reduction 𝒦 n : X.thickening (f*𝒦 O_X) n ⟶ Y.thickening 𝒦 n, compatible with thickeningι.
- `FormalScheme.Hom.IsAdic.baseChange` (instance): Adic morphisms are stable under base change along morphisms with locally noetherian fibre product.
- `FormalScheme.Hom.isAdic_ofScheme` (compatibility): Every morphism between schemes, viewed as formal schemes, is adic.

*Unit tests.*

- `FormalScheme.Hom.isAdic_Spf_restricted` (computation): Spf.map (algebraMap ℤ_[p] ℤ_[p]⟨T⟩) : Spf ℤ_[p]⟨T⟩ ⟶ Spf ℤ_[p] is adic.
- `FormalScheme.Hom.not_isAdic_Spf_powerSeries` (non-example): Spf ℤ_[p]⟦T⟧ ⟶ Spf ℤ_[p] is not adic; a definition requiring only continuity of the ring map (every morphism) would wrongly call it adic.
- `FormalScheme.Hom.isAdic_id` (degenerate): The identity of a locally noetherian formal scheme is adic, and every morphism of schemes (discrete formal schemes) is adic with 𝒦 = 0.
- `FormalScheme.Hom.isAdic_Spf_iff` (characterisation): For continuous φ : B →+* A of adic noetherian rings with ideal of definition K ⊆ B: (Spf.map φ).IsAdic ↔ IsAdic (K.map φ).

*Acceptance.*

- Spf ℤ_p⟨T⟩ → Spf ℤ_p is adic; Spf ℤ_p⟦T⟧ → Spf ℤ_p is not adic (pℤ_p⟦T⟧ is not an ideal of definition of the (p,T)-adic ring).
- For a morphism f : X → Y of locally noetherian schemes and Y′ ⊆ Y closed, f̂ : X̂_{/f⁻¹Y′} → Ŷ_{/Y′} is adic.

*Uses.* EGA I, 10.13.1: a morphism of finite type is adic with f_0 of finite type. EGA III, 5.4.2 and 5.4.5: formal schemes proper over Spf A are adic over Spf A; their systems X_n = X ×_{Spf A} Spec A/I^{n+1} are the data algebraised. AdicSpacesPartII:R2/noetherian-formal-scheme-as-adic-space: Huber’s criterion: t(f) is adic iff f is adic; t(f) locally of finite type iff f locally of finite type. AdicSpacesPartII:R2/formal-schemes-of-type-S: morphisms of type-(S) formal schemes are called adic in the same sense; R2 extends the definition beyond the noetherian case.

*Depends on.* Formal schemes and locally noetherian formal schemes (`AdicSpacesPartII:F0/locally-noetherian-formal-scheme`); Ideals of definition of a formal scheme and the thickenings X_n (`AdicSpacesPartII:F0/ideal-of-definition`); Adic rings of finite ideal type and their ideals of definition (`AdicSpacesPartII:F0/adic-ring`); Morphisms of locally noetherian formal schemes as compatible systems (`AdicSpacesPartII:F0/morphisms-as-compatible-systems`); `mathlib:IsAdic`.

*Sources.* EGA-I-1960, Ch. I, (10.12.1), printed p. 206; EGA-I-1960, Ch. I, (10.12.2), printed p. 206.


##### Adic formal S-schemes are adic inductive systems of S_n-schemes

`AdicSpacesPartII:F0/adic-systems-equivalence` (theorem; Lean module `TauCeti/AlgebraicGeometry/FormalScheme/Morphisms`, namespace `TauCeti.FormalScheme`)

Let S be a locally noetherian formal scheme with ideal of definition ℒ and S_n = (S, O_S/ℒ^{n+1}). An (S_n)-adic inductive system is a sequence of locally noetherian S_n-schemes X_n with morphisms X_m → X_n over S_m → S_n identifying X_m with X_n ×_{S_n} S_m for m ≤ n; morphisms are compatible sequences of S_n-morphisms. The functor X ↦ (X ×_S S_n)_n = (X, O_X/(ℒO_X)^{n+1})_n is an equivalence from adic formal S-schemes (locally noetherian, adic structure morphism) to (S_n)-adic inductive systems with X_0 locally noetherian; its quasi-inverse sends (X_n) to its colimit (AdicSpacesPartII:F0/colimit-of-thickenings), whose structure morphism to S is adic (EGA I, 10.12.3, 10.12.3.1). In particular Hom_S(X, Y) ≃ lim_n Hom_{S_n}(X_n, Y_n) (EGA I, 10.12.3.2).

*Hypotheses.* S locally noetherian formal scheme with ideal of definition ℒ; X_0 locally noetherian.

*Construction / proof route.*

1. From X to systems: 𝒥 := ℒO_X is an ideal of definition; X_n → S_n is induced and the squares are cartesian (AdicSpacesPartII:F0/adic-morphism-of-formal-schemes, isAdic_iff_isPullback).
2. From systems to X: the kernels of O_{X_n} → O_{X_m} are 𝒥_n^{m+1} where 𝒥_n = ℒO_{X_n}, pulled back from S (base change of the closed immersions S_m → S_n); 𝒥_1 is of finite type over O_{X_0} because ℒ/ℒ² is; hence (X_n) is an adic thickening system (AdicSpacesPartII:F0/colimit-of-thickenings), its colimit X is locally noetherian, and the limit of the structure maps f_n is a morphism f : X → S (AdicSpacesPartII:F0/morphisms-as-compatible-systems).
3. f is adic: affine-locally S = Spf A, X_n = Spec B_n, B = lim B_n; the image of the ideal I of A is dense in ker(B → B_0) and every ideal of the noetherian adic ring B is closed, so IB is the ideal of definition ker(B → B_0) (EGA I, proof of 10.12.3.1; AdicSpacesPartII:F0/adic-ring, API quotient: ideals are closed).
4. Morphisms: AdicSpacesPartII:F0/morphisms-as-compatible-systems (iii).

*Acceptance.*

- For S = Spf ℤ_p, the system X_n = P¹_{ℤ/p^{n+1}} is adic; its colimit is the p-adic completion of P¹_{ℤ_p}.
- The system X_n = Spec(ℤ/p^{n+1})[T]/(T^{n+1}) over S_n = Spec ℤ/p^{n+1} is not adic (X_0 = Spec F_p[T]/(T) but X_1 ×_{S_1} S_0 = Spec F_p[T]/(T²) ≠ X_0).

*Uses.* EGA III, 5.1.7 and 5.4.2 (Scholies): coherent sheaves and morphisms over Spf A are compatible systems over A/I^{n+1}.

*Depends on.* Adic morphisms of locally noetherian formal schemes (`AdicSpacesPartII:F0/adic-morphism-of-formal-schemes`); The formal scheme attached to an adic system of thickenings (`AdicSpacesPartII:F0/colimit-of-thickenings`); A locally noetherian formal scheme is the colimit of its thickenings (`AdicSpacesPartII:F0/formal-scheme-as-colimit`); Morphisms of locally noetherian formal schemes as compatible systems (`AdicSpacesPartII:F0/morphisms-as-compatible-systems`); Adic rings of finite ideal type and their ideals of definition (`AdicSpacesPartII:F0/adic-ring`); `mathlib:CategoryTheory.Limits.pullback`.

*Sources.* EGA-I-1960, Ch. I, (10.12.3) Théorème, printed p. 206; EGA-I-1960, Ch. I, (10.12.3.2), printed p. 207.

##### Formal schemes of finite ideal type adic over S are adic inductive systems

`AdicSpacesPartII:F0/adic-systems-equivalence-finite-ideal-type` (theorem; Lean module `TauCeti/AlgebraicGeometry/FormalScheme/Morphisms`, namespace `TauCeti.FormalScheme`)

Let S be a formal scheme of finite ideal type with an ideal of definition ℒ of finite type, S_n = (S, O_S/ℒ^{n+1}). X → S is adic over S if ℒO_X is an ideal of definition of X (Fujiwara–Kato I, Definition 1.3.1). X ↦ (X ×_S S_n)_n is an equivalence from formal schemes of finite ideal type adic over S to (S_n)-adic inductive systems (S_n-schemes X_n with X_m = X_n ×_{S_n} S_m, no finiteness hypothesis); the quasi-inverse is the colimit of `F0/colimit-of-thickenings`, which is adic over S with ℒO_X = ker(O_X → O_{X_0}) (Fujiwara–Kato I, Exercise I.1.8). X is locally noetherian iff X_0 is; for locally noetherian S this is `F0/adic-systems-equivalence`.

*Hypotheses.* S of finite ideal type; ℒ an ideal of definition of finite type; no noetherian hypothesis.

*Construction / proof route.*

1. Forward: 𝒥 = ℒO_X is of finite type and X_m = X_n ×_{S_n} S_m because the ideal of X_m in X_n is ℒ^{m+1}O_{X_n} (EGA I, proof of (10.12.3)).
2. Quasi-inverse: an adic system satisfies (a)–(c) of `F0/colimit-of-thickenings` (ℒO_{X_1} is of finite type because ℒ is), so its colimit X is of finite ideal type with 𝒥^{n+1} = ker(O_X → O_{X_n}) (EGA I (10.6.4); Fujiwara–Kato I, Proposition 1.4.3), and the structure maps glue to f : X → S (`F0/thickening-colimit-finite-ideal-type` (iii)).
3. Adicness ℒO_X = 𝒥: EGA's proof of (10.12.3.1) uses that every ideal of a noetherian adic ring is closed; instead, affine-locally B = lim B_n with B_m = B_n/L^{m+1}B_n, and Fujiwara–Kato I, Proposition 0.7.2.12 gives ker(B → B_0) = L·B (via 0.7.2.11 and Nakayama in the complete ring B). This is the route of Fujiwara–Kato's solution to Exercise I.1.8.
4. Full faithfulness: `F0/morphisms-as-compatible-systems-finite-ideal-type` (iii); essential surjectivity: `F0/thickening-colimit-finite-ideal-type` (iii).

*Acceptance.*

- X_n = Spec (O_K/ϖ^{n+1})[T_1, …, T_d] over Spf O_K (possibly non-discretely valued K) is adic with colimit Spf O_K⟨T_1, …, T_d⟩.
- Étale O_K/ϖ-schemes lift to formal schemes adic and étale over Spf O_K, e.g. Spec (O_K/ϖ)[T, (T² + 1)⁻¹] ↦ Spf O_K⟨T, (T² + 1)⁻¹⟩.
- X_n = Spec (ℤ/p^{n+1})[T]/(T^{n+1}) over Spec ℤ/p^{n+1} is not adic.

*Uses.* AdicSpacesPartII:R2/formal-etale-site-invariance: étale formal schemes over a non-noetherian admissible 𝔛 as colimits of compatible étale systems, with morphisms levelwise. Fujiwara–Kato I, proof of Proposition 6.1.12 (effective descent for adically P morphisms).

*Depends on.* The formal scheme attached to an adic system of thickenings (`AdicSpacesPartII:F0/colimit-of-thickenings`); A formal scheme of finite ideal type is the colimit of its thickenings (`AdicSpacesPartII:F0/thickening-colimit-finite-ideal-type`); Morphisms of formal schemes of finite ideal type as compatible systems (`AdicSpacesPartII:F0/morphisms-as-compatible-systems-finite-ideal-type`); Adic rings (`AdicSpacesPartII:F0/adic-ring`); Ideals of definition (`AdicSpacesPartII:F0/ideal-of-definition`); Formal schemes (`AdicSpacesPartII:F0/locally-noetherian-formal-scheme`); `mathlib:CategoryTheory.Limits.pullback`; `mathlib:IsAdicComplete`; `mathlib:IsAdicComplete.le_jacobson_bot`; `mathlib:Submodule.le_of_le_smul_of_le_jacobson_bot`.

*Sources.* EGA-I-1960, Ch. I, (10.12.3) and proof of (10.12.3.1), printed pp. 206–207; FujiwaraKato-RigidGeometryI, Chapter I, Exercise I.1.8, p. 280, and its solution, p. 736; Chapter 0, Proposition 7.2.12, p. 158; Chapter I, Proposition 1.4.3, p. 267.

##### Morphisms of finite type of locally noetherian formal schemes

`AdicSpacesPartII:F0/formal-morphism-finite-type` (definition; Lean module `TauCeti/AlgebraicGeometry/FormalScheme/Morphisms`, namespace `TauCeti.FormalScheme`)

Let Y be a locally noetherian formal scheme with ideal of definition 𝒦 and f : X → Y a morphism of formal schemes. f is of finite type if X is locally noetherian, f is adic, and the reduction f_0 : (X, O_X/𝒥) → (Y, O_Y/𝒦) with 𝒥 = f*(𝒦)O_X is a morphism of schemes of finite type (Mathlib LocallyOfFiniteType and QuasiCompact) (EGA I, 10.13.1 (a), 10.13.3). Equivalent conditions: (b) X is locally noetherian and the colimit of an adic system (X_n) over (Y_n) with X_0 → Y_0 of finite type; (c) every point of Y has a noetherian affine formal neighbourhood V = Spf B such that f⁻¹(V) is a finite union of noetherian affine formal opens Spf A_i with each A_i ≅ B{T_1,…,T_r}/𝔞 topologically (EGA I, 10.13.1). The condition does not depend on 𝒦, and then every f_n is of finite type. Affine criterion: Spf A → Spf B (noetherian) is of finite type iff A is topologically a quotient of some B{T} (EGA I, 10.13.4). The local variant f locally of finite type (Huber’s notion used in R2) drops quasi-compactness of f_0.

*Hypotheses.* Y locally noetherian; 'finite type' of schemes includes quasi-compactness (EGA I, 6.3.1).

*Construction / proof route.*

1. (a) ⇒ (b): AdicSpacesPartII:F0/adic-systems-equivalence.
2. (b) ⇒ (c): locally Y = Spf B; X_0 is a finite union of affines U_i finite type over B/K; U_i is affine in every X_n, and the formal open on U_i is Spf(lim A_{i,n}) with A_{i,n} = A_{i,m}/K^{n+1}A_{i,m}; AdicSpacesPartII:F0/topologically-finite-type-criterion ((a) ⇒ (c)) gives the presentation.
3. (c) ⇒ (a): AdicSpacesPartII:F0/topologically-finite-type-criterion ((c) ⇒ (a)): A/KA is of finite type over B/K and KA is an ideal of definition.
4. Independence of 𝒦: (c) does not mention 𝒦.

*API.*

- `FormalScheme.Hom.FiniteType` (structure): class: X locally noetherian, f.IsAdic, and f_0 is LocallyOfFiniteType and QuasiCompact.
- `FormalScheme.Hom.finiteType_iff_reduction` (characterisation): f.FiniteType ↔ f.IsAdic ∧ ∀ n, (f.reduction 𝒦 n) is of finite type, for any ideal of definition 𝒦 of Y.
- `FormalScheme.Hom.finiteType_Spf_iff` (characterisation): Spf A → Spf B (noetherian) is of finite type iff A ≅ B{T}/𝔞 topologically over B (EGA I, 10.13.4).
- `FormalScheme.Hom.FiniteType.comp` (instance): Composition of finite-type morphisms is of finite type (EGA I, 10.13.5 (i)).
- `FormalScheme.Hom.FiniteType.baseChange` (instance): If f : X → S is of finite type and S′ → S has S′ locally noetherian, X ×_S S′ is locally noetherian and of finite type over S′ (EGA I, 10.13.5 (ii)).
- `FormalScheme.Hom.FiniteType.isNoetherian` (other): If f is of finite type and Y is noetherian then X is noetherian (EGA I, 10.13.2).
- `FormalScheme.Hom.LocallyOfFiniteType` (other): class: every point of X has an open neighbourhood U with f|_U of finite type; the notion Huber and R2 use.
- `FormalScheme.Hom.FiniteType.completion` (compatibility): For g : X → Y of finite type between locally noetherian schemes and closed Y′, X′ = g⁻¹(Y′), the completion ĝ is of finite type (EGA I, 10.13.6).

*Unit tests.*

- `FormalScheme.Hom.finiteType_restricted` (computation): Spf ℤ_[p]⟨T₁,…,T_r⟩ ⟶ Spf ℤ_[p] is of finite type, and so is Spf (ℤ_[p]⟨T⟩ ⧸ 𝔞) ⟶ Spf ℤ_[p] for every ideal 𝔞.
- `FormalScheme.Hom.not_finiteType_powerSeries` (non-example): Spf ℤ_[p]⟦T⟧ ⟶ Spf ℤ_[p] is not of finite type, although its reduction Spec F_p → Spec F_p modulo the ideals of definition (p,T) and (p) is of finite type: the adicness condition is essential.
- `FormalScheme.Hom.finiteType_ofScheme` (compatibility): For a morphism g of locally noetherian schemes, (FormalScheme.ofScheme.map g).FiniteType ↔ LocallyOfFiniteType g ∧ QuasiCompact g.
- `FormalScheme.Hom.finiteType_id` (degenerate): The identity of a locally noetherian formal scheme is of finite type.

*Acceptance.*

- Spf B{T₁,…,T_r} → Spf B is of finite type; Spf ℤ_p⟦T⟧ → Spf ℤ_p is not (not adic).
- For a morphism of finite type of locally noetherian schemes f : X → Y and Y′ closed, f̂ is of finite type (EGA I, 10.13.6).

*Uses.* EGA III, 3.4.1: proper morphisms of formal schemes are of finite type with proper reduction. AdicSpacesPartII:R2/noetherian-formal-scheme-as-adic-space: t(f) is locally of finite type iff f is locally of finite type (Huber 1994, 4.2). AdicSpacesPartII:R2 (PadicDifferentialEquationsAndRigidCohomology request): formal schemes locally of finite type over Spf O_K and their generic fibres. AdicSpacesPartII:F0/formal-fibre-product: base change of a finite-type morphism stays locally noetherian and of finite type.

*Depends on.* Adic morphisms of locally noetherian formal schemes (`AdicSpacesPartII:F0/adic-morphism-of-formal-schemes`); Adic formal S-schemes are adic inductive systems of S_n-schemes (`AdicSpacesPartII:F0/adic-systems-equivalence`); Adic algebras topologically of finite type over an adic noetherian ring (`AdicSpacesPartII:F0/topologically-finite-type-criterion`); Restricted power series over an adic noetherian ring (`AdicSpacesPartII:F0/restricted-power-series-adic`); `mathlib:AlgebraicGeometry.LocallyOfFiniteType`; `mathlib:AlgebraicGeometry.QuasiCompact`.

*Sources.* EGA-I-1960, Ch. I, (10.13.1) a), printed p. 207; EGA-I-1960, Ch. I, (10.13.3) Définition, printed p. 208; EGA-I-1960, Ch. I, (10.13.4) Corollaire, printed p. 208; EGA-I-1960, Ch. I, (10.13.5) Proposition (i), printed p. 208.


##### Properness, finiteness and closed immersions are insensitive to thickenings

`AdicSpacesPartII:F0/thickening-invariance` (lemma; Lean module `TauCeti/AlgebraicGeometry/FormalScheme/Morphisms`, namespace `TauCeti.FormalScheme`)

Let Y ⊆ Y′ be a closed immersion of schemes that is a homeomorphism (a thickening, e.g. defined by a locally nilpotent ideal), f′ : X′ → Y′ a morphism and X = Y ×_{Y′} X′ with f : X → Y the base change, and assume f and f′ are locally of finite type. Then f′ is proper (resp. finite, a closed immersion) if and only if f is (Stacks Tag 0BPG).

*Hypotheses.* (Y ⊆ Y′) a thickening; X = Y ×_{Y′} X′; f and f′ locally of finite type.

*Construction / proof route.*

1. If f′ has the property, so does its base change f (Mathlib IsProper.isStableUnderBaseChange; finite morphisms and closed immersions are stable under base change).
2. Conversely: underlying spaces and continuous maps of f and f′ coincide and remain so after any base change (a base change of a thickening is a thickening), so universal closedness transfers; the diagonal of f′ is a thickening of the diagonal of f, and a closed-embedding thickening with surjective stalk maps after reduction is a closed immersion, so separatedness transfers; hence properness (Mathlib IsProper = separated + universally closed + locally of finite type).
3. Closed immersions: topologically a closed embedding, and surjectivity of O_{Y′} → f′_*O_{X′} follows from surjectivity modulo the nilpotent ideal by Nakayama on stalks; finiteness: f′ is affine (affineness of a thickening, EGA I, 5.1.9) and integral since f is (Stacks Tag 0BPG).

*Acceptance.*

- For Y′ = Spec ℤ/p², Y = Spec F_p and X′ = P¹_{ℤ/p²}: X′ → Y′ is proper because P¹_{F_p} → Spec F_p is.
- Without the condition X = Y ×_{Y′} X′ the statement fails: for Y′ = Spec ℤ/p², Y = Spec F_p, X′ = A¹_{Y′} and X ⊂ X′ the closed point V(p, t), X → Y is an isomorphism (proper) while X′ → Y′ is not proper.

*Depends on.* `mathlib:AlgebraicGeometry.IsProper`; `mathlib:AlgebraicGeometry.IsProper.isStableUnderBaseChange`; `mathlib:AlgebraicGeometry.IsClosedImmersion`; `mathlib:AlgebraicGeometry.IsFinite`; `mathlib:AlgebraicGeometry.IsSeparated`; `mathlib:AlgebraicGeometry.UniversallyClosed`; `mathlib:AlgebraicGeometry.LocallyOfFiniteType`; `mathlib:Submodule.eq_bot_of_le_smul_of_le_jacobson_bot`.

*Sources.* Stacks-Project, Tag 0BPG (More on Morphisms, Lemma 37.3.4); EGA-III-1-1961, Ch. III, (3.4.1), printed p. 119.


##### Proper morphisms of locally noetherian formal schemes

`AdicSpacesPartII:F0/proper-formal-morphism` (definition; Lean module `TauCeti/AlgebraicGeometry/FormalScheme/Morphisms`, namespace `TauCeti.FormalScheme`)

A morphism f : X → Y of locally noetherian formal schemes is proper if f is of finite type (AdicSpacesPartII:F0/formal-morphism-finite-type) and, for an ideal of definition 𝒦 of Y and 𝒥 = f*(𝒦)O_X, the reduction f_0 : (X, O_X/𝒥) → (Y, O_Y/𝒦) is a proper morphism of schemes (Mathlib IsProper) (EGA III, 3.4.1). This does not depend on 𝒦, and then every f_n : X_n → Y_n is proper. A closed subset Z of X is proper over Y if, viewed in X_0, it is proper over Y_0 (the reduced closed subscheme on Z is proper over Y_0). For a proper morphism g : X → Y of locally noetherian schemes, a closed subset Y′ ⊆ Y and X′ = g⁻¹(Y′), the completion ĝ : X̂_{/X′} → Ŷ_{/Y′} is proper (EGA III, 3.4.1).

*Hypotheses.* X, Y locally noetherian formal schemes.

*Construction / proof route.*

1. f_n proper for all n: f is adic, so X_0 = X_n ×_{Y_n} Y_0 (AdicSpacesPartII:F0/adic-morphism-of-formal-schemes), Y_0 ⊆ Y_n is a thickening and all f_n are of finite type (AdicSpacesPartII:F0/formal-morphism-finite-type); AdicSpacesPartII:F0/thickening-invariance gives f_n proper iff f_0 proper.
2. Independence of 𝒦: for another ideal of definition 𝒦′ ⊆ 𝒦 the reductions modulo 𝒦 and 𝒦′ are members of such adic systems (𝒦 contains a power of 𝒦′ and conversely), so the same invariance applies (EGA III, 3.4.1).
3. Completion: ĝ is adic of finite type (AdicSpacesPartII:F0/formal-morphism-finite-type) and its reduction is the base change of g to V(𝓘) ⊆ Y, which is proper (Mathlib IsProper.isStableUnderBaseChange).

*API.*

- `FormalScheme.Hom.IsProper` (structure): class: f.FiniteType and the reduction f_0 is IsProper.
- `FormalScheme.Hom.isProper_iff_reduction` (characterisation): f.IsProper ↔ f.FiniteType ∧ ∀ n, IsProper (f.reduction 𝒦 n), for any ideal of definition 𝒦 of Y.
- `FormalScheme.Hom.IsProper.comp` (instance): Proper morphisms are stable under composition.
- `FormalScheme.Hom.IsProper.baseChange` (instance): Proper morphisms are stable under base change along morphisms of locally noetherian formal schemes (the product is locally noetherian by finite type).
- `FormalScheme.Hom.IsProper.completion` (compatibility): For g proper between locally noetherian schemes and X′ = g⁻¹(Y′), ĝ is proper.
- `FormalScheme.IsProperSupport` (other): A closed subset Z ⊆ X is proper over Y if the reduced closed subscheme of X_0 on Z is proper over Y_0; for X = X̂_{/X′} and Z closed in X′ this agrees with properness of Z ⊆ X over Y (EGA III, 3.4.1).
- `FormalScheme.Hom.IsProper.isClosedMap` (other): A proper morphism is a closed map on underlying spaces.

*Unit tests.*

- `FormalScheme.Hom.isProper_completion_projectiveLine` (computation): The completion of P¹_{ℤ_[p]} along its special fibre is proper over Spf ℤ_[p].
- `FormalScheme.Hom.not_isProper_restricted` (non-example): Spf ℤ_[p]⟨T⟩ ⟶ Spf ℤ_[p] is of finite type but not proper. A definition asking only that the underlying continuous map be closed would accept it (the underlying space A¹_{F_p} → point is closed) since universal closedness is what fails.
- `FormalScheme.Hom.isProper_ofScheme` (compatibility): For g a morphism of locally noetherian schemes, (FormalScheme.ofScheme.map g).IsProper ↔ AlgebraicGeometry.IsProper g (Mathlib IsProper already implies QuasiCompact, via UniversallyClosed).
- `FormalScheme.Hom.isProper_id` (degenerate): The identity of a locally noetherian formal scheme is proper.

*Acceptance.*

- The p-adic completion of P¹_{ℤ_p} (or of any proper ℤ_p-scheme) is proper over Spf ℤ_p; Spf ℤ_p⟨T⟩ is not proper over Spf ℤ_p since A¹_{F_p} is not proper over F_p.
- A formal scheme X proper over Spf A need not be the completion of a scheme proper over Spec A (EGA III, 5.4.3); the ample-line-bundle hypothesis of AdicSpacesPartII:F0/grothendieck-algebraization is what makes it algebraic.

*Uses.* EGA III, 5.1.4, 5.4.1 and 5.4.5: the existence theorem concerns coherent sheaves with support proper over Spf A; full faithfulness and algebraisation concern formal schemes proper over Spf A. EGA III, 3.4.2: finiteness theorem for proper formal morphisms (R^q f_* of coherent is coherent), recorded as an API consequence of the formal-functions results. ModularCurvesPartII R13.1 and AlgebraicModuliForArithmeticGeometry R09.6: proper formal deformations of generalised elliptic curves and of proper moduli objects are algebraised. AdicSpacesPartII:R2/good-reduction-locus: the generic fibre of the completion of X equals X^ad exactly when X is proper, i.e. X̂ is proper over Spf O_K.

*Depends on.* Morphisms of finite type of locally noetherian formal schemes (`AdicSpacesPartII:F0/formal-morphism-finite-type`); Adic morphisms of locally noetherian formal schemes (`AdicSpacesPartII:F0/adic-morphism-of-formal-schemes`); Ideals of definition of a formal scheme and the thickenings X_n (`AdicSpacesPartII:F0/ideal-of-definition`); Properness, finiteness and closed immersions are insensitive to thickenings (`AdicSpacesPartII:F0/thickening-invariance`); `mathlib:AlgebraicGeometry.IsProper`; `mathlib:AlgebraicGeometry.IsProper.isStableUnderBaseChange`; `mathlib:AlgebraicGeometry.UniversallyClosed`.

*Sources.* EGA-III-1-1961, Ch. III, (3.4.1), printed p. 119; EGA-III-1-1961, Ch. III, (3.4.1), printed p. 119; EGA-III-1-1961, Ch. III, (3.4.1), printed p. 119.


##### Closed formal subschemes and closed immersions

`AdicSpacesPartII:F0/closed-formal-subscheme` (construction; Lean module `TauCeti/AlgebraicGeometry/FormalScheme/ClosedImmersion`, namespace `TauCeti.FormalScheme`)

Let X be a locally noetherian formal scheme and 𝒜 ⊆ O_X a coherent ideal (AdicSpacesPartII:F0/coherent-formal-module). Its support Y = Supp(O_X/𝒜) is closed and (Y, (O_X/𝒜)|_Y) is a locally noetherian formal scheme, noetherian if X is (EGA I, 10.14.1): the closed formal subscheme X.subscheme 𝒜, with canonical morphism j : X.subscheme 𝒜 → X. The assignment 𝒜 ↦ X.subscheme 𝒜 is a bijection from coherent ideals onto closed formal subschemes. A closed immersion is a morphism isomorphic over X to some j (EGA I, 10.14.2). On X = Spf A (A adic noetherian) every coherent ideal is 𝔞^Δ for an ideal 𝔞 of A and Spf A.subscheme 𝔞^Δ ≅ Spf(A/𝔞), with j = Spf of the quotient map. Closed immersions are adic and of finite type (EGA I, 10.14.3); for a locally noetherian scheme X with closed subset X′ and a closed subscheme Z of X, the completion Ẑ_{/Z∩X′} is the closed formal subscheme of X̂ defined by the completed ideal (EGA I, 10.14.7, used in EGA III, 5.1.8).

*Hypotheses.* X locally noetherian formal scheme; 𝒜 coherent ideal of O_X.

*Construction / proof route.*

1. For an ideal of definition 𝒥, the O_X/(𝒜 + 𝒥^{n+1}) are coherent O_{X_n}-modules with support Y (AdicSpacesPartII:F0/coherent-as-inverse-system); the schemes Y_n := V(𝒜 + 𝒥^{n+1}) ⊆ X_n form an adic thickening system with Y_0 locally noetherian, and O_X/𝒜 = lim O_X/(𝒜 + 𝒥^{n+1}); hence (Y, O_X/𝒜) is the formal scheme ofThickenings(Y_n) (AdicSpacesPartII:F0/colimit-of-thickenings; EGA I, 10.14.1).
2. Affine case: 𝒜 = 𝔞^Δ by AdicSpacesPartII:F0/affine-coherent-equivalence, and exactness of (-)^Δ gives O/𝒜 = (A/𝔞)^Δ, so the subscheme is Spf(A/𝔞) (AdicSpacesPartII:F0/adic-ring, API quotient).
3. Adic and finite type: affine-locally Spf(A/𝔞) → Spf A has I(A/𝔞) an ideal of definition and A/𝔞 a quotient of A{∅} (AdicSpacesPartII:F0/formal-morphism-finite-type).
4. Completion of closed subschemes: exactness of completion of coherent sheaves (AdicSpacesPartII:F0/completion-exact) applied to 0 → 𝓐 → O_X → O_Z → 0.

*API.*

- `FormalScheme.subscheme` (constructor): X.subscheme 𝒜 : FormalScheme for a coherent ideal 𝒜 ⊆ O_X; locally noetherian; noetherian if X is.
- `FormalScheme.subschemeι` (projection): j : X.subscheme 𝒜 ⟶ X, with underlying map the inclusion of Supp(O_X/𝒜) and surjective sheaf map of kernel 𝒜.
- `FormalScheme.Hom.IsClosedImmersion` (structure): class: f factors as an isomorphism followed by X.subscheme 𝒜 ⟶ X for a coherent ideal 𝒜 (then 𝒜 = ker f^♯ is unique).
- `FormalScheme.Hom.IsClosedImmersion.ker` (data): The coherent ideal ker(O_X → f_*O_Z) of a closed immersion; subscheme (ker f) ≅ Z.
- `FormalScheme.Hom.IsClosedImmersion.comp` (instance): Closed immersions are stable under composition and base change.
- `FormalScheme.Hom.IsClosedImmersion.finiteType` (instance): A closed immersion is adic and of finite type (EGA I, 10.14.3).
- `FormalScheme.subscheme_Spf` (equivalence): (Spf A).subscheme 𝔞^Δ ≅ Spf (A ⧸ 𝔞) over Spf A.
- `FormalScheme.completion_subscheme` (compatibility): For a closed subscheme Z = V(𝓐) of a locally noetherian scheme X and closed X′, Ẑ_{/Z∩X′} ≅ X̂.subscheme 𝓐̂ over X̂.

*Unit tests.*

- `FormalScheme.subscheme_Spf_quotient_example` (computation): For IsAdicRing A, A noetherian, and an ideal 𝔞: (Spf A).subscheme (𝔞^Δ) ≅ Spf (A ⧸ 𝔞), and j corresponds to Ideal.Quotient.mk 𝔞.
- `FormalScheme.subscheme_zero` (degenerate): X.subscheme 0 = X with j the identity; X.subscheme ⊤ is empty.
- `FormalScheme.subscheme_idealOfDefinition` (compatibility): For an ideal of definition 𝒥, X.subscheme 𝒥 ≅ FormalScheme.ofScheme (X.thickening 𝒥 0).
- `FormalScheme.IsClosedImmersion.not_of_homeomorph` (non-example): Spf ℤ_[p]⟦T⟧ ⟶ Spf ℤ_[p] is a homeomorphism of underlying spaces (both are points) but not a closed immersion: ℤ_[p] → ℤ_[p]⟦T⟧ is not surjective. A definition by the underlying topological map alone (closed embedding) accepts it; while Spec F_p ⟶ Spf ℤ_[p] is a closed immersion that is a homeomorphism but not an isomorphism.

*Acceptance.*

- Spf ℤ_p⟦T⟧.subscheme (T − p)^Δ ≅ Spf ℤ_p (a section of Spf ℤ_p⟦T⟧ → Spf ℤ_p).
- An ideal of definition 𝒥 is coherent and X.subscheme 𝒥 = X_0 is a scheme.

*Uses.* EGA III, 5.1.8 and 5.4.1: closed formal subschemes proper over Spf A are completions of closed subschemes; graphs of formal morphisms are closed formal subschemes. EGA III, 5.4.5: the formal scheme to be algebraised is embedded as a closed formal subscheme of the completion of a projective space. AdicSpacesPartII:R2/admissible-blow-up: admissible blow-ups and closed formal subschemes cut out by coherent ideals of O_X.

*Depends on.* Coherent modules on a locally noetherian formal scheme (`AdicSpacesPartII:F0/coherent-formal-module`); Coherent modules on a locally noetherian formal scheme as compatible systems (`AdicSpacesPartII:F0/coherent-as-inverse-system`); The formal scheme attached to an adic system of thickenings (`AdicSpacesPartII:F0/colimit-of-thickenings`); Coherent modules on Spf A are finite A-modules (`AdicSpacesPartII:F0/affine-coherent-equivalence`); Morphisms of finite type of locally noetherian formal schemes (`AdicSpacesPartII:F0/formal-morphism-finite-type`); Adic rings of finite ideal type and their ideals of definition (`AdicSpacesPartII:F0/adic-ring`); Completion of coherent sheaves is exact, agrees with pullback along X̂ → X, and commutes with ⊗, Hom and base change (`AdicSpacesPartII:F0/completion-exact`); The formal completion of a locally noetherian scheme along a closed subset (`AdicSpacesPartII:F0/formal-completion`).

*Sources.* EGA-I-1960, Ch. I, (10.14.2) Définition, printed p. 210; EGA-I-1960, Ch. I, after (10.14.2), printed p. 210; EGA-I-1960, Ch. I, after (10.14.2), printed p. 210; EGA-I-1960, Ch. I, (10.14.3) Proposition, printed p. 210.


##### An adic morphism is a closed immersion iff its reduction is

`AdicSpacesPartII:F0/formal-closed-immersion-criterion` (lemma; Lean module `TauCeti/AlgebraicGeometry/FormalScheme/ClosedImmersion`, namespace `TauCeti.FormalScheme`)

Let f : X → Y be an adic morphism of locally noetherian formal schemes, 𝒦 an ideal of definition of Y and 𝒥 = f*(𝒦)O_X. Then f is a closed immersion if and only if f_0 : (X, O_X/𝒥) → (Y, O_Y/𝒦) is a closed immersion of schemes (EGA III, 4.8.10).

*Hypotheses.* f adic; X, Y locally noetherian.

*Construction / proof route.*

1. Necessity: base change of the closed immersion f along Y_0 → Y (X_0 = X ×_Y Y_0 by adicness, AdicSpacesPartII:F0/adic-morphism-of-formal-schemes).
2. Sufficiency, local on Y: let Y = Spf B with ideal of definition K. X_0 is affine (closed in the affine Y_0), hence every X_n is affine (EGA I, 5.1.9, as in AdicSpacesPartII:F0/colimit-of-thickenings), X_n = Spec A_n, and X = Spf A with A = lim A_n, A_n = A/K^{n+1}A by adicness.
3. A is a finite B-module generated by 1: the system (A_n) satisfies the hypotheses of AdicSpacesPartII:F0/finite-module-inverse-limit over B with A_0 = A/KA cyclic over B/K (f_0 closed immersion), so A is finite over B; by Nakayama (Mathlib Submodule.eq_bot_of_le_smul_of_le_jacobson_bot, with K ⊆ Jacobson radical of B by AdicSpacesPartII:F0/adic-ring) the cyclic generator 1 of A/KA generates A, i.e. B → A is surjective.
4. Hence A = B/𝔞 and f is the closed immersion Spf(B/𝔞) → Spf B (AdicSpacesPartII:F0/closed-formal-subscheme, subscheme_Spf).

*Acceptance.*

- Spf ℤ_p⟦T⟧ → Spf ℤ_p⟦S, T⟧ (S ↦ 0) is adic with reduction Spec F_p → Spec F_p an isomorphism; it is a closed immersion.
- Without adicness the criterion fails: Spf ℤ_p⟦T⟧ → Spf ℤ_p has reduction (modulo (p,T) and (p)) an isomorphism Spec F_p → Spec F_p but is not a closed immersion.

*Depends on.* Adic morphisms of locally noetherian formal schemes (`AdicSpacesPartII:F0/adic-morphism-of-formal-schemes`); Finite modules over an adic noetherian ring as compatible systems (`AdicSpacesPartII:F0/finite-module-inverse-limit`); Closed formal subschemes and closed immersions (`AdicSpacesPartII:F0/closed-formal-subscheme`); Adic rings of finite ideal type and their ideals of definition (`AdicSpacesPartII:F0/adic-ring`); The formal scheme attached to an adic system of thickenings (`AdicSpacesPartII:F0/colimit-of-thickenings`); `mathlib:Submodule.eq_bot_of_le_smul_of_le_jacobson_bot`; `mathlib:AlgebraicGeometry.IsClosedImmersion`.

*Sources.* EGA-III-1-1961, Ch. III, (4.8.10) Corollaire, printed p. 148.


#### F0.5 Completion along a closed subset

```text
X̂_{/X′} = (X′, lim_n O_X/𝓘^{n+1}),     Spec(A)^_{/V(I)} = Spf Â,     F̂ = lim_n F/𝓘^{n+1}F ≅ i_X*F.
```

##### The formal completion of a locally noetherian scheme along a closed subset

`AdicSpacesPartII:F0/formal-completion` (construction — planet “Formal completion”; Lean module `TauCeti/AlgebraicGeometry/FormalScheme/Completion`, namespace `TauCeti.FormalScheme`)

Let X be a locally noetherian scheme and X′ ⊆ X a closed subset. Let 𝓘 ⊆ O_X be a quasi-coherent ideal of finite type with V(𝓘) = X′ (for example the ideal of the reduced induced closed subscheme). The formal completion X̂ = X̂_{/X′} is the locally noetherian formal scheme ofThickenings(V(𝓘^{n+1}))_n (AdicSpacesPartII:F0/colimit-of-thickenings): its underlying space is X′ and O_X̂ = lim_n (O_X/𝓘^{n+1})|_{X′}. It does not depend on 𝓘: all such ideals form a filtered set Φ, and on noetherian opens the powers of any one member are cofinal in Φ (EGA I, 10.8.2); 𝓘O_X̂ is an ideal of definition. For X = Spec A (A noetherian) and X′ = V(I): X̂ ≅ Spf Â where Â = AdicCompletion I A with the I-adic topology (EGA I, 10.8.5). Further: X̂_red is the reduced closed subscheme with space X′; X̂ is noetherian iff X′ is quasi-compact (EGA I, 10.8.6); there is a canonical morphism of locally ringed spaces i_X : X̂ → X (the inclusion of X′ with O_X → i_*O_X̂ the limit of the quotient maps) (EGA I, 10.8.7), which is flat (AdicSpacesPartII:F0/completion-exact); for U ⊆ X open, Û_{/U∩X′} is the open formal subscheme of X̂ on U ∩ X′; for X′ = X, X̂ = X.

*Hypotheses.* X locally noetherian scheme (Mathlib IsLocallyNoetherian); X′ closed subset; 𝓘 quasi-coherent of finite type with V(𝓘) = X′.

*Construction / proof route.*

1. The schemes X_n := V(𝓘^{n+1}) (Mathlib Scheme.IdealSheafData.subscheme) all have underlying space X′; the closed immersions X_n → X_{n+1} have kernel 𝓘^{n+1}/𝓘^{n+2}, and 𝓘/𝓘² is of finite type over O_{X_0}; so (X_n) is an adic thickening system with X_0 locally noetherian and ofThickenings gives a locally noetherian formal scheme (AdicSpacesPartII:F0/colimit-of-thickenings).
2. Affine case: Γ(X_n) = A/I^{n+1}, so X̂ = Spf(lim A/I^{n+1}) = Spf Â, and Â is noetherian and I·Â-adic (AdicSpacesPartII:F0/adic-completion-noetherian (ii), AdicSpacesPartII:F0/formal-spectrum).
3. Independence of 𝓘: for 𝓘, 𝓘′ ∈ Φ, on a noetherian affine open 𝓘^n ⊆ 𝓘′ and 𝓘′^m ⊆ 𝓘 (EGA I, 10.8.2; nilradical of O_X/𝓘 nilpotent on noetherian opens), so the two systems are cofinal and the limit sheaves agree (AdicSpacesPartII:F0/spf-ideal-independence affine-locally).
4. The canonical morphism i_X: the maps O_X → O_X/𝓘^{n+1} are compatible and give O_X → i_*lim O_X/𝓘^{n+1}; stalk maps are local because each O_{X,x} → O_{X_n,x} is surjective (EGA I, 10.8.7).

*API.*

- `FormalScheme.completion` (data): FormalScheme.completion X X′ : FormalScheme for IsLocallyNoetherian X and closed X′; locally noetherian.
- `FormalScheme.completion.ofIdeal` (constructor): For 𝓘 of finite type with support X′, the isomorphism completion X X′ ≅ ofThickenings (n ↦ (𝓘^(n+1)).subscheme); independent of 𝓘.
- `FormalScheme.completion.toScheme` (projection): i_X : completion X X′ ⟶ X as a morphism of locally ringed spaces, the inclusion X′ → X on spaces.
- `FormalScheme.completion.idealOfDefinition` (data): 𝓘·O_X̂ is an ideal of definition, with thickening n ≅ (𝓘^(n+1)).subscheme.
- `FormalScheme.completion.specIso` (equivalence): completion (Spec A) (zeroLocus I) ≅ Spf (AdicCompletion I A) for noetherian A.
- `FormalScheme.completion.restrict` (compatibility): For U ⊆ X open, completion U (U ∩ X′) ≅ (completion X X′).restrict (U ∩ X′).
- `FormalScheme.completion.isNoetherian_iff` (characterisation): completion X X′ is noetherian iff X′ is quasi-compact, for X locally noetherian (EGA I, 10.8.6).
- `FormalScheme.completion.reduction` (other): (completion X X′)_red ≅ the reduced closed subscheme of X with space X′.
- `FormalScheme.completion.self` (example): completion X univ ≅ FormalScheme.ofScheme X.
- `FormalScheme.completion.flat` (instance): i_X is flat: O_{X,x} → O_{X̂,x} is flat for x ∈ X′ (promoted: AdicSpacesPartII:F0/completion-exact).

*Unit tests.*

- `FormalScheme.completion_Spec_padic` (computation): FormalScheme.completion (Spec ℤ) (zeroLocus {p}) ≅ Spf ℤ_[p].
- `FormalScheme.completion_affine` (characterisation): For a noetherian ring A and an ideal I, FormalScheme.completion (Spec A) (zeroLocus I) ≅ Spf (AdicCompletion I A) with the I-adic topology.
- `FormalScheme.completion_self` (degenerate): For X′ = X (closed subset univ), FormalScheme.completion X univ ≅ FormalScheme.ofScheme X; for X′ = ∅ it is empty.
- `FormalScheme.completion_not_scheme` (non-example): The completion of Spec ℤ along V(p) is not a scheme viewed as a formal scheme: it is Spf ℤ_[p], a one-point space with global sections ℤ_[p], while Spec ℤ_[p] has two points. A construction taking only the closed subscheme V(𝓘) (or the colimit in schemes) loses this.
- `FormalScheme.completion_ideal_independent` (compatibility): The completions of Spec k[x,y] built from the ideals (y) and (y², x y) (both with zero locus the x-axis) are canonically isomorphic, compatibly with the canonical maps to Spec k[x,y].

*Acceptance.*

- The completion of Spec ℤ along V(p) is Spf ℤ_p; the completion of A²_k = Spec k[x,y] along the x-axis V(y) is Spf k[x]⟦y⟧.
- The completion of P¹_{ℤ_p} along its special fibre V(p) is the non-affine noetherian formal scheme obtained by gluing (AdicSpacesPartII:F0/formal-scheme-gluing).
- For X′ = X the completion is X itself (𝓘 = 0), and for X′ = ∅ it is empty.

*Uses.* EGA III, 4.1.1 and 5.1.1: the comparison and existence theorems compare X with X̂ along the preimage of V(I). AdicSpacesPartII:R2/formal-completion-and-algebraic-comparison and R2/good-reduction-locus: the generic fibre d(X̂) of the completion of a model along its special fibre, compared with the analytification of the generic fibre. ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology H1:formal-adic-comparison: for a scheme X and a finite-type ideal defining Y, the completion X̂ and the maps i : Y → X, j : U → X in Huber 3.5.12–3.5.13. CohomologyComparisons CP.0: comparison functors between a formal scheme, its special fibre and the completion of an algebraic model. ModularCurvesPartII R13.1 and tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/ModularCurves 7C: completions of curves along sections or cusps (formal groups, Tate curves); 7C constructs the completion at the zero section intrinsically as a formal group and can be compared with X̂ along the section. LocalGaloisDeformationRings L7: completions of local models at closed points are compared with framed deformation rings.

*Depends on.* The formal scheme attached to an adic system of thickenings (`AdicSpacesPartII:F0/colimit-of-thickenings`); Noetherianity of adically complete rings and of adic completions (`AdicSpacesPartII:F0/adic-completion-noetherian`); The formal spectrum Spf A of an adic ring (`AdicSpacesPartII:F0/formal-spectrum`); Spf A depends only on the topology of A (`AdicSpacesPartII:F0/spf-ideal-independence`); Formal schemes and locally noetherian formal schemes (`AdicSpacesPartII:F0/locally-noetherian-formal-scheme`); Ideals of definition of a formal scheme and the thickenings X_n (`AdicSpacesPartII:F0/ideal-of-definition`); `mathlib:AlgebraicGeometry.IsLocallyNoetherian`; `mathlib:AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.IdealSheafData`; `mathlib:AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.IdealSheafData.subscheme`; `mathlib:AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.IdealSheafData.subschemeι`; `mathlib:AdicCompletion`.

*Sources.* EGA-I-1960, Ch. I, (10.8.2) Lemme, printed p. 194; EGA-I-1960, Ch. I, (10.8.5) Proposition, printed p. 195; EGA-I-1960, Ch. I, (10.8.5) Proposition, printed p. 195; EGA-I-1960, Ch. I, after (10.8.5), printed p. 195.


##### Extension of a morphism to formal completions

`AdicSpacesPartII:F0/completion-of-morphism` (construction; Lean module `TauCeti/AlgebraicGeometry/FormalScheme/Completion`, namespace `TauCeti.FormalScheme`)

Let f : X → Y be a morphism of locally noetherian schemes and X′ ⊆ X, Y′ ⊆ Y closed with f(X′) ⊆ Y′. There is a unique morphism of formal schemes f̂ : X̂_{/X′} → Ŷ_{/Y′} with i_Y ∘ f̂ = f ∘ i_X; it is the colimit of the morphisms V(𝓘^{n+1}) → V(𝓚^{n+1}) induced by f for ideals with f*(𝓚)O_X ⊆ 𝓘, and does not depend on the ideals (EGA I, 10.9.1–10.9.2). On underlying spaces f̂ is the restriction of f to X′. Functoriality: (g ∘ f)^ = ĝ ∘ f̂ and id^ = id (EGA I, 10.9.3). Affine case: for f = Spec φ, φ : B → A, f̂ = Spf φ̂ with φ̂ : B̂ → Â the continuous extension (EGA I, 10.9.1). Base change: if X′ = f⁻¹(Y′) then X̂ ≅ X ×_Y Ŷ as formal schemes, where X is viewed as a formal scheme (EGA I, 10.9.9), and f̂ is adic; completion commutes with fibre products (EGA I, 10.9.7).

*Hypotheses.* X, Y locally noetherian; f(X′) ⊆ Y′; base change statement needs X′ = f⁻¹(Y′); product statement needs X ×_S Y locally noetherian.

*Construction / proof route.*

1. Choose 𝓚 of finite type with V(𝓚) = Y′ and 𝓘 with V(𝓘) = X′ and f*(𝓚)O_X ⊆ 𝓘 (take 𝓘 the ideal of the reduced induced structure; EGA I, 10.9.1); then f*(𝓚^{n+1})O_X ⊆ 𝓘^{n+1} and f induces compatible f_n; define f̂ = colim f_n (AdicSpacesPartII:F0/morphisms-as-compatible-systems (ii)).
2. Uniqueness and independence: two choices of ideals give cofinal systems; the compatibility with i_X, i_Y determines f̂ on the sheaf level since O_X̂ is the limit (AdicSpacesPartII:F0/formal-completion).
3. Affine case: f_n corresponds to B/K^{n+1} → A/I^{n+1}; the limit is the continuous extension φ̂ (Mathlib AdicCompletion.map for modules; IsAdicComplete.liftRingHom for rings).
4. Base change X̂ = X ×_Y Ŷ: affine-locally (B̂ ⊗̂_B A) = Â for the KA-adic completion (AdicSpacesPartII:F0/completed-tensor-product-adic with discrete A), using the fibre product of formal schemes (AdicSpacesPartII:F0/formal-fibre-product).

*API.*

- `FormalScheme.completion.map` (functoriality): completion.map f (h : f  X′ ⊆ Y′) : completion X X′ ⟶ completion Y Y′.
- `FormalScheme.completion.map_toScheme` (compatibility): completion.map f h ≫ i_Y = i_X ≫ f.
- `FormalScheme.completion.map_unique` (universal-property): A morphism g : X̂ ⟶ Ŷ with g ≫ i_Y = i_X ≫ f equals completion.map f.
- `FormalScheme.completion.map_id` (functoriality): map id = id.
- `FormalScheme.completion.map_comp` (functoriality): map (f ≫ g) = map f ≫ map g.
- `FormalScheme.completion.pullbackIso` (equivalence): If X′ = f⁻¹(Y′): completion X X′ ≅ pullback (ofScheme.map f) (i_Y) as formal schemes (EGA I, 10.9.9).
- `FormalScheme.completion.map_isAdic` (instance): If X′ = f⁻¹(Y′) then completion.map f is adic; if moreover f is of finite type (resp. proper) so is completion.map f.
- `FormalScheme.completion.prodIso` (compatibility): completion (X ×_S Y) (p⁻¹X′ ∩ q⁻¹Y′) ≅ X̂ ×_{Ŝ} Ŷ when X ×_S Y is locally noetherian (EGA I, 10.9.7).

*Unit tests.*

- `FormalScheme.completion.map_id_example` (degenerate): completion.map (𝟙 X) = 𝟙 (completion X X′).
- `FormalScheme.completion.map_comp_example` (characterisation): completion.map (f ≫ g) = completion.map f ≫ completion.map g whenever f(X′) ⊆ Y′ and g(Y′) ⊆ Z′.
- `FormalScheme.completion.map_Spec` (computation): For φ : B →+* A noetherian with φ(K) ⊆ I, completion.map (Spec.map φ) corresponds under specIso to Spf.map of AdicCompletion.map-induced ring hom B̂ → Â.
- `FormalScheme.completion.map_toScheme_example` (compatibility): completion.map f ≫ i_Y = i_X ≫ f.
- `FormalScheme.completion.map_not_adic` (non-example): For Spec ℤ[x] → Spec ℤ with X′ = V(p, x), Y′ = V(p), completion.map is Spf ℤ_[p]⟦x⟧ → Spf ℤ_[p], which is not adic; adicness needs X′ = f⁻¹(Y′).

*Acceptance.*

- For the inclusion f : A¹_{ℤ_p} → P¹_{ℤ_p} and X′, Y′ the special fibres, f̂ : Spf ℤ_p⟨x⟩ → P̂¹ is the open immersion of the first chart.
- For f = Spec(ℤ → ℤ[x]) and Y′ = V(p), X′ = V(p): f̂ : Spf ℤ_p⟨x⟩ → Spf ℤ_p; with X′ = V(p, x) instead, f̂ : Spf ℤ_p⟦x⟧ → Spf ℤ_p, which is not adic.

*Uses.* EGA III, 4.1.1, 5.1.1 and 5.4.1: f̂ : X̂ → Ŷ is the formal morphism in the comparison theorem, the existence theorem and the full-faithfulness theorem. AdicSpacesPartII:R2/formal-completion-and-algebraic-comparison: the square of σ’s for f locally of finite type and its completion f̂ (Huber 1.9.5). NeronModelsAndSemistableAbelianVarieties R11.1: completions of morphisms of models over a complete DVR (extension of morphisms of Néron models checked on completions).

*Depends on.* The formal completion of a locally noetherian scheme along a closed subset (`AdicSpacesPartII:F0/formal-completion`); Morphisms of locally noetherian formal schemes as compatible systems (`AdicSpacesPartII:F0/morphisms-as-compatible-systems`); Completed tensor product of adic rings of finite ideal type (`AdicSpacesPartII:F0/completed-tensor-product-adic`); Fibre products of formal schemes (`AdicSpacesPartII:F0/formal-fibre-product`); `mathlib:AdicCompletion.map`; `mathlib:IsAdicComplete.liftRingHom`.

*Sources.* EGA-I-1960, Ch. I, (10.9.1), printed p. 198; EGA-I-1960, Ch. I, (10.9.1), printed p. 198; EGA-I-1960, Ch. I, (10.9.3), printed p. 199; EGA-I-1960, Ch. I, (10.9.9) Corollaire, printed p. 200; EGA-I-1960, Ch. I, (10.9.7) Proposition, printed p. 200.


##### Morphisms with equal completions agree near the closed subset

`AdicSpacesPartII:F0/completion-morphism-germ` (lemma; Lean module `TauCeti/AlgebraicGeometry/FormalScheme/Completion`, namespace `TauCeti.FormalScheme`)

Let S be a scheme, X and Y locally noetherian S-schemes with Y of finite type over S, X′ ⊆ X and Y′ ⊆ Y closed, and f, g : X → Y two S-morphisms with f(X′) ⊆ Y′ and g(X′) ⊆ Y′. Then f̂ = ĝ as morphisms X̂_{/X′} → Ŷ_{/Y′} if and only if f and g coincide on an open neighbourhood of X′ (EGA I, 10.9.4).

*Hypotheses.* Y of finite type over S (needed for necessity); X, Y locally noetherian.

*Construction / proof route.*

1. Sufficiency: completion only depends on a neighbourhood of X′ (AdicSpacesPartII:F0/formal-completion, restrict; AdicSpacesPartII:F0/completion-of-morphism).
2. Necessity: f̂ = ĝ gives f(x) = g(x) on X′; the question is local, so take X, Y, S affine with rings A, B, R, B of finite type over R generated by b_1,…,b_r, and f, g given by ρ, σ : B → A.
3. The continuous extensions of ρ, σ to the completions agree, so for each b_i the section ρ(b_i) − σ(b_i) of O_X maps to 0 in Γ(X̂, O_X̂); by AdicSpacesPartII:F0/completion-detects-near-closed (kernel of Γ(X, F) → Γ(X̂, F̂)) it vanishes on a neighbourhood of X′; finitely many generators give one neighbourhood on which ρ = σ, hence a basic open D(h) ⊇ X′ ∩ Spec A on which f = g (EGA I, 10.9.4).

*Acceptance.*

- Two sections of A¹_{ℤ_p} → Spec ℤ_p given by x ↦ a, x ↦ b with a ≡ b mod p^n for all n are equal (ℤ_p separated): with X = Spec ℤ_p, X′ = V(p) the completion determines them.

*Uses.* EGA III, 5.4.1: injectivity in the full-faithfulness theorem.

*Depends on.* Extension of a morphism to formal completions (`AdicSpacesPartII:F0/completion-of-morphism`); The formal completion of a locally noetherian scheme along a closed subset (`AdicSpacesPartII:F0/formal-completion`); What completion sees: sections and maps near the closed subset (`AdicSpacesPartII:F0/completion-detects-near-closed`).

*Sources.* EGA-I-1960, Ch. I, (10.9.4) Proposition, printed p. 199.


##### Completion of a coherent sheaf along a closed subset

`AdicSpacesPartII:F0/completion-of-coherent-sheaf` (construction; Lean module `TauCeti/AlgebraicGeometry/FormalScheme/Completion`, namespace `TauCeti.FormalScheme`)

Let X be a locally noetherian scheme, X′ ⊆ X closed with completion X̂ = X̂_{/X′}, and F a coherent O_X-module. The completion of F along X′ is F̂ = F_{/X′} := lim_n (F ⊗_{O_X} O_X/𝓘^{n+1})|_{X′} for any 𝓘 of finite type with V(𝓘) = X′; it is independent of 𝓘, a coherent O_X̂-module, and its sections over X̂ are the formal sections of F along X′ (EGA I, 10.8.4). For quasi-compact open U, Γ(U ∩ X′, F̂) = lim_n Γ(U, F/𝓘^{n+1}F). A morphism u : F → G induces û : F̂ → Ĝ, (v ∘ u)^ = v̂ ∘ û, so completion is an additive functor Coh(X) → Coh(X̂). For X = Spec A, F = M~ with M finite: Γ(X̂, F̂) = M̂ = AdicCompletion I M ≅ M ⊗_A Â (EGA I, 10.8.4, 10.10.1; EGA 0, 7.3.3). There is a canonical functorial isomorphism i_X*(F) ≅ F̂, and completion is exact (AdicSpacesPartII:F0/completion-exact). Completion is compatible with ⊗ and Hom: (F ⊗ G)^ ≅ F̂ ⊗ Ĝ, Hom(F, G)^ ≅ Hom(F̂, Ĝ) (EGA I, 10.8.10), and with pullback: for f : X → Y and coherent G on Y, (f*G)^ ≅ f̂*(Ĝ) (EGA I, 10.9.5).

*Hypotheses.* X locally noetherian; F coherent (Mathlib-level: a finitely presented quasi-coherent O_X-module).

*Construction / proof route.*

1. Define F̂ as the limit of the O_{X_n}-modules F_n := F ⊗ O_X/𝓘^{n+1} viewed on the common space X′; it is an O_X̂-module since O_X̂ = lim O_X/𝓘^{n+1} (AdicSpacesPartII:F0/formal-completion). It is finitely presented: locally F has a presentation O^m → O^n → F → 0 with O = O_{Spec A}, A noetherian, and adic completion of finite A-modules is exact (Mathlib AdicCompletion.map_exact), so Ô^m → Ô^n → F̂ → 0 is exact on the corresponding affine formal open.
2. Independence of 𝓘 as for AdicSpacesPartII:F0/formal-completion (cofinal systems).
3. Affine description: Γ(X̂, F̂) = lim M/I^{n+1}M = AdicCompletion I M, and M ⊗_A Â ≅ M̂ for finite M over noetherian A (Mathlib AdicCompletion.ofTensorProductEquivOfFiniteNoetherian).
4. Functoriality in F: a morphism u induces compatible maps u ⊗ O_X/𝓘^{n+1} and their limit û; (v ∘ u)^ = v̂ ∘ û. The ⊗, Hom and pullback compatibilities listed as API items are proved in AdicSpacesPartII:F0/completion-exact.

*API.*

- `FormalScheme.completeModule` (functoriality): The additive functor Coh(X) ⥤ Coh(completion X X′), F ↦ F̂.
- `FormalScheme.completeModule.sectionsIso` (equivalence): For quasi-compact open U, Γ(U ∩ X′, F̂) ≅ lim_n Γ(U, F/𝓘^(n+1)F).
- `FormalScheme.completeModule.specIso` (equivalence): For X = Spec A: Γ(X̂, (tilde M)^) ≅ AdicCompletion I M ≅ M ⊗[A] AdicCompletion I A.
- `FormalScheme.completeModule.pullbackIso` (equivalence): i_X*(F) ≅ F̂, natural in F (EGA I, 10.8.8 (ii)).
- `FormalScheme.completeModule.tensorIso` (compatibility): (F ⊗ G)^ ≅ F̂ ⊗ Ĝ.
- `FormalScheme.completeModule.homIso` (compatibility): Hom(F, G)^ ≅ Hom(F̂, Ĝ) (internal Hom of coherent modules).
- `FormalScheme.completeModule.pullbackCompletionIso` (compatibility): (f*G)^ ≅ (completion.map f)*(Ĝ) (EGA I, 10.9.5).
- `FormalScheme.completeModule.support` (other): Supp F̂ = Supp F ∩ X′ (EGA I, 10.8.12).
- `FormalScheme.completeModule.reductionIso` (projection): F̂ ⊗ O_{X̂_n} ≅ F/𝓘^(n+1)F, i.e. (F̂)_n = F_n.

*Unit tests.*

- `FormalScheme.completeModule_structureSheaf` (degenerate): (O_X)^ ≅ O_X̂ as O_X̂-modules.
- `FormalScheme.completeModule_Spec` (computation): For X = Spec A, X′ = zeroLocus I and M a finite A-module, Γ(X̂, (tilde M)^) ≅ AdicCompletion I M as Â-modules.
- `FormalScheme.completeModule_self` (compatibility): For X′ = X, F̂ ≅ F under completion X univ ≅ ofScheme X.
- `FormalScheme.completeModule_supportDisjoint` (characterisation): If Supp F ∩ X′ = ∅ then F̂ = 0; more precisely Supp F̂ = Supp F ∩ X′ (EGA I, 10.8.12).
- `FormalScheme.completeModule_torsion` (non-example): For X = Spec ℤ, X′ = V(p) and F = (ℤ/ℓ)~ with ℓ ≠ p prime, F ≠ 0 but F̂ = 0: completion is not faithful on coherent sheaves; it only detects F near X′.

*Acceptance.*

- For X = Spec ℤ, X′ = V(p), F = (ℤ/p²)~ ⊕ ℤ~: F̂ corresponds to the ℤ_p-module ℤ/p² ⊕ ℤ_p; for F = (ℤ[1/p])~, which is quasi-coherent but not coherent, the limit is 0, illustrating why coherence is required.
- For X′ = X, F̂ = F.

*Uses.* EGA III, 4.1.1–4.1.5: the theorem on formal functions compares (R^n f_*F)^ with R^n f̂_*(F̂). EGA III, 5.1.4: Grothendieck existence: F ↦ F̂ is an equivalence for X proper over Spec A. AdicSpacesPartII:F0/associated-formal-module: M^Δ on Spf A is the completion of M~ along V(I). TorsionCohomologyInfrastructure TC.0: compatibility of ideal-of-boundary sheaves with completion.

*Depends on.* The formal completion of a locally noetherian scheme along a closed subset (`AdicSpacesPartII:F0/formal-completion`); Coherent modules on a locally noetherian formal scheme (`AdicSpacesPartII:F0/coherent-formal-module`); Extension of a morphism to formal completions (`AdicSpacesPartII:F0/completion-of-morphism`); `mathlib:AdicCompletion`; `mathlib:AdicCompletion.map_exact`; `mathlib:AdicCompletion.ofTensorProductEquivOfFiniteNoetherian`; `mathlib:AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Modules`; `mathlib:SheafOfModules.IsFinitePresentation`.

##### Completion of coherent sheaves is exact, agrees with pullback along X̂ → X, and commutes with ⊗, Hom and base change

`AdicSpacesPartII:F0/completion-exact` (lemma; Lean module `TauCeti/AlgebraicGeometry/FormalScheme/Completion`, namespace `TauCeti.FormalScheme`)

Let X be a locally noetherian scheme, X′ ⊆ X closed and i_X : X̂ → X the canonical morphism. (i) F ↦ F̂ is an exact functor on coherent O_X-modules. (ii) The canonical map i_X*(F) → F̂ is an isomorphism of O_X̂-modules, natural in F. (iii) i_X is flat: for x ∈ X′, O_{X̂,x} is a flat O_{X,x}-module (EGA I, 10.8.8–10.8.9). (iv) For coherent F, G there are natural isomorphisms (F ⊗ G)^ ≅ F̂ ⊗ Ĝ and Hom(F, G)^ ≅ Hom(F̂, Ĝ) (EGA I, 10.8.10). (v) For a morphism f : X → Y of locally noetherian schemes with f(X′) ⊆ Y′ and coherent G on Y, (f*G)^ ≅ f̂*(Ĝ) (EGA I, 10.9.5).

*Hypotheses.* X locally noetherian; F coherent.

*Construction / proof route.*

1. (i) Local on X; on an affine open Spec A (A noetherian) with X′ = V(I), a short exact sequence of coherent sheaves is 0 → M′~ → M~ → M″~ → 0 with finite A-modules, and completion of finite modules over a noetherian ring is exact (Mathlib AdicCompletion.map_exact, AdicCompletion.map_injective, AdicCompletion.map_surjective).
2. (ii) Both sides are right exact in F and commute with finite direct sums; F is locally a cokernel of O^m → O^n, so reduce to F = O_X, where both sides are O_X̂ (EGA I, 10.8.8 (ii)).
3. (iii) Flatness of i_X at x ∈ X′ means that O_{X,x} → O_{X̂,x} is flat; by the local criterion of EGA 0, 6.7.3 it suffices that F ↦ i_X*F is exact on coherent O_X-modules, which is (i) and (ii). (Affine-locally this is the flatness of Â over A, Mathlib AdicCompletion.flat_of_isNoetherian, on global sections.)
4. (iv) By (ii), completion is pullback along i_X; pullback commutes with ⊗ for every morphism of ringed spaces and with internal Hom of finitely presented modules along flat morphisms (EGA 0, 4.3.3.1 and 6.7.6), using (iii).
5. (v) From (ii) and i_Y ∘ f̂ = f ∘ i_X (AdicSpacesPartII:F0/completion-of-morphism): f̂*Ĝ = f̂*i_Y*G = i_X*f*G = (f*G)^.

*Acceptance.*

- For X = Spec ℤ and X′ = V(p) the exact sequence 0 → ℤ → ℤ → ℤ/p → 0 (multiplication by p) completes to 0 → ℤ_p → ℤ_p → F_p → 0.

*Uses.* EGA III, 5.2.2: kernels, images and cokernels of maps between algebraizable sheaves are algebraizable.

*Depends on.* The formal completion of a locally noetherian scheme along a closed subset (`AdicSpacesPartII:F0/formal-completion`); Completion of a coherent sheaf along a closed subset (`AdicSpacesPartII:F0/completion-of-coherent-sheaf`); Extension of a morphism to formal completions (`AdicSpacesPartII:F0/completion-of-morphism`); `mathlib:AdicCompletion.map_exact`; `mathlib:AdicCompletion.map_injective`; `mathlib:AdicCompletion.map_surjective`; `mathlib:AdicCompletion.flat_of_isNoetherian`; `mathlib:Module.Flat`.

*Sources.* EGA-I-1960, Ch. I, (10.8.8) Proposition, printed p. 196; EGA-I-1960, Ch. I, (10.8.9) Corollaire, printed p. 197; EGA-I-1960, Ch. I, (10.8.10) Corollaire, printed p. 197; EGA-I-1960, Ch. I, (10.9.5) Proposition, printed p. 199; Stacks-Project, Tag 0881 (Lemma 30.23.4).


##### What completion sees: sections and maps near the closed subset

`AdicSpacesPartII:F0/completion-detects-near-closed` (lemma; Lean module `TauCeti/AlgebraicGeometry/FormalScheme/Completion`, namespace `TauCeti.FormalScheme`)

Let X be a locally noetherian scheme, X′ ⊆ X closed, F, G coherent O_X-modules and u : F → G. (i) The kernel of Γ(X, F) → Γ(X̂, F̂) consists of the sections vanishing on an open neighbourhood of X′ (EGA I, 10.8.11). (ii) Supp F̂ = Supp F ∩ X′ (EGA I, 10.8.12). (iii) û = 0 iff u vanishes on a neighbourhood of X′ (EGA I, 10.8.13). (iv) û is a monomorphism (resp. epimorphism) iff u is one on a neighbourhood of X′ (EGA I, 10.8.14).

*Hypotheses.* X locally noetherian; F, G coherent.

*Construction / proof route.*

1. (i) Local; on Spec A with F = M~ (A noetherian, M finite), the kernel of M → M̂ = AdicCompletion I M (Mathlib AdicCompletion.of) is ⋂ I^n M, which by Krull's theorem (Mathlib Ideal.mem_iInf_smul_pow_eq_bot_iff: x ∈ ⋂ I^n M iff r • x = x for some r ∈ I) is the set of m killed by 1 − r for some r ∈ I (EGA 0, 7.3.7); such m vanishes on D(1 − r) ⊇ V(I), and conversely a section vanishing near V(I) is killed by such an element.
2. (ii) F̂ is of finite type so its support is closed and contained in Supp F ∩ X′; equality from (i) applied at points.
3. (iii) û corresponds to the section of Hom(F, G)^ ≅ Hom(F̂, Ĝ) (AdicSpacesPartII:F0/completion-exact (iv)) induced by u; apply (i) to the coherent sheaf Hom(F, G).
4. (iv) Apply (iii) to ker u and coker u, using exactness (AdicSpacesPartII:F0/completion-exact) and coherence of kernels and cokernels.

*Acceptance.*

- For X = Spec ℤ, X′ = V(p) and u = multiplication by ℓ ≠ p on O_X, û is an isomorphism and u is an isomorphism on the neighbourhood D(ℓ) of V(p), but not globally.

*Uses.* EGA III, 5.1.3: combined with 5.1.3.1 (every neighbourhood of X′ is X when f is closed), u is injective/surjective iff û is. EGA III, 4.6.8: isomorphisms of proper schemes are detected on completions.

*Depends on.* Completion of a coherent sheaf along a closed subset (`AdicSpacesPartII:F0/completion-of-coherent-sheaf`); Completion of coherent sheaves is exact, agrees with pullback along X̂ → X, and commutes with ⊗, Hom and base change (`AdicSpacesPartII:F0/completion-exact`); `mathlib:Ideal.mem_iInf_smul_pow_eq_bot_iff`; `mathlib:AdicCompletion.of`.

*Sources.* EGA-I-1960, Ch. I, (10.8.11) Proposition, printed p. 197; EGA-I-1960, Ch. I, (10.8.14) Corollaire, printed p. 198.


#### F0.6 Coherent formal modules

```text
Coh(Spf A) ≃ { finite A-modules },  M ↦ M^Δ;     Coh(X) ≃ { (F_n) : F_n ∈ Coh(X_n), u_n*F_{n+1} ≅ F_n }.
```

##### Coherent modules on a locally noetherian formal scheme

`AdicSpacesPartII:F0/coherent-formal-module` (definition; Lean module `TauCeti/AlgebraicGeometry/FormalScheme/Coherent`, namespace `TauCeti.FormalScheme`)

Let X be a locally noetherian formal scheme. An O_X-module is a sheaf of modules over the sheaf of rings O_X (Mathlib SheafOfModules over TauCeti.SheafOfModules.ringCatSheaf of the structure sheaf). It is coherent if it is locally finitely presented (Mathlib SheafOfModules.IsFinitePresentation). Because O_X is a coherent sheaf of rings (EGA I, 10.10.3, 10.11.1, proved in AdicSpacesPartII:F0/affine-coherent-equivalence), this agrees with EGA's coherence (finite type, and kernels of O_U^n → F|_U of finite type). Coh(X) denotes the full subcategory; it is abelian, closed under kernels, cokernels, extensions, ⊗ and internal Hom, and every ideal of definition is coherent. Every morphism between coherent O_X-modules is automatically continuous for the canonical topologies Γ(U, F) = lim Γ(U, F ⊗ O_X/𝒥^{n+1}) (EGA I, 10.11.6); this topology is not part of the data. For a morphism f : X → Y of locally noetherian formal schemes, f* preserves coherence.

*Hypotheses.* X locally noetherian formal scheme.

*Construction / proof route.*

1. Definition. Abelian-category properties reduce to the affine case Spf A, where Coh ≃ finite A-modules (AdicSpacesPartII:F0/affine-coherent-equivalence), and to coherence of O_X.
2. Automatic continuity: morphisms of coherent modules are limits of morphisms of the reductions (AdicSpacesPartII:F0/coherent-as-inverse-system, Hom as a limit).

*API.*

- `FormalScheme.Coh` (structure): The full subcategory of SheafOfModules O_X on the finitely presented modules; instance Abelian.
- `FormalScheme.isCoherentRing_structureSheaf` (instance): O_X is a coherent sheaf of rings; hence IsFinitePresentation ↔ (finite type ∧ kernels of O^n → F finite type).
- `FormalScheme.Coh.ker_mem` (other): Coh X is closed under kernels, cokernels, images and extensions in O_X-modules.
- `FormalScheme.Coh.tensor` (instance): F ⊗ G and Hom(F, G) are coherent for coherent F, G.
- `FormalScheme.Coh.pullback` (functoriality): f* : Coh Y ⥤ Coh X for a morphism of locally noetherian formal schemes; (g ∘ f)* ≅ f* ∘ g*.
- `FormalScheme.Coh.reduction` (projection): F ↦ F_n := F ⊗ O_X/𝒥^(n+1), a coherent O_{X_n}-module (promoted: AdicSpacesPartII:F0/coherent-as-inverse-system).
- `FormalScheme.Coh.sectionsTopology` (other): For quasi-compact open U, the limit topology on Γ(U, F) = lim Γ(U, F_n); maps of coherent modules are continuous and coherent submodules have closed sections (EGA I, 10.11.6).
- `FormalScheme.Coh.isIdealOfDefinition_coherent` (other): Every ideal of definition of X is a coherent O_X-module.

*Unit tests.*

- `FormalScheme.Coh.structureSheaf` (degenerate): O_X is an object of Coh X, and the zero module is coherent.
- `FormalScheme.Coh.Spf_equiv` (compatibility): For X = Spf A with A adic noetherian, Γ(X, ·) : Coh X ⥤ ModuleCat A lands in finite modules and is an equivalence onto them (AdicSpacesPartII:F0/affine-coherent-equivalence).
