- `FormalScheme.Coh.not_rationals` (non-example): On Spf ℤ_[p], the O-module with sections ℚ_[p] over the point is quasi-coherent in the naive sense (a module over the ring of sections) but not coherent: ℚ_[p] is not a finite ℤ_[p]-module. A definition of coherence as "locally M^Δ for some module M" without finiteness would accept it.
- `FormalScheme.Coh.ofScheme` (compatibility): For a locally noetherian scheme Y viewed as a formal scheme, Coh (ofScheme Y) is equivalent to the coherent (finitely presented) O_Y-modules of Mathlib Scheme.Modules.

*Acceptance.*

- O_X, every ideal of definition 𝒥, and M^Δ on Spf A for finite M are coherent.
- On Spf ℤ_p, the O-module associated with ℚ_p (the sheaf with sections ℚ_p) is not coherent.

*Uses.* EGA I, 10.10–10.11: coherent modules on Spf A are M^Δ; coherent modules on X are compatible systems on the X_n. EGA III, 3.4.2 and 5.1.4: R^q f_* of coherent modules under proper formal morphisms; the existence theorem identifies Coh(X̂) with Coh(X). AdicSpacesPartII:R2/admissible-blow-up: blow-ups of coherent open ideals of formal schemes; R2 extends to coherent ideals on admissible (non-noetherian) formal schemes. AlgebraicModuliForArithmeticGeometry R09.6 and ModularCurvesPartII R13.1: coherent sheaves (e.g. line bundles, relative dualizing sheaves) on formal deformations are algebraised.

*Depends on.* Formal schemes and locally noetherian formal schemes (`AdicSpacesPartII:F0/locally-noetherian-formal-scheme`); Ideals of definition of a formal scheme and the thickenings X_n (`AdicSpacesPartII:F0/ideal-of-definition`); `mathlib:SheafOfModules`; `mathlib:SheafOfModules.IsFinitePresentation`; `mathlib:SheafOfModules.IsQuasicoherent`; `tauceti:TauCeti.SheafOfModules.ringCatSheaf`; `mathlib:AlgebraicGeometry.SheafedSpace.sheaf`.

*Sources.* EGA-I-1960, Ch. I, (10.11.1) Proposition, printed p. 204; EGA-I-1960, Ch. I, (10.11.6), printed pp. 204-205.


##### The coherent module M^Δ on Spf A attached to a finite A-module

`AdicSpacesPartII:F0/associated-formal-module` (construction; Lean module `TauCeti/AlgebraicGeometry/FormalScheme/Coherent`, namespace `TauCeti.FormalScheme`)

Let A be an adic noetherian ring with ideal of definition I, X = Spec A and 𝔛 = Spf A, identified with the completion X̂_{/V(I)} (AdicSpacesPartII:F0/formal-completion, specIso). For a finite A-module M, M^Δ := (M~)^ is the completion along V(I) of the coherent sheaf M~ on X (EGA I, 10.10.1). Its sections are Γ(D(f) ∩ 𝔛, M^Δ) = M ⊗_A A_{f} = lim_n (M/I^{n+1}M)_f; an A-linear map u : M → N gives u^Δ : M^Δ → N^Δ, so M ↦ M^Δ is an additive functor from finite A-modules to coherent O_𝔛-modules. For A discrete, M^Δ = M~ (Mathlib tilde).

*Hypotheses.* A adic noetherian; M finite.

*Construction / proof route.*

1. M~ is coherent on the noetherian scheme Spec A (Mathlib tilde, finite presentation of finite modules over noetherian rings); its completion is a coherent O_𝔛-module (AdicSpacesPartII:F0/completion-of-coherent-sheaf), and 𝔛 = X̂ because A = Â.
2. Sections over D(f): Γ(D(f), (M~)^) = lim (M_f/I^{n+1}M_f) = M ⊗_A A_{f} by AdicSpacesPartII:F0/completion-of-coherent-sheaf (specIso) on the affine open D(f) and AdicSpacesPartII:F0/completed-localization.
3. Discrete case: I = 0, completion is the identity.

*API.*

- `FormalScheme.Spf.completedTilde` (constructor): M ↦ M^Δ : Coh (Spf A) for a finite A-module M.
- `FormalScheme.Spf.completedTilde.map` (functoriality): u ↦ u^Δ; map_id, map_comp; additive.
- `FormalScheme.Spf.completedTilde.basicOpenIso` (equivalence): Γ(D(f), M^Δ) ≅ M ⊗[A] A_{f}.
- `FormalScheme.Spf.completedTilde.globalSectionsIso` (equivalence): Γ(Spf A, M^Δ) ≅ M (promoted: AdicSpacesPartII:F0/affine-coherent-equivalence).
- `FormalScheme.Spf.completedTilde.completionIso` (compatibility): M^Δ ≅ (tilde M)^ under Spf A ≅ completion (Spec A) (zeroLocus I).
- `FormalScheme.Spf.completedTilde.pullbackIso` (compatibility): For continuous φ : B → A between adic noetherian rings and a finite B-module N, (Spf.map φ)*(N^Δ) ≅ (A ⊗[B] N)^Δ (EGA I, 10.10.8).
- `FormalScheme.Spf.completedTilde.ideal_map` (other): For an ideal 𝔟 ⊆ B, the image of (Spf.map φ)*(𝔟^Δ) in O_{Spf A} is (𝔟A)^Δ (EGA I, 10.10.9).

*Unit tests.*

- `FormalScheme.Spf.completedTilde_self` (degenerate): completedTilde A ≅ O_{Spf A} as O-modules.
- `FormalScheme.Spf.completedTilde_discrete` (compatibility): If A is discrete then completedTilde M ≅ tilde M under Spf A ≅ Spec A (Mathlib AlgebraicGeometry.tilde).
- `FormalScheme.Spf.completedTilde_basicOpen` (computation): Γ(D(f), completedTilde M) ≅ M ⊗[A] AdicRing.CompletedAway A f.
- `FormalScheme.Spf.completedTilde_padic_torsion` (computation): For A = ℤ_[p] and M = ZMod (p^k), Γ(Spf A, completedTilde M) = ZMod (p^k).
- `FormalScheme.Spf.completedTilde_ne_tilde` (non-example): For A = ℤ_[p] (p-adic) the tilde sheaf of M = ℤ_[p] on Spec ℤ_[p] has sections ℚ_[p] over the generic point D(p); the formal module has none there (D(p) ∩ Spf A = ∅): M^Δ is not the restriction of M~ to the open primes, it is its completion.

*Acceptance.*

- (A/𝔞)^Δ = O_{Spf(A/𝔞)} pushed forward, and A^Δ = O_{Spf A}.
- For A = ℤ_p and M = ℤ/p^k, M^Δ is the skyscraper ℤ/p^k on the point.

*Uses.* EGA I, 10.10.2–10.10.5: coherent modules on Spf A are exactly the M^Δ. EGA I, 10.10.8–10.10.9: pullback along Spf A → Spf B: f*(N^Δ) = (N ⊗_B A)^Δ, and f*(𝔟^Δ)O = (𝔟A)^Δ, used for adic morphisms. AdicSpacesPartII:R2/admissible-blow-up: coherent ideals 𝔞^Δ on affine formal schemes (noetherian case).

*Depends on.* Completion of a coherent sheaf along a closed subset (`AdicSpacesPartII:F0/completion-of-coherent-sheaf`); The formal completion of a locally noetherian scheme along a closed subset (`AdicSpacesPartII:F0/formal-completion`); The completed localisation A_{f} of an adic ring (`AdicSpacesPartII:F0/completed-localization`); The formal spectrum Spf A of an adic ring (`AdicSpacesPartII:F0/formal-spectrum`); `mathlib:AlgebraicGeometry.tilde`; `mathlib:AlgebraicGeometry.tildeEquiv`; `mathlib:Module.Finite`.

*Sources.* EGA-I-1960, Ch. I, (10.10.1), printed p. 201.


##### Coherent modules on Spf A are finite A-modules

`AdicSpacesPartII:F0/affine-coherent-equivalence` (theorem; Lean module `TauCeti/AlgebraicGeometry/FormalScheme/Coherent`, namespace `TauCeti.FormalScheme`)

Let A be an adic noetherian ring with ideal of definition I and 𝔛 = Spf A. (i) M ↦ M^Δ is exact and Γ(𝔛, M^Δ) ≅ M naturally (EGA I, 10.10.2 (i)). (ii) (M ⊗_A N)^Δ ≅ M^Δ ⊗ N^Δ, Hom_A(M, N)^Δ ≅ Hom(M^Δ, N^Δ), and u ↦ u^Δ is a bijection Hom_A(M, N) ≃ Hom(M^Δ, N^Δ) (EGA I, 10.10.2 (ii)–(iii)). (iii) O_𝔛 is a coherent sheaf of rings (EGA I, 10.10.3). (iv) For an O_𝔛-module F the following are equivalent (EGA I, 10.10.5): (a) F is coherent; (b) F ≅ lim F_n for a system (F_n) of coherent O_{Spec(A/I^{n+1})}-modules with F_{n+1} ⊗ O_{X_n} ≅ F_n; (c) F ≅ M^Δ for a finite A-module M, necessarily M ≅ Γ(𝔛, F). Hence Γ(𝔛, ·) and (·)^Δ are inverse equivalences between Coh(Spf A) and finite A-modules, and the system in (b) is isomorphic to (F ⊗ O_{X_n}) (EGA I, 10.10.6).

*Hypotheses.* A adic noetherian; modules finite.

*Construction / proof route.*

1. (i) Exactness: composite of the exact functors M ↦ M~ (Mathlib tilde, exact on modules) and completion (AdicSpacesPartII:F0/completion-exact). Γ(𝔛, M^Δ) = M̂ = M because finite modules over the adic noetherian A are complete and separated (AdicSpacesPartII:F0/finite-module-inverse-limit (i)).
2. (ii) From Mathlib tildeEquiv (⊗ and Hom for quasi-coherent sheaves on Spec A with finite modules) and the ⊗/Hom compatibilities of completion (AdicSpacesPartII:F0/completion-of-coherent-sheaf); bijectivity on Hom by applying (i) to the finite module Hom_A(M, N).
3. (iii) Local; the kernel of v : O^n → O is u^Δ for u : A^n → A (by (ii)), and ker u is finite since A is noetherian; exactness of (·)^Δ gives ker v = (ker u)^Δ of finite type (EGA I, 10.10.3).
4. (iv) (b) ⇒ (c): F_n = M_n~ with M_n finite over A_n = A/I^{n+1} (Mathlib tildeEquiv on the affine X_n), compatible; M := lim M_n is finite with M/I^{n+1}M = M_n (AdicSpacesPartII:F0/finite-module-inverse-limit (ii)); then F = lim F_n = M^Δ by definition of completion. (c) ⇒ (b): take F_n = (M/I^{n+1}M)~. (c) ⇒ (a): M = coker(A^m → A^n) and (iii). (a) ⇒ (b): F_n := F ⊗ O/𝒥^{n+1} is a coherent O_{X_n}-module; the canonical w : F → lim F_n is an isomorphism, checked locally on a presentation O^m → O^n → F → 0, where it reduces to (c) (EGA I, 10.10.5).

*Acceptance.*

- Coh(Spf ℤ_p) ≃ finite ℤ_p-modules; Coh(Spf k⟦t⟧) ≃ finite k⟦t⟧-modules.
- The ideal of definition I^Δ ⊆ O_𝔛 corresponds to I ⊆ A.

*Depends on.* The coherent module M^Δ on Spf A attached to a finite A-module (`AdicSpacesPartII:F0/associated-formal-module`); Completion of coherent sheaves is exact, agrees with pullback along X̂ → X, and commutes with ⊗, Hom and base change (`AdicSpacesPartII:F0/completion-exact`); Completion of a coherent sheaf along a closed subset (`AdicSpacesPartII:F0/completion-of-coherent-sheaf`); Finite modules over an adic noetherian ring as compatible systems (`AdicSpacesPartII:F0/finite-module-inverse-limit`); The formal spectrum Spf A of an adic ring (`AdicSpacesPartII:F0/formal-spectrum`); `mathlib:AlgebraicGeometry.tilde`; `mathlib:AlgebraicGeometry.tildeEquiv`; `mathlib:AlgebraicGeometry.isQuasicoherent_iff_isIso_fromTildeΓ`; `mathlib:SheafOfModules.IsFinitePresentation`.

*Sources.* EGA-I-1960, Ch. I, (10.10.2) Proposition, printed p. 201; EGA-I-1960, Ch. I, (10.10.2) Proposition (iii), printed p. 201; EGA-I-1960, Ch. I, (10.10.3) Proposition, printed p. 202; EGA-I-1960, Ch. I, (10.10.5) Proposition, printed p. 202.


##### Coherent modules on a locally noetherian formal scheme as compatible systems

`AdicSpacesPartII:F0/coherent-as-inverse-system` (theorem; Lean module `TauCeti/AlgebraicGeometry/FormalScheme/Coherent`, namespace `TauCeti.FormalScheme`)

Let X be a locally noetherian formal scheme, 𝒥 an ideal of definition and X_n = (X, O_X/𝒥^{n+1}), u_{mn} : X_m → X_n (m ≤ n). (i) An O_X-module F is coherent iff it is isomorphic to lim_n F_n for an inverse system (F_n) of coherent O_{X_n}-modules with u_{mn}*(F_n) ≅ F_m for m ≤ n; the system is then isomorphic to (F ⊗ O_{X_n})_n (EGA I, 10.11.3). Thus F ↦ (F ⊗ O_{X_n})_n is an equivalence from Coh(X) to the category of such compatible systems, with quasi-inverse lim. (ii) Hom_{O_X}(F, G) ≅ lim_n Hom_{O_{X_n}}(F_n, G_n), and likewise for the Hom sheaves and for ⊗ (EGA I, 10.11.4, 10.11.7). (iii) A morphism θ : F → G of coherent modules is surjective iff θ_0 : F_0 → G_0 is (EGA I, 10.11.5). (iv) O_X and every ideal of definition are coherent (EGA I, 10.11.1). In particular, for a noetherian scheme X with a coherent ideal 𝓘, Coh(X̂_{/V(𝓘)}) is equivalent to Stacks' category Coh(X, 𝓘) of inverse systems (F_n) of coherent O_X-modules with F_n annihilated by 𝓘^n and F_{n+1}/𝓘^n F_{n+1} ≅ F_n (Stacks Tag 0EHN; the Stacks index n corresponds to X_{n−1} here).

*Hypotheses.* X locally noetherian; 𝒥 an ideal of definition.

*Construction / proof route.*

1. All statements are local on X; on noetherian affine formal opens Spf A they are AdicSpacesPartII:F0/affine-coherent-equivalence (iv) and the Hom bijection of AdicSpacesPartII:F0/finite-module-inverse-limit (iii).
2. Gluing: the functor F ↦ (F_n) and lim are defined globally and the unit and counit are isomorphisms locally, hence globally.
3. (iii) Affine-locally θ = u^Δ with u : M → N; θ surjective iff u surjective (exactness of (·)^Δ), iff u ⊗ A/I surjective by Nakayama (I in the Jacobson radical, AdicSpacesPartII:F0/adic-ring; Mathlib Submodule.eq_bot_of_le_smul_of_le_jacobson_bot) (EGA 0, 7.1.14).
4. The comparison with Stacks' Coh(X, 𝓘) uses AdicSpacesPartII:F0/formal-completion (thickenings V(𝓘^{n+1}) and coherent O_{X_n}-modules as coherent O_X-modules killed by 𝓘^{n+1}).

*Acceptance.*

- On Spf ℤ_p, the system (ℤ/p^{n+1})_n gives O and the system (ℤ/p)_n (constant, transitions identity) gives the skyscraper F_p = (ℤ/p)^Δ; the system (ℤ/p^{n+1} ⊕ ℤ/p^{n+1})_n gives O².
- The system (ℤ/p^{min(n+1, k)})_n is compatible and gives (ℤ/p^k)^Δ.

*Uses.* EGA III, 5.1.7 (Scholie): the existence theorem in terms of compatible systems of coherent sheaves on X_n = X ×_Y Spec A/I^{n+1}. Stacks Tags 087V, 0886, 0CYW: Grothendieck existence is proved for Coh(X, 𝓘); this theorem transports it to Coh(X̂).

*Depends on.* Coherent modules on Spf A are finite A-modules (`AdicSpacesPartII:F0/affine-coherent-equivalence`); Finite modules over an adic noetherian ring as compatible systems (`AdicSpacesPartII:F0/finite-module-inverse-limit`); Ideals of definition of a formal scheme and the thickenings X_n (`AdicSpacesPartII:F0/ideal-of-definition`); A locally noetherian formal scheme is the colimit of its thickenings (`AdicSpacesPartII:F0/formal-scheme-as-colimit`); Coherent modules on a locally noetherian formal scheme (`AdicSpacesPartII:F0/coherent-formal-module`); Adic rings of finite ideal type and their ideals of definition (`AdicSpacesPartII:F0/adic-ring`); The formal completion of a locally noetherian scheme along a closed subset (`AdicSpacesPartII:F0/formal-completion`); `mathlib:Submodule.eq_bot_of_le_smul_of_le_jacobson_bot`.

*Sources.* EGA-I-1960, Ch. I, (10.11.3) Théorème, printed p. 204; EGA-I-1960, Ch. I, after (10.11.3), printed p. 204; EGA-I-1960, Ch. I, (10.11.4) Corollaire, printed p. 204; EGA-I-1960, Ch. I, (10.11.5) Corollaire, printed p. 204; Stacks-Project, Tag 0EHN (Section 30.23).


#### F0.7 The theorem on formal functions

For `f : X → Spec A` proper, `A` noetherian, `I ⊆ A` and `F` coherent:

```text
H^p(X, F)^∧_I  ≅  lim_n H^p(X, F/I^{n+1}F),        (R^p f_*F)^  ≅  R^p f̂_*(F̂)  ≅  lim_n R^p f_*(F/𝓘^{n+1}F).
```

The proof is Serre's (EGA III, 4.1.7): the graded module `⊕_k H^p(X, I^kF)` over the Rees algebra is
finite, which makes the kernels of `H^p(X,F) → H^p(X,F_n)` an `I`-good filtration and the system
`(H^p(X, F_n))` Mittag-Leffler.

##### Finiteness and uniform Serre vanishing for graded coherent modules over a proper scheme

`AdicSpacesPartII:F0/graded-cohomology-finiteness` (lemma; Lean module `TauCeti/AlgebraicGeometry/FormalScheme/FormalFunctions`, namespace `TauCeti.FormalScheme`)

Let A be a noetherian ring, B = ⊕_{k≥0} B_k a finitely generated graded A-algebra, f : X → Spec A a proper morphism, ℬ = f*(B~) and 𝓕 = ⊕_k 𝓕_k a quasi-coherent graded ℬ-module of finite type. (i) For every p ≥ 0 the graded B-module ⊕_k H^p(X, 𝓕_k) is finite; in particular, for an ideal I ⊆ A and a coherent O_X-module F, ⊕_k H^p(X, I^k F) is a finite module over the Rees algebra ⊕_k I^k (EGA III, 3.3.1–3.3.2; Stacks Tag 0897 (1)). (ii) If L is an ample invertible O_X-module, there is d_0 such that H^p(X, 𝓕_k ⊗ L^{⊗d}) = 0 for all p > 0, all k ≥ 0 and all d ≥ d_0 (Stacks Tag 0897 (2); EGA III, 2.4.1 (ii) in the projective case). Cohomology is TauCeti.AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Modules.Cohomology with its A-module structure (AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Modules.cohomologyBaseModule).

*Hypotheses.* A noetherian; B finitely generated graded A-algebra; f proper; 𝓕 of finite type over ℬ; (ii): L ample on X (relative to Spec A).

*Construction / proof route.*

1. Let π : X′ := Spec_X(ℬ) = Spec B ×_{Spec A} X → X; X′ → Spec B is proper (base change) and X′ is noetherian (supplier tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/StableReduction Layer 2 and AlgebraicModuliForArithmeticGeometry:R09.1 for relative Spec; Mathlib IsProper.isStableUnderBaseChange).
2. 𝓕 = π_*𝓕′ for a coherent O_{X′}-module 𝓕′ (finite type over ℬ), and H^p(X, 𝓕) = H^p(X′, 𝓕′) because π is affine (supplier: cohomology along affine morphisms, StableReduction Layer 2).
3. (i) H^p(X′, 𝓕′) is a finite B-module by finiteness of coherent cohomology for proper morphisms to a noetherian affine base (supplier StableReduction Layer 2; EGA III, 3.2.1); the grading is preserved.
4. (ii) π*L is ample on X′ (pullback of an ample invertible sheaf along an affine morphism; supplier R09.1); projection formula π_*(𝓕′ ⊗ π*L^d) = 𝓕 ⊗ L^d; Serre vanishing on X′ proper over the noetherian Spec B (supplier R09.1, EGA III, 2.2.1) gives one d_0 for the single coherent sheaf 𝓕′, hence for all graded pieces simultaneously.

*Acceptance.*

- For X = P^r_A, I ⊆ A and F = O_X, ⊕_k H^r(X, I^k O(−r−1)) = ⊕_k I^k is the Rees algebra itself, a finite module over itself.

*Depends on.* stage `tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/StableReduction#layer-2-coherent-curve-theory-duality-and-positivity` (see Dependencies); stage `AlgebraicModuliForArithmeticGeometry:R09.1` (see Dependencies); `tauceti:TauCeti.AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Modules.Cohomology`; `tauceti:AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Modules.cohomologyBaseModule`; `tauceti:AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Modules.cohomologyMapBaseLinear`; `mathlib:AlgebraicGeometry.IsProper`; `mathlib:AlgebraicGeometry.IsProper.isStableUnderBaseChange`; `mathlib:IsNoetherianRing`.

*Sources.* EGA-III-1-1961, Ch. III, (3.3.2) Corollaire, printed p. 118; Stacks-Project, Tag 0897 (Lemma 30.19.3); Stacks-Project, Tag 0897 (Lemma 30.19.3).


##### Good filtrations and the Mittag-Leffler property of H^p(X, F/I^{n+1}F)

`AdicSpacesPartII:F0/formal-functions-affine` (lemma; Lean module `TauCeti/AlgebraicGeometry/FormalScheme/FormalFunctions`, namespace `TauCeti.FormalScheme`)

Let A be a noetherian ring, I ⊆ A an ideal, f : X → Spec A proper, F a coherent O_X-module, F_n := F/I^{n+1}F, and p ≥ 0. Then there is c ≥ 0 such that: (i) Ker(H^p(X, F) → H^p(X, F_n)) ⊆ I^{n+1−c}·H^p(X, F) for n + 1 ≥ c, so the filtration of H^p(X, F) by these kernels defines the I-adic topology (it is I-good); (ii) the inverse system (H^p(X, F_n))_n satisfies the Mittag-Leffler condition, and Im(H^p(X, F_k) → H^p(X, F_n)) = Im(H^p(X, F) → H^p(X, F_n)) for all k ≥ n + c (EGA III, 4.1.7.9–4.1.7.21; Stacks Tag 02OB).

*Hypotheses.* A noetherian; f proper; F coherent; fixed degree p.

*Construction / proof route.*

1. Let S = ⊕_k I^k (Rees algebra, finitely generated since I is). By AdicSpacesPartII:F0/graded-cohomology-finiteness (i), E = ⊕_k H^p(X, I^k F) and N = ⊕_k H^{p+1}(X, I^{k+1} F) are finite graded S-modules, where a ∈ I^r acts by the maps induced by multiplication I^k F → I^{k+r}F (EGA III, 4.1.7.7).
2. (i) By the long exact sequence of 0 → I^{n+1}F → F → F_n → 0 (Tau Ceti cohomologyδ and exact_cohomologyMap_cohomologyδ, A-linear by cohomologyMapBaseLinear), R_n := Ker(H^p(X,F) → H^p(X,F_n)) = Im(H^p(X, I^{n+1}F) → H^p(X, F)); ⊕ R_n is a graded quotient of a submodule of E, hence finite over S, which is equivalent to the filtration (R_n) being I-good (EGA III, 4.1.7.9–4.1.7.11; Bourbaki AC III §3 no 1 thm 1); an I-good filtration satisfies R_{n} ⊆ I^{n+1−c}H for large n.
3. (ii) Q_n := Im(H^p(X, F_n) → H^{p+1}(X, I^{n+1}F)) forms a graded S-submodule of N, hence finite; it is killed by a fixed power of the image of I^{n+1} and satisfies Q_{n+h} = S_h Q_n for n ≥ n_0, so for suitable m the maps Q_{n+m} → Q_n vanish for n ≥ n_0 (EGA III, 4.1.7.12–4.1.7.20).
4. Chasing the ladder of long exact sequences for n and n + m (EGA III, 4.1.7.21) gives Im(H^p(X,F_{n+m}) → H^p(X,F_n)) = Im(H^p(X,F) → H^p(X,F_n)), whence the Mittag-Leffler property.

*Acceptance.*

- For X = P¹_{k[t]}, I = (t), F = O(−2), p = 1: H^1(X, F) = k[t], H^1(X, F_n) = k[t]/(t^{n+1}), the transition maps are surjective and the kernels are (t^{n+1}) = I^{n+1}H^1 (c = 0).

*Depends on.* Finiteness and uniform Serre vanishing for graded coherent modules over a proper scheme (`AdicSpacesPartII:F0/graded-cohomology-finiteness`); Inverse limits of Mittag-Leffler systems of abelian groups (`AdicSpacesPartII:F0/mittag-leffler-exactness`); stage `tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/StableReduction#layer-2-coherent-curve-theory-duality-and-positivity` (see Dependencies); `tauceti:TauCeti.AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Modules.Cohomology`; `tauceti:AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Modules.cohomologyBaseModule`; `tauceti:AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Modules.cohomologyMapBaseLinear`; `tauceti:TauCeti.AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Modules.cohomologyδ`; `tauceti:TauCeti.AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Modules.exact_cohomologyMap_cohomologyδ`; `mathlib:CategoryTheory.Functor.IsMittagLeffler`.

*Sources.* EGA-III-1-1961, Ch. III, (4.1.7) Corollaire, printed p. 125; EGA-III-1-1961, Ch. III, (4.1.7.9) Lemme, printed p. 126; EGA-III-1-1961, Ch. III, footnote to (4.1.7), printed p. 126; Stacks-Project, Tag 02OB (Lemma 30.20.4); Stacks-Project, Tag 02OB (Lemma 30.20.4).


##### The theorem on formal functions

`AdicSpacesPartII:F0/theorem-on-formal-functions` (theorem — planet “Theorem on formal functions”; Lean module `TauCeti/AlgebraicGeometry/FormalScheme/FormalFunctions`, namespace `TauCeti.FormalScheme`)

Let A be a noetherian ring, I ⊆ A an ideal, f : X → Spec A a proper morphism, F a coherent O_X-module and F_n := F/I^{n+1}F. For every p ≥ 0 the maps H^p(X, F)/I^{n+1}H^p(X, F) → H^p(X, F_n) induce an isomorphism of Â-modules H^p(X, F)^∧ ≅ lim_n H^p(X, F_n), where ^∧ is the I-adic completion (Mathlib AdicCompletion I) of the finite A-module H^p(X, F); it is a homeomorphism for the I-adic topology on the left and the limit topology on the right (EGA III, 4.1.7 (4.1.7.1); Stacks Tag 02OC). If A is I-adically complete, then H^p(X, F) ≅ lim_n H^p(X, F_n) (Stacks Tag 087U; EGA III, 5.1.2). The sheaf form — for Y locally noetherian, f : X → Y proper, a coherent ideal 𝓘 ⊆ O_Y and F_n = F/𝓘^{n+1}F, the completion of R^p f_*F along V(𝓘) is lim_n R^p f_*(F_n) — is part of AdicSpacesPartII:F0/formal-direct-image-comparison (EGA III, 4.1.5).

*Hypotheses.* A noetherian (not necessarily complete); f proper; F coherent; the complete-base corollary needs A I-adically complete (Mathlib IsAdicComplete I A).

*Construction / proof route.*

1. H := H^p(X, F) is a finite A-module (finiteness of coherent cohomology for proper morphisms; supplier tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/StableReduction Layer 2) with the A-module structure of Tau Ceti cohomologyBaseModule.
2. Let N_n := Im(H → H^p(X, F_n)) and K_n := Ker(H → H^p(X, F_n)). By AdicSpacesPartII:F0/formal-functions-affine (ii), lim_n H^p(X, F_n) = lim_n N_n (the eventual images are the N_n); by AdicSpacesPartII:F0/mittag-leffler-exactness applied to 0 → N_n → H^p(X,F_n) → H^p(X,F_n)/N_n → 0, whose last term has limit 0 by (ii).
3. lim N_n = lim H/K_n is the completion of H for the filtration (K_n); by AdicSpacesPartII:F0/formal-functions-affine (i), I^{n+1}H ⊆ K_n ⊆ I^{n+1−c}H, so this filtration defines the I-adic topology and lim H/K_n = lim H/I^{n+1}H = AdicCompletion I H (Stacks Tag 02OC proof).
4. Complete base: a finite module over an I-adically complete noetherian ring is I-adically complete (AdicSpacesPartII:F0/finite-module-inverse-limit (i), stated for adic noetherian rings; A with the I-adic topology is one by AdicSpacesPartII:F0/adic-ring).

*Acceptance.*

- For A = k[t], I = (t), X = P¹_A, F = O(−2) and p = 1: H^1(X, F)^∧ = k⟦t⟧ = lim_n H^1(P¹_{k[t]/t^{n+1}}, O(−2)) = lim_n k[t]/(t^{n+1}).
- For p = 0 and F = O_X with f_*O_X = A′ finite over A: Â′ = lim_n H^0(X, O_X/I^{n+1}O_X); for X = Spec A′ finite this is the classical A′ ⊗ Â ≅ lim A′/I^{n+1}A′.
- Properness is needed: for f : X = A²_k ∖ {(0,0)} → A¹_k = Spec k[t] (projection to the coordinate t), F = O_X and p = 0: H^0(X, O_X) = k[x, t], whose completion is k[x]⟦t⟧, whereas X ∩ V(t^{n+1}) is the thickened punctured line and lim_n H^0(X, O_X/t^{n+1}) = k[x, x⁻¹]⟦t⟧.

*Uses.* EGA III, 4.2–4.4: Zariski’s connectedness theorem and Zariski’s main theorem are deduced from the p = 0 case at a point (AdicSpacesPartII:F0/formal-functions-at-point). EGA III, 5.1.3 and Stacks Tag 0883: full faithfulness of completion for proper X: p = 0 applied to the coherent sheaf Hom(G, F). tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/JacobianChallenge Layer C: Grothendieck’s construction of the Picard scheme uses the theorem on formal functions; that layer imports this node. AlgebraicModuliForArithmeticGeometry R09.6: algebraisation and versality arguments compare H^p on a proper family with the limit over its infinitesimal neighbourhoods. NeronModelsAndSemistableAbelianVarieties R11.1: properness and connectedness arguments for models over complete discrete valuation rings.

*Depends on.* Good filtrations and the Mittag-Leffler property of H^p(X, F/I^{n+1}F) (`AdicSpacesPartII:F0/formal-functions-affine`); Inverse limits of Mittag-Leffler systems of abelian groups (`AdicSpacesPartII:F0/mittag-leffler-exactness`); Finite modules over an adic noetherian ring as compatible systems (`AdicSpacesPartII:F0/finite-module-inverse-limit`); Adic rings of finite ideal type and their ideals of definition (`AdicSpacesPartII:F0/adic-ring`); stage `tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/StableReduction#layer-2-coherent-curve-theory-duality-and-positivity` (see Dependencies); `mathlib:AdicCompletion`; `mathlib:IsAdicComplete`; `tauceti:TauCeti.AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Modules.Cohomology`; `tauceti:AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Modules.cohomologyBaseModule`; `tauceti:AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Modules.cohomologyMapBaseLinear`.

*Sources.* Stacks-Project, Tag 02OC (Theorem 30.20.5); Stacks-Project, Tag 02OC (Theorem 30.20.5); EGA-III-1-1961, Ch. III, (4.1.6) Remarques (ii), printed p. 125; Stacks-Project, Tag 087U (Lemma 30.20.6).


##### Formal functions at a point of the base

`AdicSpacesPartII:F0/formal-functions-at-point` (lemma; Lean module `TauCeti/AlgebraicGeometry/FormalScheme/FormalFunctions`, namespace `TauCeti.FormalScheme`)

Let Y be a locally noetherian scheme, f : X → Y proper, F a coherent O_X-module, y ∈ Y and X_k := X ×_Y Spec(O_{Y,y}/𝔪_y^{k+1}) (underlying space f⁻¹(y)). Then (R^p f_*F)_y is a finite O_{Y,y}-module, hence 𝔪_y-adically separated, and there is a canonical isomorphism ((R^p f_*F)_y)^∧ ≅ lim_k H^p(X_k, F ⊗ O_{Y,y}/𝔪_y^{k+1}) (EGA III, 4.2.1). For p = 0: ((f_*F)_y)^∧ ≅ lim_k H^0(f⁻¹(y), F ⊗ O_{Y,y}/𝔪_y^{k+1}) (EGA III, 4.2.4).

*Hypotheses.* Y locally noetherian; f proper; F coherent; y ∈ Y.

*Construction / proof route.*

1. R^p f_*F is coherent (supplier tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/StableReduction Layer 2), so its stalk is finite over the noetherian local ring O_{Y,y} and separated (Krull; Mathlib Ideal.iInf_pow_smul_eq_bot_of_le_jacobson).
2. Flat base change along Spec O_{Y,y} → Y (supplier tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/JacobianChallenge Layer C; EGA III, 1.4.15): (R^p f_*F)_y ≅ H^p(X ×_Y Spec O_{Y,y}, F′), with X ×_Y Spec O_{Y,y} proper over Spec O_{Y,y} (Mathlib IsProper.isStableUnderBaseChange).
3. Apply AdicSpacesPartII:F0/theorem-on-formal-functions with A = O_{Y,y}, I = 𝔪_y.

*Acceptance.*

- Zariski’s connectedness (EGA III, 4.3.1): if f_*O_X = O_Y then (f_*O_X)_y^∧ = Ô_{Y,y} is local, so lim_k H^0(X_k, O) has no nontrivial idempotents and f⁻¹(y) is connected.
- Fibre dimension vanishing (EGA III, 4.2.2): if dim f⁻¹(y) = r then H^p(X_k, ·) = 0 for p > r, so R^p f_*F = 0 near y for p > r.

*Depends on.* The theorem on formal functions (`AdicSpacesPartII:F0/theorem-on-formal-functions`); stage `tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/StableReduction#layer-2-coherent-curve-theory-duality-and-positivity` (see Dependencies); stage `tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/JacobianChallenge#layer-c-relative-coherent-cohomology-and-base-change` (see Dependencies); `mathlib:AlgebraicGeometry.IsProper.isStableUnderBaseChange`; `mathlib:Ideal.iInf_pow_smul_eq_bot_of_le_jacobson`; `mathlib:IsLocalRing`.

*Sources.* EGA-III-1-1961, Ch. III, (4.2), printed p. 129; EGA-III-1-1961, Ch. III, (4.2.1) Proposition, printed pp. 129-130.


##### Cohomology of an inverse limit of sheaves

`AdicSpacesPartII:F0/cohomology-of-mittag-leffler-limit` (lemma; Lean module `TauCeti/Topology/Sheaves/MittagLefflerLimit`, namespace `TauCeti`)

Let X be a topological space, (F_k)_{k∈ℕ} an inverse system of sheaves of abelian groups and F = lim_k F_k. Assume: (i) there is a basis 𝔅 of the topology such that for every U ∈ 𝔅 and every i ≥ 0 the system (H^i(U, F_k))_k is Mittag-Leffler; (ii) for every x ∈ X and i > 0, colim_{x∈U∈𝔅} lim_k H^i(U, F_k) = 0; (iii) the transition maps F_{k+1} → F_k are surjective. Then for every i ≥ 0 the canonical map H^i(X, F) → lim_k H^i(X, F_k) is surjective, and it is bijective when (H^{i−1}(X, F_k))_k is Mittag-Leffler (EGA 0_III, 13.3.1). Cohomology is Mathlib CategoryTheory.Sheaf.H of the Zariski site of X.

*Hypotheses.* X any topological space; ℕ-indexed systems; hypotheses (i)–(iii).

*Construction / proof route.*

1. Flasque case (EGA 0_III, 13.3.1 a): if all F_k and all kernels of F_{k+1} → F_k are flasque (Mathlib TopCat.Presheaf.IsFlasque), the alternating Čech complexes of any open cover form systems with surjective transitions whose cohomology vanishes in positive degrees (Čech cohomology of flasque sheaves; supplier SchemeAndStackFoundations:SF.2), so by the limit form of AdicSpacesPartII:F0/mittag-leffler-exactness for complexes (EGA 0_III, 13.2.3) the Čech cohomology of F = lim F_k vanishes on every open, hence H^i(X, F) = 0 for i > 0 (Tau Ceti subsingleton_H_succ_of_isFlasque for the flasque terms, Čech-to-derived comparison from SF.2).
2. General case (EGA 0_III, 13.3.1 b): apply Godement’s canonical flasque resolution F_k → C^•(X, F_k), an exact functor with flasque terms (supplier SchemeAndStackFoundations:SF.2); by (iii) the systems (C^i(X, F_k))_k have surjective transitions with flasque kernels, so their limits are acyclic by the flasque case; hypotheses (i)–(ii) with AdicSpacesPartII:F0/mittag-leffler-exactness show that lim_k C^•(X, F_k) is a resolution of F; therefore H^i(X, F) = H^i(lim_k Γ(X, C^•(X, F_k))), and EGA 0_III, 13.2.3 (limits of Mittag-Leffler systems of complexes, from AdicSpacesPartII:F0/mittag-leffler-exactness) gives surjectivity onto lim H^i(X, F_k), and bijectivity when (H^{i−1}(X, F_k)) is Mittag-Leffler.

*Acceptance.*

- For X a point, H^i = 0 for i > 0 and the statement reduces to H^0(lim F_k) = lim H^0(F_k).
- On a noetherian formal scheme 𝔛 with ideal of definition 𝒥 and a coherent F, the system F_k = F/𝒥^{k+1}F on the affine formal basis satisfies (i)–(iii).

*Depends on.* Inverse limits of Mittag-Leffler systems of abelian groups (`AdicSpacesPartII:F0/mittag-leffler-exactness`); stage `SchemeAndStackFoundations:SF.2` (see Dependencies); `mathlib:CategoryTheory.Sheaf.H`; `mathlib:TopCat.Presheaf.IsFlasque`; `tauceti:TauCeti.Topology.subsingleton_H_succ_of_isFlasque`; `mathlib:CategoryTheory.Functor.IsMittagLeffler`.

*Sources.* EGA-III-1-1961, Ch. 0, proof of (13.3.1) b), printed p. 68; EGA-III-1-1961, Ch. 0, (13.3.1) Proposition, printed p. 81 (Publ. IHES 11); EGA-III-1-1961, Ch. 0, (13.3.1) Proposition (iii).


##### Comparison of algebraic and formal higher direct images

`AdicSpacesPartII:F0/formal-direct-image-comparison` (theorem; Lean module `TauCeti/AlgebraicGeometry/FormalScheme/FormalFunctions`, namespace `TauCeti.FormalScheme`)

Let Y be a locally noetherian scheme, f : X → Y proper, Y′ ⊆ Y closed with coherent ideal 𝓘, X′ = f⁻¹(Y′), f̂ : X̂ → Ŷ the completion (AdicSpacesPartII:F0/completion-of-morphism), F a coherent O_X-module, F̂ its completion and F_k = F/𝒥^{k+1}F with 𝒥 = f*(𝓘)O_X. Let R^n f̂_*(F̂) be the sheaf on Ŷ associated with V ↦ H^n(f̂⁻¹(V), F̂) (cohomology of the underlying abelian sheaves). Then R^n f̂_*(F̂) is a coherent O_Ŷ-module and the canonical maps φ_n : (R^n f_*F)^ → R^n f̂_*(F̂) and ψ_n : R^n f̂_*(F̂) → lim_k R^n f_*(F_k) are isomorphisms of O_Ŷ-modules; ψ_n ∘ φ_n is the canonical map (EGA III, 4.1.5). For Y = Spec A affine noetherian: H^n(X̂, F̂) ≅ H^n(X, F)^∧ ≅ lim_k H^n(X, F_k) (EGA III, 4.1.7), and for every affine open V of Y, H^n(X̂ ∩ f⁻¹(V), F̂) ≅ Γ(V ∩ Y′, R^n f̂_*(F̂)) (EGA III, 4.1.9).

*Hypotheses.* Y locally noetherian; f proper; F coherent.

*Construction / proof route.*

1. Affine case Y = Spec A: F_k is supported on X′ and H^n(X, F_k) = H^n(X̂, F_k) (EGA III, 4.1.3.2). Apply AdicSpacesPartII:F0/cohomology-of-mittag-leffler-limit to F̂ = lim F_k on the space X′ with 𝔅 the affine opens: on affine U, H^i(U, F_k) = 0 for i > 0 (affine acyclicity, supplier tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/JacobianChallenge Layer B) and H^0(U, F_{k+1}) → H^0(U, F_k) is surjective, so (i)–(iii) hold; (H^{n−1}(X, F_k)) is Mittag-Leffler by AdicSpacesPartII:F0/formal-functions-affine. Hence ψ_{n,X} : H^n(X̂, F̂) ≅ lim_k H^n(X, F_k).
2. The composite with φ is the isomorphism of AdicSpacesPartII:F0/theorem-on-formal-functions, so φ is an isomorphism too.
3. Sheaf form: Γ(V, R^n f_*F) = H^n(f⁻¹(V), F) for affine V (supplier StableReduction Layer 2; EGA III, 1.4.11), Γ(V ∩ Y′, (R^n f_*F)^) is its completion since R^n f_*F is coherent (AdicSpacesPartII:F0/completion-of-coherent-sheaf), and the affine case applied to f⁻¹(V) → V gives φ_n, ψ_n on the basis of affine opens; coherence of R^n f̂_*(F̂) follows from φ_n (EGA III, 4.1.8).

*Acceptance.*

- For X = P¹_{ℤ_p}, Y = Spec ℤ_p, Y′ = V(p) and F = O(−2): H^1(X̂, Ô(−2)) = ℤ_p, the cohomology of the formal completion P̂¹ agrees with that of P¹.

*Uses.* EGA III, 3.4.2–3.4.3: finiteness theorem for proper formal morphisms; for completions of proper morphisms it is the coherence of R^n f̂_*(F̂) proved here. EGA III, 5.1.2 and 5.2.3: H^n(X̂, F̂) = H^n(X, F) for X proper over complete A; used in EGA’s proof of existence. CohomologyComparisons CP.0: algebraic versus formal proper-cohomology comparison for coherent coefficients.

*Depends on.* Cohomology of an inverse limit of sheaves (`AdicSpacesPartII:F0/cohomology-of-mittag-leffler-limit`); Good filtrations and the Mittag-Leffler property of H^p(X, F/I^{n+1}F) (`AdicSpacesPartII:F0/formal-functions-affine`); The theorem on formal functions (`AdicSpacesPartII:F0/theorem-on-formal-functions`); Extension of a morphism to formal completions (`AdicSpacesPartII:F0/completion-of-morphism`); Completion of a coherent sheaf along a closed subset (`AdicSpacesPartII:F0/completion-of-coherent-sheaf`); Coherent modules on a locally noetherian formal scheme as compatible systems (`AdicSpacesPartII:F0/coherent-as-inverse-system`); stage `tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/StableReduction#layer-2-coherent-curve-theory-duality-and-positivity` (see Dependencies); stage `tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/JacobianChallenge#layer-b-coherent-cohomology-over-k-genus-riemannroch-serre-duality` (see Dependencies); `mathlib:CategoryTheory.Sheaf.H`; `tauceti:TauCeti.AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Modules.Cohomology`; `tauceti:AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Modules.cohomologyBaseModule`; `tauceti:AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Modules.cohomologyMapBaseLinear`.

*Sources.* EGA-III-1-1961, Ch. III, (4.1.5) Théorème, printed p. 125; EGA-III-1-1961, Ch. III, proof of (4.1.5) and (4.1.8), printed pp. 125, 129; EGA-III-1-1961, Ch. III, (4.1.6) Remarques (ii), printed p. 125.


#### F0.8 Grothendieck's existence theorem

For `A` adic noetherian and `X` proper over `Spec A` (more generally separated of finite type, for sheaves
with proper support), completion `Coh(X) → Coh(X̂)` is an equivalence. The proof: full faithfulness from
formal functions in degree 0; the projective case from uniform Serre vanishing on the thickenings; the
general case by noetherian induction, Chow's lemma, comparison along the modification up to a power of the
exceptional ideal, and dévissage.

##### Over a complete base, every neighbourhood of the closed fibre is everything

`AdicSpacesPartII:F0/closed-fibre-neighbourhood` (lemma; Lean module `TauCeti/AlgebraicGeometry/FormalScheme/Existence`, namespace `TauCeti.FormalScheme`)

Let A be an adic noetherian ring with ideal of definition I, f : X → Spec A a morphism whose underlying map is closed (for instance f proper), and X′ = f⁻¹(V(I)). Then every open subset V ⊆ X containing X′ equals X (EGA III, 5.1.3.1).

*Hypotheses.* A adic noetherian; f a closed map.

*Construction / proof route.*

1. f(X ∖ V) is closed in Spec A and disjoint from V(I).
2. Every nonempty closed subset of Spec A contains a closed point, a maximal ideal 𝔪, and I ⊆ 𝔪 because I lies in the Jacobson radical (AdicSpacesPartII:F0/adic-ring; Mathlib IsAdicComplete.le_jacobson_bot); so every nonempty closed subset meets V(I). Hence X ∖ V = ∅.

*Acceptance.*

- For X = P¹_{ℤ_p}, any open containing the special fibre P¹_{F_p} is all of X.
- For the non-closed morphism X = Spec ℚ_p → Spec ℤ_p, X′ = ∅ and V = ∅ is a neighbourhood of X′ different from X.

*Depends on.* Adic rings of finite ideal type and their ideals of definition (`AdicSpacesPartII:F0/adic-ring`); `mathlib:IsAdicComplete.le_jacobson_bot`; `mathlib:AlgebraicGeometry.UniversallyClosed`; `mathlib:AlgebraicGeometry.IsProper`.

*Sources.* EGA-III-1-1961, Ch. III, (5.1.3.1) Lemme, printed p. 150.


##### Completion of coherent sheaves is fully faithful over a complete base

`AdicSpacesPartII:F0/existence-fully-faithful` (lemma; Lean module `TauCeti/AlgebraicGeometry/FormalScheme/Existence`, namespace `TauCeti.FormalScheme`)

Let A be an adic noetherian ring with ideal of definition I, f : X → Spec A separated of finite type, X̂ the completion along X′ = f⁻¹(V(I)), and F, G coherent O_X-modules such that Supp F ∩ Supp G is proper over Spec A. Then u ↦ û is a bijection Hom_{O_X}(F, G) ≅ Hom_{O_X̂}(F̂, Ĝ). If moreover f is closed (e.g. X proper over A), u is injective (resp. surjective) iff û is (EGA III, 5.1.3; Stacks Tag 0883 for X proper).

*Hypotheses.* A adic noetherian; f separated of finite type; Supp F ∩ Supp G proper over Spec A (automatic if X is proper).

*Construction / proof route.*

1. H := Hom(F, G) is coherent with Supp H ⊆ Supp F ∩ Supp G. Choose a closed subscheme Z ⊆ X with underlying space Supp H, proper over Spec A (the annihilator ideal of H has zero locus Supp H), so H is the pushforward of a coherent O_Z-module and cohomology of H on X equals that on Z (EGA III, 4.1.10).
2. Hom(F̂, Ĝ) = Γ(X̂, Hom(F̂, Ĝ)) = Γ(X̂, Ĥ) (AdicSpacesPartII:F0/completion-exact (iv)), and Γ(X̂, Ĥ) = lim_n H^0(X, H/I^{n+1}H) (AdicSpacesPartII:F0/completion-of-coherent-sheaf, sectionsIso on the quasi-compact X′).
3. By AdicSpacesPartII:F0/theorem-on-formal-functions (complete base, p = 0, applied on Z proper over A): lim_n H^0(X, H/I^{n+1}H) = H^0(X, H) = Hom(F, G); the composite is u ↦ û (Stacks Tag 0883 via Tag 0882).
4. Injectivity/surjectivity: û injective (surjective) iff u is so on a neighbourhood of X′ (AdicSpacesPartII:F0/completion-detects-near-closed (iv)), and every neighbourhood of X′ is X when f is closed (AdicSpacesPartII:F0/closed-fibre-neighbourhood).

*Acceptance.*

- For X = P¹_{ℤ_p}: Hom(O(a), O(b)) = H^0(P¹, O(b − a)) and its completion Hom(Ô(a), Ô(b)) agree (both free of rank b − a + 1, or 0).
- Without properness the map is not surjective: for X = A¹_{ℤ_p}, Hom(O, O) = ℤ_p[x] whereas Hom(Ô, Ô) = ℤ_p⟨x⟩.

*Depends on.* The theorem on formal functions (`AdicSpacesPartII:F0/theorem-on-formal-functions`); Completion of a coherent sheaf along a closed subset (`AdicSpacesPartII:F0/completion-of-coherent-sheaf`); Completion of coherent sheaves is exact, agrees with pullback along X̂ → X, and commutes with ⊗, Hom and base change (`AdicSpacesPartII:F0/completion-exact`); What completion sees: sections and maps near the closed subset (`AdicSpacesPartII:F0/completion-detects-near-closed`); Over a complete base, every neighbourhood of the closed fibre is everything (`AdicSpacesPartII:F0/closed-fibre-neighbourhood`); Coherent modules on a locally noetherian formal scheme as compatible systems (`AdicSpacesPartII:F0/coherent-as-inverse-system`).

*Sources.* EGA-III-1-1961, Ch. III, (5.1.3) Corollaire, printed p. 149; EGA-III-1-1961, Ch. III, (4.5.3) Corollaire, printed p. 139; Stacks-Project, Tag 0883 (Lemma 30.24.1); Stacks-Project, Tag 0882 (Lemma 30.23.5).


##### Uniform vanishing and lifting of sections on a proper formal scheme with an ample reduction

`AdicSpacesPartII:F0/formal-serre-vanishing` (lemma; Lean module `TauCeti/AlgebraicGeometry/FormalScheme/Existence`, namespace `TauCeti.FormalScheme`)

Let A be an adic noetherian ring with ideal of definition I, A_n = A/I^{n+1}, 𝔛 → Spf A a proper morphism of formal schemes with adic system X_n = 𝔛 ×_{Spf A} Spec A_n (AdicSpacesPartII:F0/adic-systems-equivalence), L an invertible O_𝔛-module with L_0 = L ⊗ O_{X_0} ample on X_0, and F a coherent O_𝔛-module with reductions F_n = F ⊗ O_{X_n} (AdicSpacesPartII:F0/coherent-as-inverse-system); write F_n(d) = F_n ⊗ L_n^{⊗d}. There is n_0 such that for all d ≥ n_0 and all k ≥ 0: (i) H^q(X_0, (I^{k+1}F_{k+1}) ⊗ L_0^{⊗d}) = 0 for q > 0, where I^{k+1}F_{k+1} = Ker(F_{k+1} → F_k) is viewed as a coherent O_{X_0}-module; (ii) H^0(X_{k+1}, F_{k+1}(d)) → H^0(X_k, F_k(d)) is surjective; (iii) if also H^q(X_0, F_0(d)) = 0 for q > 0, then H^q(X_k, F_k(d)) = 0 for all q > 0 and k; (iv) Γ(𝔛, F ⊗ L^{⊗d}) → H^0(X_k, F_k(d)) is surjective for every k (EGA III, 5.2.3; Stacks Tags 0884 and the proof of 089A).

*Hypotheses.* A adic noetherian; 𝔛 proper over Spf A; L invertible with L_0 ample on X_0; F coherent.

*Construction / proof route.*

1. The kernels K_k := Ker(F_{k+1} → F_k) = I^{k+1}F_{k+1} are killed by I, so are coherent O_{X_0}-modules, and K := ⊕_k K_k is a finite type graded module over f_0*(gr_I A)~ (affine-locally ⊕ I^{k+1}M/I^{k+2}M over ⊕ I^k/I^{k+1}; Stacks Tag 087Z, via AdicSpacesPartII:F0/affine-coherent-equivalence).
2. (i) X_0 is proper over the noetherian ring A_0 = A/I and gr_I A is a finitely generated graded A_0-algebra; apply AdicSpacesPartII:F0/graded-cohomology-finiteness (ii) with L_0 ample (ampleness in the sense of the supplier AlgebraicModuliForArithmeticGeometry:R09.1).
3. (ii) Long exact sequence of 0 → K_k(d) → F_{k+1}(d) → F_k(d) → 0 on X_{k+1} (Tau Ceti cohomologyδ; sections_surjective): H^1(X_{k+1}, K_k(d)) = H^1(X_0, K_k ⊗ L_0^d) = 0 gives surjectivity.
4. (iii) Induction on k with the same sequences.
5. (iv) Γ(𝔛, F ⊗ L^d) = lim_k H^0(X_k, F_k(d)) (sheaf limit, AdicSpacesPartII:F0/coherent-as-inverse-system), and a limit of a system with surjective transitions surjects onto each term (AdicSpacesPartII:F0/mittag-leffler-exactness).

*Acceptance.*

- For 𝔛 = P̂¹_{ℤ_p} and L = Ô(1): for d ≥ 0, H^0(P¹_{ℤ/p^{k+1}}, O(d)) = (ℤ/p^{k+1})[x,y]_d and the transition maps are surjective; H^1 vanishes for d ≥ −1.

*Depends on.* Finiteness and uniform Serre vanishing for graded coherent modules over a proper scheme (`AdicSpacesPartII:F0/graded-cohomology-finiteness`); Coherent modules on a locally noetherian formal scheme as compatible systems (`AdicSpacesPartII:F0/coherent-as-inverse-system`); Adic formal S-schemes are adic inductive systems of S_n-schemes (`AdicSpacesPartII:F0/adic-systems-equivalence`); Coherent modules on Spf A are finite A-modules (`AdicSpacesPartII:F0/affine-coherent-equivalence`); Inverse limits of Mittag-Leffler systems of abelian groups (`AdicSpacesPartII:F0/mittag-leffler-exactness`); Proper morphisms of locally noetherian formal schemes (`AdicSpacesPartII:F0/proper-formal-morphism`); stage `AlgebraicModuliForArithmeticGeometry:R09.1` (see Dependencies); `tauceti:TauCeti.AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Modules.sections_surjective`; `tauceti:TauCeti.AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Modules.cohomologyδ`; `tauceti:TauCeti.AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Modules.exact_cohomologyMap_cohomologyδ`.

*Sources.* EGA-III-1-1961, Ch. III, (5.2.3) Proposition, printed p. 151; Stacks-Project, Tag 0884 (Lemma 30.24.2); Stacks-Project, Tag 087Z (Lemma 30.23.8).


##### Grothendieck existence for projective schemes

`AdicSpacesPartII:F0/existence-projective-case` (lemma; Lean module `TauCeti/AlgebraicGeometry/FormalScheme/Existence`, namespace `TauCeti.FormalScheme`)

Let A be an adic noetherian ring with ideal of definition I and f : X → Spec A proper with an ample invertible O_X-module L (X projective over A). Then completion F ↦ F̂ is an equivalence Coh(X) ≃ Coh(X̂) (EGA III, 5.2.5; Stacks Tag 0885).

*Hypotheses.* A adic noetherian; X proper over Spec A with an ample invertible sheaf L.

*Construction / proof route.*

1. Fully faithful by AdicSpacesPartII:F0/existence-fully-faithful.
2. Every G ∈ Coh(X̂) is a quotient of a completion: L_0 = L|_{X_0} is ample (restriction of an ample sheaf to a closed subscheme; supplier AlgebraicModuliForArithmeticGeometry:R09.1); choose d with d ≥ n_0 of AdicSpacesPartII:F0/formal-serre-vanishing for G and L̂ and with G_0 ⊗ L_0^d globally generated (Serre’s theorem, supplier R09.1); lift finitely many generating sections compatibly through the surjections (formal-serre-vanishing (ii)) to maps ((L^{−d})^{⊕t})_n → G_n; the induced map ((L^{−d})^{⊕t})^ → G is surjective because it is surjective on reductions at n = 0 (AdicSpacesPartII:F0/coherent-as-inverse-system (iii)).
3. Apply this to the kernel (Coh(X̂) is abelian, AdicSpacesPartII:F0/coherent-formal-module) to get a presentation û′ : ((L^{−e})^{⊕s})^ → ((L^{−d})^{⊕t})^ → G → 0; by full faithfulness û′ = û for u : (L^{−e})^{⊕s} → (L^{−d})^{⊕t}; by exactness of completion (AdicSpacesPartII:F0/completion-exact), G ≅ (coker u)^.

*Acceptance.*

- On X = P^r_{ℤ_p}, every compatible system of coherent sheaves on P^r_{ℤ/p^{n+1}} is the reduction of a coherent sheaf on P^r_{ℤ_p}; e.g. compatible line bundles are O(d) for a single d.

*Depends on.* Completion of coherent sheaves is fully faithful over a complete base (`AdicSpacesPartII:F0/existence-fully-faithful`); Uniform vanishing and lifting of sections on a proper formal scheme with an ample reduction (`AdicSpacesPartII:F0/formal-serre-vanishing`); Coherent modules on a locally noetherian formal scheme as compatible systems (`AdicSpacesPartII:F0/coherent-as-inverse-system`); Coherent modules on a locally noetherian formal scheme (`AdicSpacesPartII:F0/coherent-formal-module`); Completion of coherent sheaves is exact, agrees with pullback along X̂ → X, and commutes with ⊗, Hom and base change (`AdicSpacesPartII:F0/completion-exact`); stage `AlgebraicModuliForArithmeticGeometry:R09.1` (see Dependencies).

*Sources.* EGA-III-1-1961, Ch. III, (5.2.5), printed p. 153; Stacks-Project, Tag 0885 (Lemma 30.24.3).


##### Comparison along a proper modification up to a power of the exceptional ideal

`AdicSpacesPartII:F0/existence-modification` (lemma; Lean module `TauCeti/AlgebraicGeometry/FormalScheme/Existence`, namespace `TauCeti.FormalScheme`)

Let Y be a noetherian scheme, 𝓙, 𝓚 ⊆ O_Y quasi-coherent ideals, π : X → Y proper and an isomorphism over Y ∖ V(𝓚), 𝓘 = π⁻¹𝓙·O_X, G ∈ Coh(Ŷ_{/V(𝓙)}) (a compatible system (G_n)), F a coherent O_X-module and β : π̂*G ≅ F̂ in Coh(X̂_{/V(𝓘)}). Then there is a morphism α : G → (π_*F)^ in Coh(Ŷ) whose kernel and cokernel are annihilated by a power of 𝓚 (Stacks Tag 088B; EGA III, 5.3.4).

*Hypotheses.* Y noetherian; π proper, isomorphism over the complement of V(𝓚).

*Construction / proof route.*

1. π_*F is coherent (supplier tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/StableReduction Layer 2), so (π_*F)^ makes sense.
2. Define γ_n : G_n → π_*π*G_n → π_*(F/𝓘^nF) (adjunction, then π_*β_n); on an affine open Spec B of Y, lim_n H^0(X_B, F/𝓘^nF) is the 𝓙-adic completion of H^0(X_B, F) by AdicSpacesPartII:F0/theorem-on-formal-functions (p = 0); via AdicSpacesPartII:F0/affine-coherent-equivalence the limit of the γ_n is a map α of finite B̂-modules, unique, hence glues (Stacks Tag 088B).
3. Kernel and cokernel of G → π_*π*G and of the comparison are coherent and vanish over Y ∖ V(𝓚) where π is an isomorphism; coherent modules supported in V(𝓚) on a noetherian scheme are killed by a power of 𝓚, uniformly on a finite affine cover (Stacks Tag 0888).

*Acceptance.*

- If π is an isomorphism (𝓚 = O_Y allowed), α is an isomorphism.

*Depends on.* The theorem on formal functions (`AdicSpacesPartII:F0/theorem-on-formal-functions`); Coherent modules on Spf A are finite A-modules (`AdicSpacesPartII:F0/affine-coherent-equivalence`); Coherent modules on a locally noetherian formal scheme as compatible systems (`AdicSpacesPartII:F0/coherent-as-inverse-system`); Completion of a coherent sheaf along a closed subset (`AdicSpacesPartII:F0/completion-of-coherent-sheaf`); stage `tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/StableReduction#layer-2-coherent-curve-theory-duality-and-positivity` (see Dependencies).

*Sources.* Stacks-Project, Tag 088B (Lemma 30.25.3); EGA-III-1-1961, Ch. III, (5.3.4) Lemme, printed p. 154.


##### Algebraizing a formal module that maps to a completion with bounded torsion kernel and cokernel

`AdicSpacesPartII:F0/bounded-torsion-algebraization` (lemma; Lean module `TauCeti/AlgebraicGeometry/FormalScheme/Existence`, namespace `TauCeti.FormalScheme`)

Let X be a noetherian scheme, 𝓘 ⊆ O_X a quasi-coherent ideal, H a coherent O_X-module and G ∈ Coh(X̂_{/V(𝓘)}) (equivalently a compatible system (G_n), AdicSpacesPartII:F0/coherent-as-inverse-system). If α : G → Ĥ is a morphism whose kernel and cokernel are annihilated by a power of 𝓘, then there is a triple (F, a, β), unique up to unique isomorphism, with F a coherent O_X-module, a : F → H a morphism whose kernel and cokernel are annihilated by a power of 𝓘, and β : G ≅ F̂ with α = â ∘ β (Stacks Tag 0889 (1)). X is not assumed complete along 𝓘.

*Hypotheses.* X noetherian (not necessarily complete along V(𝓘)); H coherent; kernel and cokernel of α killed by 𝓘^t for some t.

*Construction / proof route.*

1. Uniqueness reduces the construction to affine opens X = Spec A (A noetherian), 𝓘 = I~, where G corresponds to a finite Â-module M′ (AdicSpacesPartII:F0/coherent-as-inverse-system with AdicSpacesPartII:F0/affine-coherent-equivalence and AdicSpacesPartII:F0/formal-completion, specIso), H to a finite A-module N with Ĥ ↔ N ⊗_A Â (Mathlib AdicCompletion.ofTensorProductEquivOfFiniteNoetherian), and α to φ : M′ → N ⊗_A Â with I^t-torsion kernel and cokernel.
2. Let M := N ×_{N ⊗ Â} M′ (fibre product of A-modules) and ψ : M → N the projection. Because A → Â is flat (Mathlib AdicCompletion.flat_of_isNoetherian) and A/I^n ≅ Â/I^nÂ, I-power-torsion modules are the same over A and over Â; hence ker ψ ≅ ker φ and coker ψ ≅ coker φ are I^t-torsion and M ⊗_A Â → M′ is an isomorphism compatible with φ (Stacks Tag 0ALK, More on Algebra 15.91.17, whose hypotheses — A → Â flat, I finitely generated, A/I ≅ Â/IÂ — hold here).
3. M is finite over A: it is an extension of a submodule of the finite module N by the I^t-torsion module ker φ, which is a finite Â-module killed by I^t, hence a finite A/I^t = Â/I^tÂ-module (Stacks Tag 05EU); so M^ = M ⊗_A Â ≅ M′ and F := M~ works.
4. Uniqueness: two triples differ by a map inducing an isomorphism on completions and on the parts away from V(𝓘); glue the affine constructions.

*Acceptance.*

- If α is an isomorphism, F = H. For X = Spec ℤ, 𝓘 = (p), H = O and G = (p ℤ_p)^Δ ⊂ Ô (α the inclusion, cokernel F_p killed by p), the triple is F = pℤ ⊂ ℤ = H.

*Depends on.* Coherent modules on a locally noetherian formal scheme as compatible systems (`AdicSpacesPartII:F0/coherent-as-inverse-system`); Coherent modules on Spf A are finite A-modules (`AdicSpacesPartII:F0/affine-coherent-equivalence`); The formal completion of a locally noetherian scheme along a closed subset (`AdicSpacesPartII:F0/formal-completion`); `mathlib:AdicCompletion.ofTensorProductEquivOfFiniteNoetherian`; `mathlib:AdicCompletion.flat_of_isNoetherian`; `mathlib:Module.Finite`.

*Sources.* Stacks-Project, Tag 0889 (Lemma 30.23.6); Stacks-Project, Tag 0889 (Lemma 30.23.6), proof; Stacks-Project, Tag 0ALK (More on Algebra, Lemma 15.91.17).


##### Dévissage: extending algebraizability from thickenings of a closed subscheme

`AdicSpacesPartII:F0/existence-devissage` (lemma; Lean module `TauCeti/AlgebraicGeometry/FormalScheme/Existence`, namespace `TauCeti.FormalScheme`)

Let X be a noetherian scheme, 𝓘, 𝓚 ⊆ O_X quasi-coherent ideals, X_e = V(𝓚^e) with 𝓘_e = 𝓘O_{X_e}, and G ∈ Coh(X̂_{/V(𝓘)}) (a compatible system (G_n)). Assume: (1) completion Coh(X_e) → Coh((X_e)^_{/V(𝓘_e)}) is an equivalence for every e ≥ 1; (2) there are a coherent O_X-module H and a morphism α : G → Ĥ whose kernel and cokernel are annihilated by a power of 𝓚. Then G ≅ F̂ for a coherent O_X-module F (Stacks Tag 088A; EGA III, 5.3.1–5.3.2).

*Hypotheses.* X noetherian; (1) for all e; (2) as stated.

*Construction / proof route.*

1. Identify coherent O_{X_e}-modules with coherent O_X-modules killed by 𝓚^e. By (1), for each e the system (G_n/𝓚^eG_n)_n is the completion of a coherent G_e killed by 𝓚^e; the maps G_{e+1} → G_e induce G_{e+1}/𝓚^eG_{e+1} ≅ G_e, so (G_e)_e is a compatible system for 𝓚, i.e. an object of Coh(X̂_{/V(𝓚)}) (AdicSpacesPartII:F0/coherent-as-inverse-system).
2. α induces maps G_e → H/𝓚^eH (full faithfulness in (1)); if 𝓚^t kills kernel and cokernel of α, then 𝓚^{4t} kills kernel and cokernel of all G_e → H/𝓚^eH (Stacks Tag 0888, Remark 30.25.1, an affine-local statement about finite modules).
3. AdicSpacesPartII:F0/bounded-torsion-algebraization, applied to (G_e) → Ĥ_{/V(𝓚)}, gives a coherent F with F/𝓚^eF ≅ G_e compatibly.
4. Reducing modulo 𝓘^n, the triple (F/𝓘^nF, …) algebraizes (G_n/𝓚^eG_n)_e → (H/(𝓘^n + 𝓚^e)H)_e, so by the uniqueness in AdicSpacesPartII:F0/bounded-torsion-algebraization, F/𝓘^nF ≅ G_n compatibly in n; hence G ≅ F̂ (Stacks Tag 088A).

*Acceptance.*

- If 𝓚 = 0 then X_e = X for every e and hypothesis (1) is already the conclusion.
- If α is an isomorphism the conclusion holds with F = H; the lemma is used when α is an isomorphism only away from V(𝓚), as produced by AdicSpacesPartII:F0/existence-modification.

*Depends on.* Algebraizing a formal module that maps to a completion with bounded torsion kernel and cokernel (`AdicSpacesPartII:F0/bounded-torsion-algebraization`); Coherent modules on a locally noetherian formal scheme as compatible systems (`AdicSpacesPartII:F0/coherent-as-inverse-system`); Completion of coherent sheaves is exact, agrees with pullback along X̂ → X, and commutes with ⊗, Hom and base change (`AdicSpacesPartII:F0/completion-exact`); Completion of a coherent sheaf along a closed subset (`AdicSpacesPartII:F0/completion-of-coherent-sheaf`).

*Sources.* Stacks-Project, Tag 088A (Lemma 30.25.2); EGA-III-1-1961, Ch. III, (5.3.1) Lemme, printed p. 154.


##### Coherent formal modules with proper support live on a proper closed subscheme

`AdicSpacesPartII:F0/existence-proper-support-reduction` (lemma; Lean module `TauCeti/AlgebraicGeometry/FormalScheme/Existence`, namespace `TauCeti.FormalScheme`)

Let A be an adic noetherian ring with ideal of definition I, X separated of finite type over Spec A, and G ∈ Coh(X̂) whose support is proper over Spf A (AdicSpacesPartII:F0/proper-formal-morphism, IsProperSupport). Then there is a closed subscheme Z ⊆ X, proper over Spec A, such that G is annihilated by the completed ideal of Z, i.e. G is the pushforward of a coherent module on Ẑ (Stacks Tag 088E, first part of the proof; EGA III, 5.3.5).

*Hypotheses.* A adic noetherian; X separated of finite type over Spec A.

*Construction / proof route.*

1. Noetherian induction on quasi-coherent ideals 𝓚 ⊆ O_X for which the claim holds for all G annihilated by 𝓚 (Stacks Tag 088E): assume the claim for all proper closed subschemes of X.
2. Chow’s lemma (supplier AlgebraicModuliForArithmeticGeometry:R09.2): π : X′ → X proper surjective, an isomorphism over a dense open U, with an open immersion j : X′ → P into a scheme P projective over Spec A (supplier R09.1). The support of π̂*G is π⁻¹ of the support of G, proper over A, hence closed in P; so j_*π*(G_n) is a compatible system of coherent modules on P (AdicSpacesPartII:F0/coherent-as-inverse-system), and by AdicSpacesPartII:F0/existence-projective-case it is the completion of a coherent F′ on P.
3. Supp F′ ⊆ j(X′): the image in Spec A of the closed set Supp F′ ∖ j(X′) is closed (P → Spec A is proper) and does not meet V(I) (its points over V(I) lie in the support of F′/IF′ = j_*π*G_0, contained in j(X′)); a nonempty closed subset of Spec A meets V(I) since I lies in the Jacobson radical (AdicSpacesPartII:F0/adic-ring), so the set is empty. Hence F′|_{X′} is supported on a closed subscheme of X′ proper over A and (F′|_{X′})^ ≅ π̂*G.
4. H := π_*(F′|_{X′}) is coherent (supplier StableReduction Layer 2) with support proper over A; AdicSpacesPartII:F0/existence-modification gives α : G → Ĥ with kernel and cokernel killed by 𝓚^t, 𝓚 the ideal of the reduced complement X ∖ U ≠ X; kernel and cokernel are coherent formal modules with proper support annihilated by 𝓚^t, so by the induction hypothesis they are supported on proper closed subschemes; modules supported on proper closed subschemes form a Serre subcategory (Stacks Tag 088E), so G is supported on one.

*Acceptance.*

- For X = A¹_{ℤ_p} and G = Ô_{V(x)} (the completion of the structure sheaf of the section x = 0, proper over ℤ_p), Z = V(x).

*Depends on.* Comparison along a proper modification up to a power of the exceptional ideal (`AdicSpacesPartII:F0/existence-modification`); Grothendieck existence for projective schemes (`AdicSpacesPartII:F0/existence-projective-case`); Proper morphisms of locally noetherian formal schemes (`AdicSpacesPartII:F0/proper-formal-morphism`); Coherent modules on a locally noetherian formal scheme as compatible systems (`AdicSpacesPartII:F0/coherent-as-inverse-system`); Adic rings of finite ideal type and their ideals of definition (`AdicSpacesPartII:F0/adic-ring`); stage `AlgebraicModuliForArithmeticGeometry:R09.2` (see Dependencies); stage `AlgebraicModuliForArithmeticGeometry:R09.1` (see Dependencies); stage `tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/StableReduction#layer-2-coherent-curve-theory-duality-and-positivity` (see Dependencies).

*Sources.* EGA-III-1-1961, Ch. III, (5.3.5), printed p. 155; EGA-III-1-1961, Ch. III, (5.3.5), printed p. 155; Stacks-Project, Tag 088E (Theorem 30.27.1).


##### Grothendieck’s existence theorem

`AdicSpacesPartII:F0/grothendieck-existence` (theorem — planet “Grothendieck existence theorem”; Lean module `TauCeti/AlgebraicGeometry/FormalScheme/Existence`, namespace `TauCeti.FormalScheme`)

Let A be an adic noetherian ring with ideal of definition I, Y = Spec A, f : X → Y a separated morphism of finite type, X′ = f⁻¹(V(I)), X̂ = X̂_{/X′} and Ŷ = Spf A. Then F ↦ F̂ is an equivalence from the category of coherent O_X-modules whose support is proper over Spec A to the category of coherent O_X̂-modules whose support is proper over Spf A (EGA III, 5.1.4; Stacks Tag 088E). In particular, if X is proper over Spec A then Coh(X) ≃ Coh(X̂) (EGA III, 5.1.6); equivalently, with X_n = X ×_Y Spec(A/I^{n+1}), coherent O_X-modules correspond to compatible systems (F_n) of coherent O_{X_n}-modules with F_{n+1} ⊗ O_{X_n} ≅ F_n, morphisms to compatible systems of morphisms (EGA III, 5.1.7; Stacks Tag 088F).

*Hypotheses.* A adic noetherian (complete and separated for the I-adic topology); f separated of finite type; supports proper over Spec A (automatic when X is proper).

*Construction / proof route.*

1. Full faithfulness: AdicSpacesPartII:F0/existence-fully-faithful.
2. Proper case, essential surjectivity (Stacks Tag 088C): noetherian induction on quasi-coherent ideals 𝓚, assuming the statement for all closed subschemes V(𝓚), 𝓚 ≠ 0; Chow’s lemma for X proper over A (supplier AlgebraicModuliForArithmeticGeometry:R09.2) gives π : X′ → X proper surjective, an isomorphism over a dense open U, with X′ projective over A; by AdicSpacesPartII:F0/existence-projective-case, π̂*G ≅ F̂′; by AdicSpacesPartII:F0/existence-modification there is α : G → (π_*F′)^ with kernel and cokernel killed by a power of 𝓚 = ideal of X ∖ U; AdicSpacesPartII:F0/existence-devissage concludes.
3. Proper supports: by AdicSpacesPartII:F0/existence-proper-support-reduction both sides are supported on completions of closed subschemes Z ⊆ X proper over A, and coherent modules on Z are coherent O_X-modules killed by the ideal of Z (and likewise on Ẑ ⊆ X̂, AdicSpacesPartII:F0/closed-formal-subscheme); apply the proper case to Z.
4. System form: AdicSpacesPartII:F0/coherent-as-inverse-system for X̂, whose thickenings are the X_n (AdicSpacesPartII:F0/formal-completion).

*Acceptance.*

- For X = P^r_{ℤ_p}: Coh(P^r_{ℤ_p}) ≃ Coh(P̂^r) ≃ compatible systems on P^r_{ℤ/p^{n+1}}; in particular Pic(P̂^r) = ℤ.
- EGA III after 5.1.7: over a local adic noetherian A the Y_n are spectra of artinian local rings, so geometry over A reduces largely to geometry over artinian rings.
- Properness of supports is needed: for X = A¹_{ℤ_p}, O_X̂ has non-proper support and End(O_X̂) = ℤ_p⟨x⟩ ≠ ℤ_p[x] = End(O_X), so completion is not an equivalence on all coherent sheaves.

*Uses.* AlgebraicModuliForArithmeticGeometry R09.6: algebraisation of formal deformations of coherent sheaves and of closed subschemes over complete local rings (R10/R13 algebraisation statements). ModularCurvesPartII R13.1: generalised elliptic curves over complete bases are algebraised from compatible systems over A/I^{n+1} (Deligne–Rapoport). NeronModelsAndSemistableAbelianVarieties R11.1: extension of morphisms and of coherent data over complete discrete valuation rings. LocalGaloisDeformationRings L7 / R08.3: projective local models and bounded-height lattice moduli: formal families over the deformation ring are algebraised to projective schemes before taking scheme-theoretic images. ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology H1:formal-adic-comparison: finite étale covers and coherent data on the completion of a proper scheme come from the scheme.

*Depends on.* Completion of coherent sheaves is fully faithful over a complete base (`AdicSpacesPartII:F0/existence-fully-faithful`); Grothendieck existence for projective schemes (`AdicSpacesPartII:F0/existence-projective-case`); Comparison along a proper modification up to a power of the exceptional ideal (`AdicSpacesPartII:F0/existence-modification`); Dévissage: extending algebraizability from thickenings of a closed subscheme (`AdicSpacesPartII:F0/existence-devissage`); Coherent formal modules with proper support live on a proper closed subscheme (`AdicSpacesPartII:F0/existence-proper-support-reduction`); Coherent modules on a locally noetherian formal scheme as compatible systems (`AdicSpacesPartII:F0/coherent-as-inverse-system`); The formal completion of a locally noetherian scheme along a closed subset (`AdicSpacesPartII:F0/formal-completion`); Closed formal subschemes and closed immersions (`AdicSpacesPartII:F0/closed-formal-subscheme`); Completion of a coherent sheaf along a closed subset (`AdicSpacesPartII:F0/completion-of-coherent-sheaf`); stage `AlgebraicModuliForArithmeticGeometry:R09.2` (see Dependencies).

*Sources.* EGA-III-1-1961, Ch. III, (5.1.1), printed p. 149; EGA-III-1-1961, Ch. III, (5.1.4) Théorème, printed p. 150; EGA-III-1-1961, Ch. III, (5.1.6) Corollaire, printed p. 150; EGA-III-1-1961, Ch. III, (5.1.7) Scholie, printed p. 150; Stacks-Project, Tag 088C (Proposition 30.25.4); Stacks-Project, Tag 088F (Remark 30.27.2).


#### F0.9 Morphisms and algebraization (formal GAGA)

```text
Hom_S(X, Y) ≅ Hom_{Spf A}(X̂, Ŷ)   (X proper, Y separated of finite type over S = Spec A);
𝔛 proper over Spf A with L invertible, L ⊗ O_{X_0} ample  ⟹  𝔛 ≅ X̂ with X projective over S, L ≅ M̂, M ample.
```

The ampleness hypothesis is only on the reduction `L_0 = L/IL` on `X_0 = 𝔛 ×_{Spf A} Spec(A/I)`; it cannot be
dropped (EGA III, 5.4.3).

##### Closed formal subschemes proper over Spf A are completions

`AdicSpacesPartII:F0/closed-subscheme-algebraization` (lemma; Lean module `TauCeti/AlgebraicGeometry/FormalScheme/Algebraization`, namespace `TauCeti.FormalScheme`)

Let A be an adic noetherian ring with ideal of definition I and f : X → Spec A separated of finite type. Then Z ↦ Ẑ is a bijection from closed subschemes of X proper over Spec A to closed formal subschemes of X̂ proper over Spf A (EGA III, 5.1.8). Equivalently (Stacks Tag 0899): a compatible system of closed subschemes Z_n ⊆ X_n = X ×_{Spec A} Spec A/I^{n+1} with Z_{n+1} ∩ X_n = Z_n and Z_0 proper over A/I comes from a unique closed subscheme Z ⊆ X proper over A.

*Hypotheses.* A adic noetherian; f separated of finite type.

*Construction / proof route.*

1. A closed formal subscheme 𝔜 ⊆ X̂ proper over Spf A is X̂.subscheme 𝒜 with O_X̂/𝒜 coherent of proper support (AdicSpacesPartII:F0/closed-formal-subscheme); by AdicSpacesPartII:F0/grothendieck-existence O_X̂/𝒜 ≅ Ĝ with G coherent of proper support, and the quotient map O_X̂ → Ĝ is û for a unique u : O_X → G (AdicSpacesPartII:F0/existence-fully-faithful), surjective on a neighbourhood of the proper support hence G = O_X/𝓐 for a coherent ideal 𝓐 with V(𝓐) proper over A.
2. Then 𝒜 = 𝓐̂ (exactness, AdicSpacesPartII:F0/completion-exact) and 𝔜 = Ẑ for Z = V(𝓐) (AdicSpacesPartII:F0/closed-formal-subscheme, completion_subscheme).
3. Injectivity: Ẑ determines 𝓐̂ and hence the surjection O_X → O_Z up to isomorphism by full faithfulness.

*Acceptance.*

- For X = A¹_{ℤ_p} and a ∈ ℤ_p, the closed formal subscheme V(x − a) of X̂ = Spf ℤ_p⟨x⟩ is proper over Spf ℤ_p and is the completion of the closed subscheme V(x − a) ≅ Spec ℤ_p of A¹_{ℤ_p}.
- Properness is needed: X̂ = Spf ℤ_p⟨x⟩ is a closed formal subscheme of itself that is not proper over Spf ℤ_p, and it is not the completion of a closed subscheme proper over ℤ_p.

*Depends on.* Grothendieck’s existence theorem (`AdicSpacesPartII:F0/grothendieck-existence`); Completion of coherent sheaves is fully faithful over a complete base (`AdicSpacesPartII:F0/existence-fully-faithful`); Closed formal subschemes and closed immersions (`AdicSpacesPartII:F0/closed-formal-subscheme`); Completion of coherent sheaves is exact, agrees with pullback along X̂ → X, and commutes with ⊗, Hom and base change (`AdicSpacesPartII:F0/completion-exact`).

*Sources.* EGA-III-1-1961, Ch. III, (5.1.8) Corollaire, printed p. 151; Stacks-Project, Tag 0899 (Lemma 30.28.1).


##### Isomorphisms and closed immersions of proper schemes are detected on completions

`AdicSpacesPartII:F0/completion-detects-isomorphism` (lemma; Lean module `TauCeti/AlgebraicGeometry/FormalScheme/Algebraization`, namespace `TauCeti.FormalScheme`)

Let Z be a locally noetherian scheme, g : X → Z and h : Y → Z proper, Z′ ⊆ Z closed, X′ = g⁻¹(Z′), Y′ = h⁻¹(Z′), and f : X → Y a Z-morphism with completion f̂ : X̂ → Ŷ. Then f̂ is an isomorphism (resp. a closed immersion) iff there is an open neighbourhood U of Z′ such that f restricted to g⁻¹(U) → h⁻¹(U) is an isomorphism (resp. a closed immersion) (EGA III, 4.6.8).

*Hypotheses.* Z locally noetherian; g, h proper.

*Construction / proof route.*

1. Sufficiency: completion is local on a neighbourhood and preserves isomorphisms and closed immersions (AdicSpacesPartII:F0/completion-of-morphism, AdicSpacesPartII:F0/closed-formal-subscheme).
2. Necessity, local around y ∈ Y′: f̂ injective on X′ implies f⁻¹(y) is at most one point, so f is quasi-finite at the points of f⁻¹(y); the quasi-finite locus is open (Mathlib Scheme.Hom.isOpen_quasiFiniteAt), and since f is proper (a Z-morphism between proper Z-schemes) its complement has closed image not containing y; over the complement V of that image f is proper and locally quasi-finite, hence finite (Mathlib IsFinite.of_isProper_of_locallyQuasiFinite).
3. For finite f over V, X = Spec_V(ℬ) with ℬ = f_*O_X coherent, and f̂ corresponds to Ô_Y → ℬ̂; f̂ an isomorphism (resp. closed immersion) means û is bijective (resp. surjective) for u : O_Y → ℬ, hence u is so on a neighbourhood of Y′ (AdicSpacesPartII:F0/completion-detects-near-closed (iv)).
4. Neighbourhoods: if u is an isomorphism (surjective) on an open W ⊇ Y′, then U := Z ∖ h(Y ∖ W) is an open neighbourhood of Z′ since h is closed (Mathlib UniversallyClosed), and g⁻¹(U) → h⁻¹(U) has the property.

*Acceptance.*

- For Z = Spec ℤ_p, Z′ = V(p), X = Y = P¹_{ℤ_p} and f an automorphism: f is determined by f̂, and a Z-morphism f with f̂ an isomorphism is an isomorphism over U = Z (every neighbourhood of V(p) in Spec ℤ_p is everything).
- Properness is needed: for Z = Y = Spec ℤ, Z′ = V(p) and X = Spec ℤ_(p) with its canonical map f (X is not proper over Z), f̂ : Spf ℤ_p → Spf ℤ_p is an isomorphism but f is not an isomorphism over any open neighbourhood of V(p).

*Depends on.* Extension of a morphism to formal completions (`AdicSpacesPartII:F0/completion-of-morphism`); Closed formal subschemes and closed immersions (`AdicSpacesPartII:F0/closed-formal-subscheme`); What completion sees: sections and maps near the closed subset (`AdicSpacesPartII:F0/completion-detects-near-closed`); Completion of a coherent sheaf along a closed subset (`AdicSpacesPartII:F0/completion-of-coherent-sheaf`); `mathlib:AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Hom.isOpen_quasiFiniteAt`; `mathlib:AlgebraicGeometry.IsFinite.of_isProper_of_locallyQuasiFinite`; `mathlib:AlgebraicGeometry.LocallyQuasiFinite`; `mathlib:AlgebraicGeometry.IsFinite`; `mathlib:AlgebraicGeometry.IsProper`; `mathlib:AlgebraicGeometry.UniversallyClosed`.

*Sources.* EGA-III-1-1961, Ch. III, (4.6.8) Proposition, printed p. 144.


##### Morphisms from proper schemes are determined by their completions

`AdicSpacesPartII:F0/formal-morphism-full-faithfulness` (theorem; Lean module `TauCeti/AlgebraicGeometry/FormalScheme/Algebraization`, namespace `TauCeti.FormalScheme`)

Let A be an adic noetherian ring with ideal of definition I, S = Spec A, S_n = Spec A/I^{n+1}, X → S proper and Y → S separated of finite type, and let X̂, Ŷ be the completions along the preimages of V(I). Then f ↦ f̂ is a bijection Hom_S(X, Y) ≅ Hom_{Spf A}(X̂, Ŷ) (EGA III, 5.4.1). Equivalently, S-morphisms X → Y correspond to compatible systems of S_n-morphisms X_n → Y_n (EGA III, 5.4.2; Stacks Tag 0A42). Consequently X ↦ X̂ is a fully faithful functor from schemes proper over Spec A to formal schemes proper over Spf A; formal schemes in its essential image are called algebraizable.

*Hypotheses.* A adic noetherian; X proper over S; Y separated of finite type over S.

*Construction / proof route.*

1. Injectivity: if f̂ = ĝ then f = g on a neighbourhood of X′ (AdicSpacesPartII:F0/completion-morphism-germ, Y of finite type over S), and that neighbourhood is X (AdicSpacesPartII:F0/closed-fibre-neighbourhood, X → S closed).
2. Surjectivity: given h : X̂ → Ŷ, let W = X ×_S Y (separated of finite type over S, noetherian); Ŵ = X̂ ×_{Spf A} Ŷ (AdicSpacesPartII:F0/completion-of-morphism, prodIso). The graph Γ_h : X̂ → Ŵ is a closed immersion: on each thickening it is the graph X_n → X_n ×_{S_n} Y_n, a closed immersion because Y_n → S_n is separated (base change of the diagonal, Mathlib IsSeparated), and an adic morphism whose reduction is a closed immersion is one (AdicSpacesPartII:F0/formal-closed-immersion-criterion).
3. Its image is a closed formal subscheme of Ŵ proper over Spf A (isomorphic to X̂), hence equal to T̂ for a closed subscheme T ⊆ W proper over S (AdicSpacesPartII:F0/closed-subscheme-algebraization).
4. The projection p : T → X is a morphism of proper S-schemes with p̂ an isomorphism, hence an isomorphism over a neighbourhood of X′ (AdicSpacesPartII:F0/completion-detects-isomorphism), hence everywhere (AdicSpacesPartII:F0/closed-fibre-neighbourhood); f := q ∘ p⁻¹ has graph T, so f̂ = h (graph compatibility of completion, EGA I, 10.9.8).
5. System form: AdicSpacesPartII:F0/adic-systems-equivalence identifies Hom_{Spf A}(X̂, Ŷ) with lim_n Hom_{S_n}(X_n, Y_n).

*Acceptance.*

- Aut_S(P¹_{ℤ_p}) = PGL_2(ℤ_p) = lim_n PGL_2(ℤ/p^{n+1}) = Aut(P̂¹).
- Separatedness of Y is needed for the graph argument; properness of X is needed: Hom_S(A¹_{ℤ_p}, A¹_{ℤ_p}) = ℤ_p[x] is strictly smaller than Hom(Spf ℤ_p⟨x⟩, Spf ℤ_p⟨x⟩) = ℤ_p⟨x⟩.

*Uses.* AlgebraicModuliForArithmeticGeometry R09.6: uniqueness of algebraisations and algebraisation of morphisms between proper families. ModularCurvesPartII R13.1: extension of the group law and of level structures from the formal completion of a generalised elliptic curve. NeronModelsAndSemistableAbelianVarieties R11.1: homomorphisms of proper models over complete discrete valuation rings from compatible systems.

*Depends on.* Morphisms with equal completions agree near the closed subset (`AdicSpacesPartII:F0/completion-morphism-germ`); Over a complete base, every neighbourhood of the closed fibre is everything (`AdicSpacesPartII:F0/closed-fibre-neighbourhood`); Extension of a morphism to formal completions (`AdicSpacesPartII:F0/completion-of-morphism`); An adic morphism is a closed immersion iff its reduction is (`AdicSpacesPartII:F0/formal-closed-immersion-criterion`); Closed formal subschemes proper over Spf A are completions (`AdicSpacesPartII:F0/closed-subscheme-algebraization`); Isomorphisms and closed immersions of proper schemes are detected on completions (`AdicSpacesPartII:F0/completion-detects-isomorphism`); Adic formal S-schemes are adic inductive systems of S_n-schemes (`AdicSpacesPartII:F0/adic-systems-equivalence`); `mathlib:AlgebraicGeometry.IsSeparated`; `mathlib:AlgebraicGeometry.IsClosedImmersion`; `mathlib:CategoryTheory.Limits.pullback`.

*Sources.* EGA-III-1-1961, Ch. III, (5.4.1) Théorème, printed p. 156; EGA-III-1-1961, Ch. III, after (5.4.1), printed p. 157; EGA-III-1-1961, Ch. III, (5.4.2) Scholie, printed p. 157; Stacks-Project, Tag 0A42 (Lemma 30.28.3).


##### Grothendieck’s algebraization theorem (formal GAGA)

`AdicSpacesPartII:F0/grothendieck-algebraization` (theorem — planet “Formal GAGA”; Lean module `TauCeti/AlgebraicGeometry/FormalScheme/Algebraization`, namespace `TauCeti.FormalScheme`)

Let A be an adic noetherian ring with ideal of definition I, S = Spec A, 𝔖 = Spf A, S_n = Spec A/I^{n+1}, f : 𝔛 → 𝔖 a proper morphism of formal schemes (AdicSpacesPartII:F0/proper-formal-morphism) with X_n = 𝔛 ×_𝔖 S_n, and L an invertible O_𝔛-module such that L_0 = L ⊗ O_{X_0} is ample on X_0. Then 𝔛 is algebraizable: there are a scheme X proper over S and an isomorphism X̂ ≅ 𝔛 (X is unique up to unique isomorphism by AdicSpacesPartII:F0/formal-morphism-full-faithfulness), and for any such X there is an ample invertible O_X-module M with M̂ ≅ L; in particular X is projective over S (EGA III, 5.4.5). Equivalently (Stacks Tag 089A): a compatible system of schemes X_n over S_n with cartesian squares, X_0 proper over S_0, and invertible L_n with L_{n+1}|_{X_n} ≅ L_n and L_0 ample, comes from a proper X → S with an ample invertible L, X_n ≅ X ×_S S_n and L_n ≅ L|_{X_n}. The ampleness hypothesis cannot be dropped: there are formal schemes proper over Spf A that are not algebraizable (EGA III, 5.4.3).

*Hypotheses.* A adic noetherian with ideal of definition I; 𝔛 → Spf A proper; L invertible on 𝔛 with L_0 ample on the reduction X_0 (only the reduction modulo I is assumed ample).

*Construction / proof route.*

1. By AdicSpacesPartII:F0/formal-serre-vanishing (iv) with F = O_𝔛 there is n_0 with Γ(𝔛, L^n) → Γ(X_0, L_0^n) surjective for n ≥ n_0; choose n ≥ n_0 with L_0^n very ample over S_0 (supplier AlgebraicModuliForArithmeticGeometry:R09.1: some power of an ample sheaf on a proper scheme over a noetherian ring is very ample).
2. Γ(X_0, L_0^n) is a finite A-module (supplier tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/StableReduction Layer 2); choose a finitely generated A-submodule E ⊆ Γ(𝔛, L^n) mapping onto it. The maps E/I^{k+1}E ⊗ O_{X_k} → L_k^n are surjective (surjective at k = 0 by very ampleness, then by Nakayama) and define S_k-morphisms g_k : X_k → P(E) ×_S S_k (universal property of the projective bundle P(E), supplier R09.1) forming a compatible system, hence a morphism g : 𝔛 → P̂(E) over 𝔖 (AdicSpacesPartII:F0/adic-systems-equivalence).
3. g_0 is a closed immersion (very ampleness), so g is a closed immersion (AdicSpacesPartII:F0/formal-closed-immersion-criterion); 𝔛 is thus a closed formal subscheme of P̂(E), proper over 𝔖, hence 𝔛 ≅ T̂ for a closed subscheme T ⊆ P(E) proper over S (AdicSpacesPartII:F0/closed-subscheme-algebraization). Set X := T; it is projective over S.
4. L is coherent on X̂, so L ≅ M̂ for a coherent O_X-module M (AdicSpacesPartII:F0/grothendieck-existence); M is invertible: M̂ is invertible, so M is invertible on a neighbourhood of X′ (Nakayama at points of X′; AdicSpacesPartII:F0/completion-detects-near-closed), which is X (AdicSpacesPartII:F0/closed-fibre-neighbourhood).
5. M^n ≅ O_{P(E)}(1)|_X because their completions agree (full faithfulness on coherent sheaves, AdicSpacesPartII:F0/existence-fully-faithful); O(1)|_X is very ample, so M is ample (supplier R09.1). Uniqueness of X: AdicSpacesPartII:F0/formal-morphism-full-faithfulness.

*Acceptance.*

- For X_n = P¹_{ℤ/p^{n+1}} with L_n = O(1), the algebraization is P¹_{ℤ_p} with O(1).
- Every formal deformation over Spf A (A complete local noetherian with residue field k) of a smooth projective curve C_0 over k is algebraizable: an ample line bundle on C_0 lifts to every thickening because the obstruction lies in H²(C_0, O) = 0, so the hypothesis of the theorem holds.
- EGA III, 5.4.3: proper formal schemes over Spf A need not be algebraizable (formal deformations of complex tori or K3 surfaces along which no ample line bundle lifts); the theorem does not apply because no L with L_0 ample exists.

*Uses.* AlgebraicModuliForArithmeticGeometry R09.6: effectivity of formal deformations of polarised objects (polarised abelian schemes, curves) used in Artin representability and R10/R13 algebraisation. ModularCurvesPartII R13.1: Deligne–Rapoport: a formal generalised elliptic curve with an ample (level-structure or zero-section) line bundle is algebraised to a generalised elliptic curve over the complete base. LocalGaloisDeformationRings L7: bounded-height lattice moduli: formal families of lattices inside a projective Grassmannian are algebraised to projective schemes over the deformation ring. NeronModelsAndSemistableAbelianVarieties R11.1: algebraisation of formal abelian schemes with a polarisation over complete discrete valuation rings. AdicSpacesPartII:R2: projective formal models: an admissible formal model with an ample reduction line bundle is the completion of a projective model, so its generic fibre is an analytification (R1).

*Depends on.* Uniform vanishing and lifting of sections on a proper formal scheme with an ample reduction (`AdicSpacesPartII:F0/formal-serre-vanishing`); Adic formal S-schemes are adic inductive systems of S_n-schemes (`AdicSpacesPartII:F0/adic-systems-equivalence`); An adic morphism is a closed immersion iff its reduction is (`AdicSpacesPartII:F0/formal-closed-immersion-criterion`); Closed formal subschemes proper over Spf A are completions (`AdicSpacesPartII:F0/closed-subscheme-algebraization`); Grothendieck’s existence theorem (`AdicSpacesPartII:F0/grothendieck-existence`); What completion sees: sections and maps near the closed subset (`AdicSpacesPartII:F0/completion-detects-near-closed`); Over a complete base, every neighbourhood of the closed fibre is everything (`AdicSpacesPartII:F0/closed-fibre-neighbourhood`); Completion of coherent sheaves is fully faithful over a complete base (`AdicSpacesPartII:F0/existence-fully-faithful`); Morphisms from proper schemes are determined by their completions (`AdicSpacesPartII:F0/formal-morphism-full-faithfulness`); Proper morphisms of locally noetherian formal schemes (`AdicSpacesPartII:F0/proper-formal-morphism`); stage `AlgebraicModuliForArithmeticGeometry:R09.1` (see Dependencies); stage `tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/StableReduction#layer-2-coherent-curve-theory-duality-and-positivity` (see Dependencies).

*Sources.* EGA-III-1-1961, Ch. III, (5.4.5) Théorème, printed p. 157; EGA-III-1-1961, Ch. III, (5.4.5) Théorème, printed pp. 157-158; EGA-III-1-1961, Ch. III, (5.4.5) Théorème, printed p. 158; EGA-III-1-1961, Ch. III, proof of (5.4.5), printed p. 158; EGA-III-1-1961, Ch. III, (5.4.3) Remarque, printed p. 157; Stacks-Project, Tag 089A (Theorem 30.28.4).
