#### F0 acceptance tests

- `Spf ℤ_p` is a one-point locally ringed space with sections `ℤ_p`, different from `Spec ℤ_p`; the
  completion of `Spec ℤ` along `V(p)` is `Spf ℤ_p`; the completion of `P¹_{ℤ_p}` along its special fibre is
  a non-affine noetherian formal scheme, proper over `Spf ℤ_p`, obtained by gluing two copies of
  `Spf ℤ_p⟨x⟩`.
- Morphisms `Spf ℤ_p⟦T⟧ → Spf ℤ_p⟦S⟧` are the elements of `(p, T)`; `Spf ℤ_p⟦T⟧ → Spf ℤ_p` is not adic and
  not of finite type, `Spf ℤ_p⟨T⟩ → Spf ℤ_p` is adic of finite type and not proper.
- `Coh(Spf ℤ_p)` is the category of finite `ℤ_p`-modules; on `Spec ℤ` the completion along `V(p)` kills
  `(ℤ/ℓ)~` for `ℓ ≠ p` and `(ℤ[1/p])~`.
- Theorem on formal functions for `P¹_{k[t]}`, `F = O(−2)`, `p = 1`: `k⟦t⟧ = lim k[t]/(t^{n+1})`; failure
  for the non-proper `A²_k ∖ {0} → A¹_k` in degree 0 (`k[x]⟦t⟧` against `k[x, x⁻¹]⟦t⟧`).
- Existence for `P^r_{ℤ_p}`: compatible systems of coherent sheaves on `P^r_{ℤ/p^{n+1}}` come from
  `P^r_{ℤ_p}`; failure of full faithfulness for `A¹_{ℤ_p}` (`ℤ_p[x]` against `ℤ_p⟨x⟩`).
- `Aut(P̂¹_{ℤ_p}) = PGL_2(ℤ_p)`; the system `(P¹_{ℤ/p^{n+1}}, O(1))` algebraizes to `(P¹_{ℤ_p}, O(1))`; formal
  deformations of smooth projective curves algebraize because ample line bundles lift; proper formal
  schemes without such a line bundle need not algebraize.
- The formal torus `Spf O_C⟨T^{±1}⟩` over `O_C` is a (non-noetherian) formal scheme of the same category as
  the noetherian `Spf ℤ_p⟨T^{±1}⟩`, of which it is the base change.

## R2. Formal schemes, generic fibres and Hasse domains

<a id="r2"></a>

### R2. Formal schemes, generic fibres, and Hasse domains

**Dependencies:** [AdicSpacesPartII F0](README.md#f0) (Spf and formal schemes of finite ideal type, gluing,
fibre products, colimits of thickenings, noetherian formal completion); [AdicSpacesPartII R0](README.md#r0) (adic morphisms, finite-type classes, completed
tensor products and fibre products, separated/finite/étale/smooth morphisms);
[AdicSpacesPartII R1](README.md#r1) (rigid-analytic spaces, analytification X ↦ X^ad and Huber's rigid–adic
functor r); the anchor
[Foundations of adic spaces](../../tau-ceti/AdicSpaces/README.md), Layers 0–5; the Tau Ceti roadmap
StableReduction, Layer 0 (ring-level Fitting ideals, for the flattening theorem).

This layer builds the formal-model side of nonarchimedean geometry over a complete valuation ring of
rank one that is **not** assumed discretely valued. It constructs admissible formal schemes and their
ring theory, Huber's generic-fibre functor d on formal schemes of type (S) (which contains both the
non-noetherian admissible formal schemes of Bosch–Lütkebohmert and the locally noetherian formal
schemes of F0, including Conrad's category FS_C), the specialisation map and tubes, rig-points,
admissible blow-ups, Raynaud's theorem, the flattening and quasi-finite-model theorems with Conrad's
fibral finiteness criterion, the comparison of the generic fibre of a completion with the analytified
algebraic generic fibre (the good-reduction locus), smooth formal schemes with their étale sites,
Frobenius lifts and residue discs, and finally fractional valuation bounds, domains cut out by sections
of line bundles, their formal models and the Hasse domains X(ε) with their transition maps.

Boundaries, stated once: F0 owns Spf and the category of formal schemes of finite ideal type (with
gluing, fibre products and colimits of thickenings), noetherian formal completion, coherent formal
modules and formal GAGA; R2 owns the conditions 'locally tfp', 'admissible' and 'type (S)' on those formal
schemes, their ring theory over non-noetherian O_K, the generic fibre and every formal/analytic
comparison (RS-05).
ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology H1 owns the morphism of étale topoi λ_X: d(X)_ét → X_ét and nearby cycles;
R2 supplies the continuous map λ_X and the functor on étale objects. PadicDifferentialEquationsAndRigid
Cohomology RD.3 owns frames, strict neighbourhoods and j†; R2 supplies generic fibres, sp and tubes.
HilbertModularVarietiesAndShimuraCurves H2 and the modular-curve roadmaps own the Hasse invariant of a
specific moduli problem; R2 supplies the construction for an abstract triple (𝔛, ω, Ha). R3 owns
coherent sheaves on adic spaces; R2 uses only coherent ideals and coherent modules on formal schemes.

#### Conventions

1. **Base.** K is a field complete for a nontrivial rank-one nonarchimedean absolute value; O_K = K° is
   its valuation ring, m_K its maximal ideal, k = O_K/m_K, and ϖ ∈ O_K a pseudouniformiser
   (0 < |ϖ| < 1). O_K is noetherian exactly when K is discretely valued; no statement of this layer
   assumes it unless it says so. In the p-adic statements K ⊇ Q_p, |p| = p⁻¹, and p is a
   pseudouniformiser.
2. **Topologies.** Formal O_K-schemes locally of tf presentation carry the ϖ-adic topology, never the
   m_K-adic one (for K = C_p, m_K² = m_K and the m_K-adic completion of O_K[T] is k[T]).
3. **'Admissible'.** An admissible O_K-algebra is topologically finitely presented and ϖ-torsion-free
   (Bosch–Lütkebohmert). This is unrelated to EGA's admissible topological rings; Lean names use
   `IsAdmissibleAlgebra` and `FormalScheme.IsAdmissible` and their docstrings say so.
4. **Formal schemes.** Formal schemes are F0's formal schemes of finite ideal type (locally Spf A with A
   complete separated adic with finitely generated ideal of definition, EGA I (10.1.2), no noetherian
   hypothesis), with F0's gluing, fibre products, completed tensor products and colimits of thickenings;
   admissibility and condition (S) are conditions on them. F0 states the colimit property of thickenings,
   morphisms as compatible systems and the adic-systems equivalence in the same generality
   (`F0/thickening-colimit-finite-ideal-type`, `F0/morphisms-as-compatible-systems-finite-ideal-type`,
   `F0/adic-systems-equivalence-finite-ideal-type`).
5. **Generic fibre.** The generic fibre is Huber's d(X), an analytic adic space, with the specialisation
   map λ_X: d(X) → X. For formal O_K-schemes locally of tf presentation, d(X) = r(X_rig) where X_rig is
   Raynaud's rigid generic fibre and r is R1's rigid–adic functor; rigid-analytic statements from the
   sources are transported through r: every node is stated in adic form or carries its adic
   translation.
6. **Tubes.** In the adic space the tube of a closed subset Z of the special fibre is the *interior* of
   the closed set λ⁻¹(Z); λ⁻¹(Z) itself is closed and contains extra higher-rank boundary points. The
   rigid tube sp⁻¹(Z) (Berthelot) is the set of classical points of the adic tube.
7. **Fractional bounds.** |f| ≤ |g|^{a/b} means v(f^b) ≤ v(g^a); no element 'g^{a/b}' of the base
   field is used. When an element c with c^b = g^a·(unit) exists in an explicitly chosen extension
   (for example p^ε ∈ Z_p^cycl), the two conventions agree.
8. **Hasse domains.** X(ε) = {|H̃a| ≥ |p|^ε} is formed with 0 ≤ ε < 1 and any local lift H̃a of the
   Hasse invariant; its formal model needs an element p^ε ∈ O_K.
9. **Namespaces.** Ring-level objects in `TauCeti.Huber`, sets of valuations in
   `TauCeti.ValuationSpectrum`, formal schemes in `TauCeti.FormalScheme`, adic-space geometry in
   `TauCeti.AdicSpace`.


#### R2.1 Algebras topologically of finite presentation

**Tfp and admissible algebras** (`Huber.IsTopologicallyFinitePresentation`, `Huber.IsAdmissibleAlgebra`).
O_K⟨ξ_1, …, ξ_n⟩ is Tau Ceti's completed restricted power-series ring `restrictedMvPowerSeriesCompletion n O_K`
for the ϖ-adic topology, i.e. the ϖ-adic completion of O_K[ξ]. An O_K-algebra A is *topologically of finite
type* (tft) if A ≅ O_K⟨ξ⟩/a, *topologically finitely presented* (tfp) if a can be chosen finitely generated
(independent of the presentation), and *admissible* if it is tfp and has no ϖ-torsion, i.e. is O_K-flat.
The generic fibre A_K = A[1/ϖ] of a tfp algebra is a K-affinoid algebra; for admissible A the map
A → A_K is injective. Over a discretely valued K, tft = tfp.

*Node* `AdicSpacesPartII:R2/topologically-finitely-presented-algebra` (definition), module `TauCeti/RingTheory/Huber/TopologicallyFinitePresentation`.

API:

- `Huber.IsTopologicallyFinitePresentation` (structure): For a ϖ-adically complete O_K-algebra A: there exist n and finitely many f_1, …, f_m ∈ O_K⟨ξ_1, …, ξ_n⟩ with A ≅ O_K⟨ξ⟩/(f_1, …, f_m) as O_K-algebras.
- `Huber.IsTopologicallyFinitePresentation.of_presentation` (constructor): O_K⟨ξ⟩/(f_1, …, f_m) is tfp, for any finitely many f_j.
- `Huber.IsTopologicallyFinitePresentation.isTopologicallyFiniteType` (compatibility): If A is tfp then algebraMap O_K A is TauCeti.Huber.IsTopologicallyFiniteType for the ϖ-adic topologies (trivial weights T_i = {1}).
- `Huber.IsTopologicallyFinitePresentation.isAdicComplete` (characterisation): A tfp algebra is ϖ-adically Hausdorff and complete: IsAdicComplete (ϖ) A (Bosch–Lütkebohmert I 1.1(b)).
- `Huber.IsTopologicallyFinitePresentation.iff_of_surjective` (characterisation): If A is tft and O_K⟨η⟩ → A is any continuous surjection, then A is tfp if and only if its kernel is finitely generated.
- `Huber.IsTopologicallyFinitePresentation.completeLocalization` (constructor): For f ∈ A the completed localisation A_{f} (AdicSpacesPartII:F0/completed-localization, the ϖ-adic completion of A[1/f]) is isomorphic to A⟨ζ⟩/(1 − fζ), hence tfp; it depends only on the open set {f ≠ 0} of Spec(A/ϖ).
- `Huber.IsTopologicallyFinitePresentation.isAdicRing` (compatibility): A tfp O_K-algebra with its ϖ-adic topology is an adic ring of finite ideal type (AdicSpacesPartII:F0/adic-ring) with ideal of definition ϖA.
- `Huber.IsTopologicallyFinitePresentation.quotient` (constructor): If A is tfp and b ⊆ A is finitely generated then A/b and A⟨η_1, …, η_r⟩ are tfp.
- `Huber.IsTopologicallyFinitePresentation.iff_mod` (characterisation): A ϖ-adically complete and separated O_K-algebra A is tft if and only if A/ϖA is an O_K/ϖ-algebra of finite type (Bosch–Lütkebohmert I Lemma 1.5); if A is tfp then each A/ϖ^{m}A is a finitely presented O_K/ϖ^{m}-algebra.
- `Huber.IsTopologicallyFinitePresentation.genericFibre` (data): A ⊗_{O_K} K = A[1/ϖ] is a quotient of K⟨ξ⟩, i.e. a K-affinoid algebra; with ring of definition the image of A and ideal ϖ it is a complete Tate ring, strongly noetherian by the anchor's Layer 0.5.
- `Huber.IsAdmissibleAlgebra` (structure): A is IsTopologicallyFinitePresentation and Submodule.torsionBy O_K A ϖ = 0 (no ϖ-torsion, hence no ϖ-power torsion).
- `Huber.isAdmissibleAlgebra_iff_flat` (characterisation): For tfp A: IsAdmissibleAlgebra A ↔ Module.Flat O_K A.
- `Huber.IsAdmissibleAlgebra.injective_toGenericFibre` (other): For admissible A the map A → A[1/ϖ] is injective, so A is an O_K-lattice in the affinoid algebra A[1/ϖ].
- `Huber.IsTopologicallyFinitePresentation.torsionQuotient` (constructor): For tfp A the ϖ-power torsion ideal A[ϖ^∞] is finitely generated and A/A[ϖ^∞] is admissible, with A[1/ϖ] = (A/A[ϖ^∞])[1/ϖ].

Unit tests:

- `topologicallyFinitePresentation_test_restricted` (computation): O_K⟨T⟩ satisfies IsAdmissibleAlgebra over O_K, and its generic fibre O_K⟨T⟩ ⊗_{O_K} K is isomorphic to K⟨T⟩ as a topological K-algebra.
- `topologicallyFinitePresentation_test_torsion` (non-example): A = O_K⟨T⟩/(ϖT) is IsTopologicallyFinitePresentation but not IsAdmissibleAlgebra (the class of T is a nonzero ϖ-torsion element), and its torsion-free quotient is O_K.
- `topologicallyFinitePresentation_test_madic` (non-example): For K = C_p (where m_K² = m_K), the m_K-adic completion of O_K[T] is k[T]; hence a definition using the m_K-adic topology instead of the ϖ-adic one gives a different, wrong ring.
- `topologicallyFinitePresentation_test_zeroVars` (degenerate): With no variables, O_K is admissible, and O_K/ϖ^m (m ≥ 1) is tfp but not admissible.
- `topologicallyFinitePresentation_test_discrete` (compatibility): If K is discretely valued, every tft O_K-algebra is tfp (O_K⟨ξ⟩ is noetherian), and admissible means: noetherian, ϖ-adically complete, flat and tft over O_K.

Acceptance: O_K⟨T⟩ is admissible and O_K⟨T⟩ ⊗_{O_K} K = K⟨T⟩ is the Tate algebra. O_K⟨T⟩/(ϖT) is tfp but not admissible. For K = C_p the m_K-adic completion of O_K[T] is k[T], not O_K⟨T⟩, so the ϖ-adic topology is forced.

**The finiteness lemma** (Bosch–Lütkebohmert I Lemma 1.2; Fujiwara–Kato 0.9.2.1 and 0.8.5.3). For A tft
over O_K, a ϖ-saturated submodule of a finite free A-module is finitely generated; equivalently the
ϖ-power torsion of every finitely generated A-module is finitely generated and its torsion-free quotient
is finitely presented. Saturation is necessary: m_K ⊂ O_K is not finitely generated for non-discrete
K. The proof reduces to M_K ∩ O_K⟨ξ⟩^r with M_K finitely generated over the noetherian ring K⟨ξ⟩; the
final finiteness step is Bosch–Lütkebohmert's citation of [BGR 5.2.7/7] or Raynaud–Gruson (3.4.6),
recorded as an unread import.

*Node* `AdicSpacesPartII:R2/saturated-submodule-finitely-generated` (lemma), module `TauCeti/RingTheory/Huber/TopologicallyFinitePresentation`.

Hypotheses: O_K a complete valuation ring of rank one (Fujiwara–Kato: any height), ϖ ∈ m_K nonzero; A topologically of finite type over O_K; Saturation cannot be dropped: m_K ⊂ O_K (non-discrete K) is not finitely generated and not saturated.

Acceptance: A = O_K⟨T⟩, M = (T − c) with c ∈ O_K: saturated, generated by one element. Necessity of saturation: for K = C_p, the O_K-submodule m_K ⊂ O_K (A = O_K, F = O_K) is not finitely generated and is not saturated (ϖ·1 ∈ m_K, 1 ∉ m_K).

**Flat and tft implies tfp** (Bosch–Lütkebohmert I Proposition 1.1; Fujiwara–Kato I 2.3.2). A tft algebra
is ϖ-adically complete; a finitely generated ideal of O_K⟨ξ⟩ is closed; and if A = O_K⟨ξ⟩/a has no
ϖ-torsion then a is saturated, hence finitely generated. Consequence: every K-affinoid algebra
K⟨ξ⟩/b has the admissible model O_K⟨ξ⟩/(b ∩ O_K⟨ξ⟩). The torsion-freeness hypothesis is necessary:
O_K⟨T⟩/(m_K T) is tft and not tfp for non-discrete K.

*Node* `AdicSpacesPartII:R2/flat-tft-is-tfp` (lemma), module `TauCeti/RingTheory/Huber/TopologicallyFinitePresentation`.

Hypotheses: O_K complete of rank one (Fujiwara–Kato: any height); K need not be discretely valued; (c) needs the absence of ϖ-torsion: O_K⟨T⟩/(m_K T) is tft but not tfp for non-discrete K.

Acceptance: Every K-affinoid algebra B = K⟨ξ⟩/b has the admissible model A = O_K⟨ξ⟩/(b ∩ O_K⟨ξ⟩) with A[1/ϖ] = B. For non-discrete K, O_K⟨T⟩/(m_K T) is tft, has ϖ-torsion, and is not tfp: the flatness hypothesis in (c) is necessary.

**Coherence** (Bosch–Lütkebohmert I 1.3–1.4). A tfp O_K-algebra is a coherent ring; annihilators and
ϖ-power torsion of coherent modules are coherent. This is what makes coherent ideal sheaves, strict
transforms and torsion-free quotients available on non-noetherian formal schemes.

*Node* `AdicSpacesPartII:R2/tfp-algebra-coherent` (lemma), module `TauCeti/RingTheory/Huber/TopologicallyFinitePresentation`.

Hypotheses: O_K complete of rank one; in the noetherian case (II) the statement is noetherianity.

Acceptance: The ϖ-torsion ideal of O_K⟨T⟩/(ϖT) is (T), finitely generated, and the quotient O_K is admissible.

**Locality** (Bosch–Lütkebohmert I 1.6–1.7). For A ϖ-adically complete and separated and a cover of
Spf A by formal affines Spf B_i: A is tfp (resp. admissible) iff every B_i is; A → B_i is flat and
A → ∏ B_i faithfully flat. Flatness of coherent modules can be tested modulo every ϖ^m.

*Node* `AdicSpacesPartII:R2/tfp-locality` (lemma), module `TauCeti/RingTheory/Huber/TopologicallyFinitePresentation`.

Hypotheses: A ϖ-adically complete and separated; The cover is by formal affine opens, each B_i with the ϖ-adic topology.

Acceptance: The cover of Spf O_K⟨T⟩ by Spf O_K⟨T⟩⟨T⁻¹⟩ = Spf O_K⟨T, T⁻¹⟩ and Spf O_K⟨T⟩⟨(1 − T)⁻¹⟩ gives a faithfully flat map O_K⟨T⟩ → O_K⟨T,T⁻¹⟩ × O_K⟨T,(1−T)⁻¹⟩.


#### R2.2 Admissible formal schemes, type (S) and FS_C

**Admissible formal schemes** (`FormalScheme.IsLocallyTFP`, `FormalScheme.IsAdmissible`; planet
*Admissible formal scheme*). A formal O_K-scheme is locally of tf presentation if it is covered by
Spf A with A tfp; it is admissible if moreover O_X has no ϖ-torsion, equivalently every affine
coordinate ring is admissible, equivalently every stalk is O_K-flat. The underlying space equals that
of the special fibre X_s, a k-scheme locally of finite type, and is locally noetherian although O_X is
not. Fibre products in the admissible category are the formal fibre products divided by ϖ-torsion.
A coherent open ideal is a coherent ideal containing some ϖ^N. The ϖ-adic completion of a flat
O_K-scheme locally of finite presentation is admissible. Over a discretely valued K, admissible formal
schemes are exactly F0's locally noetherian formal schemes that are flat and adic of finite type over
Spf O_K. The campaign's acceptance test is here: the formal torus Spf O_C⟨T^{±1}⟩ over O_C is admissible
and not locally noetherian, and is the completed base change of the noetherian formal torus
Spf Z_p⟨T^{±1}⟩.

*Node* `AdicSpacesPartII:R2/admissible-formal-scheme` (definition), module `TauCeti/AlgebraicGeometry/FormalScheme/Admissible`.

API:

- `FormalScheme.IsLocallyTFP` (structure): X over Spf O_K has an open cover by Spf A with A IsTopologicallyFinitePresentation over O_K (ϖ-adic topology).
- `FormalScheme.IsAdmissible` (structure): X is IsLocallyTFP and O_X has no ϖ-torsion.
- `FormalScheme.isAdmissible_spf_iff` (characterisation): Spf A is admissible iff A is IsAdmissibleAlgebra.
- `FormalScheme.isAdmissible_iff_affineOpens` (characterisation): X is admissible iff Γ(U, O_X) is admissible for every formal affine open U, iff this holds for the members of one affine open cover (node tfp-locality).
- `FormalScheme.isAdmissible_iff_flat_stalks` (characterisation): For X locally tfp: X is admissible iff every stalk O_{X,x} is a flat O_K-module.
- `FormalScheme.IsAdmissible.ofIsOpenImmersion` (instance): An open formal subscheme of an admissible formal scheme is admissible.
- `FormalScheme.specialFibre` (data): X_s := X ×_{Spf O_K} Spec k, a k-scheme locally of finite type, with a homeomorphism of underlying spaces X_s → X.
- `FormalScheme.admissiblePullback` (universal-property): For admissible X → Z ← Y the closed formal subscheme of X ×_Z Y cut out by its ϖ-torsion ideal is admissible and is the fibre product in the category of admissible formal O_K-schemes; it equals X ×_Z Y when X or Y is flat over Z.
- `FormalScheme.torsionFreeQuotient` (universal-property): For X locally tfp the ϖ-torsion ideal is coherent and X^{tf} := V(torsion) is admissible; every morphism from an admissible formal scheme to X factors uniquely through X^{tf}.
- `FormalScheme.CoherentOpenIdeal` (structure): A coherent ideal 𝒜 ⊆ O_X containing ϖ^m O_X for some m; locally 𝒜 = (f_0, …, f_r)O_{Spf A} with ϖ^m ∈ (f_0, …, f_r).
- `FormalScheme.IsAdmissible.completion` (compatibility): The ϖ-adic completion X̂ of an O_K-scheme X locally of finite presentation is IsLocallyTFP, and is admissible when X is O_K-flat.
- `FormalScheme.IsAdmissible.iff_of_discreteValuation` (compatibility): If K is discretely valued, X is admissible iff X is a locally noetherian formal scheme (F0), flat over Spf O_K and adic locally of finite type over Spf O_K.
- `FormalScheme.IsAdmissible.isTypeS` (relation): Every admissible (indeed every locally tfp) formal O_K-scheme is of type (S), via condition (b) with s = ϖ.
- `FormalScheme.CoherentModule` (structure): A coherent O_X-module on X locally of tf presentation: on every formal affine open Spf A it is the sheaf attached to a coherent (equivalently finitely presented, node tfp-algebra-coherent) A-module (Bosch–Lütkebohmert I §1).

Unit tests:

- `admissible_test_formalAffineLine` (computation): Spf O_K⟨T⟩ is IsAdmissible over Spf O_K and its special fibre is isomorphic to A¹_k = Spec k[T].
- `admissible_test_torsion` (non-example): X = Spf(O_K⟨T⟩/(ϖT)) is IsLocallyTFP but not IsAdmissible; its special fibre is A¹_k while its torsion-free quotient is Spf O_K, whose special fibre is a point.
- `admissible_test_powerSeries` (non-example): Spf O_K[[T]] with the (ϖ,T)-adic topology is not IsLocallyTFP over Spf O_K (ϖ does not generate an ideal of definition), even though for discretely valued K it is a locally noetherian formal O_K-scheme.
- `admissible_test_completion_projectiveLine` (compatibility): The ϖ-adic completion of P¹_{O_K} is IsAdmissible, is covered by two copies of Spf O_K⟨T⟩ meeting in Spf O_K⟨T,T⁻¹⟩, and its special fibre is P¹_k.
- `admissible_test_formalTorus` (compatibility): For C = C_p, Spf O_C⟨T^{±1}⟩ is admissible, not locally noetherian, and is the ϖ-adic completion of the base change of the noetherian formal torus Spf Z_p⟨T^{±1}⟩.
- `admissible_test_base` (degenerate): Spf O_K is admissible and terminal among admissible formal O_K-schemes; its special fibre is Spec k.

Acceptance: Spf O_K⟨T⟩ is admissible with special fibre A¹_k. The ϖ-adic completion of P¹_{O_K} is admissible, glued from two copies of Spf O_K⟨T⟩. Campaign acceptance: the formal torus Spf O_C⟨T^{±1}⟩ over O_C (C = C_p) is admissible but not locally noetherian, while Spf Z_p⟨T^{±1}⟩ is both, and the former is the ϖ-adic completion of the base change of the latter.

**Formal schemes of type (S)** (`FormalScheme.IsTypeS`). Huber's condition: locally Spf A with A adic and
either (a) A noetherian, or (b) some s ∈ A generates an ideal of definition and the Tate ring A(1/s) is
strongly noetherian. The layer proves how the three classes in play relate:

```text
locally noetherian (F0)  ⊆  type (S) via (a)
Conrad's FS_C            ⊆  locally noetherian (C noetherian)
locally tfp over O_K     ⊆  type (S) via (b), s = ϖ   (includes all admissible formal schemes)
```

For non-discrete K, Spf O_K⟨T⟩ is of type (S)(b), not (a), and not in any FS_C; Spf R_0[[T]] (R_0 a
complete DVR) is in FS_{R_0} and of type (S)(a), not (b); Spf O_K[[T]] with the (ϖ,T)-adic topology is
not of type (S) at all, which is why Conrad works with FS_C over a noetherian C → O_K.

*Node* `AdicSpacesPartII:R2/formal-schemes-of-type-S` (definition), module `TauCeti/AlgebraicGeometry/FormalScheme/TypeS`.

API:

- `FormalScheme.IsTypeS` (structure): Every point has a formal affine neighbourhood Spf A, A adic, with A noetherian or with some s ∈ A generating an ideal of definition and A(1/s) strongly noetherian.
- `FormalScheme.IsTypeS.of_isLocallyNoetherian` (instance): Locally noetherian formal schemes (F0) are of type (S).
- `FormalScheme.IsTypeS.of_isLocallyTFP` (instance): Formal O_K-schemes locally of tf presentation, in particular admissible ones, are of type (S) with s = ϖ.
- `FormalScheme.IsTypeS.of_mem_FSC` (relation): Every object of Conrad's FS_C is of type (S) via (a).
- `FormalScheme.IsTypeS.ofIsOpenImmersion` (instance): Open formal subschemes of type-(S) formal schemes are of type (S).
- `FormalScheme.IsTypeS.idealOfDefinition_fg` (other): For X of type (S), every formal affine open Spf A has an adic topology with a finitely generated ideal of definition.
- `FormalScheme.IsTypeS.completion` (other): If f: X → Y is a morphism of schemes locally of finite type, Y' ⊆ Y is defined by an ideal of finite type and Ŷ is of type (S), then the completion X̂ along f⁻¹(Y') is of type (S) and f̂ is adic (Huber 1996 (1.9.5)).
- `FormalScheme.IsTypeS.spf_microbial` (example): Spf A is of type (S) for every microbial valuation ring A with its valuation topology.
- `FormalScheme.not_isTypeS_powerSeries_of_not_discrete` (example): For K not discretely valued, Spf O_K[[T]] with the (ϖ,T)-adic topology is not of type (S).

Unit tests:

- `typeS_test_admissible_not_noetherian` (characterisation): For K = C_p, Spf O_K⟨T⟩ is IsTypeS through condition (b) with s = ϖ and does not satisfy condition (a).
- `typeS_test_powerSeries_nondiscrete` (non-example): For K = C_p, Spf O_K[[T]] with the (ϖ,T)-adic topology is not IsTypeS: O_K[[T]] is not noetherian and no principal ideal is an ideal of definition.
- `typeS_test_dvr_powerSeries` (computation): For a complete discrete valuation ring R_0, Spf R_0[[T]] is IsTypeS through (a) but not through (b), and it is an object of FS_{R_0}.
- `typeS_test_microbial` (compatibility): For every complete rank-one valuation ring O_K, Spf O_K is IsTypeS via (b) with s = ϖ, and A(1/s) = K.
- `typeS_test_discrete` (degenerate): For a noetherian ring A with the discrete topology, Spec A viewed as a formal scheme is of type (S) via (a); its generic fibre d(Spec A) is empty.

Acceptance: Spf O_K for a complete rank-one O_K (not necessarily discretely valued) is of type (S) via (b). A noetherian adic formal scheme is of type (S) via (a), and then d(X) = t(X)_a (node generic-fibre-functor-d). Spf O_K⟨T⟩ over C_p is of type (S) but not an object of Conrad's FS_C.


#### R2.3 Generic fibres

**Huber's functor t** (`FormalScheme.toAdicSpace`). For X locally noetherian, t(X) is universal among adic
spaces with a morphism of locally and topologically ringed spaces (Z, O_Z⁺) → (X, O_X); t(Spf A) =
Spa(A, A); the centre map π_X(x) = {a : |a(x)| < 1}; t is fully faithful and detects adic and
locally-finite-type morphisms (Huber 1994 4.1–4.2). The trivial valuations form a copy of X inside t(X).
Sheafiness of Spa(A, A) for noetherian adic A (Huber 1994 Theorem 2.2) is R0's noetherian-type sheafiness node.

*Node* `AdicSpacesPartII:R2/noetherian-formal-scheme-as-adic-space` (construction), module `TauCeti/AlgebraicGeometry/FormalScheme/ToAdicSpace`.

API:

- `FormalScheme.toAdicSpace` (constructor): The functor t from locally noetherian formal schemes to adic spaces.
- `FormalScheme.toAdicSpace_spf` (simp): t(Spf A) ≅ Spa(A, A) for a noetherian adic ring A.
- `FormalScheme.centerMap` (projection): π_X: (t(X), O⁺) → (X, O_X), a morphism of locally and topologically ringed spaces.
- `FormalScheme.centerMap_spf_apply` (simp): On Spf A: π(x) = {a ∈ A : |a(x)| < 1}, the image of the closed point of Spec κ(x)⁺.
- `FormalScheme.toAdicSpace.lift` (universal-property): A morphism of locally and topologically ringed spaces (Z, O⁺_Z) → (X, O_X) from an adic space factors as π_X ∘ g for a unique morphism of adic spaces g: Z → t(X).
- `FormalScheme.toAdicSpace.lift_comp_centerMap` (universal-property): π_X ∘ lift λ = λ, and lift is unique with this property.
- `FormalScheme.toAdicSpace.map_id` (functoriality): t(id_X) = id and t(g ∘ f) = t(g) ∘ t(f).
- `FormalScheme.toAdicSpace.fullyFaithful` (functoriality): t is fully faithful.
- `FormalScheme.toAdicSpace_isAdic_iff` (compatibility): f is adic (EGA I 10.12) iff t(f) is an adic morphism (AdicSpacesPartII:R0/adic-morphism).
- `FormalScheme.toAdicSpace_locallyOfFiniteType_iff` (compatibility): f is locally of finite type (EGA I 10.13) iff t(f) is locally of finite type (R0/finite-type-morphism-classes).
- `FormalScheme.trivialValuationSection` (data): ι_X: X → t(X), sending an open prime p to the trivial valuation of κ(p), with π_X ∘ ι_X = id and image the trivial-valuation locus.

Unit tests:

- `toAdicSpace_test_spf_Zp` (computation): t(Spf Z_p) = Spa(Z_p, Z_p) has exactly two points; the closed point is non-analytic and maps under π to the unique point of Spf Z_p; the other is Spa(Q_p, Z_p).
- `toAdicSpace_test_ZpT` (computation): The analytic locus of t(Spf Z_p[[T]]) equals the union over n ≥ 1 of the rational subsets R(Tⁿ/p), is the open unit disc over Q_p, and is not quasi-compact.
- `toAdicSpace_test_discrete` (degenerate): For a noetherian ring A with the discrete topology, every point of t(Spec A) = Spa(A, A) is non-analytic, and π restricted to the trivial valuations is a homeomorphism onto Spec A.
- `toAdicSpace_test_notEssentiallySurjective` (non-example): Spa(Q_p, Z_p) is not isomorphic to t(X) for any locally noetherian formal scheme X: a nonempty t(X) contains a non-analytic point (a trivial valuation) over each point of X.
- `toAdicSpace_test_fullyFaithful` (characterisation): Morphisms Spf Z_p[[S]] → Spf Z_p[[T]] of formal schemes correspond bijectively to morphisms t(Spf Z_p[[S]]) → t(Spf Z_p[[T]]) of adic spaces, i.e. to elements T ↦ g ∈ (p, S)Z_p[[S]].

Acceptance: t(Spf Z_p) = Spa(Z_p, Z_p) has two points: the trivial valuation modulo p (non-analytic) and the p-adic valuation (analytic). The analytic locus of t(Spf Z_p[[T]]) is the open unit disc over Q_p, the union of the rational subsets R(Tⁿ/p) (Hübner, Example 8.7).

**The generic fibre d** (`FormalScheme.genericFibre`; planet *Generic fibre*). For X of type (S),
Proposition 1.9.1 gives an analytic adic space d(X) with λ_X: d(X) → X universal among adic spaces
mapping to X on which the ideal of definition generates the unit ideal and O_X lands in O⁺. Affine
formulas: d(Spf A) = t(Spf A)_a for A noetherian; d(Spf A) = Spa(A(1/s), B) in case (b), B the integral
closure of A in A(1/s). The plus ring is the integral closure, not A: for A = O_K[X]/(X² − ϖ²) (p ≠ 2)
the image of A in A_K ≅ K × K is not integrally closed. Over O_K, d(X) is the open locus over the
generic point of Spa(O_K, O_K), ϖ-torsion is invisible (d(X^{tf}) = d(X)), open formal subschemes give
open subspaces d(U) = λ⁻¹(U), and d(U) is spectral for affine U.

*Node* `AdicSpacesPartII:R2/generic-fibre-functor-d` (construction), module `TauCeti/AlgebraicGeometry/FormalScheme/GenericFibre`.

API:

- `FormalScheme.genericFibre` (constructor): d(X), an analytic adic space, for X of type (S).
- `FormalScheme.genericFibre.lift` (universal-property): A morphism of topologically ringed spaces g: Z → X from an adic space satisfying (a) and (b) factors uniquely as λ_X ∘ g̃ with g̃: Z → d(X).
- `FormalScheme.genericFibre.lift_unique` (universal-property): Two morphisms Z → d(X) with the same composite to X are equal.
- `FormalScheme.genericFibre.map` (functoriality): An adic morphism f: X → Y of type-(S) formal schemes induces d(f): d(X) → d(Y) with λ_Y ∘ d(f) = f ∘ λ_X; d(id) = id and d(g ∘ f) = d(g) ∘ d(f).
- `FormalScheme.genericFibre_spf_of_typeSb` (simp): If sA is an ideal of definition and A(1/s) strongly noetherian, d(Spf A) ≅ Spa(A(1/s), integralClosure A A(1/s)).
- `FormalScheme.genericFibre_spf_of_isNoetherian` (compatibility): For A noetherian adic, d(Spf A) ≅ t(Spf A)_a = spaAnalytic of (A, A).
- `FormalScheme.genericFibre_ofIsOpenImmersion` (compatibility): For an open formal subscheme U ⊆ X, d(U) → d(X) is an open immersion with image λ⁻¹(U).
- `FormalScheme.genericFibre_torsionFreeQuotient` (simp): For X locally tfp over O_K, d(X^{tf}) → d(X) is an isomorphism.
- `FormalScheme.genericFibre_isAnalytic` (instance): Every point of d(X) is analytic.
- `FormalScheme.genericFibre_spectralSpace` (instance): For U affine of type (S), d(U) is a spectral space and λ is a spectral map (Huber 1996 (1.9.3)).
- `FormalScheme.genericFibre_quasiCompact` (other): If X is quasi-compact and locally tfp over O_K then d(X) is quasi-compact and quasi-separated.
- `FormalScheme.genericFibre_spf_microbial` (example): For a microbial valuation ring A with fraction field L, d(Spf A) = Spa(L, A) and λ is a homeomorphism onto Spf A (Huber 1996 1.9.2(i)).

Unit tests:

- `genericFibre_test_formalAffineLine` (computation): d(Spf O_K⟨T⟩) is the adic space Spa(K⟨T⟩, O_K⟨T⟩), whose underlying set is closedPolydisc 1 K.
- `genericFibre_test_powerSeries_dvr` (computation): For K discretely valued with uniformiser ϖ, d(Spf O_K[[T]]) is the union of the rational subsets {|Tⁿ| ≤ |ϖ|}, n ≥ 1, of the closed disc, and is not quasi-compact.
- `genericFibre_test_torsion` (degenerate): d(Spf O_K/ϖ) = ∅ and d(Spf O_K⟨T⟩/(ϖT)) ≅ d(Spf O_K) = Spa(K, O_K): ϖ-torsion does not contribute.
- `genericFibre_test_plusRing` (non-example): For p ≠ 2 and A = O_K[X]/(X² − ϖ²), A[1/ϖ] ≅ K × K and the image of A is not integrally closed (X/ϖ ↦ (1, −1) is integral but not in A); the plus ring of d(Spf A) is the integral closure O_K × O_K, while spa of A and of its integral closure agree (spa_integralClosure).
- `genericFibre_test_noetherian` (compatibility): For A = Z_p⟨T⟩ (both (a) and (b) apply) the two affine formulas agree: Spa(Z_p⟨T⟩, Z_p⟨T⟩)_a = Spa(Q_p⟨T⟩, Z_p⟨T⟩).

Acceptance: d(Spf O_K) = Spa(K, O_K) for a complete rank-one valued field K, a one-point space mapping to the closed point of Spf O_K. d(Spf O_K⟨T⟩) is the closed unit disc Spa(K⟨T⟩, O_K⟨T⟩). For K discretely valued, d(Spf O_K[[T]]) is the open unit disc, not quasi-compact.

**Comparison with Raynaud's generic fibre.** For X locally tfp over O_K, the plus ring of d(Spf A) is
A_K° (Huber 1994 Lemma 4.4 with BGR 6.3.4), so d(Spf A) = Spa(A_K, A_K°) = r(Sp A_K), and gluing along
Laurent domains gives d(X) ≅ r(X_rig), functorially (Huber 1996 Example 1.9.2(ii); Huber 1994 Remark
4.6(ii) in the discretely valued case). Hence d(X) is locally of finite type over Spa(K, O_K),
quasi-separated, and quasi-compact when X is.

*Node* `AdicSpacesPartII:R2/raynaud-generic-fibre` (comparison), module `TauCeti/AlgebraicGeometry/FormalScheme/GenericFibre`.

Hypotheses: K complete, nontrivial rank-one valuation; O_K may be non-noetherian; X locally tfp over Spf O_K; r and its properties are those of AdicSpacesPartII:R1/rigid-adic-comparison-functor.

Acceptance: d(Spf O_K⟨T⟩) = r(Sp K⟨T⟩) is the closed unit disc; d of the ϖ-adic completion of P¹_{O_K} is r of the rigid projective line glued from two closed unit discs along {|T| = 1} (Conrad, Several approaches, Example 3.3.9). For K discretely valued with uniformiser ϖ, X = Spf(O_K⟨T⟩/(T² − ϖ)) = Spf O_L with L = K(√ϖ) (Eisenstein), d(X) = Spa(L, O_L) is one point and X_rig = Sp L.

**Fibre products and base field.** d(X ×_Z Y) ≅ d(X) ×_{d(Z)} d(Y) for locally tfp formal O_K-schemes,
using R0's completed tensor products (Bosch–Lütkebohmert I Corollary 4.6 in rigid form), and
d(X ⊗̂_{O_K} O_{K'}) ≅ d(X) ×_{Spa K} Spa K' for every complete extension K'/K.

*Node* `AdicSpacesPartII:R2/generic-fibre-fibre-products` (lemma), module `TauCeti/AlgebraicGeometry/FormalScheme/GenericFibre`.

Hypotheses: X, Y, Z locally tfp over O_K; K'/K any complete extension of rank-one valued fields in (b).

Acceptance: d(Spf O_K⟨S⟩ ×_{Spf O_K} Spf O_K⟨T⟩) = d(Spf O_K⟨S,T⟩) is the closed unit bidisc, the fibre product of two closed unit discs over Spa(K, O_K). For P, P' formal O_K-schemes of finite type, (P × P')_K = P_K × P'_K (PadicDifferentialEquationsAndRigidCohomology request).


#### R2.4 Specialisation, tubes and rig-points

**The specialisation map** (`FormalScheme.specialisation`). λ(x) = {a ∈ A : |a(x)| < 1} is the centre of
x. λ is continuous: λ⁻¹(D(s)) = {|s| ≥ 1} is open and λ⁻¹(V(s)) = {|s| < 1} is closed. It is natural in
X and compatible with admissible blow-ups. For X admissible, classical points go to closed points of
X_s and every closed point is hit (rig-points); on classical points λ is Berthelot's sp, which in the
rigid language is 'anticontinuous'. For X quasi-compact admissible, λ over all admissible blow-ups
identifies (d(X), O⁺) with the Zariski–Riemann limit of formal models (Hübner Theorem 8.9, whose proof
relies on unread notes of Bhatt).

*Node* `AdicSpacesPartII:R2/specialisation-map` (construction), module `TauCeti/AlgebraicGeometry/FormalScheme/Specialisation`.

API:

- `FormalScheme.specialisation` (data): λ_X: d(X) → X, the continuous map of Proposition 1.9.1.
- `FormalScheme.specialisation_spf_apply` (simp): For X = Spf A: λ(x) = {a ∈ A : v_x(a) < 1}.
- `FormalScheme.specialisation_eq_center` (characterisation): λ(x) is the image of the closed point of Spec κ(x)⁺ under Spec κ(x)⁺ → Spec A.
- `FormalScheme.continuous_specialisation` (other): λ_X is continuous.
- `FormalScheme.specialisation_preimage_basicOpen` (characterisation): λ⁻¹(D(s)) = {x : |s(x)| ≥ 1} = rationalSubset {1} s, open; λ⁻¹(V(s)) = {|s| < 1}, closed.
- `FormalScheme.specialisation_naturality` (functoriality): λ_Y ∘ d(f) = f ∘ λ_X for every adic morphism f: X → Y of type-(S) formal schemes.
- `FormalScheme.specialisation_classical_isClosed` (relation): For X admissible and x classical, λ(x) is a closed point of X_s.
- `FormalScheme.exists_classical_specialisation_eq` (relation): For X admissible, every closed point of X_s equals λ(x) for some classical x.
- `FormalScheme.specialisation_blowUp` (compatibility): For an admissible blow-up φ: X' → X, φ ∘ λ_{X'} = λ_X ∘ d(φ).
- `FormalScheme.rigidSpecialisation` (compatibility): On classical points, λ agrees with Berthelot's sp: X_rig → X under node raynaud-generic-fibre and R1's identification of classical points.
- `FormalScheme.specialisationLimitHomeomorph` (equivalence): For X quasi-compact admissible, d(X) → lim_{X'} |X'| over admissible blow-ups is a homeomorphism (Zariski–Riemann).

Unit tests:

- `specialisation_test_closedDisc` (computation): For X = Spf O_K⟨T⟩, λ sends the Gauss point to the generic point of A¹_k and the classical point T = c (c ∈ O_K) to the closed point T = c̄.
- `specialisation_test_Spf_OK` (degenerate): For X = Spf O_K, d(X) = Spa(K, O_K) is one point and λ maps it to the unique point of Spf O_K.
- `specialisation_test_preimage_closed` (non-example): In the closed unit disc, λ⁻¹({0}) = {|T| < 1} is closed and not open: it contains the rank-two point η_{1⁻} (the specialisation of the Gauss point towards 0) but no open neighbourhood of it.
- `specialisation_test_blowUp` (compatibility): For the admissible blow-up X' of (T, ϖ) on Spf O_K⟨T⟩, λ_X(η_{|ϖ|}) is the closed point 0 of A¹_k, while λ_{X'}(η_{|ϖ|}) is the generic point of the exceptional component, and φ ∘ λ_{X'} = λ_X.
- `specialisation_test_surjective_closed` (characterisation): For X admissible, the set of λ(x) with x classical is exactly the set of closed points of X_s.

Acceptance: For X = Spf O_K⟨T⟩: λ(Gauss point) is the generic point of A¹_k and λ(T = c) is the closed point T = c̄ for c ∈ O_K. λ⁻¹({0}) = {|T| < 1} is closed and not open in the closed unit disc.

**Tubes** (`FormalScheme.tube`). For U open in X_s, ]U[ = λ⁻¹(U) = d(X|_U). For Z closed and X = Spf A
with Z = V(ϖ, f_1, …, f_r),

```text
]Z[ = ⋃_{m ≥ 1} { x : |f_i(x)|^m ≤ |ϖ| for all i } = interior of λ⁻¹(Z),
```

independent of the f_i and of ϖ; for T = U ∩ Z, ]T[ = λ⁻¹(U) ∩ ]Z[. Classical points of ]T[ are exactly
Berthelot's sp⁻¹(T), and r carries the admissible open sp⁻¹(T) to ]T[. Closed tubes of fractional
radius, [Z]_q = {|f_i| ≤ |ϖ|^q}, are quasi-compact and exhaust ]Z[. The tubes of {0} and of its open
complement in A¹_k do not cover the closed disc: the missing rank-two point η_{1⁻} is the adic
shadow of the non-admissible rigid covering {|t| = 1} ⊔ {|t| < 1}.

*Node* `AdicSpacesPartII:R2/tube` (construction), module `TauCeti/AlgebraicGeometry/FormalScheme/Tube`.

API:

- `FormalScheme.tube` (constructor): ]T[ ⊆ d(X) for T ⊆ X locally closed.
- `FormalScheme.tube_of_isOpen` (simp): For U open: ]U[ = λ⁻¹(U), the image of d(X|_U).
- `FormalScheme.tube_spf_of_isClosed` (characterisation): For X = Spf A and Z = V(ϖ, f_1, …, f_r): ]Z[ = ⋃_m {|f_i|^m ≤ |ϖ| ∀ i}, independent of the f_i and of ϖ.
- `FormalScheme.tube_eq_interior_preimage` (characterisation): For Z closed: ]Z[ = interior(λ⁻¹(Z)).
- `FormalScheme.isOpen_tube` (other): ]T[ is open in d(X).
- `FormalScheme.tube_inter` (relation): ]T ∩ T'[ = ]T[ ∩ ]T'[ and ]U ∩ Z[ = λ⁻¹(U) ∩ ]Z[.
- `FormalScheme.tube_preimage` (functoriality): For f: Y → X adic between admissible formal schemes: d(f)⁻¹(]T[) = ]f⁻¹(T)[.
- `FormalScheme.tube_classicalPoints` (compatibility): The classical points of ]T[ are the classical x with λ(x) ∈ T; under r they form Berthelot's admissible open sp⁻¹(T).
- `FormalScheme.closedTube` (constructor): [Z]_q = {|f_i| ≤ |ϖ|^q ∀ i} for q ∈ ℚ_{>0} (fractional convention), a quasi-compact open; ]Z[ = ⋃_q [Z]_q.
- `FormalScheme.tube_blowUp` (compatibility): For an admissible blow-up φ: X' → X, d(φ) maps ]φ⁻¹(T)[ isomorphically onto ]T[.

Unit tests:

- `tube_test_origin_disc` (computation): For X = Spf O_K⟨T⟩ and Z = {0} ⊆ A¹_k, tube X Z = ⋃_{m ≥ 1} {x : |T(x)|^m ≤ |ϖ|}, the open unit disc.
- `tube_test_preimage_not_open` (non-example): For X = Spf O_K⟨T⟩ and Z = {0}, the point η_{1⁻} lies in λ⁻¹(Z) but not in tube X Z; so defining the adic tube as λ⁻¹(Z) gives a closed, non-open set.
- `tube_test_classical` (compatibility): The classical points of tube X {0} for X = Spf O_K⟨T⟩ are the Galois orbits of c ∈ K̄ with |c| < 1, i.e. Berthelot's sp⁻¹(0).
- `tube_test_open_complement` (characterisation): For X = Spf O_K⟨T⟩: tube X (A¹_k ∖ {0}) = {|T| = 1}, and tube X {0} ∪ tube X (A¹_k ∖ {0}) ≠ d(X).
- `tube_test_whole` (degenerate): tube X X_s = d(X) and tube X ∅ = ∅.

Acceptance: X = Spf O_K⟨T⟩, Z = {0}: ]Z[ is the open unit disc ⋃_m {|T|^m ≤ |ϖ|}. X = Spf O_K⟨T⟩, U = A¹_k ∖ {0}: ]U[ = {|T| = 1}; ]U[ ∪ ]{0}[ misses the point η_{1⁻}, matching the non-admissible rigid covering {|t| = 1} ⊔ {|t| < 1} of {|t| ≤ 1} (Conrad, genpaper, before the proof of A.1.4).

**Rig-points** (`FormalScheme.RigPoint`). Closed immersions Spf B → X with B a local domain of
dimension one (Bosch–Lütkebohmert I §3). B is finite over O_K with normalisation the valuation ring of
the finite extension Frac(B)/K; rig-points are invariant under admissible blow-up; on Spf A they
correspond to maximal ideals of A_K; every closed point of X_s underlies one (via [BGR 7.1.5/4]).
They are the classical points of d(X).

*Node* `AdicSpacesPartII:R2/rig-point` (definition), module `TauCeti/AlgebraicGeometry/FormalScheme/RigPoint`.

API:

- `FormalScheme.RigPoint` (structure): A closed immersion Spf B → X of admissible formal O_K-schemes with B a local domain of dimension 1.
- `FormalScheme.RigPoint.residueField` (data): Frac(B), a finite extension of K.
- `FormalScheme.RigPoint.integralClosure_eq_valuationRing` (characterisation): The integral closure of B in Frac(B) is the valuation ring of Frac(B), and B is finite over O_K.
- `FormalScheme.RigPoint.map` (functoriality): A morphism Y → X induces rig-pts(Y) → rig-pts(X); residue fields may shrink.
- `FormalScheme.RigPoint.equivOfBlowUp` (equivalence): For an admissible blow-up X' → X, rig-pts(X') → rig-pts(X) is a bijection preserving residue fields.
- `FormalScheme.RigPoint.equivMaxSpec` (equivalence): For X = Spf A: rig-points ↔ primes p with ϖ ∉ p and dim A/p = 1 ↔ maximal ideals of A ⊗_{O_K} K.
- `FormalScheme.RigPoint.exists_of_isClosedPoint` (other): Every closed point of X_s is the special point of a rig-point.
- `FormalScheme.RigPoint.equivClassicalPoints` (compatibility): Rig-points of X ↔ classical points of d(X); the special point of u equals λ of the classical point.
- `FormalScheme.RigPoint.specialPoint` (projection): The closed point of X_s underlying u.

Unit tests:

- `rigPoint_test_disc` (computation): For c ∈ O_K, the O_K-algebra map O_K⟨T⟩ → O_K, T ↦ c, defines a rig-point of Spf O_K⟨T⟩ with residue field K whose special point is T = c̄ and whose classical point is T = c.
- `rigPoint_test_notDim1` (non-example): The closed immersion Spec k → Spf O_K⟨T⟩ at T = 0 is not a rig-point: k is a field (dimension 0) and Spec k is not admissible (it is ϖ-torsion).
- `rigPoint_test_blowUp` (compatibility): For the admissible blow-up X' of (T, ϖ) on Spf O_K⟨T⟩, the rig-point T = 0 lifts uniquely to X', into the chart Spf O_K⟨T, U⟩/(T − ϖU) at U = 0, with the same residue field K.

#### R2.5 Admissible blow-ups and Raynaud's theorem

**Admissible blow-ups** (`FormalScheme.admissibleBlowUp`; planet *Admissible blow-up*). For a coherent
open ideal 𝒜 on admissible X, Bl_𝒜 X = lim_m Proj(⊕ 𝒜ⁿ ⊗ O_X/ϖ^{m+1}). Over Spf A with 𝒜 = (f_0, …, f_r)
it is covered by the charts

```text
Spf ( A⟨ζ_j : j ≠ i⟩ / (f_i ζ_j − f_j)  modulo ϖ-torsion ),   ϖ-torsion = f_i-torsion,
```

it is admissible, 𝒜 becomes invertible, and it has the universal property among all formal schemes on
which 𝒜 is invertible. It is an isomorphism away from V(𝒜), proper and surjective on special fibres,
compatible with base change (strict transforms), multiplicative in 𝒜; for quasi-compact X composites of
admissible blow-ups are admissible blow-ups and any two are dominated by a third, so admissible
blow-ups of X form a cofiltered system. Openness of 𝒜 is essential: blowing up the non-open ideal
(S, T) of Spf O_K⟨S, T⟩ changes the generic fibre.

*Node* `AdicSpacesPartII:R2/admissible-blow-up` (construction), module `TauCeti/AlgebraicGeometry/FormalScheme/AdmissibleBlowUp`.

API:

- `FormalScheme.admissibleBlowUp` (constructor): X' = Bl_𝒜 X for a coherent open ideal 𝒜.
- `FormalScheme.admissibleBlowUp.π` (projection): φ: Bl_𝒜 X → X.
- `FormalScheme.admissibleBlowUp.isAdmissible` (instance): Bl_𝒜 X is admissible.
- `FormalScheme.admissibleBlowUp.isInvertible` (other): 𝒜O_{Bl_𝒜 X} is an invertible ideal sheaf.
- `FormalScheme.admissibleBlowUp.lift` (universal-property): ψ: Z → X with 𝒜O_Z invertible lifts to Z → Bl_𝒜 X.
- `FormalScheme.admissibleBlowUp.lift_comp_π` (universal-property): π ∘ lift ψ = ψ; the lift is unique.
- `FormalScheme.admissibleBlowUp.chart` (data): Over Spf A with 𝒜 = (f_0, …, f_r): the open Spf(A⟨ζ⟩/(f_iζ_j − f_j)/ϖ-torsion) where f_i generates, with ϖ-torsion = f_i-torsion.
- `FormalScheme.admissibleBlowUp.isIso_of_disjoint` (other): φ is an isomorphism over X ∖ V(𝒜).
- `FormalScheme.admissibleBlowUp.baseChange` (compatibility): For Y → X in the admissible category, the strict transform of Y is Bl_{𝒜O_Y} Y (Bosch–Lütkebohmert I Remark 2.3).
- `FormalScheme.admissibleBlowUp.isProper_surjective_specialFibre` (other): φ is proper, and surjective on special fibres.
- `FormalScheme.admissibleBlowUp.mul` (relation): Bl_{ℬO_{X'}}(Bl_𝒜 X) ≅ Bl_{𝒜ℬ} X over X.
- `FormalScheme.admissibleBlowUp.comp` (relation): For X quasi-compact, a composite of admissible blow-ups is an admissible blow-up.
- `FormalScheme.admissibleBlowUp.extend` (other): For X quasi-compact and admissible blow-ups of finitely many opens U_i, there is one admissible blow-up of X restricting to blow-ups dominating each.
- `FormalScheme.admissibleBlowUp.dominate` (relation): Any two admissible blow-ups of X are dominated by the blow-up of the product ideal.
- `FormalScheme.strictTransform` (constructor): For a coherent ℳ: ℳ' = φ*ℳ / Ann_{φ*ℳ}(𝒜O_{X'})-supported part; equals φ*ℳ modulo ϖ-torsion when ℳ' is torsion-free.
- `FormalScheme.strictTransformBaseChange` (constructor): For f: X → T locally of tf presentation, a coherent O_X-module ℳ and the admissible blow-up φ: T' → T of a coherent open ideal 𝒜: ℳ' = ℳ_{X'}/(sections of ℳ_{X'} supported over V(𝒜), i.e. killed by a power of 𝒜O_{X'}) on X' = X ×_T T' (Raynaud–Gruson I 5.1.1(ii)); this torsion lies in the ϖ-power torsion, and for ℳ = O_X it defines the strict transform of X, a closed formal subscheme of X ×_T T'.
- `FormalScheme.strictTransformBaseChange_comp` (relation): For admissible blow-ups T'' → T' → T whose centres avoid an open U ⊆ T (resp. its preimage), with U ⊇ the generic fibre schematically dense, the strict transform along T'' → T is the strict transform along T'' → T' of the strict transform along T' → T: all are the quotient by the sections vanishing over U (Raynaud–Gruson I 5.3.2).
- `FormalScheme.admissibleBlowUp.comp_of_disjoint` (relation): For X quasi-compact, an open U ⊆ X and admissible blow-ups X' → X with centre disjoint from U and X'' → X' with centre disjoint from the preimage of U, the composite is an admissible blow-up with centre disjoint from U (Raynaud–Gruson I 5.1.4, 'U-admissible').

Unit tests:

- `admissibleBlowUp_test_disc_origin` (computation): For X = Spf O_K⟨T⟩ and 𝒜 = (T, ϖ): X' is covered by Spf O_K⟨U⟩ (T = ϖU) and Spf O_K⟨T,V⟩/(TV − ϖ), and X'_s is the union of P¹_k (exceptional) and A¹_k (strict transform of X_s) meeting in one point.
- `admissibleBlowUp_test_unit` (degenerate): For 𝒜 = O_X or 𝒜 = ϖ^n O_X, φ: X' → X is an isomorphism.
- `admissibleBlowUp_test_nonOpenCentre` (non-example): Blowing up the non-open ideal (S, T) of Spf O_K⟨S,T⟩ (formal completion of the scheme blow-up of the origin) changes the generic fibre: it produces the blow-up of the origin in the closed bidisc, which is not isomorphic to the bidisc; so the openness condition in the definition is necessary for node generic-fibre-inverts-admissible-blow-ups.
- `admissibleBlowUp_test_universal` (characterisation): For 𝒜 = (T, ϖ) on Spf O_K⟨T⟩ and ψ: Spf O_K → Spf O_K⟨T⟩, T ↦ ϖ², the ideal ψ*𝒜 = (ϖ) is invertible and ψ lifts uniquely to X', into the chart U = T/ϖ with U ↦ ϖ.
- `admissibleBlowUp_test_scheme` (compatibility): For X = Spf A and a = (ϖ, f), φ⁻¹(X) is the ϖ-adic completion of the Proj of the Rees algebra reesAlgebra a over Spec A, modulo ϖ-torsion.
- `strictTransform_test_annulus` (computation): For X = Spf O_K⟨ζ, ξ⟩/(ζξ − ϖ) → T = Spf O_K⟨ζ⟩ and 𝒜 = (ζ, ϖ): on the chart ζ = ϖu of T' the pull-back of O_X is O_K⟨u, ξ⟩/(ϖ(uξ − 1)), and its strict transform is O_K⟨u, ξ⟩/(uξ − 1) ≅ O_K⟨u, u⁻¹⟩.

Acceptance: The admissible blow-up of (T, ϖ) on Spf O_K⟨T⟩ has charts Spf O_K⟨U⟩ (T = ϖU) and Spf O_K⟨T, V⟩/(TV − ϖ); its special fibre is P¹_k ∪ A¹_k meeting in one point. Blowing up an invertible open ideal (e.g. ϖ^n O_X) is an isomorphism.

**Blow-ups are invisible on the generic fibre.** The chart where f_i generates has generic fibre the
rational subset R(f_0, …, f_r/f_i) (Tau Ceti's `spaLocalizationHomeomorph`), and these cover Spa(A_K, A_K°)
because the f_i generate the unit ideal of A_K (`spa_eq_biUnion_rationalSubset_of_span_eq_top`); hence
d(Bl_𝒜 X) → d(X) is an isomorphism.

*Node* `AdicSpacesPartII:R2/generic-fibre-inverts-admissible-blow-ups` (lemma), module `TauCeti/AlgebraicGeometry/FormalScheme/AdmissibleBlowUp`.

Hypotheses: 𝒜 coherent and open (ϖ^N ∈ 𝒜); X admissible.

Acceptance: For 𝒜 = (T, ϖ) on Spf O_K⟨T⟩ the charts have generic fibres {|T| ≤ |ϖ|} and {|ϖ| ≤ |T| ≤ 1}, which cover the closed unit disc (Conrad, Several approaches, Exercise 3.3.12).

**Adjoining bounded functions.** For A admissible and f_i ∈ A_K°, B = A[f_1, …, f_n] is admissible, finite
over A, and Spf B → Spf A is the admissible blow-up of (ϖ^r, ϖ^r f_i) (Bosch–Lütkebohmert I 4.5).

**Quasi-compact opens come from formal opens after blow-up** (Bosch–Lütkebohmert I 4.4). In the adic
language, quasi-compact opens of Spa(A_K, A_K°) are finite unions of rational subsets, so the rigid
input 4.2 (Gerritzen–Grauert) is not needed; each rational subset is a chart of the blow-up of its
defining functions.

*Node* `AdicSpacesPartII:R2/quasi-compact-opens-from-blow-ups` (lemma), module `TauCeti/AlgebraicGeometry/FormalScheme/AdmissibleBlowUp`.

Hypotheses: X quasi-compact admissible; U_i quasi-compact opens of the adic space d(X).

Acceptance: U = {|T| ≥ |ϖ|} ⊆ d(Spf O_K⟨T⟩) is d of the chart Spf O_K⟨T,V⟩/(TV − ϖ) of the blow-up of (T, ϖ). Non-example: the open unit disc {|T| < 1} is not quasi-compact and is d of no open formal subscheme of any admissible blow-up.

**Affinoids have formal models**: B = K⟨ξ⟩/b is A_K for A = O_K⟨ξ⟩/(b ∩ O_K⟨ξ⟩).

*Node* `AdicSpacesPartII:R2/affinoid-admissible-model` (lemma), module `TauCeti/AlgebraicGeometry/FormalScheme/Raynaud`.

Hypotheses: B a quotient of a Tate algebra K⟨ξ⟩ (K complete of rank one).

Acceptance: For B = K⟨ξ⟩/(ξ² − c) with c ∈ K, |c| ≤ 1, A = O_K⟨ξ⟩/(ξ² − c).

**Raynaud's theorem** (planet *Raynaud's theorem*). The functor X ↦ X_rig (equivalently X ↦ d(X)) induces an
equivalence

```text
{quasi-compact admissible formal O_K-schemes}[admissible blow-ups⁻¹]
      ≃ {quasi-compact quasi-separated rigid K-spaces}
      ≃ {quasi-compact quasi-separated adic spaces locally of finite type over Spa(K, O_K)},
```

with (a) blow-ups inverted, (b) faithfulness through rig-points, (c) morphisms of generic fibres realised
after blowing up the source, (d) isomorphisms realised by common blow-ups, (e) existence of formal
models by induction on affinoid covers, and Hom in the localised category computed as a colimit over
admissible blow-ups (calculus of fractions). No discreteness of K is assumed. The open unit disc is
quasi-separated but not quasi-compact and has no quasi-compact formal model.

*Node* `AdicSpacesPartII:R2/raynaud-theorem` (theorem), module `TauCeti/AlgebraicGeometry/FormalScheme/Raynaud`.

Hypotheses: K complete, nontrivial rank one; O_K may be non-noetherian; Quasi-compactness of formal models and quasi-compactness plus quasi-separatedness of rigid spaces are necessary: X ↦ X_rig produces only quasi-separated spaces, and the open unit disc has no quasi-compact formal model.

Acceptance: The closed annulus {|ϖ| ≤ |T| ≤ 1} (qcqs) has the formal model Spf O_K⟨T, V⟩/(TV − ϖ); the closed disc has models Spf O_K⟨T⟩ and its blow-up at (T, ϖ), which become isomorphic in the localised category. The rigid projective line has formal models P̂¹_{O_K} and all its admissible blow-ups; morphisms between rigid projective lines of degree d are realised on suitable blow-ups. Non-example: the open unit disc is quasi-separated but not quasi-compact, and has no quasi-compact admissible formal model.


#### R2.6 Separatedness, flattening, quasi-finite models and finiteness criteria

**Separatedness is detected on the generic fibre** (Bosch–Lütkebohmert I 4.7): the schematic closure of
the rigid diagonal is admissible by the finiteness lemma and equals the diagonal on closed points by
rig-points.

*Node* `AdicSpacesPartII:R2/formal-model-separatedness` (lemma), module `TauCeti/AlgebraicGeometry/FormalScheme/Raynaud`.

Hypotheses: X, Y admissible over a complete rank-one O_K; The adic reformulation uses Huber's comparison of separatedness for rigid and adic morphisms (R1/proper-separated-comparisons).

Acceptance: The ϖ-adic completion of the affine line with doubled origin in the special fibre only (glue two copies of Spf O_K⟨T⟩ along the formal open Spf O_K⟨T, T⁻¹⟩) is not separated, and its generic fibre (two closed discs glued along the annulus {|T| = 1}) is not separated either.

**Properness comparison** (Huber 1996 Remark 1.3.18). For flat formal models over O_K: d(f) separated ⟺ f
separated; d(f) proper ⟺ f proper; d(f) partially proper ⟺ f is proper on every irreducible component of
the special fibre. Huber quotes the non-public [Hu4]; the non-discrete properness input is Temkin's; the
proofs are recorded as obligations.

*Node* `AdicSpacesPartII:R2/formal-rigid-properness-comparison` (comparison), module `TauCeti/AlgebraicGeometry/FormalScheme/Raynaud`.

Hypotheses: X, Y flat and locally of finite type over Spf O_K, K complete of rank one, discreteness not assumed; Huber states the remark quoting [Hu4, 3.11, 3.13] (not public); the rigid-analytic 'f proper ⇒ f_rig proper' without discreteness is Temkin [Te, Cor. 4.4, 4.5], and the discretely valued case is Lütkebohmert [L1] — none read.

Acceptance: P̂¹_{O_K} → Spf O_K is proper and P^{1,ad}_K → Spa(K, O_K) is proper. Spf O_K⟨T⟩ → Spf O_K is not proper (special fibre A¹_k) and the closed unit disc is not proper over Spa(K, O_K) (it is not partially proper). Mumford's formal model of G_m for the Tate curve (an infinite chain of P¹_k's in the special fibre, each component proper) has partially proper generic fibre G_m^{ad}, as (iii) predicts.

**Flattening** (Bosch–Lütkebohmert II Theorem 5.2, from the module version Theorem 4.1): if f_rig is flat
(in dimension ≥ n), some admissible blow-up of the target makes the strict transform flat (in dimension
≥ n). Example: for X = Spf O_K⟨ζ, ξ⟩/(ζξ − ϖ) → Spf O_K⟨ζ⟩ (an open immersion of the annulus into the
disc on generic fibres, not flat formally), blowing up (ζ, ϖ) makes the strict transform an open
immersion. It is the case ℳ = O_X of the module flattening theorem, whose proof is decomposed in R2.6.1.

*Node* `AdicSpacesPartII:R2/flattening-by-blow-up` (theorem), module `TauCeti/AlgebraicGeometry/FormalScheme/Flattening`.

Hypotheses: X, Y quasi-compact admissible over Spf O_K; f_rig flat (resp. flat in dimension ≥ n) in the sense of rig-flatness at rig-points; The blow-up is of Y (the target), and X' is the strict transform, not the total transform; Classical rigid case: the base is Spf O_K; Bosch–Lütkebohmert's noetherian base case (II) is proved by parallel noetherian arguments that are not decomposed here.

**Quasi-finite and bounded-fibre-dimension models** (Bosch–Lütkebohmert II Corollary 5.3).

*Node* `AdicSpacesPartII:R2/quasi-finite-formal-model` (lemma), module `TauCeti/AlgebraicGeometry/FormalScheme/Flattening`.

locally constant rank implies finite — with no noetherian or quasi-compactness hypothesis.

formal model (the three previous nodes) and rig-points. Quasi-compactness and separatedness are both
necessary.

Conrad applies it to show that the multiplication maps defining canonical subgroups over the Hasse loci are finite (genpaper, proof of Theorem 4.1.3).

reduced spaces.

#### R2.6.1 The proof of flattening (Bosch–Lütkebohmert II §§1–4)

The flattening theorem is proved in the classical rigid case: the base is Spf O_K for a complete rank-one K, not necessarily
discretely valued; formal schemes are locally of tf presentation, X_λ = X ⊗ O_K/ϖ^{λ+1}, and fibres over t ∈ T_0 are
X ⊗ k(t) = X_0 ×_{T_0} Spec k(t). The proof has four stages: lifting from the reduction (§1), ideals of coefficients
over smooth morphisms with geometrically irreducible fibres (§2), dévissages and flatness criteria (§3), and the
flattening induction (§4). Raynaud–Gruson's scheme-theoretic results that Bosch–Lütkebohmert import were read and are
nodes when they are statements (1.1.1–1.1.3, 3.3.1, 5.4.2–5.4.3, and the formal form of 5.1.5), and proof templates
when Bosch–Lütkebohmert copy their proofs (1.2.3 for 3.3; 2.1–2.3 and 2.2 for 3.5–3.6; 2.9 for 3.8). Propositions 3.10,
3.11 (semicontinuity of rig-dimension, closedness of the non-rig-flat locus), 3.4 and 3.15 are not on the path to
Theorem 4.1 and get no node; the notion of purity (Definition 1.6, Examples 1.7) is avoided by specialising 1.8(b)
to smooth morphisms with geometrically irreducible fibres, the only case the proof uses.

**Lifting from the reduction** (§1). A family of sections generating modulo ϖ generates topologically, and a basis modulo
ϖ of a flat module is a topological basis (Nakayama on the powers of ϖ, completeness of finite modules over tfp
algebras). Smooth morphisms of the reduction lift after shrinking (lift a Jacobian presentation), and so do
factorisations through them (Mathlib's lifting of formally smooth algebras into adically complete rings); étale ones
lift uniquely. Stalk maps to generisations are flat (Bosch–Lütkebohmert I 1.8(b)).

*Node* `AdicSpacesPartII:R2/topological-generation-mod-definition-ideal` (lemma), module `TauCeti/AlgebraicGeometry/FormalScheme/Flattening/Lifting`.

Hypotheses: f affine; X and Y locally of tf presentation over O_K; Generation is required modulo ϖ (the ideal of definition), not modulo m_K; E may be infinite; the conclusion is topological generation, not generation.

Acceptance: Y = Spf O_K, X = Spf O_K⟨ζ⟩, ℳ = O_X, E = {ζ^i : i ≥ 0}: E generates (O_K/ϖ)[ζ] modulo ϖ, and every g ∈ O_K⟨ζ⟩ is Σ c_i ζ^i with c_i → 0. Topological generation cannot be replaced by generation: Σ_i ϖ^i ζ^i ∈ O_K⟨ζ⟩ is not a finite O_K-linear combination of the ζ^i.

*Node* `AdicSpacesPartII:R2/topological-basis-lifting` (lemma), module `TauCeti/AlgebraicGeometry/FormalScheme/Flattening/Lifting`.

Hypotheses: ℳ flat over O_Y; E induces a basis (not only a generating family) modulo ϖ.

Acceptance: X = Spf O_K⟨ζ⟩ over Y = Spf O_K: {ζ^i : i ≥ 0} is a topological basis of O_K⟨ζ⟩ (restricted power series have unique coefficients). Flatness is needed: for Y = X = Spf O_K, ℳ = O_K/ϖ and E = {1}, E is a basis modulo ϖ but φ: O_K → O_K/ϖ is not injective.

*Node* `AdicSpacesPartII:R2/smooth-lifting-from-level-zero` (lemma), module `TauCeti/AlgebraicGeometry/FormalScheme/Flattening/Lifting`.

Hypotheses: h_0 smooth at y; The lift is not unique; only its existence after shrinking is claimed.

Acceptance: T = Spf O_K and Y_0 = V(ξ_2 − ξ_1²) ⊆ A²_{O_K/ϖ}: Y = Spf O_K⟨ξ_1, ξ_2⟩/(ξ_2 − ξ_1²) ≅ Spf O_K⟨ξ_1⟩ is smooth of relative dimension 1. Étale case r = 0: a standard étale Y_0 = Spec (A_0[ξ]/(p̄))_{ḡ} lifts to the étale formal Y = Spf (A⟨ξ⟩/(p))⟨g⁻¹⟩.

*Node* `AdicSpacesPartII:R2/smooth-lifting-of-diagrams` (lemma), module `TauCeti/AlgebraicGeometry/FormalScheme/Flattening/Lifting`.

Hypotheses: h_0 smooth (resp. étale); Shrinking is needed in the smooth case only.

Acceptance: Étale case with h_0 = id: the lift is Y = T, h = id and g = f, uniquely. Non-uniqueness in the smooth case: for Y_0 = A¹_{T_0} → T_0 and g_0 given by a section s̄ ∈ Γ(X_0, O), lifts g correspond to lifts s ∈ Γ(X, O_X) of s̄, and s + ϖc is another lift.

*Node* `AdicSpacesPartII:R2/formal-stalk-generization-flat` (lemma), module `TauCeti/AlgebraicGeometry/FormalScheme/Flattening/Lifting`.

Hypotheses: X locally of tf presentation over O_K; stalks are the colimits of Γ(U, O_X) over open neighbourhoods, without completion.

Acceptance: X = Spf O_K⟨ζ⟩, x the point ζ = 0 of X_0 and y the generic point of X_0: O_{X,x} → O_{X,y} is flat, a colimit of the flat maps O_K⟨ζ⟩⟨g⁻¹⟩ → O_K⟨ζ⟩⟨(gh)⁻¹⟩.

**Local structure** (Raynaud–Gruson I 1.1.1–1.1.3 and Bosch–Lütkebohmert II 1.5). After elementary étale localisation
of source and target, a morphism locally of finite type factors as a finite morphism, with a single point over the
marked point, followed by a smooth morphism with geometrically integral fibres of the fibre dimension at the point:

```text
   (X, x) ←u— (X', x') —g→ (Z', z') —h→ (T', t') —v→ (T, t),   u, v elementary étale, g finite, h smooth with
                                                                 geometrically irreducible fibres of dimension dim_x(X ⊗ k(t)).
```

For schemes this is Zariski's Main Theorem in étale-local form (Mathlib has it for separated morphisms over étale, not
necessarily elementary, neighbourhoods); the formal version lifts it from the reduction.

*Node* `AdicSpacesPartII:R2/rg-etale-neighbourhood-irreducible` (lemma), module `TauCeti/AlgebraicGeometry/Morphisms/ZariskiLocalStructure`.

Hypotheses: Z geometrically normal and of finite type over k; Elementary: k(t) = k(z); T connected.

Acceptance: Z = A¹_k, z its generic point, T = A¹_k ∖ {0}: T is geometrically irreducible. The residue condition is needed: for k = ℝ, Z = Spec ℝ and T = Spec ℂ (connected, étale, k(t) ≠ k(z)), T ⊗_ℝ ℂ = Spec(ℂ × ℂ) is not irreducible.

*Node* `AdicSpacesPartII:R2/rg-geometrically-integral-fibres-etale-locally` (lemma), module `TauCeti/AlgebraicGeometry/Morphisms/ZariskiLocalStructure`.

Hypotheses: T → S smooth; Only the fibre over s is assumed geometrically integral.

Acceptance: If all fibres of T → S are geometrically integral (for instance T = A^n_S), one can take S' = S and U' = T. Shrinking is needed: over S = Spec k[u], T = A¹_S ⊔ A¹_{D(u)} is smooth with geometrically integral fibre over s = (u) but two-component fibres over u ≠ 0; U' = A¹_S works and U' ≠ T.

*Node* `AdicSpacesPartII:R2/rg-zariski-local-structure` (theorem), module `TauCeti/AlgebraicGeometry/Morphisms/ZariskiLocalStructure`.

Hypotheses: X locally of finite type over S (no noetherian hypothesis); Elementary étale: trivial residue field extension at the marked points.

Acceptance: X = S: n = 0 and one can take Y = T = S' an affine open neighbourhood of s. X = A^n_S: T = X restricted to an affine open neighbourhood, Y = T. X = Spec k[a, b]/(b² − a³) over S = Spec k at the cusp: n = 1, T = A¹_k with coordinate a, and Y → T finite of degree 2 with a single point over a = 0.

*Node* `AdicSpacesPartII:R2/formal-zariski-local-structure` (theorem), module `TauCeti/AlgebraicGeometry/FormalScheme/Flattening/Lifting`.

Hypotheses: f locally of tf presentation; no flatness assumption; The dimension is that of the fibre of the reduction at x.

Acceptance: If f is smooth at x with geometrically irreducible fibre of dimension d, take X' = Z' and g = id locally. f: X = Spf O_K⟨ζ, ξ⟩/(ζξ − ϖ) → T = Spf O_K⟨ζ⟩ at x = (ζ, ξ): d = 1 (the fibre over ζ = 0 is the ξ-line), and one may take Z' = D¹_T = Spf O_K⟨ζ, ξ⟩, g the closed immersion and h the projection, without étale localisation.

**Topological bases** (Raynaud–Gruson I 3.3.1, Bosch–Lütkebohmert II 1.8(b)). A smooth algebra with geometrically integral
fibres is a projective module; over a connected noetherian base it is then free, locally (finitely generated case) or
globally (Bass); lifting a basis gives, locally on T, a topological basis of B over A for every smooth surjective
Spf B → Spf A with geometrically irreducible fibres.

*Node* `AdicSpacesPartII:R2/rg-smooth-geometrically-integral-projective` (lemma), module `TauCeti/RingTheory/Smooth/Projective`.

Hypotheses: A arbitrary (no noetherian hypothesis); Every fibre geometrically integral (empty fibres excluded).

Acceptance: B = A[t_1, …, t_n]: free on the monomials. B = A[t, t⁻¹]: free on the t^k, k ∈ ℤ. The fibre hypothesis is needed: B = k[u, u⁻¹] over A = k[u] is smooth with empty fibre over u = 0, and is not a projective k[u]-module (a projective module over a principal ideal domain is free, and k[u, u⁻¹] is u-divisible).

*Node* `AdicSpacesPartII:R2/smooth-geometrically-irreducible-topological-basis` (lemma), module `TauCeti/AlgebraicGeometry/FormalScheme/Flattening/Lifting`.

Hypotheses: h smooth and surjective, fibres geometrically irreducible of one dimension m; The basis exists locally on T, possibly infinite.

Acceptance: B = A⟨ζ_1, …, ζ_m⟩: the monomials ζ^ν form a topological basis. B = A⟨ζ, ζ⁻¹⟩: the ζ^k, k ∈ ℤ, form a topological basis. m = 0: fibres Spec k(t) force Z_0 → T_0 to be an isomorphism locally, with basis {1}.

**Ideals of coefficients** (§2). For Z → T and a coherent ideal 𝒥 ⊆ O_Z, the ideal of coefficients is the
smallest coherent 𝒞 ⊆ O_T with 𝒥 ⊆ 𝒞O_Z, universally; its zero locus is the set of points whose fibre lies in V(𝒥).
With a topological basis (e_i) and generators f_j = Σ a_{ij}e_i it is (a_{ij}): for f = a_0 + a_1ξ + … + a_nξ^n ∈ A⟨ξ⟩
the content is (a_0, …, a_n). Open ideals always have (open) ideals of coefficients along smooth morphisms with
geometrically irreducible fibres; on generic fibres every ideal has a rigid ideal of coefficients, and a coherent ideal
whose rigid ideal of coefficients is the unit ideal has an open one. Over a height-one valuation ring contents are
principal and multiplicative (Gauss's lemma), which, applied at rig-points, shows that fibres over the generic fibre are
integral with generic point pB, and that the associated primes of B are these generic points.

*Node* `AdicSpacesPartII:R2/ideal-of-coefficients` (definition), module `TauCeti/AlgebraicGeometry/FormalScheme/Flattening/Coefficients`.

API:

- `FormalScheme.IsIdealOfCoefficients` (structure): For h: Z → T and coherent 𝒥 ⊆ O_Z, 𝒞 ⊆ O_T: conditions (i) and (ii) of Definition 2.1.
- `FormalScheme.IsIdealOfCoefficients.unique` (extensionality): Two ideals of coefficients of 𝒥 are equal.
- `FormalScheme.IsIdealOfCoefficients.le_map` (characterisation): 𝒥 ⊆ 𝒞O_Z, and 𝒞 ⊆ 𝒞' for every coherent 𝒞' ⊆ O_T with 𝒥O_{Z'} ⊆ 𝒞'O_{Z'} after every base change.
- `FormalScheme.IsIdealOfCoefficients.baseChange` (functoriality): For T' → T, 𝒞O_{T'} is an ideal of coefficients of 𝒥O_{Z ×_T T'}.
- `FormalScheme.IsIdealOfCoefficients.restrict` (compatibility): Restriction to an open U ⊆ T and to h⁻¹(U) preserves ideals of coefficients.
- `FormalScheme.IsIdealOfCoefficients.glue` (other): Ideals of coefficients existing on the members of an open cover of T glue to an ideal of coefficients on T (by uniqueness).
- `FormalScheme.IsIdealOfCoefficients.mem_zeroLocus_iff` (characterisation): For t ∈ T_0: t ∈ V(𝒞) iff Z ⊗ k(t) ⊆ V(𝒥); for a rig-point t of T: t factors through V(𝒞) iff the rigid fibre over t lies in V(𝒥).
- `FormalScheme.IsIdealOfCoefficients.isOpen` (other): Remark 2.2: if 𝒥 is open and h is faithfully flat then 𝒞 is open.
- `FormalScheme.isIdealOfCoefficients_of_topologicalBasis` (constructor): Affine formula: with a topological basis (e_i) of B over A and b = (f_1, …, f_r), the coordinate ideal a = (a_{ij}) is the ideal of coefficients when finitely generated.
- `FormalScheme.content` (data): c(f) ⊆ A, the ideal of coefficients of fB for f ∈ B, when it exists.
- `FormalScheme.content_polynomial` (example): For f = Σ a_i ξ^i ∈ A[ξ] ⊆ A⟨ξ⟩: c(f) = (a_0, …, a_n).

Unit tests:

- `idealOfCoefficients_test_polynomial` (computation): Over A = O_K and B = O_K⟨ξ⟩, the content of f = ϖ² + ϖξ + ϖ³ξ² is (ϖ).
- `idealOfCoefficients_test_unit` (degenerate): For h surjective, the ideal of coefficients of 𝒥 = O_Z is O_T; for h faithfully flat and 𝒥 = 𝒜O_Z with 𝒜 ⊆ O_T coherent, it is 𝒜.
- `idealOfCoefficients_test_baseChange` (compatibility): For Z = Spf O_K⟨a, ζ⟩ → T = Spf O_K⟨a⟩ and 𝒥 = (aζ, ϖ): 𝒞 = (a, ϖ); after the base change a ↦ 0 to T' = Spf O_K, 𝒥' = (ϖ) and 𝒞' = (ϖ) = 𝒞O_{T'}.
- `idealOfCoefficients_test_notZeroLocus` (non-example): For A = O_K⟨a⟩, B = A⟨ζ⟩ and 𝒥 = (a²ζ, ϖ), (a², ϖ) is the ideal of coefficients and (a, ϖ) is not, although both have the same zero locus: a definition by the set of t with Z ⊗ k(t) ⊆ V(𝒥) fails.

Acceptance: Z = Spf A⟨ξ⟩ → T = Spf A and f = a_0 + a_1ξ + … + a_nξ^n ∈ A[ξ]: c(f) = (a_0, …, a_n) (Bosch–Lütkebohmert II Example 5.1). For A = O_K⟨a⟩, B = A⟨ζ⟩ and 𝒥 = (a²ζ, ϖ): 𝒞 = (a², ϖ).

Acceptance: A = O_K⟨a⟩ and B = A⟨ζ⟩: the only associated prime of B is (0) = (0)B.

**Dévissages and flatness** (§3). A T-dévissage in dimension n of ℳ at x is a finite g: Y → Z with y the only point over
z, Z → T smooth with geometrically irreducible fibres of dimension n, and α: O_Z^ℓ → g_*ℳ bijective at the generic
point ζ of the fibre; its cokernel has smaller fibre dimension, and iterating gives dévissages in dimensions
N = n¹ > … > n^r, complete when the last cokernel vanishes. Complete dévissages exist after elementary étale
localisation. Flatness at x is read off the dévissage (Proposition 3.5):

```text
   ℳ_x flat over O_{T,t}  ⟺  every α^i is injective at z^i and 𝒫^r is flat at z^r
                          ⟺  every α^i is bijective at the generic point ζ^i and 𝒫^r is flat at z^r,
```

so the flat locus is open, and flatness in dimension ≥ n (the non-flat locus meets fibres in dimension < n) is
characterised by the α^i alone (Corollary 3.8).

**Rig-flatness and Fitting ideals** (§3). ℳ is rig-flat at a rig-point x if the localisation M_x is flat over the base;
it is rig-flat in dimension ≥ n if this holds off a closed subscheme whose rigid fibres have dimension ≤ n − 1. On a
smooth Z → T with geometrically irreducible fibres of dimension m, rig-flatness in dimension ≥ m above a rig-point t is
freeness of N_ζ at the generic point ζ = tB. Fitting ideals of coherent modules on formal schemes glue the ring-level
Fitting ideal (owned by StableReduction Layer 0); if F_r(M) is invertible and M is free of rank r at the associated
points of A, then M/Ann_M(F_r(M)) is locally free of rank r (Raynaud–Gruson 5.4.3, Bosch–Lütkebohmert's Lemma 3.14);
Example 4.3 is its diagonal case over a principal ideal domain.

**The flattening induction** (§4). In the smooth case with geometrically irreducible fibres (Special case 4.4), make the
generic rank r constant by an admissible blow-up realising an open and closed partition of the generic fibre (formal form
of Raynaud–Gruson 5.1.5), blow up the open ideal of coefficients a of F_r(M), and divide out the a-power torsion: the
strict transform is free at the generic points of the special fibres, hence flat in dimension ≥ m. In general, a
dévissage of ℳ at a generic point of the m-dimensional non-flat locus has universally injective α^i above dimension m
(Lemma 4.6), strict transforms of dévissages are dévissages (Lemma 4.5), and flattening its last module by the special
case flattens ℳ there (Lemma 4.7). Noetherian induction on the flat locus in T_0 gives Proposition 4.2, and descending
induction on m gives Theorem 4.1:

```text
   ℳ rig-flat over T in dimension ≥ n   ⟹   ∃ admissible blow-up T' → T with the strict transform of ℳ on X ×_T T'
                                             T'-flat in dimension ≥ n.
```

Example: for X = Spf O_K⟨ζ, ξ⟩/(ζξ − ϖ) → T = Spf O_K⟨ζ⟩ one blows up (ζ, ϖ), the open ideal of coefficients of
F_0 = (ζξ − ϖ).

If A_K has no non-trivial idempotents (k = 1), 𝒥 = A and T' = T.
