#### R2.7 Formal completions of schemes and the good-reduction locus

**Huber 1.9.4–1.9.6.** For f: X → Y locally of finite type and completions along a finite-type Y' with Ŷ of
type (S), φ: d(X̂) → X ×_Y d(Ŷ) is a local isomorphism, injective if f is separated, surjective if f is
universally specializing. The source says 'One can easily prove'; the node supplies the proofs (charts
{|T_i| ≤ 1} of the analytification, valuative criteria of separatedness and universal closedness).

*Node* `AdicSpacesPartII:R2/formal-completion-and-algebraic-comparison` (comparison), module `TauCeti/AlgebraicGeometry/FormalScheme/AlgebraicComparison`.

Hypotheses: X̂ (resp. Ŷ) of type (S); the ideal defining Y' of finite type; f locally of finite type; (ii) requires f separated; (iii) requires f universally specializing; σ and the fibre product X ×_Y d(Ŷ) come from Huber 1994 [Hu, 4.6.iv], [Hu4, 3.10.7] and [Hu, 3.8]; [Hu4] is not public.

Acceptance: For X = A¹_{O_K} → Y = Spec O_K (not proper), φ identifies d(X̂) with the closed unit disc inside the adic affine line over Spa(K, O_K): a local isomorphism which is injective but not surjective. For X proper over Y, d(X̂) ≅ X ×_Y d(Ŷ).

**The good-reduction locus.** For X separated and locally of finite type over O_K, d(X̂) → X_K^ad is an
open embedding onto

```text
X_K^{ad,int} = { x ∈ X_K^ad : Spec κ(x) → X extends to Spec κ(x)⁺ → X },
```

and an isomorphism when X is proper. λ(x) is the image of the closed point of that extension; a classical
point is integral iff it extends to an O_{K'}-point. Examples: A¹ gives the closed unit disc, G_m the
unit circle {|T| = 1}, P^n all of P^{n,ad}_K.

*Node* `AdicSpacesPartII:R2/good-reduction-locus` (theorem), module `TauCeti/AlgebraicGeometry/FormalScheme/AlgebraicComparison`.

Hypotheses: X separated and locally of finite type over O_K; K complete, nontrivial rank one, discreteness not assumed; X_K^ad is Huber's fibre product X ×_{Spec O_K} Spa(K, O_K) (R1); The converse 'image = X_K^ad implies proper' needs flatness and is node good-reduction-locus-properness-converse.

Acceptance: X = A¹_{O_K}: the image is the closed unit disc {|T| ≤ 1} ⊂ A^{1,ad}_K (not all of it). X = G_{m,O_K} = Spec O_K[T, T⁻¹]: the image is {|T| = 1}. X = P¹_{O_K}: φ is an isomorphism d(P̂¹) ≅ P^{1,ad}_K; more generally for P = P̂ⁿ, P_K ≅ P^{n,ad}_K (PadicDifferentialEquationsAndRigidCohomology request). For a smooth proper curve X over O_K (K finite over Q_p), d(X̂) = X_K^ad and λ is the specialisation to X_k (ColemanIntegration request).

**Converse.** For X flat and quasi-projective over O_K, d(X̂) = X_K^ad forces X proper: compactify in
P^N, use rig-points over the missing special-fibre points and the fact that a dense Zariski open has
dense analytification (R1's compatibility of closures with analytification), so a nowhere dense
Zariski closed subset has analytification with empty interior. Flatness is necessary: Spec O_K ⊔ A¹_{O_K/ϖ} has φ an isomorphism and is not
proper. General separated X needs Nagata over O_K (AdicCoefficientsAndComparisons L2) and is not
claimed.

*Node* `AdicSpacesPartII:R2/good-reduction-locus-properness-converse` (lemma), module `TauCeti/AlgebraicGeometry/FormalScheme/AlgebraicComparison`.

Hypotheses: X quasi-projective over O_K (for general separated X of finite type the compactification step needs Nagata's theorem over O_K, which this roadmap does not own); X flat over O_K.

Acceptance: X = P¹_{O_K} minus a closed point x of the special fibre: φ_X has image P^{1,ad}_K ∖ ]x[ ≠ X_K^ad, and X is not proper — consistent with the lemma. X = Bl_x(P¹_{O_K}) ∖ (strict transform of P¹_k) has proper generic and special fibres, is flat and separated, but is not proper; its φ_X has image the residue disc ]x[ ≠ P^{1,ad}_K, as the lemma predicts.


#### R2.8 Conrad's FS_C, smooth formal schemes, étale sites, Frobenius lifts and residue discs

**Conrad's Berthelot-type functor** (Theorem 3.1.5): for C adic noetherian with C → O_k continuous and k
arbitrary, X ↦ X^rig on FS_C represents Hom^cont_C(·, X); Spf(C[[q]])^rig is the open unit disc; the
functor preserves immersions, fibre products, base field and coefficient changes, separatedness, and by
Theorem 3.1.6 finiteness, smoothness, properness, flatness and fibre dimension.

*Node* `AdicSpacesPartII:R2/berthelot-type-rig-functor-nonnoetherian-base` (construction), module `TauCeti/AlgebraicGeometry/FormalScheme/BerthelotGenericFibre`.

API:

- `FormalScheme.FSC` (structure): Locally noetherian formal schemes over Spf C with reduced scheme locally of finite type over C_red.
- `FormalScheme.rigOfFSC` (constructor): X ↦ X^rig.
- `FormalScheme.rigOfFSC.homEquiv` (universal-property): Hom_k(Z, X^rig) ≃ Hom^cont_C(Z, X), naturally in the rigid space Z.
- `FormalScheme.rigOfFSC_isOpenImmersion` (functoriality): Open (resp. closed) immersions go to open (resp. closed) immersions and open covers to admissible covers.
- `FormalScheme.rigOfFSC_pullback` (compatibility): (X ×_Y Z)^rig ≅ X^rig ×_{Y^rig} Z^rig (3.1.5(a)).
- `FormalScheme.rigOfFSC_baseChangeField` (compatibility): k' ⊗̂_k X^rig_{/k} ≅ X^rig_{/k'} for an analytic extension k'/k (3.1.5(b)).
- `FormalScheme.rigOfFSC_changeCoefficients` (compatibility): X^rig ≅ (Spf C' ×_{Spf C} X)^rig for C → C' compatible with the maps to R (3.1.5(c)).
- `FormalScheme.rigOfFSC_isSeparated` (other): f separated ⇒ f^rig separated (3.1.5(d)).
- `FormalScheme.rigOfFSC_quasiCompact` (other): f topologically of finite type ⇒ f^rig quasi-compact (3.1.5(e)).
- `FormalScheme.rigOfFSC_powerSeries` (example): Spf(C[[q]])^rig ≅ Δ, the open unit disc.
- `FormalScheme.rigOfFSC_preserves` (other): For f locally topologically of finite type: finite ⇒ finite; formally smooth of pure relative dimension d ⇒ smooth of pure relative dimension d (formally étale ⇒ étale); finite flat of rank d ⇒ same; proper ⇒ proper; (faithfully) flat ⇒ (faithfully) flat; fibre dimension ≤ d ⇒ same; flat with geometrically reduced fibres of pure dimension d ⇒ same (Theorem 3.1.6).
- `FormalScheme.rigOfFSC_eq_genericFibre` (compatibility): For k discretely valued and C = R, r(X^rig) ≅ d(X) = t(X)_a for X in FS_R, compatibly with specialisation (de Jong 7.2.4; Huber 1994 Remark 4.6(ii) for X topologically of finite type).

Unit tests:

- `rigOfFSC_test_powerSeries` (computation): For C = Z (discrete) and any k, Spf(Z[[q]])^rig is the open unit disc Δ = {|t| < 1} over k, admissibly covered by the closed discs {|t| ≤ r}.
- `rigOfFSC_test_nondiscrete` (non-example): For k = C_p, Spf O_k⟨T⟩ is not an object of FS_C for any C (it is not locally noetherian); its generic fibre is given by Raynaud's functor instead.
- `rigOfFSC_test_restricted` (compatibility): For k discretely valued and C = R, Spf R{{T}}^rig is the closed unit disc, equal to Raynaud's generic fibre of Spf R⟨T⟩.
- `rigOfFSC_test_point` (degenerate): Spf(C)^rig = Sp(k), the final object of rigid spaces over k.

Acceptance: Spf(Z[[q]])^rig over any k (C = Z discrete) is the open unit disc over k. When k is discretely valued and C = R the functor recovers de Jong's [deJ, 7.2.4, 7.2.6].

**Smooth formal schemes** (`FormalScheme.IsSmooth`). Bosch–Lütkebohmert II Definition 1.1 (local Jacobian
presentation in D^n_Y); equivalent to flatness plus smoothness of the special fibre, and to smoothness of
every level X_m → Y_m; locally étale over formal affine space; Ω¹ = lim Ω¹_{X_m/Y_m} locally free of rank
d. Smoothness is not detected on the generic fibre: Spf O_K⟨S,T⟩/(ST − ϖ) is not smooth.

*Node* `AdicSpacesPartII:R2/smooth-formal-scheme` (definition), module `TauCeti/AlgebraicGeometry/FormalScheme/Smooth`.

API:

- `FormalScheme.IsSmoothAt` (structure): Smoothness at x of relative dimension d via a local Jacobian presentation in D^n_Y.
- `FormalScheme.IsSmooth` (structure): Smooth at every point; FormalScheme.IsEtale is relative dimension 0.
- `FormalScheme.isSmoothAt_iff_flat_specialFibre` (characterisation): f is smooth at x of relative dimension d iff f is flat at x and f_0 is smooth at x of relative dimension d.
- `FormalScheme.isSmooth_iff_forall_level` (characterisation): f is smooth iff every f_m: X_m → Y_m is smooth (AlgebraicGeometry.Smooth).
- `FormalScheme.IsSmooth.exists_etale_affineSpace` (characterisation): If f is smooth of relative dimension d at x, there are an open U ∋ x and an étale U → D^d_Y over Y.
- `FormalScheme.kaehler` (data): Ω¹_{X/Y} = lim_m Ω¹_{X_m/Y_m}, a coherent O_X-module with continuous derivation d.
- `FormalScheme.IsSmooth.kaehler_locallyFree` (other): For f smooth of relative dimension d, Ω¹_{X/Y} is locally free of rank d, free on dT_i over an étale chart to D^d_Y.
- `FormalScheme.IsSmooth.isAdmissible` (instance): A formal scheme smooth over Spf O_K is admissible.
- `FormalScheme.IsSmooth.comp` (functoriality): Smooth morphisms are stable under composition and base change; étale ones likewise.
- `FormalScheme.IsSmooth.of_isEtale` (relation): If 𝔛 is smooth of relative dimension d over Spf O_K and 𝔜 → 𝔛 is étale, 𝔜 is smooth of relative dimension d and Ω¹_{𝔜/O_K} is the pullback of Ω¹_{𝔛/O_K}.
- `FormalScheme.IsSmooth.genericFibre` (compatibility): If f is smooth of relative dimension d then d(f) is smooth of relative dimension d (R0/smooth-morphism); if f is étale then d(f) is étale.
- `FormalScheme.IsEtale.lift_unique` (universal-property): For f étale, liftings along nilpotent thickenings of affine formal schemes exist and are unique (Algebra.FormallyEtale.iff_comp_bijective on each level).
- `FormalScheme.IsElementaryEtaleNbhd` (structure): An étale neighbourhood of x ∈ X_0 is an étale pointed morphism (X', x') → (X, x); it is elementary if moreover k(x') = k(x) (Bosch–Lütkebohmert II §1).

Unit tests:

- `smoothFormal_test_affineSpace` (computation): Spf O_K⟨T_1, …, T_d⟩ → Spf O_K is smooth of relative dimension d and Ω¹ is free with basis dT_1, …, dT_d.
- `smoothFormal_test_torus` (computation): The formal torus Spf W(κ)⟨T_1^{±1}, …, T_d^{±1}⟩ is smooth of relative dimension d over Spf W(κ).
- `smoothFormal_test_semistable` (non-example): Spf O_K⟨S,T⟩/(ST − ϖ) → Spf O_K is flat with smooth generic fibre but is not smooth: its special fibre k[S,T]/(ST) is singular at the origin.
- `smoothFormal_test_levels` (compatibility): For a smooth O_K-scheme X, the ϖ-adic completion X̂ is smooth over Spf O_K, and each X̂_m = X ⊗ O_K/ϖ^{m+1} is smooth in the sense of mathlib AlgebraicGeometry.Smooth.
- `smoothFormal_test_identity` (degenerate): id: Spf O_K → Spf O_K is étale (smooth of relative dimension 0) and Ω¹ = 0.

Acceptance: Spf O_K⟨T_1, …, T_d⟩ and the formal torus Spf O_K⟨T_1^{±1}, …, T_d^{±1}⟩ are smooth of relative dimension d with Ω¹ free on dT_i. Spf O_K⟨S,T⟩/(ST − ϖ) is flat, with smooth generic fibre (an annulus), but not smooth over Spf O_K.

**Étale sites.** 𝔛_ét ≃ (𝔛_0)_ét ≃ (𝔛_{s,red})_ét by topological invariance of the étale site (Stacks
039R/04DZ, EGA IV 18.1.2) at each level; and 𝔜 ↦ d(𝔜) is a continuous functor 𝔛_ét → d(𝔛)_ét
(generic fibres of étale formal morphisms are étale; coverings go to jointly surjective families).
PadicHodgeTheory builds w: X_proét → 𝔛_ét from this functor and AdicEtaleGeometry A1.

*Node* `AdicSpacesPartII:R2/formal-etale-site-invariance` (comparison), module `TauCeti/AlgebraicGeometry/FormalScheme/EtaleSite`.

Hypotheses: 𝔛 locally tfp over O_K (the same holds for adic noetherian formal schemes with an ideal of definition); The étale site of the adic space d(𝔛) is AdicEtaleGeometry A1's; the morphism of topoi w: X_proét → 𝔛_ét is built by the consumer from the functor of (b).

Acceptance: For 𝔛 = Spf Z_p⟨T⟩ the étale 𝔛-schemes correspond to étale F_p[T]-schemes; Spf Z_p⟨T, (T^{p−1} − 1)⁻¹⟩ corresponds to the open D(T^{p−1} − 1) ⊆ A¹_{F_p}. The finite étale cover Spf W(F_{p²}) → Spf Z_p corresponds to Spec F_{p²} → Spec F_p, and its generic fibre is Spa(Q_{p²}) → Spa(Q_p), finite étale of degree 2.

**Frobenius lifts.** On Spf R étale over the formal torus Spf W(κ)⟨T^{±1}⟩ there is a unique σ-semilinear
Frobenius lift with T_i ↦ T_i^p, obtained level by level from formal étaleness and p-adic completeness
(Tan–Tong Remark 2.20); a global lift need not exist.

*Node* `AdicSpacesPartII:R2/frobenius-lift-etale-over-torus` (lemma), module `TauCeti/AlgebraicGeometry/FormalScheme/FrobeniusLift`.

Hypotheses: κ perfect of characteristic p; R p-adically complete, étale (levelwise) over W⟨T^{±1}⟩; Uniqueness uses p-adic completeness and formal unramifiedness.

Acceptance: On the torus itself φ(Σ a_ν T^ν) = Σ σ(a_ν) T^{pν}. On 𝔛 = Spf W⟨T^{±1}, (T − 1)⁻¹⟩ (open in the torus), φ((T − 1)⁻¹) = (T^p − 1)⁻¹, which lies in R because T^p − 1 ≡ (T − 1)^p mod p is invertible.

**Residue discs.** For 𝔛 smooth of relative dimension d at a k-rational point x and local parameters t_i,
t: ]x[ → D^d_{<1} is an isomorphism onto the open unit polydisc; parameter changes are automorphisms
given by power series over O_K with invertible linear part (for curves, t' = u t (1 + h), |u| = 1,
|h| < 1, when t and t' vanish at a common point). Non-rational points give twisted discs that split
after an unramified extension. The proof (étale chart, closed tubes of radius |ϖ|^{1/m}, topological
invariance) works over any complete rank-one K.

*Node* `AdicSpacesPartII:R2/residue-disc` (lemma), module `TauCeti/AlgebraicGeometry/FormalScheme/ResidueDisc`.

Hypotheses: 𝔛 smooth over Spf O_K of relative dimension d near x (node smooth-formal-scheme); K complete of rank one; x a k-rational closed point for the isomorphism with D^d_{<1}.

Acceptance: 𝔛 = P̂¹_{O_K}, x = 0 ∈ P¹(k): ]x[ = {|T| < 1} with t = T; x = ∞: ]∞[ = {|T| > 1} with t = 1/T. For K discretely valued and a smooth proper curve X over O_K with x ∈ X_k(k), a local parameter at a lift of x identifies ]x[ with the open unit disc (ColemanIntegration request). Non-example: for K = Q_p and x ∈ P¹_{F_p} the closed point T² = 2 (p odd, 2 a non-square mod p), ]x[ has no Q_p-point and is not isomorphic to the open unit disc over Q_p; over Q_{p²} it splits into two open unit discs.


#### R2.9 Fractional bounds, section domains and Hasse domains

**Fractional bounds** (`ValuationSpectrum.fracPowLE`, `ValuationSpectrum.fracPowGE`). For q = a/b ∈ ℚ_{≥0}:

```text
|f| ≤ |g|^q  :⟺  v(f^b) ≤ v(g^a),        |f| ≥ |g|^q  :⟺  v(f^b) ≥ v(g^a),
```

independent of the representative (a, b). For g a unit these are the rational subsets R({f^b, g^a}/g^a)
and R({g^a, f^b}/f^b). If an explicit extension contains c with c^b = g^a·(unit), then |f| ≤ |g|^q iff
|f| ≤ |c| on its adic spectrum. Rounding the exponent, or assuming |p|^{1/2} ∈ |Q_p^×|, gives wrong sets.

*Node* `AdicSpacesPartII:R2/fractional-valuation-bound` (definition), module `TauCeti/AlgebraicGeometry/AdicSpace/Spa/FractionalBound`.

API:

- `ValuationSpectrum.fracPowLE` (constructor): {v ∈ Spv A : v(f^{q.den}) ≤ v(g^{q.num})}.
- `ValuationSpectrum.fracPowGE` (constructor): {v ∈ Spv A : v(f^{q.den}) ≥ v(g^{q.num})}.
- `ValuationSpectrum.mem_fracPowLE_iff` (characterisation): For every a ∈ ℕ, b ∈ ℕ_{>0} with q = a/b: v ∈ fracPowLE f g q ↔ v(f^b) ≤ v(g^a).
- `ValuationSpectrum.fracPowLE_natCast` (simp): fracPowLE f g n = {v : v(f) ≤ v(g^n)} for n ∈ ℕ.
- `ValuationSpectrum.fracPowLE_inter_spa` (compatibility): If g is a unit: fracPowLE f g q ∩ spa A⁺ = rationalSubset A⁺ {f^b, g^a} (g^a).
- `ValuationSpectrum.fracPowGE_inter_spa` (compatibility): If g is a unit: fracPowGE f g q ∩ spa A⁺ = rationalSubset A⁺ {g^a, f^b} (f^b).
- `ValuationSpectrum.fracPowLE_mono` (relation): On {v(g) ≤ 1}: q ≤ q' ⇒ fracPowLE f g q' ⊆ fracPowLE f g q and fracPowGE f g q ⊆ fracPowGE f g q'.
- `ValuationSpectrum.comap_fracPowLE` (functoriality): For φ: A → B: (Spv φ)⁻¹(fracPowLE f g q) = fracPowLE (φ f) (φ g) q.
- `ValuationSpectrum.fracPowLE_iff_of_pow_eq` (compatibility): If c^b = g^a u with u, u⁻¹ ∈ A⁺ and q = a/b, then for v ∈ spa A⁺: v ∈ fracPowLE f g q ↔ v(f) ≤ v(c).
- `ValuationSpectrum.fracPowGE_mul_unit` (relation): If u, u⁻¹ ∈ A⁺: fracPowGE (u f) g q ∩ spa A⁺ = fracPowGE f g q ∩ spa A⁺ (and likewise for LE).
- `ValuationSpectrum.fracPowLE_pow` (relation): fracPowLE (f^n) g (n q) = fracPowLE f g q for n > 0.
- `ValuationSpectrum.fracPowLE_mul` (relation): fracPowLE f g q ∩ fracPowLE f' g q' ⊆ fracPowLE (f f') g (q + q').

Unit tests:

- `fracPowLE_test_halfDisc` (computation): In Spa(Q_p⟨T⟩, Z_p⟨T⟩): fracPowLE T p (1/2) = {v : v(T²) ≤ v(p)}; the classical point T = p lies in it, the classical point T = 1 does not, and it contains no Q_p-rational point with |T| = p^{-1/2}.
- `fracPowLE_test_representative` (characterisation): fracPowLE f g (2/4) = fracPowLE f g (1/2) for all f, g: membership is v(f⁴) ≤ v(g²) iff v(f²) ≤ v(g).
- `fracPowLE_test_rounding` (non-example): Rounding the exponent down (|f| ≤ |g|^{⌊q⌋}) is a different set: for q = 1/2, f = T, g = p it gives the whole unit disc {|T| ≤ 1} ≠ {|T²| ≤ |p|}.
- `fracPowLE_test_root` (compatibility): For L = Q_p(√p) with c = √p (c² = p): the preimage of fracPowLE T p (1/2) in Spa(L⟨T⟩, O_L⟨T⟩) equals {v : v(T) ≤ v(c)}.
- `fracPowLE_test_zero` (degenerate): fracPowLE f g 0 = {v : v(f) ≤ 1} and fracPowGE f g 0 = {v : v(f) ≥ 1}.

Acceptance: {|T| ≤ |p|^{1/2}} ⊆ Spa(Q_p⟨T⟩, Z_p⟨T⟩) is {|T²| ≤ |p|}; its Q_p-rational points are those with |T| ≤ |p|, while its points over Q_p(√p) include T = √p. fracPowLE f g (2/4) = fracPowLE f g (1/2).

**Section domains** (`FormalScheme.sectionDomainGE`). For ℒ invertible on an admissible 𝔛, s ∈ Γ(𝔛, ℒ) and
q ≥ 0, 𝔛_η(|s| ≥ |ϖ|^q) is glued from fracPowGE(f_j, ϖ, q) over trivialisations s = f_j e_j. Independence
of generators: units of the formal model have absolute value one on the generic fibre. Independence of
lifts: s ≡ s' mod ϖ^c ℒ with c > q gives the same domain, so a section modulo ϖ^m (m > q) defines a
domain through arbitrary local lifts. For q = 0 the domain is the tube of the locus where s̄ generates.
The domain depends on the integral structure ℒ, not only on ℒ_η.

*Node* `AdicSpacesPartII:R2/section-valuation-domain` (construction), module `TauCeti/AlgebraicGeometry/FormalScheme/SectionDomain`.

API:

- `FormalScheme.sectionDomainGE` (constructor): 𝔛_η(|s| ≥ |ϖ|^q) ⊆ d(𝔛).
- `FormalScheme.sectionDomainLE` (constructor): 𝔛_η(|s| ≤ |ϖ|^q) ⊆ d(𝔛).
- `FormalScheme.sectionDomainGE_of_trivialization` (simp): On U = Spf A with ℒ|_U = O e and s = f e: sectionDomainGE ∩ d(U) = fracPowGE f ϖ q ∩ d(U) = rationalSubset {ϖ^a, f^b} (f^b).
- `FormalScheme.sectionDomainGE_indep_generator` (characterisation): The local descriptions for two generators e, ue (u a unit) agree.
- `FormalScheme.isOpen_sectionDomainGE` (other): The domain is open; quasi-compact if 𝔛 is.
- `FormalScheme.sectionDomainGE_preimage` (functoriality): For g: 𝔜 → 𝔛: d(g)⁻¹(sectionDomainGE s q) = sectionDomainGE (g*s) q.
- `FormalScheme.sectionDomainGE_congr` (characterisation): If s − s' ∈ ϖ^c ℒ with c > q then sectionDomainGE s q = sectionDomainGE s' q.
- `FormalScheme.sectionDomainGE_ofMod` (constructor): For s̄ ∈ Γ(𝔛, ℒ/ϖ^m ℒ) and q < m: the domain defined through arbitrary local lifts.
- `FormalScheme.sectionDomainGE_mono` (relation): q ≤ q' ⇒ sectionDomainGE s q ⊆ sectionDomainGE s q'.
- `FormalScheme.sectionDomainGE_zero` (example): sectionDomainGE s 0 = {|s| = 1} = λ⁻¹(𝔛_s ∖ V(s̄)) = tube of the locus where s̄ generates ℒ/ϖ.
- `FormalScheme.sectionDomainGE_pow` (relation): sectionDomainGE (s^{⊗n}) (n q) = sectionDomainGE s q in ℒ^{⊗n}.
- `FormalScheme.sectionDomainGE_tensor` (relation): sectionDomainGE s q ∩ sectionDomainGE t q' ⊆ sectionDomainGE (s ⊗ t) (q + q') in ℒ ⊗ ℳ.

Unit tests:

- `sectionDomain_test_projectiveLine` (computation): For 𝔛 = P̂¹_{O_K}, ℒ = O(1), s = T_0 and q = 1: sectionDomainGE s 1 = {x : |T_0(x)| ≥ |ϖ| · max(|T_0(x)|, |T_1(x)|)}, the complement of the open disc {|T_0/T_1| < |ϖ|}.
- `sectionDomain_test_generatorIndependence` (characterisation): On 𝔛 = Spf O_K⟨T, T⁻¹⟩ with ℒ = O, the generators e and T·e give the same domain for s = T² e = T·(Te): {|T²| ≥ |ϖ|^q} = {|T| ≥ |ϖ|^q} because |T| = 1 on d(𝔛).
- `sectionDomain_test_liftIndependence` (characterisation): On Spf O_K⟨T⟩ with ℒ = O and q = 1/2: s = T and s' = T + ϖ give the same domain {|T²| ≥ |ϖ|}; for q = 1 they do not (the point T = −ϖ lies in the first but not the second).
- `sectionDomain_test_integralStructure` (non-example): Replacing ℒ by the lattice ϖ⁻¹ℒ ⊇ ℒ in the same ℒ_η multiplies the local coordinates of s by ϖ and changes the domain from {|s| ≥ |ϖ|^q} to {|s|_ℒ ≥ |ϖ|^{q−1}}; a definition using only ℒ_η is ill-defined.
- `sectionDomain_test_degenerate` (degenerate): If s̄ generates ℒ/ϖℒ everywhere then the domain is d(𝔛) for every q ≥ 0; if s = 0 it is empty.

Acceptance: For 𝔛 = P̂¹_{O_K}, ℒ = O(1), s = T_0: 𝔛_η(|s| ≥ |ϖ|^q) is P^{1,ad}_K minus the open disc {|z| < |ϖ|^q} around z = T_0/T_1 = 0. Replacing ℒ by the lattice ℒ' = ϖ⁻¹ℒ ⊇ ℒ in the same ℒ_η (so s ∈ Γ(ℒ) ⊆ Γ(ℒ') with coordinate ϖf for the generator ϖ⁻¹e) changes 𝔛_η(|s| ≥ |ϖ|^q) into 𝔛_η(|s| ≥ |ϖ|^{q−1}) computed in ℒ (empty for q < 1): the domain depends on the formal model of the line bundle.

**Formal models of section domains** (`FormalScheme.sectionDomainModel`). For c ∈ O_K ∖ {0}, the open chart
𝔛(|s| ≥ |c|) of the admissible blow-up of (s, c) where s generates; locally Spf(A⟨u⟩/(fu − c)/torsion),
representing on flat formal schemes the sections u of ℒ⁻¹ with u·s = c; its generic fibre is
{|s| ≥ |c|}; lifts s' = s + c't with c' ∈ c·m_K give canonically isomorphic models
(u ↦ u(1 + (c'/c)ut)⁻¹); no torsion needs killing when s̄ is a non-zero-divisor mod ϖ. This is an open
formal subscheme of an admissible blow-up, not the blow-up itself (see the recorded misprint in Scholze's
Lemma III.2.13).

*Node* `AdicSpacesPartII:R2/section-domain-formal-model` (construction), module `TauCeti/AlgebraicGeometry/FormalScheme/SectionDomain`.

API:

- `FormalScheme.sectionDomainModel` (constructor): 𝔛(|s| ≥ |c|), an admissible formal scheme over 𝔛.
- `FormalScheme.sectionDomainModel.toBlowUp` (structure): An open immersion 𝔛(|s| ≥ |c|) → Bl_{(s,c)} 𝔛 onto the locus where s generates.
- `FormalScheme.sectionDomainModel_affine` (simp): Over Spf A with ℒ = Ae, s = fe: Spf(A⟨u⟩/(fu − c) / ϖ-torsion).
- `FormalScheme.sectionDomainModel.homEquiv` (universal-property): For ϖ-torsion-free Z and g: Z → 𝔛: lifts of g ≃ {u ∈ Γ(Z, g*ℒ⁻¹) : u · g*s = c}.
- `FormalScheme.sectionDomainModel.u_mul_s` (data): The tautological section u of ℒ⁻¹ with u·s = c.
- `FormalScheme.sectionDomainModel_genericFibre` (compatibility): d(𝔛(|s| ≥ |c|)) → d(𝔛) is an open immersion onto {|s| ≥ |c|} = sectionDomainGE s q when |c| = |ϖ|^q.
- `FormalScheme.sectionDomainModel_isoOfLift` (equivalence): For s' = s + c't with c' ∈ c·m_K: a canonical 𝔛-isomorphism 𝔛(|s| ≥ |c|) ≅ 𝔛(|s'| ≥ |c|), u ↦ u(1 + (c'/c)ut)⁻¹.
- `FormalScheme.sectionDomainModel_isoOfAssociated` (equivalence): For c'' = wc with w ∈ O_K^×: 𝔛(|s| ≥ |c|) ≅ 𝔛(|s| ≥ |c''|), u ↦ wu.
- `FormalScheme.sectionDomainModel_flat_of_isRegular` (other): If locally f̄ is a non-zero-divisor on A/ϖ and c ∈ m_K, then A⟨u⟩/(fu − c) has no ϖ-torsion.
- `FormalScheme.sectionDomainModel_mapOfDvd` (functoriality): If c ∣ c' in O_K there is a unique 𝔛-morphism 𝔛(|s| ≥ |c|) → 𝔛(|s| ≥ |c'|) with u ↦ (c'/c)u, an open immersion on generic fibres.

Unit tests:

- `sectionDomainModel_test_annulus` (computation): For 𝔛 = Spf O_K⟨T⟩, ℒ = O, s = T, c = ϖ: sectionDomainModel = Spf O_K⟨T,u⟩/(Tu − ϖ), already ϖ-torsion-free, with generic fibre {|ϖ| ≤ |T| ≤ 1}.
- `sectionDomainModel_test_torsion` (non-example): For s = ϖT on Spf O_K⟨T⟩ and c = ϖ, the ring O_K⟨T,u⟩/(ϖTu − ϖ) has nonzero ϖ-torsion (the class of Tu − 1); only after killing it does one get O_K⟨T, T⁻¹⟩, whose generic fibre {|T| = 1} = {|ϖT| ≥ |ϖ|} is correct.
- `sectionDomainModel_test_points` (characterisation): For s = T, c = ϖ on Spf O_K⟨T⟩: the O_K-point T ↦ ϖ lifts uniquely (u = 1), while T ↦ ϖ² does not lift (uϖ² = ϖ has no solution in O_K).
- `sectionDomainModel_test_unitThreshold` (degenerate): For c = 1 the model is the open formal subscheme D(s̄) = 𝔛 ∖ V(s̄), and no blow-up is needed; for s = 1 it is 𝔛.
- `sectionDomainModel_test_scholze` (compatibility): For 𝔛 = X* (p-adic completion of the minimal compactification), ℒ = ω^{⊗(p−1)}, s = H̃a and c = p^ε ∈ Z_p^cycl, the model is Scholze's X*(ε) and its generic fibre is {|Ha| ≥ |p|^ε}.

Acceptance: 𝔛 = Spf O_K⟨T⟩, ℒ = O, s = T, c = ϖ: the model is Spf O_K⟨T, u⟩/(Tu − ϖ), with generic fibre the annulus {|ϖ| ≤ |T| ≤ 1}. Scholze's X*(ε) → X* for the Hasse invariant (Lemma III.2.13) is this construction with ℒ = ω^{⊗(p−1)}, s = H̃a, c = p^ε.

**Hasse domains** (`FormalScheme.hasseDomain`, `FormalScheme.hasseDomainModel`; planet *Hasse domain*).
For (𝔛, ω, Ha) with Ha ∈ Γ(𝔛 ⊗ O_K/p, ω^{⊗(p−1)}) and 0 ≤ ε < 1: X(ε) = {|H̃a| ≥ |p|^ε} for any local lift,
and, when p^ε ∈ O_K, the formal model 𝔛(ε) (Scholze Definition III.2.12: pairs (g, u) with
u·Ha(ḡ) = p^ε mod p, modulo u ~ u(1 + p^{1−ε}h)), with d(𝔛(ε)) = X(ε). X(0) is the tube of the ordinary
locus. For ε = 1 the domain depends on the lift; for K = Q_p and ε = 1/2 the domain is defined but its
model needs Z_p[√p].

*Node* `AdicSpacesPartII:R2/hasse-domain` (construction), module `TauCeti/AlgebraicGeometry/FormalScheme/HasseDomain`.

API:

- `FormalScheme.hasseDomain` (constructor): X(ε) ⊆ d(𝔛) for 0 ≤ ε < 1.
- `FormalScheme.hasseDomain_eq_sectionDomainGE` (characterisation): X(ε) = sectionDomainGE H̃a ε for every local lift H̃a.
- `FormalScheme.hasseDomain_indep_lift` (characterisation): X(ε) does not depend on the lifts (ε < 1).
- `FormalScheme.hasseDomainModel` (constructor): 𝔛(ε) when p^ε ∈ O_K.
- `FormalScheme.hasseDomainModel.homEquiv` (universal-property): Maps Spf S → 𝔛(ε) over 𝔛 (S flat p-adically complete) ↔ u ∈ Γ(g*ω^{⊗(1−p)}) with u·Ha(ḡ) = p^ε in S/p, modulo u ~ u(1 + p^{1−ε}h).
- `FormalScheme.hasseDomainModel_genericFibre` (compatibility): d(𝔛(ε)) = X(ε).
- `FormalScheme.hasseDomainModel_isoOfLift` (equivalence): Different local lifts give canonically isomorphic models.
- `FormalScheme.hasseDomain_zero` (example): X(0) = tube of the ordinary locus.
- `FormalScheme.hasseDomain_mono` (relation): ε ≤ ε' ⇒ X(ε) ⊆ X(ε').
- `FormalScheme.hasseDomain_preimage` (functoriality): For g: 𝔜 → 𝔛 with ω_𝔜 = g*ω and Ha_𝔜 = g*Ha: d(g)⁻¹(X(ε)) = 𝔜(ε).
- `FormalScheme.hasseDomainModel_flat` (other): If Ha is a non-zero-divisor on 𝔛 ⊗ F_p (e.g. 𝔛 ⊗ F_p normal and Ha nonzero on every component), the local rings O⟨u⟩/(uH̃a − p^ε) are p-torsion-free (Scholze Lemma III.2.10).

Unit tests:

- `hasseDomain_test_toy` (computation): For 𝔛 = Spf Z_p⟨T⟩, ω = O, Ha = T mod p: hasseDomain (1/2) = {v : v(T²) ≥ v(p)}, and over O_K = Z_p[√p] the model is Spf O_K⟨T,u⟩/(Tu − √p).
- `hasseDomain_test_liftAtOne` (non-example): For ε = 1 the locus depends on the lift: with H̃a = T and H̃a' = T + p on Spf Z_p⟨T⟩, the classical point T = −p lies in {|T| ≥ |p|} but not in {|T + p| ≥ |p|}; hence the restriction ε < 1.
- `hasseDomain_test_ordinary` (degenerate): hasseDomain 0 = {|Ha| = 1} = tube of the ordinary locus 𝔛_s ∖ V(Ha); for Ha invertible (𝔛_s ordinary) every X(ε) is d(𝔛).
- `hasseDomain_test_scholze` (compatibility): For Scholze's X* over Z_p^cycl with p^ε ∈ Z_p^cycl, hasseDomainModel ε ≅ X*(ε) of Definition III.2.12 and its generic fibre is {|Ha| ≥ |p|^ε}.
- `hasseDomain_test_noRoot` (non-example): For K = Q_p and ε = 1/2 there is no element of Q_p of absolute value |p|^{1/2}: hasseDomain (1/2) is still defined by |H̃a²| ≥ |p|, while the formal model requires Z_p[√p] (or the blow-up of (H̃a², p) in ω^{⊗2(p−1)}).

Acceptance: Toy case 𝔛 = Spf Z_p⟨T⟩, ω = O, Ha = T mod p, ε = 1/2: X(1/2) = {|T²| ≥ |p|}; over O_K = Z_p[√p] the model is Spf O_K⟨T, u⟩/(Tu − √p). For the modular curve (Γ(N), N ≥ 3) with ω the Hodge bundle, X(ε) is BHW's ε-nearly ordinary locus X*(ε), and 𝔛(ε) is the canonical formal model of BHW Definition 4.1.

**Transition maps.** For ε' ≤ ε < 1: X(ε') ⊆ X(ε) rational on charts; ι_{ε',ε}: 𝔛(ε') → 𝔛(ε) with
u = (c_ε/c_{ε'})u', transitive; X(<ε) = ⋃_{ε'<ε} X(ε') is the interior of {|Ha| > |p|^ε} (same classical
points; they differ by higher-rank points), matching Conrad's admissible cover of S^{>h}; the closure of
X(0) lies in every X(ε), ε > 0.

*Node* `AdicSpacesPartII:R2/hasse-domain-transition-maps` (lemma), module `TauCeti/AlgebraicGeometry/FormalScheme/HasseDomain`.

Hypotheses: 0 ≤ ε'' ≤ ε' ≤ ε < 1; chosen elements c_ε ∈ O_K of valuation ε for the formal statements (b),(c).

Acceptance: For 𝔛 = Spf Z_p⟨T⟩, Ha = T and c_{1/2} = √p, c_{1/4} = p^{1/4} over Z_p[p^{1/4}]: ι_{1/4,1/2} is u = p^{1/4}u' from Spf⟨T,u'⟩/(Tu' − p^{1/4}) to Spf⟨T,u⟩/(Tu − p^{1/2}); on generic fibres {|T| ≥ |p|^{1/4}} ⊆ {|T| ≥ |p|^{1/2}}. Conrad's admissible cover of S^{>h_0} by the S^{≥h}, h ∈ (h_0, 1), is (d) in the elliptic case.

**Conrad's Hasse loci** (Theorem 4.1.1). For a generalized elliptic curve E → S and h(E_s) = max(|a|, 1/p),
S^{>h} and S^{≥h} are admissible opens, compatible with base change and extension of k, locally
{|a_{Γ_A}| > h} on the formal completion of the proper moduli scheme; for h = |p|^ε ∈ (1/p, 1],
S^{≥h} = X(ε).

*Node* `AdicSpacesPartII:R2/hasse-loci-admissible-opens` (construction), module `TauCeti/AlgebraicGeometry/AdicSpace/HasseLocus`.

API:

- `AdicSpace.hasseInvariantValue` (data): h(E_s) = max(|a|, 1/p) for a fibre E_s, via a semistable model after finite extension.
- `AdicSpace.hasseLocusGT` (constructor): S^{>h} for h ∈ [1/p, 1) ∩ √|k^×|.
- `AdicSpace.hasseLocusGE` (constructor): S^{≥h} for h ∈ (1/p, 1] ∩ √|k^×|.
- `AdicSpace.isOpen_hasseLocusGE` (other): S^{>h} and S^{≥h} are (admissible) opens.
- `AdicSpace.hasseLocusGE_quasiCompact` (other): S^{≥h} → S is quasi-compact.
- `AdicSpace.hasseLocus_baseChange` (compatibility): Formation commutes with base change S' → S.
- `AdicSpace.hasseLocus_extendScalars` (compatibility): Formation commutes with analytic extension of k (for quasi-separated or pseudo-separated S).
- `AdicSpace.iUnion_hasseLocusGE` (relation): S^{>h_0} = ⋃_{h ∈ (h_0,1)} S^{≥h}, an admissible cover.
- `AdicSpace.hasseLocusGE_local` (characterisation): On (Spf A)^rig with formal group Spf A[[X]]: S^{≥h} = {|a_{Γ_A}| ≥ h}, independent of X.
- `AdicSpace.hasseLocusGE_eq_hasseDomain` (compatibility): For the universal curve and h = |p|^ε, S^{≥h} is the Hasse domain X(ε) of node hasse-domain.

Unit tests:

- `hasseLocus_test_ordinary` (computation): For an elliptic curve E over k with good ordinary reduction, h(E) = 1, so the point lies in S^{≥1}; for good supersingular reduction h(E) < 1.
- `hasseLocus_test_floor` (degenerate): h(E_s) ≥ 1/p always, so the locus {h(E_s) ≥ 1/p} is all of S; this is why S^{≥h} is only defined for h > 1/p.
- `hasseLocus_test_withoutMax` (non-example): For h < 1/p the locus {|a_{Γ_A}| ≥ h} can be strictly smaller than S (a can be divisible by p), whereas {h(E_s) ≥ h} = S: dropping the max(·, 1/p) in Definition B.3.3 gives a different, coordinate-dependent set.
- `hasseLocus_test_hasseDomain` (compatibility): For S = M^an with the universal curve and h = |p|^ε, 0 ≤ ε < 1: S^{≥h} = X(ε), the Hasse domain of M̂ with ω the Hodge bundle and Ha the Hasse invariant.
- `hasseLocus_test_fractionalThreshold` (characterisation): For h = |c|^{1/n} ∈ √|k^×| (c ∈ k^×), S^{≥h} ∩ (Spf A)^rig = {|a_{Γ_A}^n| ≥ |c|}, independent of the choice of (c, n) representing h.

Acceptance: {h(E) = 1} is the locus of potentially ordinary or potentially toric reduction; h(E) < 1 iff potentially supersingular reduction (Conrad after Remark B.3.4). S^{≥h} → S is quasi-compact for non-strict inequalities.

#### Acceptance tests

- Spf O_C⟨T^{±1}⟩ is admissible and not locally noetherian; it is the completed base change of the
  noetherian formal torus Spf Z_p⟨T^{±1}⟩ (campaign contract).
- d(Spf O_K⟨T⟩) is the closed unit disc; d(Spf O_K[[T]]) (K discretely valued) is the open unit disc;
  d(Spf O_K/ϖ) = ∅.
- The tube of 0 in the closed disc is the open disc, and λ⁻¹(0) is strictly larger (it contains η_{1⁻}).
- The blow-up of (T, ϖ) on Spf O_K⟨T⟩ has special fibre P¹_k ∪ A¹_k and the same generic fibre.
- Raynaud: the closed annulus has the model Spf O_K⟨T,V⟩/(TV − ϖ); the open disc has no quasi-compact
  model.
- Flattening: Spf O_K⟨ζ, ξ⟩/(ζξ − ϖ) → Spf O_K⟨ζ⟩ becomes an open immersion after blowing up (ζ, ϖ).
- Good reduction: A¹_{O_K} ↦ closed disc, G_m ↦ {|T| = 1}, P¹ ↦ all of P^{1,ad}_K; the flatness
  hypothesis of the converse fails for Spec O_K ⊔ A¹_{O_K/ϖ}.
- Residue discs of P̂¹ at 0 and ∞ are {|T| < 1} and {|T| > 1}; a degree-two closed point of P¹_{F_p}
  gives a twisted disc with no Q_p-point.
- Frobenius on the torus: φ(Σ a_ν T^ν) = Σ σ(a_ν) T^{pν}.
- {|T| ≤ |p|^{1/2}} = {|T²| ≤ |p|} in Spa(Q_p⟨T⟩, Z_p⟨T⟩); X(1/2) for Ha = T has model
  Spf Z_p[√p]⟨T,u⟩/(Tu − √p); for ε = 1 the Hasse locus depends on the lift.
- Fibral finiteness: {|t| = 1} ⊔ {|t| < 1} → {|t| ≤ 1} is flat with fibres of rank one and not finite
  (not quasi-compact).

## R3. Coherent sheaves and finite traces


**Dependencies:** [AdicSpacesPartII R0](README.md#r0), [AdicSpacesPartII R1](README.md#r1), [AdicSpacesPartII R2](README.md#r2), [AdicSpacesPartII F0](README.md#f0);
the Tau Ceti anchor roadmap `tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/AdicSpaces`, Layers 0, 2, 3, 4 and 5; DiamondsAndVStacks D0 (Čech-to-derived comparison);
TropicalAndBerkovichArithmetic TB.0 (Gel'fand spectra); AlgebraicModuliForArithmeticGeometry R09.3 (Chow's lemma and dévissage);
Tau Ceti ModularCurves 0E (faithfully flat descent).

This layer builds the coherent and finite-trace theory of analytic adic spaces on top of the anchor's
structure sheaf. It has four strands, each ending in a named theorem:

1. **Affinoid coherent theory under noetherian hypotheses.** For an affinoid Spa(A, A⁺) with A complete of one of
   Huber's two noetherian types, the sheaf M̃ of a finite module is acyclic (Huber 1994, Theorem 2.5), and in the
   strongly noetherian Tate case every coherent sheaf is some M̃ (**Kiehl's theorem**), proved for all strongly
   noetherian Tate rings by glueing squares. Coherent sheaves, their operations, coherent ideals, finite algebras and
   quasi-Stein spaces (Kiehl's Theorems A and B) follow.
2. **Finite projective gluing without noetherian hypotheses.** On a sheafy Tate affinoid, vector bundles are exactly
   the finite projective modules (**Kiehl gluing**, Kedlaya–Liu Theorem 2.7.7), on top of Čech acyclicity of 𝒪 for every
   sheafy Tate pair (Kedlaya–Liu Theorem 2.4.23, proved in R3.1); this is the range used by perfectoid and
   sousperfectoid consumers, where rational localisation is not flat. The Kedlaya–Liu splitting criterion for stable
   uniformity and the spectral-norm isometry criterion belong here.
3. **Proper coherent direct images.** **Kiehl's proper mapping theorem** for proper morphisms of adic spaces locally of
   finite type over a complete nonarchimedean field K, with compatibility with affinoid subdomains, completed extension
   of K and étale base change of affinoids, and **proper GAGA** over affinoid K-algebras (this last also realises R1).
4. **Traces.** The trace of a finite projective (finite locally free) algebra, which Mathlib's `Algebra.trace` does not
   provide in the non-free case, its sheafification for finite locally free morphisms of schemes and of adic spaces
   (the **trace map**), base change, composition, the perfect trace pairing of finite étale maps, compatibility with the
   algebraic trace under analytification, and pull–identify–trace operators on correspondences.

**Imported, not planned here.** The sheaf property of the structure sheaf 𝒪_X and its Tate acyclicity for strongly
noetherian rings, the strongly noetherian flatness chain, the definition of (stable) uniformity and the Buzzard–Verberkmoes theorem belong to the
anchor's Layer 4. Adic spaces, open and closed subspaces and gluing belong to the anchor's Layer 5. Completed tensor
products, fibre products, finite, proper and étale morphisms belong to R0; analytification of schemes and the
rigid–adic comparison belong to R1. The étale trace of sheaves of abelian groups is ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology H3's; the
coherent trace here is compared with, never identified with, it. Algebraic Hecke correspondences are ModularCurvesPartII
R14.1's; pull–identify–trace here is their analytic counterpart. Almost-mathematics refinements on perfectoid
affinoids are PerfectoidSpaces P2's, torsor descent is PerfectoidSpaces P9's, sousperfectoid rings are R5's.

### Conventions

- K is a complete nonarchimedean field with nontrivial absolute value, K° its valuation ring and ϖ a pseudouniformiser.
  An *affinoid K-algebra* is a quotient of some K⟨X₁,…,Xₙ⟩; it is complete, noetherian and strongly noetherian Tate.
- "Complete" includes Hausdorff (anchor convention 3). An affinoid ring (A, A⁺) is of *noetherian type* if A is complete
  and either has a noetherian ring of definition (type I) or is a strongly noetherian Tate ring (type II,
  `TauCeti.Huber.IsStronglyNoetherian`).
- A *sheafy* Tate pair is one whose structure presheaf is a sheaf on all rational subsets (anchor Layer 3.4,
  `Huber.IsSheafyPair`). Rational subsets R(T/s) have coordinate rings A⟨T/s⟩ (anchor Layer 3.1).
- Tensor products M ⊗_A B are ordinary tensor products; for finite M over the rings of this layer they coincide with
  completed tensor products, and the construction M̃ is made only for finite M. Completed tensor products of rings are
  R0's.
- Čech complexes are alternating and augmented. Hⁱ(X, F) is sheaf cohomology of the underlying abelian sheaf on the
  topological space X (as in Tau Ceti's `Scheme.Modules.Cohomology`). "Acyclic on 𝔘" means exactness of the augmented
  Čech complex in all degrees.
- A *vector bundle* is an 𝒪_X-module locally isomorphic to 𝒪ⁿ (Mathlib's `SheafOfModules.IsLocallyFree` with finite
  local bases). "Finite projective", "finite locally free" and "finitely generated and locally free" modules are the
  same (Kedlaya–Liu Definition 1.1.2).
- *Proper* morphisms of adic spaces are R0's (+weakly finite type, separated, universally closed). Kiehl's properness
  (relatively compact affinoid coverings) is the rigid notion used in the proofs and is compared with R0's by R1.
- The trace of an endomorphism of a finite projective module is `LinearMap.projectiveTrace` (contraction through
  `dualTensorHomEquiv`). Mathlib's `LinearMap.trace` and `Algebra.trace` are used only where modules are free: they are
  defined to be 0 when no finite basis exists. A trace is never defined as a sum over geometric points; that formula is a
  theorem for finite étale maps only.

### R3.1 The associated sheaf and acyclicity for finite modules

Huber's Theorem 2.5 in both of its cases. Case II (strongly noetherian Tate) is reduced to the anchor's Tate acyclicity of 𝒪 by flatness of rational localisation; Case I (noetherian ring of definition) follows Huber's Raynaud-style argument with formal blow-ups and is the only place where non-analytic points occur. The covering-reduction principle of Kedlaya–Liu Proposition 2.4.20 is stated once here and used for both kinds of gluing, and for the Čech acyclicity of 𝒪 on sheafy Tate affinoids (Kedlaya–Liu Proposition 2.4.21, Lemma 2.4.22, Theorem 2.4.23).

#### The sheaf M̃ = M ⊗ 𝒪_X associated with a finite module on a noetherian affinoid

`AdicSpacesPartII:R3/associated-module-sheaf` · construction · declaration `AdicSpace.tilde` · module `TauCeti/AlgebraicGeometry/AdicSpace/Coherent/Tilde`

Let (A, A⁺) is a Huber pair with A complete and Hausdorff, and A is of one of Huber's two noetherian types: (I) A has a noetherian ring of definition, or (II) A is a strongly noetherian Tate ring (TauCeti.Huber.IsStronglyNoetherian: every A⟨X₁,…,Xₙ⟩ is noetherian), let X = Spa(A, A⁺) and let M be a finitely generated A-module. The associated presheaf M̃ (Huber's M ⊗ 𝒪_A) is the presheaf of topological 𝒪_X-modules on X defined on the rational basis by M̃(U) = M ⊗_A 𝒪_X(U) for U = R(T/s), where 𝒪_X(U) = A⟨T/s⟩ is the complete rational localisation of anchor Layer 3.1 and the ordinary (uncompleted) tensor product carries its natural 𝒪_X(U)-module topology (the quotient topology along any surjection 𝒪_X(U)ⁿ ↠ M ⊗_A 𝒪_X(U)); the restriction for rational V ⊆ U is id_M ⊗ ρ_{V,U}. On an arbitrary open W ⊆ X, M̃(W) = lim M̃(V) over the rational V ⊆ W, with the inverse-limit topology. An A-linear map φ : M → N induces φ̃ : M̃ → Ñ, functorially. Convention: the tensor product is not completed; for finite M over these rings M ⊗_A 𝒪_X(U) is already complete and equals the completed tensor product (Huber Lemmas 2.3(iii), 2.4(ii)), and the construction is only made for finitely generated M.

*Hypotheses.* A complete and Hausdorff; A has a noetherian ring of definition or is a strongly noetherian Tate ring; A⁺ ⊆ A a ring of integral elements (anchor Layer 0.2); M a finitely generated A-module.

*Construction.*

1. On rational subsets: for U = R(T/s), set M̃(U) = M ⊗_A A⟨T/s⟩; independence of the presentation (T, s) is transported along the canonical isomorphisms between localisations of two presentations of the same rational subset (anchor Layer 3.1).
2. Topology: 𝒪_X(U) is complete noetherian (type II: rational localisations of strongly noetherian Tate rings are strongly noetherian, tauceti:TauCeti.Huber.PairOfDefinition.isStronglyNoetherian_completion; type I: 𝒪_X(U) again has a noetherian ring of definition, Huber 1994 before (1.4)); the natural topology on the finite module M ⊗_A 𝒪_X(U) is its module topology (tauceti:TauCeti.Huber.IsTateRing.isModuleTopology in type II; Huber Lemma 2.3 in type I), complete and Hausdorff with every submodule closed (tauceti:TauCeti.Huber.isClosed_of_isNoetherian).
3. Restriction maps id_M ⊗ ρ_{V,U} are continuous because every A-linear map of finite modules with module topologies is continuous; the cocycle identities are those of 𝒪_X (anchor Layer 3.3).
4. Extension to all opens by the limit over rational subsets, exactly as for 𝒪_X in anchor Layer 3.3; the two definitions agree on rational subsets because the rational subsets contained in a rational U are cofinal and U is one of them.
5. Functoriality: φ ⊗ id on rational subsets, compatible with restriction.

*API.*

- `AdicSpace.tilde` (constructor): For a finite A-module M, the presheaf of topological 𝒪_X-modules M̃ on X = Spa(A, A⁺).
- `AdicSpace.tilde_obj_rationalSubset` (characterisation): For U = R(T/s), M̃(U) = M ⊗_A A⟨T/s⟩ as topological A⟨T/s⟩-modules.
- `AdicSpace.tilde_map` (functoriality): An A-linear φ : M → N induces φ̃ : M̃ → Ñ, with tilde_map_id and tilde_map_comp.
- `AdicSpace.tildeRestrictIso` (compatibility): For a rational U with coordinate pair (B, B⁺) (so Spa(B, B⁺) ≅ U by spaLocalizationHomeomorph), M̃|_U ≅ (M ⊗_A B)~ as presheaves on Spa(B, B⁺) (Huber (1.4)).
- `AdicSpace.tildeSelfIso` (example): Ã ≅ 𝒪_X as presheaves of topological 𝒪_X-modules; more generally (Aⁿ)~ ≅ 𝒪_Xⁿ.
- `AdicSpace.tildeTensorIso` (compatibility): For finite M, N and rational U, (M ⊗_A N)~(U) ≅ M̃(U) ⊗_{𝒪_X(U)} Ñ(U), naturally in M and N.
- `AdicSpace.tilde_exact` (other): In type II (strongly noetherian Tate), for every rational U the functor M ↦ M̃(U) is exact, because A → 𝒪_X(U) is flat (tauceti flat_toCompletionLoc).
- `AdicSpace.completeSpace_tilde_obj` (instance): For rational U, M̃(U) is complete and Hausdorff, and every A-linear map of finite modules induces a strict map M̃(U) → Ñ(U).
- `AdicSpace.tilde_obj_top` (characterisation): M̃(X) = M ⊗_A A = M (X is the rational subset R({1}/1) and 𝒪_X(X) = A, anchor Layer 3.5).

*Unit tests.*

- `AdicSpace.tilde_test_quotient` (computation): For A = K⟨T⟩, M = A/(T) and U = {|T| ≥ 1}, M̃(U) = 0 (T is a unit on U), while for U = {|T| ≤ |ϖ|}, M̃(U) ≅ K.
- `AdicSpace.tilde_test_zero_and_self` (degenerate): 0̃ = 0, and for M = A the presheaf Ã is isomorphic, as a presheaf of topological 𝒪_X-modules, to 𝒪_X.
- `AdicSpace.tilde_test_not_algebraic_localisation` (non-example): For A = ℚ_p⟨T⟩, M = A and U = {|T| ≥ 1}: the algebraic localisation M ⊗_A A[1/T] = ℚ_p⟨T⟩[1/T] is not M̃(U) = ℚ_p⟨T, T⁻¹⟩, since Σ_{n≥0} pⁿT⁻ⁿ lies in the latter and not in the former; the definition must use the completed rational localisation.
- `AdicSpace.tilde_test_completed_tensor` (compatibility): For finite M the canonical map M ⊗_A 𝒪_X(U) → M ⊗̂_A 𝒪_X(U) is a topological isomorphism; for the non-finite module M = ⊕_{n∈ℕ} A it is not surjective (Σ ϖⁿ e_n ⊗ 1 is a limit not in the algebraic tensor product), which is why the construction is restricted to finite M.

*Acceptance.* For A = K⟨T⟩ over a complete nonarchimedean field K and M = A/(T), M̃(U) = 𝒪_X(U)/T·𝒪_X(U) on every rational U; on U = {|T| ≥ 1} it is 0. For M = A, Ã is the structure presheaf 𝒪_X itself. For finite M the natural map M ⊗_A 𝒪_X(U) → M ⊗̂_A 𝒪_X(U) is a topological isomorphism (Huber Lemma 2.3(iii)).

*Used by.* Huber 1994, Theorem 2.5 — the sheaf and acyclicity theorem is stated for M ⊗ 𝒪_A, so the object must exist with its topology; Kedlaya–Liu 2015, Theorem 2.5.20(a)-(b) — M̃ is the functor whose essential image is the coherent sheaves (Kiehl) and whose Čech cohomology is computed; Kiehl 1967 (Theorem A und B), Definition 1.1 and Theorem 1.2 — U-coherent sheaves are glued from associated sheaves M̃_i; AdicSpacesPartII:R3/coherent-sheaf, AdicSpacesPartII:R3/tate-kiehl-affinoid — local model of a coherent sheaf and the functor of Kiehl's equivalence; PadicDifferentialEquationsAndRigidCohomology:RD.3/j-dagger (request to R3) — coherent sheaves on affinoids correspond to finite modules via M ↦ M̃; PadicHodgeTheory:P8/coherent-cohomology-against-graded-structural-sheaf — coherent cohomology on affinoid covers is computed by Čech complexes of M ⊗ 𝒪(U_I).

*Prerequisites.* `tauceti:TauCeti.ValuationSpectrum.spa`, `tauceti:TauCeti.ValuationSpectrum.rationalSubset`, `tauceti:TauCeti.Huber.PairOfDefinition.completionLocObj`, `tauceti:TauCeti.Huber.IsStronglyNoetherian`, `tauceti:TauCeti.Huber.PairOfDefinition.isStronglyNoetherian_completion`, `tauceti:TauCeti.Huber.IsTateRing.isModuleTopology`, `tauceti:TauCeti.Huber.isClosed_of_isNoetherian`, `tauceti:TauCeti.ValuationSpectrum.spaLocalizationHomeomorph`, `tauceti:TauCeti.Huber.PairOfDefinition.flat_toCompletionLoc`, `tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/AdicSpaces#layer-3-rational-localisation-and-the-structure-presheaf`, `AdicSpacesPartII:R0/locally-noetherian-adic-space`.

*Sources.* Huber-GeneralizationFormalRigid-1994, §2, definition preceding Theorem 2.5, printed p. 525; Huber-GeneralizationFormalRigid-1994, §2, Theorem 2.5, printed p. 525; Kiehl-TheoremAB-1967, §1, Definition 1.1, printed p. 259.

The Čech-complex inputs of Huber's Case I are planned in R0 (R0a.1a), which precedes R3: exactness of the extended Čech complex of localisations (`AdicSpacesPartII:R0/localization-cech-complex-exact`), completion of strict exact complexes (`AdicSpacesPartII:R0/strict-complex-completion-exact`), Huber's (1.3) for every finite module (`AdicSpacesPartII:R0/noetherian-rod-laurent-cech-strict`) and the sheaf theorem with standard rational refinements (`AdicSpacesPartII:R0/noetherian-rod-sheafy`). R3 uses them for M̃.

#### Tate acyclicity for finite modules over a strongly noetherian Tate affinoid

`AdicSpacesPartII:R3/tate-acyclicity-finite-modules` · theorem · declaration `AdicSpace.tilde_isAcyclic` · module `TauCeti/AlgebraicGeometry/AdicSpace/Coherent/Acyclicity`

Let (A, A⁺) is a Huber pair with A a complete Hausdorff strongly noetherian Tate ring and A⁺ a ring of integral elements, X = Spa(A, A⁺) and M a finite A-module. Then: (i) for every rational subset U ⊆ X and every finite covering 𝔘 of U by rational subsets, the augmented alternating Čech complex 0 → M̃(U) → ∏ M̃(U_i) → ∏ M̃(U_i ∩ U_j) → ⋯ is exact and all its differentials are strict; (ii) M̃ is a sheaf of complete Hausdorff topological 𝒪_X-modules; (iii) Hⁱ(U, M̃) = 0 for i > 0 and H⁰(U, M̃) = M ⊗_A 𝒪_X(U) for every rational U. In particular M̃(X) = M.

*Hypotheses.* (A, A⁺) is a Huber pair with A a complete Hausdorff strongly noetherian Tate ring and A⁺ a ring of integral elements; M finitely generated; Hⁱ is sheaf cohomology of the underlying abelian sheaf on the topological space U.

*Proof.*

1. Intersections of rational subsets are rational (anchor Layer 2.2), so for a finite rational covering the Čech complex of M̃ is M ⊗_A Č(𝔘, 𝒪_X) termwise (finite products commute with ⊗).
2. Č(𝔘, 𝒪_X) augmented is exact in all degrees for every finite rational covering of every rational subset (anchor Layer 4.1 conclusion, imported).
3. Each 𝒪_X(V), V rational, is flat over A (tauceti:TauCeti.Huber.PairOfDefinition.flat_toCompletionLoc), so M ↦ Č(𝔘, M̃) is exact (mathlib:Module.Flat.lTensor_exact).
4. Choose 0 → N → Aⁿ → M → 0 with N finite (A noetherian, tauceti:TauCeti.Huber.isNoetherianRing_of_isStronglyNoetherian); the long exact homology sequence (mathlib:CategoryTheory.ShortComplex.ShortExact.homology_exact₂) and the vanishing of Čech cohomology above the length of 𝔘 give Ȟⁱ(𝔘, M̃) ≅ Ȟ^{i+1}(𝔘, Ñ) for i ≥ 1, hence 0 by descending induction; exactness in degree 0 follows from the five lemma (Huber (II.3): reduce to M = Aⁿ).
5. Strictness: each M̃(V) is complete Hausdorff with the module topology over the complete noetherian Tate ring 𝒪_X(V) (tauceti:TauCeti.Huber.PairOfDefinition.isStronglyNoetherian_completion, tauceti:TauCeti.Huber.IsTateRing.isModuleTopology); images of differentials are kernels of the next differential, hence closed, so the differentials are strict (tauceti:TauCeti.Huber.IsTateRing.isStrictMap_of_isClosed_range).
6. Sheaf property for arbitrary open covers: reduce to rational covers (tauceti:TauCeti.ValuationSpectrum.isSheaf_iff_isSheafFor_rationalCover) refined by standard rational covers (tauceti:TauCeti.ValuationSpectrum.exists_span_eq_top_forall_rationalSubset_subset_of_isTateRing; Huber Lemma 2.6); the limit topology is the product-subspace topology because the equaliser is closed (Huber, via EGA 0.3.2.2).
7. Sheaf cohomology: Čech acyclicity for the cofinal system of finite rational covers of every rational subset of the basis gives Hⁱ = 0 (Cartan's criterion, Stacks Tag 01EW, supplied by DiamondsAndVStacks:D0).

*Acceptance.* Concrete instance (Tate's theorem with coefficients): A = K⟨T⟩, M = A/(T), covering U₁ = {|T| ≤ |ϖ|}, U₂ = {|T| ≥ |ϖ|}: the Čech complex is 0 → K → K ⊕ 0 → 0 → 0, exact. For M = A the theorem is the anchor's Tate acyclicity for 𝒪_X; the node adds no new case for M = A. M̃(X) = M for every finite M, so M ↦ M̃ is fully faithful (Hom(M̃, Ñ) = Hom_A(M, N)).

*Used by.* PadicHodgeTheory:P8/coherent-cohomology-against-graded-structural-sheaf — coherent cohomology computed by Čech complexes of affinoid covers; PadicDifferentialEquationsAndRigidCohomology:RD.3/j-dagger — Theorem B on affinoids.

*Prerequisites.* `AdicSpacesPartII:R3/associated-module-sheaf`, `tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/AdicSpaces#layer-2-affinoid-spectra-and-rational-subsets`, `tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/AdicSpaces#layer-4-sheafiness-and-tate-acyclicity`, `tauceti:TauCeti.Huber.PairOfDefinition.flat_toCompletionLoc`, `mathlib:Module.Flat.lTensor_exact`, `tauceti:TauCeti.Huber.isNoetherianRing_of_isStronglyNoetherian`, `mathlib:CategoryTheory.ShortComplex.ShortExact.homology_exact₂`, `tauceti:TauCeti.Huber.PairOfDefinition.isStronglyNoetherian_completion`, `tauceti:TauCeti.Huber.IsTateRing.isModuleTopology`, `tauceti:TauCeti.Huber.IsTateRing.isStrictMap_of_isClosed_range`, `tauceti:TauCeti.ValuationSpectrum.isSheaf_iff_isSheafFor_rationalCover`, `tauceti:TauCeti.ValuationSpectrum.exists_span_eq_top_forall_rationalSubset_subset_of_isTateRing`, `DiamondsAndVStacks:D0`.

*Sources.* Huber-GeneralizationFormalRigid-1994, §2, Theorem 2.5, printed p. 525; Huber-GeneralizationFormalRigid-1994, §2, proof of Theorem 2.5, Case II, (II.3), printed p. 531; Huber-GeneralizationFormalRigid-1994, §2, proof of Theorem 2.5, printed p. 531; KedlayaLiu-RelativeFoundations-2015, §2.5, Remark 2.5.23, pp. 52-53; Stacks-Project, Tag 01EW, Lemma 20.11.9.

#### Acyclicity of M̃ when A has a noetherian ring of definition (Huber Theorem 2.5, Case I)

`AdicSpacesPartII:R3/noetherian-rod-acyclicity-finite-modules` · theorem · declaration `AdicSpace.tilde_isAcyclic_of_noetherianRingOfDefinition` · module `TauCeti/AlgebraicGeometry/AdicSpace/Coherent/NoetherianDefinition`

Let (A, A⁺) be a complete affinoid ring such that A has a noetherian ring of definition, X = Spa(A, A⁺) and M a finite A-module. Then M̃ is a sheaf of complete topological groups on X, and Hⁱ(U, M̃) = 0 for every i > 0 and every rational subset U ⊆ X. The Čech input — exact strict Čech complexes of M ⊗ 𝒪 on standard rational coverings of rational subsets, which refine every open covering, and the case M = A (sheafiness of 𝒪_X) — is AdicSpacesPartII:R0/noetherian-rod-sheafy (Huber (1.5)); this node adds the sheaf M̃ and sheaf-cohomology vanishing.

*Hypotheses.* A complete with a noetherian ring of definition; M finitely generated; U rational.

*Proof.*

1. For every rational U, M̃(U) = M ⊗_A 𝒪_X(U) with its natural topology is complete (AdicSpacesPartII:R0/noetherian-rod-module-complete over 𝒪_X(U), which has a noetherian ring of definition by AdicSpacesPartII:R0/noetherian-rod-sheafy (a)), and M̃|_U ≅ (M ⊗_A 𝒪_X(U))~ (Huber (1.4); AdicSpacesPartII:R3/associated-module-sheaf, API tildeRestrictIso).
2. Every open covering of a rational U is refined by a standard rational covering whose augmented Čech complex of M̃ is exact with strict differentials (AdicSpacesPartII:R0/noetherian-rod-sheafy (b), (c)); hence M̃ is a sheaf of complete topological groups on the basis of rational subsets and on X (EGA 0_I 3.2.2; tauceti:TauCeti.ValuationSpectrum.isSheaf_iff_isSheafFor_rationalCover).
3. Čech acyclicity on the cofinal system of standard rational coverings of every rational subset gives sheaf-cohomology vanishing (Cartan's criterion, Stacks Tag 01EW, supplied by DiamondsAndVStacks:D0).

*Acceptance.* For A = ℤ_p⟨T⟩ with the p-adic topology (A⁺ = A), Ã = 𝒪_X is a sheaf and H¹(X, 𝒪_X) = 0 for X = Spa(A, A), the adic space t(Spf ℤ_p⟨T⟩) of Huber §4. The statement includes non-analytic points: for A = ℤ_p (discrete ring of definition ℤ_p) X = Spa(ℤ_p, ℤ_p) has a closed non-analytic point and the theorem still applies.

*Used by.* AdicSpacesPartII:R2/noetherian-formal-scheme-as-adic-space — t(Spf A) = Spa(A, A) is an adic space: the case M = A gives the sheaf property of 𝒪 for noetherian adic A.

*Prerequisites.* `AdicSpacesPartII:R3/associated-module-sheaf`, `AdicSpacesPartII:R0/noetherian-rod-sheafy`, `AdicSpacesPartII:R0/noetherian-rod-module-complete`, `DiamondsAndVStacks:D0`, `tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/AdicSpaces#layer-3-rational-localisation-and-the-structure-presheaf`, `tauceti:TauCeti.ValuationSpectrum.isSheaf_iff_isSheafFor_rationalCover`.

*Sources.* Huber-GeneralizationFormalRigid-1994, §2, proof of Theorem 2.5, printed p. 525; Huber-GeneralizationFormalRigid-1994, §2, (1.5), printed p. 529; Huber-GeneralizationFormalRigid-1994, §2, Lemma 2.6, printed p. 531.

#### Reduction of local transitive properties of rational coverings to simple Laurent coverings

`AdicSpacesPartII:R3/rational-covering-reduction` · lemma · declaration `AdicSpace.rationalCovering_induction` · module `TauCeti/AlgebraicGeometry/AdicSpace/Coherent/CoveringReduction`

Let (A, A⁺) be a complete Tate Huber pair (A contains a topologically nilpotent unit). Let P be a property of finite rational coverings of rational subsets of Spa(A, A⁺) such that (a) P is local: if P holds for a refinement of a covering then it holds for the covering; (b) P is transitive: if P holds for {U → V_i} and for coverings {V_i → W_ij} of each V_i then it holds for the composite covering {U → W_ij}; (c) P holds for every simple Laurent covering {v(f) ≤ 1}, {v(f) ≥ 1} of every rational subset. Then P holds for every finite rational covering of every rational subset.

*Hypotheses.* A Tate (a topologically nilpotent unit exists, used to rescale in Lemma 2.4.19(b)); P local, transitive, true for simple Laurent coverings.

*Proof.*

1. Lemma 2.4.19(a): every rational covering is refined by a standard rational covering (in the Tate case: tauceti:TauCeti.ValuationSpectrum.exists_span_eq_top_forall_rationalSubset_subset_of_isTateRing).
2. Lemma 2.4.19(b): for a standard rational covering generated by f₁,…,fₙ, rescale by a power of the pseudouniformiser so that inf_x max_i |f_i(x)| > 1 on Spa(A, A⁺) (units of A are detected pointwise: anchor Layer 2); the standard Laurent covering generated by the f_i restricts to standard rational coverings generated by units.
3. Lemma 2.4.19(c): a standard rational covering generated by units is refined by the Laurent covering generated by the f_i f_j⁻¹ (a total order has a maximum).
4. Assemble: Laurent coverings by units are composites of simple Laurent coverings (use (b),(c)); standard rational coverings by units follow by (a); general standard rational coverings by (b) and the restriction step; general coverings by (a).

*Acceptance.* For P = 'the augmented Čech complex of a presheaf F is exact on every refinement pulled back to every rational subset' the lemma is KL Proposition 2.4.21's reduction. For P = 'every finite glueing datum of finite modules on the covering is effective' the lemma reduces Kiehl's theorem to simple Laurent coverings (used by AdicSpacesPartII:R3/tate-kiehl-affinoid).

*Used by.* AdicSpacesPartII:R3/tate-kiehl-affinoid — reduction of Kiehl's gluing to simple Laurent coverings; AdicSpacesPartII:R3/sheafy-tate-acyclicity-and-kiehl-gluing — reduction of finite projective gluing to simple Laurent coverings (KL Theorem 2.7.7 proof).

*Prerequisites.* `tauceti:TauCeti.ValuationSpectrum.exists_span_eq_top_forall_rationalSubset_subset_of_isTateRing`, `tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/AdicSpaces#layer-2-affinoid-spectra-and-rational-subsets`, `tauceti:TauCeti.Huber.IsTateRing`.

*Sources.* KedlayaLiu-RelativeFoundations-2015, §2.4, Proposition 2.4.20, pp. 44-45; KedlayaLiu-RelativeFoundations-2015, §2.4, Lemma 2.4.19, p. 44; Kiehl-TheoremAB-1967, §1, after Hilfssatz 1.3, printed p. 260.

The Čech acyclicity of 𝒪 on every sheafy Tate affinoid (Kedlaya–Liu Theorem 2.4.23) is proved here and not imported: the anchor's Layer 4.1 states all-degree Čech exactness only for strongly noetherian rings. The reduction of Kedlaya–Liu Proposition 2.4.21 (from all rational coverings to simple Laurent coverings) rests on the covering-reduction principle above and on a Čech refinement lemma proved with the Čech double complex; exactness at the last term of a simple Laurent covering (Kedlaya–Liu Lemma 2.4.22) holds for every complete Huber pair, so sheafiness is the only further input.

#### The two edges of a double complex with exact augmented rows and columns have the same cohomology

`AdicSpacesPartII:R3/cech-double-complex-comparison` · lemma · declaration `HomologicalComplex₂.quasiIso_augmentToTotal_of_exact` · module `TauCeti/Algebra/Homology/DoubleComplexEdges`

Let K = (K^{p,q})_{p,q ≥ 0} be a first-quadrant double complex of abelian groups, with commuting differentials d′ : K^{p,q} → K^{p+1,q} and d″ : K^{p,q} → K^{p,q+1}. Let C^• and R^• be cochain complexes of abelian groups (C^p = R^q = 0 in negative degrees) with morphisms ε′ : C^p → K^{p,0} commuting with d′ and ε″ : R^q → K^{0,q} commuting with d″, such that (i) for every p ≥ 0 the augmented column 0 → C^p → K^{p,0} → K^{p,1} → ⋯ (maps ε′, d″) is exact, and (ii) for every q ≥ 0 the augmented row 0 → R^q → K^{0,q} → K^{1,q} → ⋯ (maps ε″, d′) is exact. Let Tot(K) be the total complex, Tot(K)ⁿ = ⊕_{p+q=n} K^{p,q} with differential d′ + (−1)^p d″. Then ε′ : C^• → Tot(K) and ε″ : R^• → Tot(K) (the latter composed with the sign (−1)^0 = 1 on K^{0,q}) are morphisms of complexes and quasi-isomorphisms; in particular Hⁿ(C^•) ≅ Hⁿ(R^•) for every n ≥ 0, naturally in the data (K, C, R, ε′, ε″). This is the cohomological form of Stacks Tag 00M1, which is stated for chain complexes; the proof is the same staircase argument with the indices reversed.

*Hypotheses.* K a first-quadrant double complex of abelian groups; every augmented column 0 → C^p → K^{p,•} and every augmented row 0 → R^q → K^{•,q} exact.

*Proof.*

1. Tot(K) is the total complex of the bicomplex (Mathlib `HomologicalComplex₂` with `HomologicalComplex₂.total`; first quadrant, so each Tot(K)ⁿ is a finite direct sum); ε′ and ε″ are chain maps because d″ ∘ ε′ = 0 and d′ ∘ ε″ = 0, which hold since ε′(C^p) = ker(d″ : K^{p,0} → K^{p,1}) and dually by (i), (ii).
2. Staircase: a cocycle of Tot(K)ⁿ is (x_{n,0}, x_{n−1,1}, …, x_{0,n}); using exactness of the columns (resp. rows) one modifies it by a coboundary step by step until only the component in K^{n,0} (resp. K^{0,n}) survives, and that component lies in ε′(Cⁿ) (resp. ε″(Rⁿ)); this gives surjectivity of Hⁿ(C) → Hⁿ(Tot) (resp. Hⁿ(R) → Hⁿ(Tot)).
3. Injectivity is the same staircase argument applied to a primitive in Tot(K)^{n−1} of the image of a cocycle of C (resp. R): exactness of the columns (resp. rows) pushes the primitive into the edge. This is the proof of Stacks Tag 00M1, which identifies both edge cohomologies with the group of staircase cocycles modulo staircase coboundaries.
4. Naturality: a morphism of the data (K, C, R, ε′, ε″) commutes with the edge maps into Tot(K), hence with the induced isomorphisms.

*Acceptance.* Degenerate case: if K^{p,q} = 0 for p > 0 then (ii) says R^• ≅ K^{0,•}, (i) says C^0 = ker(K^{0,0} → K^{0,1}) and C^p = 0 for p > 0, and the lemma reduces to Hⁿ(K^{0,•}) = C^0 for n = 0 and 0 otherwise, which is (i) for p = 0. For finite coverings 𝔙 and 𝔚 of an open U with 𝔚 refining 𝔙 and K^{p,q} = ∏ F(V_{i₀…i_p} ∩ W_{j₀…j_q}), C = Č(𝔙, F), R = Č(𝔚, F), the lemma is the comparison Ȟⁿ(𝔙, F) ≅ Ȟⁿ(𝔚, F) of AdicSpacesPartII:R3/cech-acyclicity-refinement.

*Used by.* AdicSpacesPartII:R3/cech-acyclicity-refinement — compares the Čech cohomology of a covering and of a refinement through the Čech double complex; Kedlaya–Liu 2015, proof of Proposition 2.4.21 — the 'spectral sequence argument' ([BGR, Corollary 8.1.4/3]) that makes universal Čech acyclicity local.

*Prerequisites.* `mathlib:HomologicalComplex₂`, `mathlib:HomologicalComplex₂.total`.

*Sources.* Stacks-Project, Tag 00M1, Lemma 10.75.3; Stacks-Project, Tag 00M1, Lemma 10.75.3; Stacks-Project, Tag 00M1, proof of Lemma 10.75.3.

#### Čech acyclicity is inherited from a refinement whose restrictions are acyclic

`AdicSpacesPartII:R3/cech-acyclicity-refinement` · lemma · declaration `Cech.augmented_exact_iff_of_refines` · module `TauCeti/Topology/Sheaves/Cech/Refinement`

Let X be a topological space, ℬ a family of open subsets of X closed under finite intersections, and F a presheaf of abelian groups on ℬ (restriction maps along inclusions in ℬ, functorial). For U ∈ ℬ and a finite covering 𝔘 = (U_i)_{i∈I} of U by members of ℬ, call 𝔘 F-acyclic if the augmented alternating Čech complex 0 → F(U) → ∏_{i₀} F(U_{i₀}) → ∏_{i₀<i₁} F(U_{i₀i₁}) → ⋯ (for a chosen total order of I) is exact. Let 𝔙 = (V_i)_{i∈I} and 𝔚 = (W_j)_{j∈J} be finite coverings of U ∈ ℬ by members of ℬ such that 𝔚 refines 𝔙 (every W_j is contained in some V_i). Suppose that for every p ≥ 0 and every i₀ < ⋯ < i_p in I the covering 𝔚 ∩ V_{i₀…i_p} = (W_j ∩ V_{i₀…i_p})_{j∈J} of V_{i₀…i_p} is F-acyclic. Then Ȟⁿ(U, F; 𝔙) ≅ Ȟⁿ(U, F; 𝔚) for every n ≥ 0, compatibly with the maps from F(U) in degree 0; in particular 𝔙 is F-acyclic if and only if 𝔚 is. Consequence (the locality used by Kedlaya–Liu): if 𝔚 refines 𝔙 and the restriction of 𝔚 to every member of ℬ contained in U is F-acyclic ('𝔚 is universally F-acyclic'), then so is every restriction of 𝔙.

*Hypotheses.* ℬ closed under finite intersections; F a presheaf of abelian groups on ℬ; 𝔙, 𝔚 finite coverings of U by members of ℬ, 𝔚 refining 𝔙; the restrictions of 𝔚 to all finite intersections of members of 𝔙 are F-acyclic.

*Proof.*

1. The alternating Čech complex is homotopy equivalent to the full Čech complex (Stacks Tag 01FM), so it suffices to argue with full Čech complexes; all intersections below lie in ℬ.
2. Form the Čech double complex K^{p,q} = ∏_{(i₀…i_p) ∈ I^{p+1}} ∏_{(j₀…j_q) ∈ J^{q+1}} F(V_{i₀…i_p} ∩ W_{j₀…j_q}) with the two Čech differentials; C = Č^•(𝔙, F) maps to the column edge and R = Č^•(𝔚, F) to the row edge by restriction.
3. Columns: for fixed (i₀…i_p) the augmented column is the augmented Čech complex of the covering 𝔚 ∩ V_{i₀…i_p} of V_{i₀…i_p}, exact by hypothesis.
4. Rows: for fixed (j₀…j_q), W_{j₀} ⊆ V_i for some i, so the covering 𝔙 ∩ W_{j₀…j_q} of W_{j₀…j_q} has the member V_i ∩ W_{j₀…j_q} = W_{j₀…j_q}; its augmented Čech complex is homotopy equivalent to 0 (Stacks Tag 0G6S), hence exact.
5. AdicSpacesPartII:R3/cech-double-complex-comparison gives Hⁿ(C) ≅ Hⁿ(Tot K) ≅ Hⁿ(R); the two maps F(U) → C⁰ → K^{0,0} and F(U) → R⁰ → K^{0,0} are both restriction to the V_i ∩ W_j, so the isomorphism in degree 0 is compatible with the maps from F(U), and exactness of one augmented complex is equivalent to exactness of the other.
6. Consequence: for U′ ∈ ℬ with U′ ⊆ U, 𝔚 ∩ U′ refines 𝔙 ∩ U′ and its restrictions to the intersections V_{i₀…i_p} ∩ U′ are restrictions of 𝔚, hence F-acyclic; apply the first part.

*Acceptance.* If 𝔙 = (U) is the trivial covering, every 𝔚 refines it and the lemma says 𝔚 is F-acyclic iff its restriction to U is, which is a tautology; if 𝔚 = 𝔙 the hypothesis is that 𝔙 is universally acyclic on its own intersections. Kedlaya–Liu's use: universal Čech acyclicity satisfies the locality condition (a) of Proposition 2.4.20 (AdicSpacesPartII:R3/cech-acyclicity-simple-laurent-reduction).

*Used by.* AdicSpacesPartII:R3/cech-acyclicity-simple-laurent-reduction — locality and transitivity of universal Čech acyclicity; Kedlaya–Liu 2015, proof of Proposition 2.4.21 — the spectral sequence argument citing [BGR, Corollary 8.1.4/3].

*Prerequisites.* `AdicSpacesPartII:R3/cech-double-complex-comparison`.

*Sources.* KedlayaLiu-RelativeFoundations-2015, §2.4, proof of Proposition 2.4.21, p. 46; KedlayaLiu-RelativeFoundations-2015, §2.4, proof of Proposition 2.4.21, p. 46; Stacks-Project, Tag 0G6S, Lemma 20.9.3; Stacks-Project, Tag 01FM, Lemma 20.23.6.

#### Čech acyclicity of a presheaf on all rational coverings follows from simple Laurent coverings (Kedlaya–Liu Proposition 2.4.21)

`AdicSpacesPartII:R3/cech-acyclicity-simple-laurent-reduction` · lemma · declaration `AdicSpace.cech_exact_of_simpleLaurent` · module `TauCeti/AlgebraicGeometry/AdicSpace/Coherent/CoveringReduction`

Let (A, A⁺) be a complete Hausdorff Tate Huber pair, X = Spa(A, A⁺), and F a presheaf of abelian groups on the rational subsets of X. Suppose that for every rational subset U ⊆ X and every f ∈ 𝒪_X(U), with V₁ = {x ∈ U : |f(x)| ≤ 1} and V₂ = {x ∈ U : |f(x)| ≥ 1} (rational subsets of X, anchor Layer 3.1), the sequence 0 → F(U) → F(V₁) ⊕ F(V₂) → F(V₁ ∩ V₂) → 0, (s ↦ (s|V₁, s|V₂), (a, b) ↦ a|V₁₂ − b|V₁₂), is exact. Then for every rational subset U ⊆ X and every finite covering 𝔘 of U by rational subsets, the augmented alternating Čech complex of F on 𝔘 is exact: Ȟ⁰(U, F; 𝔘) = F(U) and Ȟⁱ(U, F; 𝔘) = 0 for i > 0.

*Hypotheses.* (A, A⁺) complete Hausdorff Tate; F a presheaf of abelian groups on the rational subsets of Spa(A, A⁺); the two-term Čech sequence of every simple Laurent covering of every rational subset is exact.

*Proof.*

1. Rational subsets of X form a family closed under finite intersections (anchor Layer 2.2), and the rational subsets of a rational U = Spa(B, B⁺) are the rational subsets of X contained in U (anchor Layer 3.1); so the restriction of a finite rational covering to a rational subset is again one.
2. Let P(𝔘) for a finite rational covering 𝔘 of a rational U be: 'for every rational U′ ⊆ U the covering 𝔘 ∩ U′ of U′ is F-acyclic' (Kedlaya–Liu's universal Čech acyclicity, including degree 0).
3. (c) P holds for simple Laurent coverings: the restriction of the simple Laurent covering of U defined by f to a rational U′ ⊆ U is the simple Laurent covering of U′ defined by f|U′, and for a two-member covering the augmented alternating Čech complex is the displayed sequence, exact by hypothesis.
4. (a) P is local: if a refinement 𝔚 of 𝔘 satisfies P, the consequence clause of AdicSpacesPartII:R3/cech-acyclicity-refinement (with ℬ the rational subsets) gives P(𝔘).
5. (b) P is transitive: let {C_i} satisfy P and each {D_ij}_j satisfy P as coverings of C_i; for the composite covering 𝔇 = {D_ij} of U and any rational U′ ⊆ U, 𝔇 ∩ U′ refines {C_i ∩ U′}, and the restriction of 𝔇 ∩ U′ to C_{i₀…i_p} ∩ U′ contains the covering {D_{i₀ j} ∩ C_{i₀…i_p} ∩ U′}_j, which is F-acyclic by P for {D_{i₀ j}}_j and refines the whole restriction; two applications of AdicSpacesPartII:R3/cech-acyclicity-refinement give acyclicity of 𝔇 ∩ U′.
6. AdicSpacesPartII:R3/rational-covering-reduction (Kedlaya–Liu Proposition 2.4.20) turns (a)–(c) into P for every finite rational covering of every rational subset; P with U′ = U is the conclusion.

*Acceptance.* For F = 𝒪_X of a complete strongly noetherian Tate pair the hypothesis is anchor Layer 4.1's two-piece Laurent exactness (Wedhorn Lemma 8.33) and the conclusion is its all-degree Čech exactness. For F = M ⊗_A 𝒪_X with M finite projective over a sheafy Tate A, the hypothesis follows from the case F = 𝒪_X by taking direct summands (AdicSpacesPartII:R3/finite-projective-module-acyclicity).

*Used by.* AdicSpacesPartII:R3/sheafy-cech-acyclicity — reduces Čech acyclicity of 𝒪 on a sheafy Tate affinoid to simple Laurent coverings (Kedlaya–Liu Theorem 2.4.23); Kedlaya–Liu 2015, proof of Theorem 2.8.10 — the structure presheaf of a stably uniform ring satisfies the criterion of Proposition 2.4.21.

*Prerequisites.* `AdicSpacesPartII:R3/rational-covering-reduction`, `AdicSpacesPartII:R3/cech-acyclicity-refinement`, `tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/AdicSpaces#layer-2-affinoid-spectra-and-rational-subsets`, `tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/AdicSpaces#layer-3-rational-localisation-and-the-structure-presheaf`, `tauceti:TauCeti.Huber.IsTateRing`.

*Sources.* KedlayaLiu-RelativeFoundations-2015, §2.4, Proposition 2.4.21, p. 45; KedlayaLiu-RelativeFoundations-2015, §2.4, proof of Proposition 2.4.21, p. 46; KedlayaLiu-RelativeFoundations-2015, §2.4, proof of Proposition 2.4.21, p. 46.

#### For a simple Laurent covering the difference map B₁ ⊕ B₂ → B₁₂ is surjective (Kedlaya–Liu Lemma 2.4.22)

`AdicSpacesPartII:R3/simple-laurent-difference-surjective` · lemma · declaration `Huber.PairOfDefinition.laurentDifference_surjective` · module `TauCeti/RingTheory/Huber/LocalizationTopology/Laurent/Difference`

Let (A, A⁺) be a complete Hausdorff Huber pair and f ∈ A. Let A → B₁, A → B₂, A → B₁₂ be the rational localisations (anchor Layer 3.1, Tau Ceti `PairOfDefinition.completionLocObj`) of the rational subsets S₋ = R({f, 1}/1) = {v(f) ≤ 1}, S₊ = R({1, f}/f) = {v(f) ≥ 1} and S₋ ∩ S₊ = R({1, f, f²}/f) = {v(f) = 1} of Spa(A, A⁺), and ρ₁ : B₁ → B₁₂, ρ₂ : B₂ → B₁₂ the restriction maps. Then the map B₁ ⊕ B₂ → B₁₂, (b₁, b₂) ↦ ρ₁(b₁) − ρ₂(b₂), is surjective. No sheafiness, noetherian or Tate hypothesis is made.

*Hypotheses.* (A, A⁺) complete Hausdorff Huber pair; f ∈ A arbitrary.

*Proof.*

1. Evaluation maps: A⟨T⟩ → B₁ (T ↦ f), A⟨U⟩ → B₂ (U ↦ 1/f) and A⟨T, U⟩ → B₁₂ (T ↦ f, U ↦ 1/f) are continuous and surjective (Tau Ceti `PairOfDefinition.continuous_rationalEvalHom` and `PairOfDefinition.rationalEvalHom_surjective`, applied with numerator families (f, 1), (1, f), (1, f, f²) and then specialising the variable sent to 1; the neighbourhoods of 0 of a Huber ring are countably generated by the powers of an ideal of definition).
2. Compatibility: ρ₁ composed with A⟨T⟩ → B₁ and ρ₂ composed with A⟨U⟩ → B₂ are the restrictions of A⟨T, U⟩ → B₁₂ to A⟨T⟩ and A⟨U⟩, since continuous homomorphisms out of a restricted power-series ring are determined by the images of the constants and the variables (Tau Ceti `existsUnique_continuous_ringHom_completion_weightedRestrictedSubring`); and TU ↦ f · f⁻¹ = 1 in B₁₂.
3. Given b ∈ B₁₂ choose a lift Σ_{i,j ≥ 0} a_{ij} TⁱUʲ ∈ A⟨T, U⟩, so a_{ij} → 0. For n ∈ ℤ the series a′_n = Σ_{i−j=n} a_{ij} converges in the complete nonarchimedean ring A and a′_n → 0 as |n| → ∞.
4. Put b₁ = image of Σ_{n≥0} a′_n Tⁿ in B₁ and b₂ = image of −Σ_{n≥1} a′_{−n} Uⁿ in B₂. Rearranging the convergent series in B₁₂ using TU = 1 gives ρ₁(b₁) − ρ₂(b₂) = Σ a_{ij} f^{i−j} = b.

*Acceptance.* For A = ℚ_p⟨X⟩ and f = X: B₁ = ℚ_p⟨X⟩, B₂ = ℚ_p⟨X, X⁻¹⟩ = B₁₂, and ρ₂ is the identity, so the map is onto for trivial reasons; for f = X/p the lemma is the splitting of a Laurent series on the annulus |X| = |p| into its parts of nonnegative and negative degree. Outside sheafy rings the lemma still holds: for a non-sheafy pair (Kedlaya–Liu Example 2.8.7) the two-term Čech sequence can fail to be exact only at A or at B₁ ⊕ B₂.

*Used by.* AdicSpacesPartII:R3/sheafy-cech-acyclicity — exactness at B₁₂ of the simple Laurent Čech sequence (Kedlaya–Liu Theorem 2.4.23); AdicSpacesPartII:R3/simple-laurent-glueing-square — surjectivity half of condition (a) of a glueing square.

*Prerequisites.* `tauceti:TauCeti.Huber.PairOfDefinition.rationalEvalHom_surjective`, `tauceti:TauCeti.Huber.PairOfDefinition.continuous_rationalEvalHom`, `tauceti:TauCeti.Huber.existsUnique_continuous_ringHom_completion_weightedRestrictedSubring`, `tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/AdicSpaces#layer-3-rational-localisation-and-the-structure-presheaf`.

*Sources.* KedlayaLiu-RelativeFoundations-2015, §2.4, Lemma 2.4.22, p. 46; KedlayaLiu-RelativeFoundations-2015, §2.4, proof of Lemma 2.4.22, p. 46; KedlayaLiu-RelativeFoundations-2015, §2.4, proof of Lemma 2.4.22, p. 46; KedlayaLiu-RelativeFoundations-2015, §2.4, before Lemma 2.4.22, p. 46.

#### Čech acyclicity of the structure sheaf on every sheafy Tate affinoid (Kedlaya–Liu Theorem 2.4.23)

`AdicSpacesPartII:R3/sheafy-cech-acyclicity` · theorem · declaration `AdicSpace.cech_exact_of_isSheafyPair` · module `TauCeti/AlgebraicGeometry/AdicSpace/Sheafy/CechAcyclicity`

Let (A, A⁺) be a complete Hausdorff Tate Huber pair which is sheafy (`Huber.IsSheafyPair A A⁺`, anchor Layer 3.4: the structure presheaf 𝒪_X of X = Spa(A, A⁺) is a sheaf). Then (1) for every rational subset U ⊆ X and every finite covering 𝔘 = (U_i) of U by rational subsets, the augmented alternating Čech complex 0 → 𝒪_X(U) → ∏_i 𝒪_X(U_i) → ∏_{i<j} 𝒪_X(U_i ∩ U_j) → ⋯ is exact in every degree; (2) Hⁱ(U, 𝒪_X) = 0 for every i > 0 and every rational subset U, where Hⁱ is sheaf cohomology of the underlying sheaf of abelian groups on the topological space U. In particular H⁰(X, 𝒪_X) = A and Hⁱ(X, 𝒪_X) = Ȟⁱ(X, 𝒪_X; 𝔘) = 0 for i > 0 and every finite rational covering 𝔘 of X. No noetherian or uniformity hypothesis is made: the anchor's Layer 4.1 gives (1) for strongly noetherian A, and this theorem extends it to every sheafy Tate pair (for instance perfectoid and sousperfectoid ones).

*Hypotheses.* (A, A⁺) complete Hausdorff Tate Huber pair; (A, A⁺) sheafy: 𝒪_X is a sheaf on X = Spa(A, A⁺).

*Proof.*

1. Sheafiness passes to rational subsets: for a rational U with coordinate ring (B, B⁺) = (𝒪_X(U), 𝒪_X⁺(U)), Spa(B, B⁺) → U is a homeomorphism matching rational subsets and their coordinate rings (anchor Layer 3.1), so the structure presheaf of Spa(B, B⁺) is the restriction of 𝒪_X to U, which is a sheaf; (B, B⁺) is again a complete Tate sheafy pair.
2. Simple Laurent coverings: for U = Spa(B, B⁺) rational and f ∈ B, with B₁, B₂, B₁₂ the coordinate rings of {|f| ≤ 1}, {|f| ≥ 1} and their intersection, the sequence 0 → B → B₁ ⊕ B₂ → B₁₂ → 0 is exact at B₁₂ by AdicSpacesPartII:R3/simple-laurent-difference-surjective applied to (B, B⁺), and exact at B and at B₁ ⊕ B₂ by the sheaf property of 𝒪_X for the two-member covering of U.
3. AdicSpacesPartII:R3/cech-acyclicity-simple-laurent-reduction applied to F = 𝒪_X restricted to rational subsets gives (1).
4. (2): rational subsets form a basis of the topology of X closed under finite intersections (anchor Layer 2.2), and every open covering of a rational subset is refined by a finite rational covering (rational subsets are quasi-compact, anchor Layer 3.5); with (1), Cartan's criterion (Stacks Tag 01EW, requested from DiamondsAndVStacks:D0) gives Hⁱ(U, 𝒪_X) = 0 for i > 0 and U rational, and Ȟⁱ(X, 𝒪_X; 𝔘) = Hⁱ(X, 𝒪_X).

*Acceptance.* Tate's acyclicity on the disc: for A = K⟨T⟩ (K a complete nonarchimedean field, ϖ a pseudouniformiser; sheafy by anchor Layer 4.1) and the covering {|T| ≤ |ϖ|}, {|T| ≥ |ϖ|}, the sequence 0 → K⟨T⟩ → K⟨T/ϖ⟩ ⊕ K⟨T, ϖ/T⟩ → K⟨T/ϖ, ϖ/T⟩ → 0 is exact. Beyond the anchor: for a perfectoid affinoid (R, R⁺) (sheafy, Kedlaya–Liu Theorem 3.6.15; R is not noetherian) every finite rational covering of Spa(R, R⁺) has exact augmented Čech complex and Hⁱ(Spa(R, R⁺), 𝒪) = 0 for i > 0. The sheafiness hypothesis cannot be dropped: for a non-sheafy Tate pair some simple Laurent covering of some rational subset has a sequence 0 → B → B₁ ⊕ B₂ → B₁₂ → 0 that is not exact at B or at B₁ ⊕ B₂ (otherwise AdicSpacesPartII:R3/cech-acyclicity-simple-laurent-reduction and the basis criterion of anchor Layer 3.5 would make 𝒪_X a sheaf), while exactness at B₁₂ persists (AdicSpacesPartII:R3/simple-laurent-difference-surjective).

*Used by.* AdicSpacesPartII:R3/finite-projective-module-acyclicity — acyclicity of P̃ for finite projective P as a direct summand of 𝒪ⁿ; AdicSpacesPartII:R3/sheafy-tate-acyclicity-and-kiehl-gluing — the Tate sheaf property half of Kedlaya–Liu Theorem 2.7.7; Kedlaya–Liu 2015, Theorem 3.6.15 and Definition 8.2.2 — perfectoid algebras and general sheafy adic Banach rings satisfy the Tate sheaf property.

*Prerequisites.* `AdicSpacesPartII:R3/simple-laurent-difference-surjective`, `AdicSpacesPartII:R3/cech-acyclicity-simple-laurent-reduction`, `tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/AdicSpaces#layer-2-affinoid-spectra-and-rational-subsets`, `tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/AdicSpaces#layer-3-rational-localisation-and-the-structure-presheaf`, `DiamondsAndVStacks:D0`, `tauceti:TauCeti.Huber.IsTateRing`.

*Sources.* KedlayaLiu-RelativeFoundations-2015, §2.4, Theorem 2.4.23, p. 46; KedlayaLiu-RelativeFoundations-2015, §2.4, proof of Theorem 2.4.23, p. 47; KedlayaLiu-RelativeFoundations-2015, §2.4, proof of Theorem 2.4.23, p. 47; KedlayaLiu-RelativeFoundations-2015, §2.4, proof of Proposition 2.4.21, p. 46; Stacks-Project, Tag 01EW, Lemma 20.11.9.

### R3.2 Glueing squares and Kiehl's theorem

Kedlaya–Liu's glueing squares give surjectivity of sections for finite glueing data on a simple Laurent covering; Kiehl's second-presentation trick then produces a finite module whenever rational localisation is flat, i.e. for every complete strongly noetherian Tate ring. This proves Kiehl's theorem in the generality of Huber's type II, for which Kedlaya–Liu (Remark 2.5.23) record that no precise reference exists.

#### Glueing squares of complete Tate rings

`AdicSpacesPartII:R3/glueing-square` · definition · declaration `Huber.GlueingSquare` · module `TauCeti/RingTheory/Huber/Glueing/Square`

A glueing square is a commutative square of complete Hausdorff Tate rings with continuous homomorphisms R → R₁, R → R₂, R₁ → R₁₂, R₂ → R₁₂ such that (a) the sequence 0 → R → R₁ × R₂ → R₁₂ → 0, (r₁, r₂) ↦ r₁ − r₂, is exact and strict (R carries the subspace topology of R₁ × R₂ and R₁ × R₂ → R₁₂ is open onto R₁₂); (b) R₂ → R₁₂ has dense image; (c) every maximal ideal of R is the contraction of a prime ideal of R₁ × R₂. A finite (resp. finite projective) glueing datum on it is a triple of finite (resp. finite projective) modules M₁, M₂, M₁₂ over R₁, R₂, R₁₂ with isomorphisms ψ_i : M_i ⊗_{R_i} R₁₂ ≅ M₁₂; its module of sections is M = ker(ψ₁ − ψ₂ : M₁ × M₂ → M₁₂). Convention: condition (c) replaces Kedlaya–Liu's surjectivity of Gel'fand spectra M(R₁ ⊕ R₂) → M(R), which they use only through (c); every topological ring here is metrised by the norm |x| = inf{cⁿ : ϖ⁻ⁿx ∈ R₀} of a pseudouniformiser ϖ and ring of definition R₀ (KL Remark 2.4.4).

*Hypotheses.* all four rings complete Hausdorff Tate rings; maps continuous; (a) strict exactness, (b) density, (c) maximal ideals lift.

*Construction.*
